title: Lions score nine quick points before halftime, lead Bears 19-10
summary: A safety and a touchdown have the home team up after 30 minutes of play.
full_text: The Lions and Bears were tied at the two-minute warning of Thursday's game in Detroit, but things swung in the home team's favor before the halftime break. Defensive end Derrick Moore forced Bears quarterback Caleb Williams to fumble on a sack in the end zone and Bears tackle Darnell Wright was flagged for batting the ball back into the field of play. That's a safety and Lions head coach Dan Campbell opted to accept that rather than decline the penalty and take the ball on the Chicago 14-yard-line. That choice paid off with more points for the Lions. Jared Goff and Jameson Williams hooked up for a 39-yard gain to move the ball deep into Bears territory and Goff found tight end Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard touchdown with six seconds to play in the half. That pushed Detroit's lead to 19-10 at halftime. The Bears will get the ball coming out of the locker room, but the two scores make for a big swing in momentum after the Bears erased a 10-point deficit earlier in the second quarter. Goff is 13-of-22 for 193 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs has 98 yards from scrimmage. Gibbs also scored his 16th touchdown of the season earlier in the game. The Bears lost tight end Colston Loveland to a knee injury early in the game, so he won't be part of any comeback effort that Chicago is able to put together in the final 30 minutes.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers activate Michael Pittman Jr., sign Max Hurleman to active roster
summary: Mason Rudolph will have wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. available as a target in his first start of the 2026 season.
full_text: Mason Rudolph will have wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. available as a target in his first start of the 2026 season. The Steelers activated Pittman from injured reserve on Thursday, which sets him up to face the Broncos on Friday afternoon. Pittman had seven catches for 89 yards in the first three games of the season. Rudolph will also be able to throw to Max Hurleman. Hurleman was a topic of conversation at Aaron Rodgers's final press conference as a member of the Steelers because Rodgers questioned why the front office did not have him on the active roster. The team remedied that on Thursday, but Rodgers will not be able to benefit since he was released after far more critical comments about the organization in the wake of his benching on Tuesday night. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek was placed on injured reserve and the Steelers also elevated offensive lineman Doug Nester and linebacker Jacoby Windmon from the practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears tie Lions 10-10 on Kyle Monangai TD
summary: The Bears spotted the Lions a 10-point lead in the second quarter, but they've wiped it out with four minutes to go in the first half.
full_text: The Bears spotted the Lions a 10-point lead in the second quarter, but they've wiped it out with four minutes to go in the first half. Running back Kyle Monangai scored from a yard out to make it 10-10 in Detroit. The touchdown capped an eight-play, 80-yard drive that saw Monangai's backfield mate D'Andre Swift account for the longest gain. Swift caught a short pass from Caleb Williams and followed downfield blocks for a 33-yard gain. Williams also completed a pair of passes to tight end Stephen Carlson for 30 yards on the way to the end zone. Those were Carlson's first two catches of the season and the Bears may continue to look his way now that they've lost Colston Loveland to a knee injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chargers sign Jake Browning to active roster
summary: The Chargers' starting quarterback is in the concussion protocol, so they moved to add another healthy one to the active roster on Thursday.
full_text: ' The Chargers' starting quarterback is in the concussion protocol, so they moved to add another healthy one to the active roster on Thursday. The team announced that they have signed Jake Browning off of their practice squad. Browning signed with the Chargers in October. Justin Herbert did not practice on Wednesday because of his concussion, which left DJ Uiagalelei to take the first-team reps. Uiagalelei has appeared in one game this season and he went 2-of-7 for 24 yards and a touchdown. The Chargers placed defensive back Deane Leonard on injured reserve to make room for Browning. He had 13 tackles in six appearances this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jahmyr Gibbs puts Lions up 10-0, Colston Loveland out with knee injury
summary: Loveland left the game on a cart in the first quarter.
full_text: The Lions are up two scores in the second quarter in Detroit. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs punched the ball in from the 1-yard-line with 12:51 to play in the first half and the Lions are now up 10-0 on the Bears. The Bears' comeback efforts will be hindered by the loss of tight end Colston Loveland. Loveland was carted off in the first quarter and the Lions announced that he is out for the rest of the game with a knee injury. Gibbs is now up to 16 touchdowns on the season and he's picked up 55 yards from scrimmage thus far. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has three catches for 69 yards, including a 23-yarder on the touchdown drive. Loveland lost a fumble on the Bears' first possession and the Lions forced a three-and-out on the second, so the offense needs to get in gear for Chicago.
author: Josh Alper

title: Colston Loveland goes to locker room in the first quarter
summary: A key member of the Bears offense has gone to the locker room with an injury in the first quarter.
full_text: A key member of the Bears offense has gone to the locker room with an injury in the first quarter. Tight end Colston Loveland was checked out in the sideline medical tent and then loaded onto a cart to head inside for further evaluations. Loveland had one catch for five yards, but then lost the ball on a hit by Lions defensive end Derrick Moore. Linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the ball to end the first Bears offensive possession of the day. Loveland went to the locker room after the second Chicago possession and center Garrett Bradbury also suffered an injury on that drive. The Lions drove for a field goal to open the game and remain up 3-0 with under three minutes to play in the first quarter.
author: Josh Alper

title: Art Rooney II expresses support for Mike McCarthy, calls Aaron Rodgers not a "good teammate"
summary: Steelers owner speaks about Wednesday's insanity.
full_text: After Wednesday's unprecedented chaos, it had to happen. And it did. Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the events that resulted in the benching and then the firing of quarterback Aaron Rodgers. “A change had to be made , and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled," Rooney told Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette in a Thursday interview. The change was sparked by the notion that Rodgers gave coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: “Either let me call all the plays or just release me.” Instead, McCarthy benched him. It went to the next level when, as many expected, Rodgers scurried to the McAfee show to take shots at McCarthy for missing meetings, showing up late to meetings, and falling asleep in meetings — among other things, including the ultra-embarrassing "1-2-3 Packers!" moment from halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles. “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. . . . “In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.” Rooney also confirmed that the team supports McCarthy, despite Rodgers's rant and reports confirming the facts underpinning the petty delivery of them. “I just want to say that I have 100 [percent] confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney also was asked whether Rodgers raised with the owner supposed concerns about McCarthy's health. “Nothing,” Rooney said. “Mike’s as healthy as the rest of us. Health was not an issue. I’m not sure where that part comes [from].” Rooney also addressed something that has been largely overlooked during the fast-moving drama: Rodgers's subpar performance. “The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.” They should have known it wouldn't work between Rodgers and McCarthy. It's still unclear why either one of them thought it would. McCarthy shouldn't have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And Rodgers shouldn't have wanted a second act with McCarthy. Then again, it's not as if Rodgers had many choices. In 2025, he had few takers. In 2026, he had fewer. If he was going to ensure that his final NFL throw wasn't a pick-six by playing another year, Pittsburgh wasn't just the best place. It was likely the only place.
author: Mike Florio

title: Blake Corum supplants Kyren Williams as the Rams' top tailback
summary: It's been slowly building throughout the season.
full_text: '' It's been slowly building throughout the season. On Wednesday night, it became abundantly clear. Blake Corum has become the Rams' top tailback. On his 26th birthday, Corum had a career night. Thirty-two carries, 184 yards, and a touchdown. Throw in 21 receiving yards, and he had 205 yards from scrimmage. “Happy birthday, man," coach Sean McVay told reporters after the game. "He was on the set of Netflix so we didn't even get to enjoy it with him. So, I know that kind of pissed me off, honestly." Corum's gains have come at the expense of Kyren Williams. Despite a report that he's been dealing with turf toe for a month, this week was Williams's first appearance all year on the injury report. And while the fact that Corum got the start last night and 58 snaps while Williams was limited to 38 may have had something to do with the toe, as Mike Tomlin says, "One man's misfortune is another man's opportunity." Corum seized the opportunity on Wednesday night, as part of a very un-Rams-like offensive output that included 241 rushing yards and 132 passing yards. For the season, Williams has 662 rushing yards and an average of 4.4 yards per carry. Corum has 731 yards rushing with a 5.4-yard average. Lurking in the background (but soon moving to the foreground) is the business side of the situation. Corum is in the third year of a slotted, third-round rookie deal. He's making $1.582 million in 2026, and he's eligible for a second contract as soon as the regular season ends. Williams is making $11 million per year, on a deal that runs through 2028. They'll need to reward Corum at some point, which could force them to make a decision about Williams. That's clearly coming. Last night's breakout showing in a standalone game shows that it's coming quickly.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Lions, despite their resurgence, are 1-8 in their last nine Thanksgiving games
summary: The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022.
full_text: The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022. That hasn't translated to sustained success on Thanksgiving. They're 1-8 over the last nine Thanksgiving Day games. The one win in that stretch came two years ago, against the Bears. That day, Chicago pocketed a timeout as the final 30 seconds or so ticked away, leaving the Bears without enough time to attempt a field goal that would have forced overtime in a 23-20 game. The next day, the Bears fired coach Matt Eberflus. It paved the way for the eventual hiring of Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, who returns to Ford Field today for the second time. Last year's game didn't go very well. Detroit scored 52 points. The Bears lost the Soldier Field rematch, too. This year, history takes a back seat to the immediate future. Both the Bears and the Lions are 8-2. The Lions have won all six of their home games. The winner takes control, for now, of the NFC North — and stays within striking distance of the 9-1 49ers for the No. 1 seed. It's not hyperbole to call it the most significant early-window Thanksgiving game ever. In many years, the Lions were the punching bag on turkey day. They're now the ones doing the punching. Which makes the 1-8 trend even more surprising. For the Bears, the challenge is to prove that they're Super Bowl contenders. They entered the discussion with their Week 8 Monday night win in Seattle. Today, the Bears have a chance to control the narrative. However it goes, the numbers should be eye-popping. For last year's Packers-Lions game, 47.7 million tuned in. It was a new all-time regular-season record audience, until Chiefs-Cowboys later that day shattered it with 57.23 million viewers. All three games could be compelling today. Eagles-Cowboys got a boost from both teams winning on Sunday. And Chiefs-Bills continues to be one of the top rivalries in the league — even if cold and wind and rain could take more than a little steam out of the offenses. Enjoy the day. We'll be here throughout the games, posting all relevant updates and other NFL news. It's a privilege, not a burden, to spend time on Thanksgiving doing what we always do. And we're thankful for the fact that you choose to consume it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chuck Clark, DJ Wonnum are inactive for the Lions
summary: The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears.
full_text: The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears. Safety Chuck Clark and defensive end DJ Wonnum are both inactive after being listed as questionable to play on the team's final injury report. Clark has a hamstring injury and Wonnum has a back injury. Clark's absence could lead to more playing time for Kerby Joseph, who will be playing his second game since being activated from the physically unable to perform list. The Lions will also be getting cornerback D.J. Reed back after he missed three games with a hip injury. Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw, defensive back Keith Abney, and defensive end Tyrus Wheat are also inactive for Detroit. The Bears have deactivated quarterback Case Keenum, cornerback Kyler Gordon, cornerback Isaac Yiadom, defensive back Elijah Hicks, running back Roschon Johnson, offensive lineman Jordan McFadden, and defensive lineman Jayden Loving.
author: Josh Alper

title: On Our Way Home is free on Thursday and Friday
summary: The holiday season is here.
full_text: The holiday season is here. And I'm in the mood to give something away. (It must be the whiskey.) The On Our Way Home ebook is available for free on Thursday and Friday. Why not give something away? This is the week when everyone is trying to sell you something. No one is giving you anything, with zero strings attached. On Our Way Home is primarily a Christmas story. It's also a ghost story. I cranked it out between Thanksgiving and New Year's Day a few years back. In the interests of avoiding any spoilers, I'll just say this: Download it and give it a try. It's essentially about family and redemption and reconciliation. It's also about forgiving others, while finding a way to forgive yourself. It's funny at times. It's sad at times. If you make it to the end, you'll possibly shed a tear or two. The best feedback I've gotten came from a reader who had suffered from PTSD for years. Reading On Our Way Home unlocked his ability to feel emotions again. I never intended anything like that. I just had an idea for a story, years before writing it. One year, I got caught up in the spirit of the season and it flowed, one chapter, one page, one word at a time. The price is right. If you don't like it, delete it. If you like it, keep going. Speaking of free, Quarterback of the Future is being posted , one chapter at a time. Twenty-five chapters are up. A new one is coming every day until it's done. Someone asked recently why my break from writing consists of more writing. There's something magical and, frankly, fun about creating something out of nothing. It's even more fun when people read it and enjoy it. Whether you enjoy it is up to you. If you don't, that's on me. But it won't cost you a penny to find out, if you download On Our Way Home on Thursday or Friday.
author: Mike Florio

title: After his Pittsburgh exit, what's next for Aaron Rodgers?
summary: As Aaron Rodgers enters waivers, the first question is whether any team will claim the balance of his one-year contract.
full_text: As Aaron Rodgers enters waivers, the first question is whether any team will claim the balance of his one-year contract. Obviously, no one will do it without ensuring that Rodgers actually wants to play for that team. Unless, of course, a team or two hopes to troll Rodgers by forcing him to show up to play where he doesn't want to play. Like Marty Schottenheimer did to Deion Sanders in 2002. So, yes, it would be hilarious if the Jets decide to put in the proper paperwork. The more likely outcome is that he'll clear waivers and become a free agent. It will give him the ability to sign with any team, at any time. No clear-cut contender currently needs a starter. And it would make no sense for Rodgers to sidle up to a quarterback-needy also-ran, like the Cardinals. Some have suggested that Rodgers could join the Patriots, who will be missing Drake Maye while they try to parlay 5-5 into playoff position. His August comments about the Mike Vrabel-Diana Russini situation would potentially be an impediment to that outcome. There's a spicy possibility of Rodgers aligning with the Ravens, who still play the Steelers twice. Is he that petty? At this point, it's impossible to say he's not. Rodgers's best play could be to wait. Let fate decide. Last year, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix broke his ankle late in a playoff win over the Bills. If Denver's instant desperation caused them to consider dusting off Drew Brees (despite the fact that he can't throw a football with his dominant arm), they would have surely called Rodgers, if he'd been available. Something like that can happen again. Of course, a team that loses its starter to injury between now and the Super Bowl would have to want to do business with him. Which means accepting the very strong possibility that, in time, Rodgers will have grievances to air about his experience. Because if it goes poorly, it won't be his fault. There will be other reasons for his struggles. Reasons that he has shown he has no qualms about sharing in his national-media safe space. During his 22-year career, Rodgers has played for three NFL teams. He ended up disgruntled in each location. If he adds a fourth franchise to the list, he'll likely find a way to be disgruntled there, too. Unless it's a very short-term arrangement. As short as one or two playoff games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan on Brandon Aiyuk signing with Commanders: "They got a good player"
summary: The Aaron Rodgers rigmarole has pushed plenty of other stories out of the spotlight.
full_text: ' The Aaron Rodgers rigmarole has pushed plenty of other stories out of the spotlight. Including the sudden second act for Brandon Aiyuk. Aiyuk visited the Commanders on Wednesday, two days after being released by the 49ers and one day after clearing waivers. He promptly signed with the team's practice squad. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan was asked for his thoughts on Aiyuk landing with the Commanders. “None," Shanahan told reporters. "It was just a transactional thing and it's good for Washington. They got a good player.” Indeed they did. That's why the 49ers signed him to a four-year, $120 million contract only 27 months ago. They could have traded him to the Steelers. They paid him. It all fell apart after that, perhaps fueled by the lingering rancor of the protracted and contentious contract talks. Everyone hopefully learned a lesson. Now, the Commanders have a much-needed piece to the offense. A player who can help fill the void created when Terry McLaurin was lost for the season. And the Commanders — despite being 4-5-1 — remain in solid position to make a late-season run. With seven games to play, they're two games behind the Giants. The Commanders hold the tiebreaker, thanks to the 1-0-1 record in their 2026 head-to-head competition. The Commanders face the Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons, Vikings, Jaguars, and Cowboys. The Giants have the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks, Browns, Lions, Cowboys, and Eagles. Along the way, the Commanders will also need to leapfrog the 5-6 Cowboys. Still, it's far from crazy to think the Commanders can pull it off. However it plays out, the Commanders have added a player who will potentially help them navigate the remaining schedule in a way that vaults them into the postseason. Who knows? Maybe Aiyuk will get a chance to return to Santa Clara in January. And maybe the Commanders will get a chance to do what they nearly did in Week 6. That's still weeks away. But it will be here quickly. And Commanders-49ers is one of the various potential permutations that could play out as the playoffs approach and the postseason commences.
author: Mike Florio

title: The clock is ticking on Mike McCarthy's time with the Steelers
summary: McCarthy's future likely hinges on his ability to win games down the stretch.
full_text: When it comes to the nuclear war of words that Aaron Rodgers started on Wednesday, the end result is the same as it would be if the world's superpowers ever started hunting and pecking the launch codes. Mutually assured destruction. Rodgers, as multiple former Green Bay Packers are making clear, is destroying his reputation and legacy as a teammate by breaking the fundamental code of the locker room. But he's also destroying Mike McCarthy's reputation and legacy as a coach. For a change, Rodgers's rant was centered in reality. ESPNFL reports that the things Rodgers said about McCarthy are true . Which could make it impossible for the Steelers to keep McCarthy beyond the 2026 season. His only path to salvation is to win. Starting on Friday, when the 8-2 Broncos come to town for a game against a Steelers team that, despite the sudden dysfunction, is 6-4. It's really that simple. The next seven games will become the litmus test as to whether McCarthy's now-documented snoring-and-ice-cream-sandwiches flaws are outweighed by his capabilities. Of course, the fact that Rodgers rolled a grenade into the locker room on his way out won't make that any easier. Which could be one of the reasons why Rodgers did it. Maximum chaos will make it harder for McCarthy to win. Which will make it harder for McCarthy to make it to Year 2. Which will create the impression that Rodgers has been vindicated. Sure, the initial word is that the situation doesn't impact McCarthy's standing. But the most important aspect of Wednesday's report from ESPNFL that McCarthy " has the full support of the organization " carries an important qualifier. The Steelers are "not planning to make any immediate changes." So they're not firing McCarthy or asking him to resign before Friday's game. What happens if the Steelers lose by double digits to the Broncos? What happens if the current two-game losing streak becomes an extended skid that sweeps them out of the AFC postseason field? The answer will become obvious based on how the final seven games unfold. In the immediate aftermath of Aaron Rodgers dumping Agent Orange on the organization, it's hard to imagine McCarthy surviving this. Ultimately, the decision will be made by owner Art Rooney II. And the outcome could show where the Steelers reside on the line that divides the functional from dysfunctional franchises. Functional teams admit mistakes and commence rectifying them. Dysfunctional teams deny the facts and double down.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kamren Kinchens: No ill intent on hit that concussed Christian Watson
summary: The Rams defense pitched a shutout in the second half on Wednesday night and they did it without safety Kamren Kinchens in the lineup.
full_text: '' The Rams defense pitched a shutout in the second half on Wednesday night and they did it without safety Kamren Kinchens in the lineup. Kinchens was ejected from the game just before halftime because of a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson. Kinchens was initially flagged for unnecessary roughness and the penalty was upgraded to a disqualification after video review by league officials. After the game, Kinchens said he couldn't really argue with the decision but that he didn't regret the play because Watson's injury was an unintended consequence of trying to make a play. "No ill intent ," Kinchens said. "I wasn’t trying to hurt the guy. Just playing football, fast physical football." Watson was ruled out for the rest of the game with a concussion and will have over a week to clear the protocol before the Packers' Week 13 game against the Saints.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tony Romo re-emerges, as an employee of a gambling company
summary: The unofficial path for a sports-media second act is becoming more and more clear.
full_text: The unofficial path for a sports-media second act is becoming more and more clear. Go gambling, young man . Tony Romo, whose career with CBS ended earlier this year in the aftermath of a DUI arrest that would have been overlooked if the company was otherwise happy with his work, will be the " chief predictions officer " at Betr. The press release leans in to Romo's reputation for being able to predict plays before they happen. This overlooks the fact that he got away from doing that after his first year or so in the CBS booth. It also glosses over the reality that his access to practice and production meetings equipped him with the ability to make "predictions" that (based on his inside information) also could be called "spoilers." It's not entirely clear what he'll be doing. The release says that Romo will "serve as a prominent face of the Betr brand, appearing in original content, delivering sports predictions and engaging fans across the company's expanding ecosystem of gaming products." Of course, Betr won't want his predictions to be too accurate — as it relates to its sportsbook. The sportsbooks only win when the customers lose. If the customers win too much, the sportsbook will land in one of two chapters: 11 or 7. Prediction markets are different. The companies make money on the transactions, with the participants balancing out wins and losses in the zero-sum game of who's right and who's wrong. The next question is whether this is the first step for Romo, or whether it's his primary post-CBS play. With the NFL and its broadcast partners aligned with the Coke and Pepsi of sports gambling, Romo's relationship with one of the various companies that hopes to establish itself as the RC Cola won't improve his shot at getting back into a prominent position in a broadcast booth. Regardless, Romo is back. At least he's not working for an illegal offshore sportsbook. Either way, his message will be the same to the masses as it is to those who are looking for a fresh foothold in sports media. Go gambling, young man.
author: Mike Florio

title: Micah Parsons: Our play in second half Wednesday night was inexcusable
summary: The Rams ran for 195 yards after halftime in their 26-13 win.
full_text: '' Packers defensive end Micah Parsons made his return to the lineup against the Rams on Wednesday night, but he wasn't able to help his team to a win in Los Angeles. Parsons picked up a sack late in the first half that sent the game to the break with the score tied 13-13, but he couldn't make an impact in the second half because the Rams barely threw the ball. After running 12 times for 46 yards in the first half, the Rams ran 35 times for 194 yards while outscoring the Packers 13-0 in the final 30 minutes. After the game, Parsons said it is "just inexcusable" to allow opposing teams to "dictate games like that" and said the aftermath has to be an increased level of accountability for the entire defense. "We need to figure out who's going to be a dog or not," Parsons said. "That’s just the reality of it. To me, to be honest and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don't have an answer for it, that is player — that's accountability. That's just how I really feel about it. I wasn't able to get on the field because of it, because they didn't want to waste my plays on first and second down I think the whole thing is just bad and we've got to figure out who's willing to play with us or who's playing against us at this point." The Packers don't have the luxury of having time to figure things out. The loss dropped them to 6-5 on the season and the makeup of the NFC means that they're going to have to win most of their remaining games to have any chance of advancing to the postseason.
author: Josh Alper

title: Here's a roadmap to the Aaron Rodgers developments, one of the craziest stories in years
summary: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck.
full_text: ' If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck. We've reconstructed the full timeline as to the events regarding now-former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It actually started on Monday, when coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether he has considered using one of the team's other three quarterbacks when the offense is struggling. McCarthy, whose body language in hindsight suggests he was dreading the question , said without equivocation, " Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback ." On Tuesday, Rodgers took his usual reps at practice. He conducted his usual midweek press conference. Unbeknownst to most of the media or the general public, the Steelers were changing their play-calling procedures to have quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, and not McCarthy, communicate the calls to Rodgers through the speaker in his helmet. Then came Tuesday night. At 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers issued a statement — not from coach Mike McCarthy or G.M. Omar Khan or owner Art Rooney II but from team spokesman Burt Lauten — that Mason Rudolph will start on Friday against the Broncos and Rodgers will be inactive. The news forced the Broncos to make a quick pivot in their preparations from Rodgers to Rudolph. As one source put it, the Broncos weren't sure whether it was a good thing or a bad thing . It was definitely a bad thing, all things considered, for the Steelers. By Wednesday morning, reports emerged that it was a coach’s decision . At 8:00 a.m. ET, McCarthy informed the team of the decision. Rodgers wasn’t there . As it turns out, he was excused . Enter Pat McAfee. He teased a surprise guest at 1:40 p.m. ET. As expected, it was Rodgers. Rodgers took a flamethrower to McCarthy, airing out dirty laundry that created a major mess for his now-former team. He exposed the fact that, at halftime of the Week 11 loss to the Eagles, McCarthy broke down the locker-room gathering by saying, " 1-2-3 Packers ." Rodgers also said McCarthy was falling asleep during some meetings and missing other meetings, expressing (in passive-aggressive fashion) concern for McCarthy's health. But Rodgers also said it was nothing new, and that McCarthy had done the same things in Green Bay, when they worked there together a decade ago. Rodgers also made it clear he wouldn't stay with the Steelers. After his session with McAfee and company, Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported that the Steelers were expected to release Rodgers . By the official close of business, they’d waived him . A question lingers as to whether the Steelers will try to deny Rodgers the balance of his $22 million salary. It won't be easy; they'll need to both void the guarantees and wipe out his eligibility for termination pay (in the form of his remaining salary) under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. McCarthy met with reporters on Wednesday, after all hell had broken loose. He admitted to the "1-2-3 Packers" comment, calling it an " [e]mbarrassing moment ." McCarthy also said that Rodgers was benched after issuing an "ultimatum" that was " clearly outside of his job description ." ESPNFL thereafter reported that McCarthy " has the full support " of the organization, and that the team is "not planning to make any immediate changes." The key word may be "immediate"; with few viable options only two days before a Black Friday game against the Broncos, changes could come later. The overriding takeaway is that someone with the Steelers knew or should have known that McCarthy and Rodgers couldn't co-exist. Because, obviously, they didn't co-exist. If, as Rodgers claims, McCarthy believed Rodgers got him fired in Green Bay, McCarthy shouldn't have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And if, as Rodgers claims, McCarthy was doing the same kinds of things in Green Bay that he did in Pittsburgh, Rodgers shouldn't have wanted a reunion with McCarthy. The reunion has now ended abruptly, with seven games left in the 2026 regular season. It remains to be seen whether Rodgers wants to play with another team, or whether another team wants him. Any team that signs him risks being on the receiving end of a future gripe session from Rodgers in which he lists all the things that team and/or the coach did wrong — without ever acknowledging his own role in the reality that it didn't work out. The good news, if there is any, is this: If Rodgers never plays again, his final NFL pass will have been a touchdown . Which is a better outcome than if he'd retired after the 2025 season. His final pass that year was a pick-six in the playoffs .
author: Mike Florio

title: James Jones: I'm on text threads with former Packers, none are on Aaron Rodgers' side
summary: In the dispute between Steelers coach Mike McCarthy and ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, players who were with both of them in Green Bay are squarely on McCarthy's side.
full_text: In the dispute between Steelers coach Mike McCarthy and ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, players who were with both of them in Green Bay are squarely on McCarthy's side. That's the word from former Packers wide receiver James Jones, who echoed the comments of former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang , both of whom say that in text threads of former Packers players, everyone agrees that Rodgers' criticism of McCarthy was out of line. "How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast . "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike." Jones said that even if everything Rodgers said about McCarthy's shortcomings as a coach is true, airing dirty laundry in public is unacceptable. Jones said that when a coach and a player have the kind of personal history that McCarthy and Rodgers have, they should address their differences privately. "I don't even care if it's the truth," Jones said. "Have the conversation with Mike in there. This is not something you go to the media bashing somebody. I would not do this to people that I love." It's safe to say that there's no love anymore between Rodgers and McCarthy. But there is a lot of love for McCarthy among former Packers players, who are not happy that Rodgers chose to publicly attack their coach.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jayden Daniels: Brandon Aiyuk and I put the past behind us
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media.
full_text: ' Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media. After Aiyuk signed with the Commanders this week, however, Daniels said that's all behind them. "I'm a grown man, he's a grown man," Daniels said. "Things happen. You don't know what he was going through. You don't know what I was going through at that time." Daniels said he looked up to Aiyuk when they were at Arizona State together and thinks they can have a good relationship as teammates again. "That's somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU," Daniels said. "So, like I said, I know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle our differences and just move forward from there. That's like a brother to me. Like I said, we've been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, just put the past behind us." As for the social media posts that Aiyuk made, Daniels said he was never angry about that. "I prayed for him because he's like family to me," Daniels said. "I think that was a very dark moment in his life." Daniels declined to go into specifics about recent conversations with Aiyuk but said he hopes Aiyuk will be a good addition to the Commanders. "That's between us, personal, but yeah, we did chat," Daniels said. "He works hard. Before his knee injury he was All-Pro, very explosive, big catch radius, so excited for him to have a fresh start, new opportunity to prove himself day in and day out." Aiyuk hasn't played in more than two years, but he was once one of the best receivers in the NFL. If Aiyuk can play at anything close to the level he used to play at, he can be a significant addition to the Commanders' offense. Daniels is excited about that possibility.

title: T.J. Lang blasts "despicable" Aaron Rodgers comments about Mike McCarthy
summary: T.J.
full_text: T.J. Lang blocked for Aaron Rodgers for eight seasons in Green Bay. Currently, Lang would be more inclined to knock Rodgers on his ass. Lang sharply criticized Rodgers for his decision to go public with issues that should have stayed in the Pittsburgh locker room. “ I think it’s despicable ,” Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit, via Sean Keeley of Awful Announcing . “I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates, airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. “He has blacklisted, I don’t know how many, former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just — he was sick of it. Honestly, I don’t even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. It’s a victim mentality. It’s a 'poor me, woe is me. Oh, I thought this, and it wasn’t that.’ And I’m sick, man. “I’ve been in a group chat with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do.” Most football players would feel that way. There's a code in the locker room. Rodgers violated it. “Mike McCarthy was my head coach for 8 years, and I love Mike McCarthy,” Lang said. “And I talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday night, and still have a great relationship with him. “I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably 5 years. I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. And I think it’s just absolutely despicable what he just did to Big Mike.” Rodgers isn't a whistleblower. He's a troublemaker. He didn't get his way, so he emptied a can of gasoline and tossed a match over his shoulder on the way out the door. How does any of it help his now-former teammates? Rodgers's decision to air out dirty laundry has created a massive distraction that will do nothing to help the team win. Accurate or not, the task at hand becomes harder now that everyone is buzzing about Rodgers's comments. That said, no one should be surprised. It's part and parcel of doing business with Rodgers. When it ends — and end it will — it will end poorly. Like it did in Green Bay. Like it did in New York. Like it did in Pittsburgh. Like it will end for his next team, if there is one. And if there is, the message is clear. Buyer beware.

title: Rams shut down Packers in second half for a 26-13 win in NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game
summary: The Rams running game powered them to their fifth straight win.
full_text: The Rams and Packers played to a tie in the first 30 minutes of Wednesday night's game in Los Angeles, but the second half was all Rams. Blake Corum ran for 151 yards and a score in final 30 minutes and the Rams defense shut out the Packers to pave the way to a 26-13 win. The victory is the fifth in a row for the Rams and they are now 7-4 with a Thursday night home game against the Chiefs on deck in Week 13. The win moves the Rams ahead of the Packers in the race for NFC playoff spots and Thursday's game between the Lions and Bears will have further impact on the chances for all four teams to advance to the postseason. Corum's touchdown came at the end of the Rams' first possession of the second half and he finished the game with a career-high 32 carries for 184 yards. That scoring drive ate up more than eight minutes. The Packers had a quick three-and-out, but briefly showed some life when linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper picked off Matthew Stafford to set the offense up in Los Angeles territory. Jordan Love turned the ball right back over when he hung a deep pass that safety Jaylen McCullough snagged out of the air. The Rams would then ride Corum and Kyren Williams on a pair of drives that covered more than 11 minutes. The Packers' last chance came with 6:13 left and they moved the ball to midfield before Love threw his second interception of the game. Cornerback Emmanuel Forbes got that one and the Packers were out of timeouts well before the two-minute warning. Sticking with the ground game helped to limit Packers defensive end Micah Parsons's impact in his return from last season's torn ACL. He had a sack late in the first half, but Stafford only threw eight times after the break and the Packers' run defense could not get their offense the ball often enough to get back into the game. Love was 17-of-29 for 198 yards and a touchdown, but clearly missed wide receiver Christian Watson after he left the game with a concussion. They only picked up two first downs after halftime and they'll hope that an extended break before their Week 13 trip to New Orleans is enough time for him to return to action. The Rams have several injuries of their own to monitor as guard Bill Murray joined tight ends Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee in making early exits from the game. They'd like to have all those players back next week, but they showed on Wednesday night that Corum can sometimes be enough all by himself.
author: Josh Alper

title: PFT's Thanksgiving and Week 12 2026 NFL picks
summary: All games picked for one of the most compelling weeks of the season.
full_text: It was inevitable. After flirting a couple of times with landing under .500 in a given week of picks, it finally happened. For Week 11, I went 6-7. That's what I get for trying to pick upsets. In Week 11, it was Chalk City — and 12 of 13 home teams won. And so, from now on, I'm not getting cute. I'm sticking with my first impulse. I'm not overthinking it. The first number that pops into my head will be the pick. For the year, I'm at 102-60-1. The success rate is still 62.5 percent. Here's hoping I can find a way to push it a little higher with the 16 games to be played from Wednesday through Monday. Packers at Rams (Wednesday night) Sean McVay is 0-5 against Matt LaFleur. Rams 24, Packers 20. Bears at Lions (Thursday) It's the biggest early-window Thanksgiving game ever, with both teams at 8-2. Ben Johnson's Bears gave up 52 points during last year's visit to Ford Field. They'll be determined to achieve a different result this time, in what becomes a true litmus test for the new-look Bears. If they're truly contenders, this is a game they win. Bears 23, Lions 21. Eagles at Cowboys (Thursday) It won't be a cakewalk. For Philly, it's the closest they'll get this year to a game with a postseason vibe. But the Cowboys have a chance to make a run at the Giants — if Dallas can also hold off the Commanders. Cowboys 41, Eagles 24. Chiefs at Bills (Thursday) Josh Allen is 5-0 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season, 0-4 against Mahomes in the postseason. The trend continues, thanks to conditions that are more conducive to Allen making the right throw at the right time. Bills 23, Chiefs 17. Broncos at Steelers (Friday) This one had the feel of a game the Steelers would find a way to win, until the benching of Aaron Rodgers threw everything into disarray. Broncos 20, Steelers 13. Saints at Bengals The Bengals need to get back on track, quickly, after Monday night's sluggish performance. A slump could open the door for the Browns to steal the division. Bengals 31, Saints 20. Ravens at Texans It feels like an elimination game in Houston, even if the winner will still be facing an uphill climb to the postseason. When in doubt, ride with the clearly better quarterback. Texans 27, Ravens 23. Giants at Colts This will be a far cry from the 1958 NFL Championship. The Giants are surging, and the Colts are slowly disintegrating. Giants 24, Colts 9. Titans at Jaguars As the saying goes, it's not the size of the dog in the fight but the size of the fight in the dog. Unfortunately, this fight is round two of Doberman vs. Chihuahua. Jaguars 35, Titans 20. Jets at Dolphins The Dolphins are running out of chances to get a second win (if they even want one). Dolphins 23, Jets 13. Falcons at Vikings Kirk Cousins gets the double whammy — his first home game in his second stint with the Vikings, and his first shot at revenge against the team that signed him and then drafted his replacement. Vikings 27, Falcons 13. Patriots at Chargers It's fitting that a game pitting two struggling teams coached by former Ohio State and Michigan players happens one day after a game between struggling Ohio State and Michigan teams. Patriots 16, Chargers 10. Commanders at Cardinals Monday night's upset of the Bengals means nothing if the Commanders bungle a winnable game at Arizona. Commanders 27, Cardinals 10. Seahawks at 49ers Having an extra week to prepare, coupled with the urgency of a 6-4 record, is just what the doctor ordered for the Seahawks. Seahawks 27, 49ers 23. Raiders at Browns The NFL will be happy it flexed this one into primetime. (For reasons other than getting Patriots-Chargers out of that window.) Browns 30, Raiders 27. Panthers at Buccaneers Tampa Bay is running out of chances to pull themselves back into contention. Buccaneers 27, Panthers 20.

title: Rams move ahead 20-13 on Blake Corum TD
summary: The Rams took more than eight minutes off the clock before taking the lead.
full_text: The Rams let Blake Corum do most of the heavy lifting on their opening drive of the second half. Corum ran nine time for 35 yards during a 15-play Rams drive and the final yard he picked up was a touchdown that broke a tie and put the Rams up 13-10. The drive opened the third quarter and ate up eight minutes of playing time. The Rams faced three third downs on the drive and had Matthew Stafford throw to wide receiver Konata Mumpfield each time. The first two were completions that picked up 30 yards and the third was initially ruled a touchdown on the field. Replays showed Mumpfield did not have control of the ball in the end zone, but the Rams still got a first down due to a defensive holding penalty on the day. Corum has 16 carries for 58 yards and Mumpfield has four catches for 69 yards.

title: Christian Watson ruled out with a concussion
summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was disqualified for the hit that injured Watson.
full_text: Packers wide receiver Christian Watson will not return for the second half of Wednesday night's game against the Rams. Watson went to the locker room for a concussion evaluation shortly before halftime and the Packers announced that he has been ruled out at the start of the second half. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to his injury. The Rams also lost safety Kamren Kinchens for the rest of the game on the same play. Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson. Rams tight end Davis Allen has also been ruled out with an ankle injury. title: Micah Parsons gets first sack of season, Packers and Rams tied 13-13 at halftime

full_text: Packers defensive end Micah Parsons notched his first sack in nearly a year just before halftime in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. Parsons made his return from a torn ACL against the Rams and had a couple of pressures early in the game. He got home for a sack of Matthew Stafford on the Rams' first play after a Trey Smack field goal tied the score at 13-13 with 1:50 to play in the half. The Rams ran out the clock from there and they will get the ball to start the second half at SoFi Stadium. Parsons's sack was part of an eventful final couple of minutes. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and Watson is now being evaluated for a concussion. It would be a big loss for the Packers as Watson has four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown so far on Wednesday night. Running back Kyren Williams scored the Rams' only touchdown, but their offense slowed down after picking up points on each of their first three possessions. Stafford is 12-of-15 for 98 yards while Williams and Blake Corum have 35 yards on nine carries. Packers quarterback Jordan Love is 12-of-18 for 154 yards. The Packers will be hoping for right guard Kevin Zeitler's return from an ankle injury while waiting for more word on Watson and the Rams called tight end Davis Allen to return from an ankle injury.

title: Rams S Kamren Kinchens ejected for hit on Christian Watson
summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after a hit on wide receiver Christian Watson.
full_text: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after a hit on wide receiver Christian Watson. Per the Netflix broadcast, the league office said that Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and making helmet-to-helmet contact with Watson and NFL executive vice president Troy Vincent made the final call on disqualifying him from the game. Watson held onto the ball, but went to the locker room with members of the medical staff and the catch did not count because Packers wideout Matthew Golden was flagged for offensive pass interference to offset the Kinchens foul. The play came on a fourth-and-1 and the Packers ultimately opted to kick a field goal rather than go for it again. It is now 13-13 with under two minutes to play in the half.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jordan Love, Christian Watson cut Rams lead to 13-10
summary: The points keep coming in the first half at SoFi Stadium.
full_text: The points keep coming in the first half at SoFi Stadium. A little more than three minutes after the Rams scored their first touchdown of the night, the Packers paid their first visit to the end zone. Jordan Love hooked up with Christian Watson for a six-yard score that cut the Rams' lead to 13-10 with just over eight minutes to play in the half. Watson also caught a pass on the first play of the drive and that completion went for 21 yards. Love hit Watson's fellow wideout Matthew Golden for a 39-yard gain on the next play and the quarterback scrambled for the third first down of the possession a couple of plays after that big gain. The Packers went three-and-out and turned the ball over on their first two possessions, but they are now outgaining the Rams thanks to back-to-back scoring drives.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kyren Williams makes it 13-3 Rams in second quarter
summary: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points.
full_text: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points. Running back Kyren Williams finished off the third possession with a seven-yard sprint into the end zone that pushed the Rams' lead over the Packers to 13-3 with 11:29 to play in the first half. It's the first time the Rams have scored on their first three possessions this season and it's also the first time the Packers have allowed their opponents points on their first three drives. Most of the other movement on the drive came through the air. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford completed passes to Williams, tight end Davis Allen, wide receiver Konata Mumpfield, and tight end Tyler Higbee for first downs before Williams's touchdown. The throw to Williams came just before Stafford took a hit from Packers defensive end Micah Parsons. Stafford is 10-of-12 for 87 yards while Jordan Love is 6-of-10 for 70 yards, including a 32-yarder to Christian Watson that set up Trey Smack's 54-yard field goal.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers president backs Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers release: 'Insubordination can't be tolerated'
summary: Rooney said the Steelers could not tolerate Rodgers' ultimatum or his decision to criticize McCarthy publicly days before a key game
full_text:
Steelers president Art Rooney II spent part of his Thanksgiving addressing his team's decision to bench, then release Aaron Rodgers following his actions with Mike McCarthy. McCarthy benched Rodgers after Rodgers gave him an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. The Steelers released Rodgers after he went scorched earth on McCarthy during a 35-minute interview on "The Pat McAfee Show."
"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette . "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."
Rooney took issue with Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy, especially with the Steelers just days away from playing a big game against the Denver Broncos .
"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."
Perhaps the most interesting thing Rooney said was regarding Pittsburgh's play-calling.
"The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had," Rooney said. "Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn't working."
One possible example of this may have been late in the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 8 win over the Browns . The Steelers were running at will, which made Pittsburgh's decision to call three straight passing plays inside Cleveland's 10-yard-line a head scratching decision to say the least. McCarthy accepted blame for those play calls when asked about them afterward.
Regarding his team's future, Rooney said he is optimistic that Mason Rudolph can lead the Steelers' offense. Rudolph, a nine-year veteran who has 20 career starts under his belt, delivered for the Steelers when he was in a similar spot in 2023.
When asked if he regrets his decision to bring Rodgers back, Rooney said he was disappointed with how things turned out.
"We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll," he said. "We had high expectations.
"It's easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn't expecting it to go this way this year."

title: Aaron Rodgers' former Packers teammates rip QB over Mike McCarthy criticism: 'None are on 12's side'
summary: Former Packers players criticized Rodgers for attacking McCarthy publicly and putting his ex-Steelers teammates in an uncomfortable position
full_text:
Aaron Rodgers ' recent comments about Mike McCarthy have drawn the ire of some of his former Green Bay Packers teammates. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang and former Packers receivers James Jones and Greg Jennings have publicly denounced Rodgers' treatment of McCarthy while taking their former coach's side following a chaotic 48-hour period in Pittsburgh.
Rodgers scorched McCarthy on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, accusing his now-former coach of falling asleep at meetings, being late or absent from other meetings, not watching film in a timely manner and not developing a rapport with some of his players, especially the team's defensive players. Rodgers was benched after giving McCarthy an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. McCarthy benched Rodgers, and the Steelers released him after Rodgers publicly criticized McCarthy.
"I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it."
Lang, who spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said that he is in a group chat with several former Packers who share his sentiment on the situation.
"I think it's just completely unnecessary," he said. "I think it's victim mentality."
TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/0oiS3PybCn
Jones, who also spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said he, too, is in a group text with former Packers teammates who don't agree with Rodgers' handling of McCarthy.
"How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast . "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike."
Jennings, who spent seven seasons in Green Bay and caught two touchdowns in the Packers' Super Bowl win over the Steelers, called Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy "distasteful." Jennings also criticized Rodgers for putting his former teammates in Pittsburgh in an awkward situation.
"If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said on "First Thing First." "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything."
@GregJennings weighs in on Steelers releasing former teammate Aaron Rodgers: “It was very distasteful… If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don’t do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers... They are playing for something.” pic.twitter.com/whPyBO7K2p
The general consensus among Rodgers' former Packers teammates is that Rodgers should have handled the situation behind closed doors, even if some of his accusations about McCarthy are true.
"I don't even care if it's the truth," Jones said. "Have the conversation with Mike in there. This is not something you go to the media bashing somebody. I would not do this to people that I love."

title: What all 32 NFL teams should be thankful for this Thanksgiving
summary: From MVP candidates Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy to promising rookies, new coaches and future draft picks, here is one reason each of the NFL's 32 teams can give thanks
full_text:
On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.
The gap between the best team and the worst team in the NFL is quite large, but even though not all teams have the playoffs in their future, or even a winning record, they can still be thankful for what they do have,
Thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to plan for every team. Some franchises enter the holiday firmly in the Super Bowl race, while others are already measuring progress through young players, improved units and the draft capital that could shape a brighter future.
Writer: Shanna McCarriston
Winning despite turnovers – The Bills have a lot of reasons for gratitude. This one is somewhat of a good news, bad news situation: the team is turning the ball over more than they should, but they are still getting wins. It just goes to show that great teams will find ways to win games regardless. Josh Allen , James Cook, and their record are the obvious things they should be thankful for, but this one is most interesting to me because, as a team that has turned the ball over twice in three of the last four games and five times in a single game this season, 9-1 is impressive.
Drake Maye value – The Patriots have had a difficult season in terms of injuries, so much so that they're running out of spots on IR, and on-field struggles even when healthy. Quarterback Drake Maye is out for an extended period of time, likely the rest of the season, and without him the offense fell flat. The team still had their fair share of struggles with Maye, don't get me wrong, but if him being sidelined proved anything, it's how valuable he is to the team. In a season where many were questioning his real impact, wondering if last year was a fluke, the team can be grateful that when they do get Maye back (even if it's next year), the offense will be bumped back up.
Pass defense – The Jets are another team far outside the playoff race, but it's not all bad! Heading into Week 11, the Jets pass defense was fifth-best in the league, allowing 196.8 yards per game through 10 weeks. This alone won't get them to a Super Bowl, but on a team with many issues to point to, they can be thankful that something is working.
Forcing turnovers – Looking at the Dolphins record, it can be hard to think that they have anything to be thankful for. A high draft pick is one thing they can be grateful for, but so is their defense. They were tied for fifth-most interceptions with nine through 10 weeks and added two more against the Bills last week. The run defense had the challenge of facing Jonathan Taylor , Jahmyr Gibbs and James Cook and held them to under 100 yards each.
Joe Burrow — Cincinnati boasts a reinvigorated defense (led by Dexter Lawrence ) and the best receiving duo in the NFL in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Burrow, however, remains the key to the Bengals' success. He's currently on pace to become the first player in history to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing at least 70% of his passes. He's among the MVP front-runners.
Todd Monken — With respect to John Harbaugh, Monken should win NFL Coach of the Year if the Browns continue to win. Cleveland is 6-4 and would be in the playoffs if the postseason started today. Monken has revived Deshaun Watson 's career.
Jaylen Warren — Warren was arguably the biggest reason for Pittsburgh's 6-2 start. The former undrafted rookie rushed for over 700 yards over that span that included four 100-yard games. Warren and the Steelers ' offense have fallen off in recent weeks, though. Warren becomes even more valuable within the offense as the Aaron Rodgers drama sparked a quarterback change.
Derrick Henry — While it's been a lost season in Baltimore, Ravens fans still get a chance to watch an all-time great do his thing. Henry is still playing well and setting new milestones in his 11th NFL season. This season, he's moved into third all-time in rushing touchdowns and seventh in career rushing yards.
Liam Coen – The Jaguars are now 20-7 under coach Liam Coen, who has turned this franchise from an afterthought to a Super Bowl contender. Coen has Trevor Lawrence finally living up to the lofty expectations set before him as a prospect coming out of Clemson, and has put together an impressive staff that includes defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski. Both could be head coaches next year.
C.J. Stroud – Imagine how disappointing the Texans would be this year if it weren't for the play of C.J. Stroud? He's thrown three touchdowns in three straight games, and scored at least two touchdowns in seven straight games. That's the longest such streak in franchise history. Stroud has thrown 22 touchdowns compared to just four interceptions this season. We no longer have to wonder if the Texans have a franchise quarterback.
The season is almost over – There are just six games remaining in the regular season. That's good news for Colts fans.
Future drafts – The one-win Titans traded away star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker for some nice draft capital. Tennessee now holds four first-round picks and three second-round picks in the next two drafts, which could expedite a seemingly never-ending rebuild. As long as Mike Borgonzi doesn't draft another developmental pass rusher.
Writer: Shanna McCarriston
Patrick Mahomes back on top – The Chiefs are back and so is Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City's woes of last season are over, and the fans can breathe a sigh of relief that last year was a fluke. Mahomes has 22 touchdowns with just four interceptions this year, along with 2,709 yards. He is looking like the Super Bowl contender he has been in the past, and his offense has fixed many of the mistakes they had last season. With Mahomes playing like he is, this team has a real chance of going all the way.
Division still in reach – Last season the Broncos won the division, but that was with the Chiefs struggling. This year, K.C. is among the top in the league and Denver is still within reach of the divisional title. That is a major accomplishment for Sean Payton's squad.
Mendoza Era begins – The Raiders season has been filled with ups and downs. It started off strong, but then took a turn. The hope the Raiders and their fans can have is that the Fernando Mendoza era has begun and they can start to get excited about who they anticipate to be their franchise guy.
High draft pick – The Chargers season hasn't been what they hoped, leaving lots of questions about their quarterback and coach. The good news is that they will be getting a high draft pick this year. Now they just need to do something with it.
John Harbaugh -- The New York Giants are fresh off a 23-18 win over the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) in Week 11 that has the Giants out to a two-game lead in the NFC East over the Cowboys.
New coach John Harbaugh is pushing all the right buttons and has the Giants tracking toward a division title despite Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns suffering season-ending injuries within the first three weeks of the 2026 season. He is certainly someone the Giants are grateful to have leading their football team.
Dak Prescott -- Prescott is dragging his 29th-ranked scoring defense (28.4 points per game allowed) into the NFC East division race by powering the league's No. 4 scoring offense (30.6 points per game). Prescott became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club.

title: Lions vs. Bears Thanksgiving prediction: Which team will take control of NFC North?
summary: Sole possession of first place in the NFC North is on the line at Ford Field as two 8-2 rivals clash on Thanksgiving with long winning streaks
full_text:
In the first of three Thanksgiving day games, the Detroit Lions play host to the division rival Chicago Bears in one of the biggest games of the NFL season to date.
Detroit enters this game winners of six straight and sitting in first place in the NFC North with an 8-2 record. The Lions sport one of the NFL's most efficient and explosive offenses, and their efense hasn't allowed more than 21 points in a game since all the way back in Week 4. The Lions are dealing with injury issues on that side of the ball, but they've held up surprisingly well. That will be put to the test on Thursday afternoon.
Chicago comes into this game having won five in a row and sporting an 8-2 record that matches that of Detroit, with the Bears sitting in second place in the division by virtue of a tiebreaker. The Bears also have one of the league's best offenses, while the defense has been strengthened by the acquisition of superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons , who seems to have transformed the unit up front and allowed everything else to click properly into place. That unit, too, will be tested more than ever here.
Which of these two teams will keep its winning streak alive and lay claim to sole possession of first place in the division? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Chicago is eighth in total yards and eighth in total points this season, but some of that has to do with volume. The Bears rank a surprising 14th in yards per play, 12th in points per drive and 15th in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Some of that is due to the fact that Caleb Williams missed several games with a hamstring injury, but even with Williams on the field the Bears' EPA per play mark is only the equivalent of the 10th-best offense in the league.
Chicago is one of the league's most run-oriented offenses, ranking ninth in the share of plays that turn into a rush attempt. But D'Andre Swift is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and Kyle Monangai , who has been more effective (5.0 per carry) has played in only five games.
The Lions have sported a top run defense this season in allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, but that defense took a couple of massive hits over the last few weeks with the losses of Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to injury. Still, Detroit held Tampa Bay's running backs to 84 yards on 22 carries last Sunday, when Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell had previously been destroying teams on the ground. The Bears will need Swift and Monangai to find more success if they want to control the game in the fashion they have preferred since Ben Johnson became head coach last year.
Chicago's passing game has been relatively inconsistent this year, as there have been times when Caleb Williams has looked like an elite quarterback and others when he has looked ordinary — sometimes within the same game. (Like the Sunday night showdown against the Buccaneers , for example.) Williams has completed 68.3% of his passes at 7.9 yards per attempt, but he's thrown only 10 touchdown passes against six interceptions.
He's 11th in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, but he's been highly susceptible against the blitz: he ranks fourth in EPA against four-man rushes but only checks in 19th when opponents rush five or more. Detroit has blitzed at a below-average rate this season (30.3%, per Tru Media), but would be wise to turn up the pressure a bit against a quarterback who has shown that he can be pressured into some bad decisions on occasion if you get defenders into his lap.
Still, the Lions have been highly susceptible to opposing passing attacks, even if they have been improved since the return of Brian Branch and should get another lift as Kerby Joseph rounds into form. The Lions are 27th in EPA per dropback allowed, and they're in the bottom third in opponents' explosive play rate through the air.
Detroit is most vulnerable against opposing tight ends, allowing the league's fifth-highest target share to the position, so this could be a game where the Bears finally get Colston Loveland going in a way that they haven't been able to accomplish as much as they likely wanted to this year. The Lions do limit yards after the catch better than any defense in the NFL, though, allowing only 4.0 YAC per completion, according to Tru Media. That could take away from some of Chicago's success in the screen game and possibly limit the effectiveness of Luther Burden III and — to a lesser extent because he's not as big a part of the offense — Kalif Raymond .
The Lions are third in the NFL in yards and fifth in points. They're fifth in both yards per play and points per drive, as well as fifth in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. They're second in EPA per pass attempt and third in EPA per rush attempt. They're third in passing success rate, first in rushing success rate and third in overall success rate. They are, in other words, a top-five offense by almost any measurement, and they can beat you with both the pass and the run.
Jared Goff is having a marvelous season, completing 67.8% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt with 20 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's third in the league behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in EPA per dropback, third behind only Purdy and Burrow in success rate and fourth behind only Purdy, Burrow and Patrick Mahomes in passer rating. His 8.2 yards-per-attempt average is the second-best of his tenure in Detroit, as are the 52.3% success rate and 107.7 passer rating.
He's of course blessed with one of the best skill-position corps in the league: Amon-Ra St. Brown is a picture of consistency; Jameson Williams is one of the most explosive threats in football; Sam LaPorta is a strong option and tight end; and Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushes, rushing yards, first downs, yards from scrimmage and total touchdowns.
St. Brown often gets pigeonholed as a slot guy, but in reality he plays more outside (59.2% of snaps) than he does inside (39.8%), according to Tru Media, and he's equally capable of dominating defenses from either spot. He's Goff's first read more often than not because he runs a lot of short-area routes and the Lions like to get the ball out fairly quickly in their straight dropback game, where St. Brown is often the target.
Williams is the guy the Lions turn toward when they're looking to test defenses in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. His 12.36-yard average route depth is fourth among 199 players who have run 100 or more routes this season, according to Tru Media, and he's generated an explosive gain (16-plus yards) on 26.3% of his targets, which ranks 17th among that same group of players. He and LaPorta are generally going to eat into each other's target shares in any given week, while St. Brown remains the more consistent top target.
The Bears' secondary is beatable, as Chicago ranks 22nd in net yards allowed per attempt, according to Pro-Football-Reference. Jaylon Johnson is not the same player he once was, Tyrique Stevenson is inconsistent, Kyler Gordon has barely played and Malik Muhammad has the ups and downs of a fourth-round rookie. If the Lions give Goff time to throw, he could feast on this group all afternoon.
That's where Chicago's improved defensive line comes in. Since acquiring Jeffery Simmons, the Bears rank seventh in the league in EPA per dropback, per Tru Media, in large part because they have recorded a sack on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks. Prior to acquiring Simmons, Chicago's sack rate was 8.9%. That figure still ranked third in the league through seven weeks, but it's been much improved since the Bears dropped Simmons into the middle of the defensive line.
Detroit is pretty strong up front, allowing pressure on only 32.3% of dropbacks, which ranks sixth in the NFL. The sack rate is a bit worse than that because Goff isn't the world's most mobile quarterback, but…

title: Will Mike McCarthy survive Aaron Rodgers' backlash? Steelers reportedly standing by coach, but for how long?
