full_text:
If a fraction of what Aaron Rodgers said on Wednesday is true , the Pittsburgh Steelers have a lot of things to clean up. If the majority of what Rodgers said is indeed fact, it's a downright miracle that the Steelers are 6-4 entering Friday's game with the visiting Broncos .
Rodgers, in a scorching interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" that lasted roughly 35 minutes, took Mike McCarthy to task, accusing him of falling asleep during meetings, being late or missing them altogether, falling behind on film study, and not connecting enough with players, especially defensive players.
Rodgers said that, as a team leader, he felt compelled to address McCarthy, which he did this week. During those conversations, Rodgers offered McCarthy an ultimatum: either give up play calling or release him.
The Steelers' brass backed McCarthy, who promptly benched Rodgers and made him inactive for Friday's game. Pittsburgh then released him shortly after his public criticism of McCarthy, who defended himself in a press conference Wednesday evening.
"I know how to win," McCarthy said , "and that's the facts. This is my third program, and I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization, what we've got started, and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today — because of some of the things that, frankly, should have been talked about earlier. So, this is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of."
The last sentence might be the biggest takeaway from McCarthy's 12-minute presser.
McCarthy wasn't going to acknowledge Rodgers' accusations Wednesday night for obvious reasons (he did confirm Rodgers' accusation that he accidentally said Packers instead of Steelers during halftime of last week's loss in Philadelphia). He did, however, acknowledge that he needs to make some changes, which is a positive sign for the Steelers moving forward.
McCarthy spoke to the team's leadership council after practice, and based on his comments afterward, it appears that the meeting had an impact on him.
"We had some really unique conversations in the player council meeting, and things I think that I haven't done in the past or haven't done recently," McCarthy said. "I probably should have had more dialogue early in the process when I first arrived here. I do respect Mike Tomlin and his career here and the things that are in place. I don't have a throw the baby out with the bathwater type philosophy. And so, when you have situations that create honest, direct conversation, there's good things that come out of that. Some things that (I) definitely will consider moving forward. Maybe not today or tomorrow, but there's a lot that came out of the meeting."
Really, what happened prior to this week doesn't matter nearly as much as what will transpire from this point forward. What happens moving forward is what will likely determine McCarthy's future in Pittsburgh.
If Pittsburgh rallies and makes the playoffs, it will validate the Steelers' decision to stand behind McCarthy . If the Steelers continue to struggle, however, Steelers president Art Rooney II will be forced to make a tough decision.
Rooney, if he hasn't already, needs to find out exactly what is happening inside his own facility. Is McCarthy falling asleep in meetings? Is he late or not showing up to others? Is he not watching film of future opponents in a timely manner? Is his not connecting well enough with the players? If any of those accusations are true, it raises serious concerns about McCarthy's ability to lead the Steelers.
If Rodgers' accusations are true, and the Steelers spiral and miss the playoffs, it's hard to envision McCarthy being with the team in 2027. If McCarthy comes back in that scenario, it would likely entail significant changes, including relinquishing play-calling duties.
The Steelers haven't fired a coach since 1968, and that streak will likely remain intact for quite some time. Rooney probably won't fire a coach with four years remaining on his contract, but it's possible that he and McCarthy could have a mutual parting of ways if the two sides can agree on a buyout.
The last two days have raised a lot of questions about what is actually happening within the Steelers' facility. One thing that is clear, however, is that McCarthy is at a crossroads just 10 games into his tenure in Pittsburgh. How he and his players handle the next seven games will likely determine his future in Pittsburgh beyond this season.

title: NFL Week 12 picks: Our experts face off on Bears at Lions, Chiefs at Bills and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Welcome to the most special week in the NFL . We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day."
Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories.
Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons . In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell … Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28
Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog.  … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30
Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans , but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers , and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971… Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20
Dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24
Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III . I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16
Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17
Dajani ( Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end   … Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13
Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph . I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10
Dajani ( Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18
Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense.  … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20
Dajani ( 49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season.
Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 … Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles prediction: Dallas looks for first win streak of 2026 vs. ex-QB on Thanksgiving
summary: How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Thanksgiving clash between NFC East rivals
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (5-6) have the chance to do something they haven't done yet in the 2026 season against the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day: win consecutive games.
The only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye. That was a stretch of three victories in a row against Las Vegas Raiders (33-16), the Eagles (24-21) and the Kansas City Chiefs (31-28) on Thanksgiving Day.
After Dallas' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans (1-9) on Sunday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has some hope that his squad can make a postseason push down the stretch. That's just days after Jones called his Cowboys "a bad team" in the wake of their 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) in Week 10.
"It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we wanted to do," Jones said postgame on Sunday. "We needed this kind of thing. Any team does. We needed to feel it and get a little wind under our wings, so to speak."
Quarterback Dak Prescott looks to continue his high-level play on Thanksgiving. If he replicated his Sunday performance against the Titans (325 yards passing and four touchdowns on 28-of-33 passing with a rushing touchdown), that would give Prescott 19 passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving, the record for the most Thanksgiving Day touchdowns in NFL history. Prescott's predecessor Tony Romo and Matthew Stafford currently share the record with 18 Turkey Day passing touchdowns each.
"It's a blessing. It's something that, one of my favorite games of the year," Prescott said Tuesday. "And so, just being able to put that uniform on with the John Madden seal on it, understanding the whole world's watching and how many little kids are in the position that I once was: watching the game and then ready to go outside and play my own version of it. ... I don't take it for granted."
However, there's one Cowboy who doesn't look forward to Thanksgiving: defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The four-time Pro Bowler doesn't enjoy the holiday because it goes against his in-season training and diet regimen. Williams' go-to Thanksgiving side dish is macaroni, something that is hard to resist this time of year.
"It's during the season. I'm trying to stay lean and trim, and it's a holiday right around when real football starts to come in," said Williams. "So I'm not a big fan of Thanksgiving."
That's okay, because there will be plenty of fans ready to see Williams on the field, especially against starting Eagles quarterback and former Cowboy Joe Milton. Dallas acquired Milton in a trade with the New England Patriots in April 2025, and he worked as one of Prescott's backups until the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 17. That's the same day Philadelphia placed Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve.
"Haha, it's good to see him," said Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb . "I hope he don't go crazy."
Let's dig into the matchup.
Prescott is cooking right now. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception over the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). He also ranks eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season.
Prescott credited his historic production to being able to play "balanced football" the last two weeks, with the Cowboys averaging the 12th-most rushing yards per game (125.5) since Week 10.
"It really just opens up the whole playbook," Prescott said Thursday. "So it's a credit to all of it just, in that sense, coming together. Guys up front being physical in the run game, which then allows them to pass block a little bit easier there. And guys outside just getting open, making my job easier."
In their 51-30 Week 11 win over the Titans, Schottenheimer provided Prescott and Co. their highest motion rate (63.5%) and play-action rate (58.3%) of the season, weeks after getting away from those staples through the first quarter of the year.
Cowboys Pro Bowl wide receivers Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) going up against the Eagles All-Pro cornerback tandem of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean will be the key matchups on Thursday. However, Mitchell's status was uncertain because of a hamstring injury. The Eagles held walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, and they upgraded Mitchell to limited on Tuesday after he didn't participate on Monday.
Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Mitchell will be "fine" for Thanksgiving, and the Eagles listed him without a game status on the team's final injury report after he practiced fully on Wednesday, indicating he will indeed play.
When the Eagles have the football, they'll definitely be looking to play ground-and-pound football with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley . Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career. The Cowboys have the worst run defense in football, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per game, and they struggle against Barkley's agile running style.
Both Schottenheimer and Williams described Barkley as being a "jump cut" running back with how smoothly he can hit the hole and then glide to a different spot along the line of scrimmage and in the open field. Williams compared Barkley stylistically to Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving , who went off for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in a 24-16 upset over the Cowboys in Week 5. Irving averaged a career-high 7.9 yards per carry that night at AT&T Stadium. Williams said the key is to stop Barkley's feet before he gets going.
Williams also presents a challenge for Philadelphia as he leads the NFL with 18 tackles for loss, the most in a season by a defensive tackle since 2022. He also leads all defensive tackles in quarterback pressures (40) and co-leads his position in forced fumbles (4) along with Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter . Yet, he feels he can still find higher levels of play with the Cowboys defense allowing 20-plus points in 18 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. That's the longest such streak since the 2019-2021 Jacksonville Jaguars ' run of 25 straight games, per NFL Research .
Milton earned his first career win as an NFL starting quarterback on Sunday in the Eagles' 19-16 home victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers that snapped the team's seven-game losing streak. He completed 11 of his 21 throws for 141 passing yards while rushing for 7 yards on five carries. Prescott said he saw Milton develop most in Dallas on his mental side of the game and preparation as it pertains to pass protection adjustments and discernment at the line of scrimmage.
"Joe is amazing, man. The athleticism that he has, the speed that he has, the arm talent that he has, he can do it all," Williams said. "So it's super dope to be able to go against him, especially after all the laughs and things we had in the locker room during training camp practices."
The present iteration of the Eagles lacks the offensive artillery to win a duel with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. That's especially true if Mitchell is unable to suit up on Thursday. Prescott is on a 20-game home winning streak against NFC East opponents, which is tied with Tom Brady (versus the AFC East) for the longest home winning streak by a starting quarterback against divisional opponents…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bills vs. Chiefs prediction: Which team wins latest chapter in Josh Allen-Patrick Mahomes saga?
summary: Legendary quarterbacks close out the holiday slate in one of the biggest games of the season
full_text:
The NFL's three-game Thanksgiving slate concludes with a blockbuster battle between two perennial playoff teams in the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs . A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in one of the season's biggest showdowns to date.
As is often the case when they square off in the regular season, there are significant postseason seeding implications at play in this showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Buffalo stands in control of the AFC's No. 1 seed, while Kansas City is in a tightly contested race with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West crown and the top-four seed that comes with it. Should the Chiefs beat the Bills, not only would they solidify their standing in the division hunt, but they would also then give themselves a clear path to the top overall seed and a first-round bye.
This game stands among the greatest Thanksgiving matchups in NFL history. The combined 17-3 record between the two teams is the second-best mark by win percentage entering a Thanksgiving game in the last 50 seasons.
Both sides are also playing their best football of the season heading into the holiday duel. This is just the second game in league history to feature two teams riding three-game win streaks in which all of those victories came by 17 or more points. The only other such instance came in 2007 between Tom Brady's New England Patriots and Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts . The quarterback face-off in this contest is about as legendary as that one.
It is difficult to knock Kansas City, because when it wins, it does so in resounding fashion and shows all the makings of a future Super Bowl winner. But the Chiefs' strength of schedule and results against projected playoff teams do raise questions about whether they can take down the Bills on the road in primetime. The Chiefs have only played three games against opponents with winning records all season and are just 1-2 in those contests. Both losses came on the road. Simply put, they have not shown an ability to win games like the one they are about to walk into.
At the same time, the Bills defeated each of the three best teams on their schedule thus far. Plus, for whatever reason, Allen has Mahomes' number when they meet in the regular season. Add the defensive revival into the equation, and everything comes up Bills in this matchup. Pick: Bills 38, Chiefs 33
author: Carter Bahns

title: 2026 NFL Thanksgiving schedule: What to know about Thanksgiving and Black Friday games
summary: A look at the Thanksgiving week slate and all of its fixings you need in time for Turkey Day
full_text:
The NFL has cooked up something special for this year's Thanksgiving. For the first time, a Thanksgiving Eve game was added to the Thanksgiving week slate. It's essentially an appetizer for Thursday's triple-header feast, with the dessert coming Friday with the Black Friday game.
Each game has storylines big enough to fill any plate. To keep up with everything, we've provided a rundown of how to follow the games in real time. We've also included the major thing to know for each matchup.
What to know: While he's had a lot of success in Chicago, Ben Johnson is 0-2 against Detroit, his former team. Johnson's former boss, Dan Campbell, has won four straight games against Chicago, seven of his last eight in the series and has a 7-3 overall record against the Bears.
Coaches aside, this is a matchup between two of the NFL's hottest teams. The Bears have won five straight games, while the Lions enter Thursday with a six-game winning streak. The winner of this game will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.
It'll be especially interesting when the Lions' fifth-ranked offense is on the field against Chicago's sixth-ranked defense. Jahmyr Gibbs , who is one touchdown away from breaking Barry Sanders' NFL record for the most touchdowns by a player before his 25th birthday, should have his moments. He's facing a run defense that is just 25th in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed.
What to know: Dallas is a sizable favorite, but there are several reasons to believe that the Eagles are ripe for an upset.
The Cowboys were 10-point favorites when they were upset by then-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers back in Week 5. Dallas lost that game to a backup quarterback (rookie Jalon Daniels ), and they'll face another backup Thursday in Joe Milton III , who used to play for America's Team. Milton just won his first career start Sunday against the Steelers . He made several clutch plays, including his third-down conversion to DeVonta Smith that iced the game.
If Dallas wins on Thursday, it will be the first time it's won back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys' inability to string together consecutive wins is yet another reason why Philadelphia could successfully play the role of spoiler.
What to know: This game will be billed as the latest chapter in the Josh Allen-Patrick Mahomes rivalry. Overall, the Allen-Mahomes series is tied up at five wins apiece, which makes Thursday night's game a rubber match. Allen is 0-4 against Mahomes-led teams in the playoffs, but he has a 5-1 record in regular-season starts against Mahomes that includes five straight victories.
Both quarterbacks will look to put on a show, but the winner of this game will likely come down to which supporting cast outperforms the other. On paper, the Chiefs have a few advantages, most notably their second-ranked scoring defense that will look to exploit Allen's Kryptonite: turning the ball over. Allen has thrown nine interceptions this year, including five in his last four games.
It'll be interesting to see how the Chiefs' young players fare in a big-time environment, especially Emmett Johnson , Kansas City's rookie running back, who has tallied consecutive 100-yard rushing performances while filling in for injured starter Kenneth Walker III .
What to know: This game is pretty simple. If the Steelers are going to pull off an upset, they're going to have to take advantage of Denver's suspect run defense and third-down offense. If they can't do either of those things, the Broncos will more than likely hand them their third straight loss.
Jaylen Warren was having a monster season for Pittsburgh until he and the rest of the Steelers' offense hit a wall over the last two weeks. Pittsburgh's lack of depth at receiver has led defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage, leaving little running room for Warren and back mate Rico Dowdle .
A positive for Pittsburgh is the emergence of wideout Max Hurleman , who caught a team-high six passes for 61 yards and a score against the Eagles . Plus, the recent return of Roman Wilson and the possible return of Michael Pittman , who hasn't played since Week 4, are bright spots. The Steelers will also have DK Metcalf after the league decided not to suspend him following his ejection during Sunday's loss in Philadelphia.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL on Thanksgiving halftime shows: Ranking the 10 most memorable performances
summary: A look at some of the most iconic performances from Turkey Days of the past
full_text:
NFL halftime shows have evolved since the beginning of the league. What began as marching bands and local high school bands has now turned into full productions.
Thanksgiving has featured big performances from top artists since 1997, when Reba McEntire performed at the first Salvation Army Red Kettle Kickoff halftime show, which kicks off the Salvation Army's annual Red Kettle Campaign and encourages fans to give back to those in need.
This year, three games will be played on Thanksgiving Day. Bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+ , Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills face off at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.
Wu-Tang Clan will perform in Detroit, Miranda Lambert in Texas, and the Goo Goo Dolls in New York. This doesn't include the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, where U2 will perform at halftime.
Here is a look at 10 of the most memorable Thanksgiving halftime show performances:
You can't mention Thanksgiving halftime shows without mentioning Creed's Texas performance. There were silk aerial dancers, a man flying through with giant wings, mimes, choir singers and many other elements that left people with a lot of questions.
A 77-year-old Dolly Parton took the stage in a Dallas Cowgirl costume and proved why she is a country music legend. She performed "Jolene," "9 to 5" and made a medley with Queen's "We Will Rock You" and "We Are The Champions." Any Dolly performance is automatically iconic, and this was no different.
Since she kicked off the tradition of Thanksgiving halftime shows, McEntire has to make the list. She performed at Texas Stadium with a choir and dancers, along with the Cowboys cheerleaders. The country music legend performed on a star stage and wore Cowboys blue.
Any Destiny's Child performance is automatically memorable. The Texas natives were an obvious choice for a Texas halftime show. The trio performed "Lose My Breath" and "Soldier" from their final studio album. A marching band and cheerleaders joined their performance.
Mariah Carey may be the queen of Christmas, but she also knows how to put on a great Thanksgiving performance. The pop diva performed "Shake It Off" and "Don't Forget About Us" from her album The Emancipation of Mimi. The Ford Field performance also included a marching band and dancers. Carey began the performance being carried by men in football uniforms. People on the field created an "M" and "C."
Carrie Underwood has become an NFL staple, as the singer of Sunday Night Football's theme song. Her ties to the NFL also include a Thanksgiving halftime show performance. She sang her hit song "Before He Cheats" and "We're Young and Beautiful" in Texas, with an elaborate backdrop and silk aerial dancers.
Sheryl Crow brought down the Texas house with her rock vibes on Thanksgiving Day. She performed "Good Is Good" and her biggest hit "If It Makes You Happy." With acrobatic dancers and ribbon twirlers, her exciting performance became an instant classic.
The Jonas Brothers are one of the biggest boy bands of the early 2000s and 2010s, and their performance was a hit with any Disney Channel fans. title: Rams vs. Packers prediction: Can Green Bay continue success with deep ball? Will L.A. overcome injuries?
summary: Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground attack in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve showdown
full_text:
In the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, the Los Angeles Rams play host to the Green Bay Packers . The Rams enter this game coming off their bye week, and they are incredibly banged up on offense. Puka Nacua is likely out for the year, as is Terrance Ferguson , after they each underwent surgery on lower-body injuries. Davante Adams remains out with his hamstring injury as well. The Rams will need their defense and their running backs to carry the day against a tough Packers team.
Green Bay is also coming off the bye, but is getting healthier for this game as Micah Parsons will make his season debut after tearing his ACL toward the tail end of last season. Parsons returning to the fold provides a significant boost to what has already been a good defense under Jonathan Gannon, and the offense remains one of the league's most explosive units with Jordan Love targeting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden down the field.
Will the Rams hold off the Packers at home, or will Green Bay pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Green Bay's offense is entirely based on the passing game because the Packers simply cannot run the ball. Green Bay is last in the league at 3.1 yards per carry. The Packers' 670 rushing yards are 124 fewer than the next-closest team in the league (the Bengals ). The Rams allow only 3.9 yards per carry and sport Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald up front.
The Packers are not going to find success on the ground here — and honestly, they might not even try to do so. They're probably just going to let Jordan Love drop back and let it rip. That's what they've largely done throughout this season, and it's worked quite well for them.
Love has completed 63% of his passes at 7.7 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He's ninth in the league in EPA per play, according to Tru Media, thanks largely to the fact that he's created explosives at the fourth-highest rate in the league. When you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden by your side, that's how the offense is likely going to be built. The Packers really lean into their strengths by having the strong-armed Love target their speedy wideouts with deep routes; Love has thrown 20-plus yards downfield at the second-highest rate in football.
The Rams have been the NFL's third-best defense against deep passes this year, according to Tru Media, with opponents completing only 8 of 30 deep passes for 257 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. The 30 deep passes they've faced are the sixth-fewest in the league.
It'll be fascinating to see whether Green Bay continues to attack deep downfield or if Love, Watson, Golden and tight end Tucker Kraft instead work the short and intermediate areas of the field that the Rams encourage opposing offenses to throw to because of their coverage structures. It'll also be interesting to see if Trent McDuffie shadows one of the two wideouts or if the Rams play sides with him and Josh Wallace , who has taken the place of the injured Jaylen Watson .
L.A. has allowed the league's fewest catches and second-fewest yards to wide receivers this season, according to Pro-Football-Reference, with opposing quarterbacks targeting tight ends and running backs more often than they do against other teams. Tight ends have been targeted at the fourth-highest rate (27.4% of passes, according to Tru Media) against the Rams, while backs have been targeted at the second-highest rate (20.6%).
This could be a game where Kraft is more involved in the proceedings. The Packers don't throw to their backs very often because they are not good players, so they'll probably still force the ball to Watson and Golden, even if the Rams do limit wide-receiver production.
In their first game without all three of Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, the Rams used a highly unusual personnel rotation.
Their three leading skill-position players in snaps were all tight ends — and none of those tight ends was the one the Rams drafted in the second round. Their running backs shared the field for 18 snaps after having never previously played together in their careers, according to Tru Media. And one of their two primary wide receivers (rookie sixth-round pick CJ Daniels ) played more than seven times as many snaps in Week 10 (44) as he had in his entire career before that (six).
The Rams were nevertheless able to rack up 436 yards, 28 first downs and 34 points against the decrepit Cardinals' defense. They ran the ball extremely well (202 yards) and were efficient in the passing game, with each of the wideouts creating an explosive play and the backs and tight ends chipping in with short and intermediate grabs. Matthew Stafford threw only 26 passes, but five of them created gains of at least 19 yards, and he averaged nearly 10 yards per attempt.
The Packers, though, are not the Cardinals. Green Bay enters this game allowing the third-fewest net yards per attempt in the league, which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks in addition to passing yards allowed. The Packers have also yielded only 15 touchdowns through the air while intercepting a league-high 14 passes. Their safeties, in particular, have been ballhawks, with Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney combining for nine of those 14 picks and McKinney leading the league with six on his own.
Green Bay has been just about average in generating pressure so far this season, recording a sack, hit or hurry on 36.2% of opponent dropbacks, according to Tru Media. (The league average is 36.4% this year.) Getting Parsons back in the fold should help tremendously. He led the NFL in total pressures between 2021 and 2025 despite rushing the passer considerably less often than players like Myles Garrett and Maxx Crosby , who are the only players within 30 pressures of Parsons' total during that span. Parsons will likely play limited snaps, but those snaps should be concentrated on important downs and Matthew Stafford and Co. will need to be aware of where he is at all times.
The Packers have also done a pretty strong job of limiting opposing run games, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. The Rams, though, have sported one of the best rushing attacks in the league, with Williams and Corum combining to average 4.6 yards a pop. The offensive line has cleared the way for 1.79 yards before contact per attempt, which is the second-best mark in the league behind only that of the Bills . Williams and Corum (and Ronnie Rivers) also have a combined 21.0% avoided tackle rate, per Tru Media, which is the seventh-best in football.
The Rams will likely have to lean on their run game here to move the ball, because the situation does not line up well for them through the air. The offensive line's ability to dictate the game at the line of scrimmage will likely determine whether they can achieve any degree of offensive success.
The lift the Packers get from Micah Parsons' return, plus the limitations the Rams' offense should have while working without Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, push me toward Green Bay in this game. I don't foresee the Rams moving the ball as consistently against the Packers as they did against the Cardinals in their first game without all their playmakers. Meanwhile, the Packers have the goods to challenge L.A.'s secondary downfield with Watson and Golden and over the middle with Kraft. Love should be able to get going through the air, even if Green Bay still can't run the ball. Pick: Packers 24, Rams 17
author: Jared Dubin

title: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers, confirms QB gave him 'ultimatum:' 'I know how to win'
summary: McCarthy responded to Rodgers' tirade against him
full_text:
In the wake of Aaron Rodgers' sudden benching , the now-former Pittsburgh Steeler went scorched Earth on coach Mike McCarthy , accusing him of everything from incompetence to negligence. Facing a litany of embarrassing allegations, McCarthy has now shared his side of the story.
McCarthy began his press conference by stating that he wouldn't reveal any specifics about his private conversations with Rodgers. Asked why McCarthy was the right person to lead Pittsburgh through this messy situation, McCarthy bluntly referred to his overall track record as a coach.
"I know how to win, and that's the facts," McCarthy replied. "This is my third program. I plan on winning here because of the men and because of this organization."
Explaining the decision to bench Rodgers, which ignited this firestorm, McCarthy said the quarterback gave him an "ultimatum." At that point, McCarthy felt the need to make a change.
"It was a process that went on throughout this week," McCarthy said. "We got to a point. We talk about communication and things like that. There was an ultimatum made clearly outside of his job description. So, it was my decision to bench him."
Rodgers claimed that no one informed him of McCarthy's decision to bench him, and he only found out when tight end Pat Freirmuth alerted him to the news. McCarthy refuted Rodgers' story, saying there were multiple attempts to reach him.
"I know there were continuous efforts to reach Aaron, and I know there was communication with his agent," McCarthy said. "I don't know exactly the specifics on the other side of the conversation."
ESPN reported that McCarthy "has the full support" of the Steelers organization and "will remain their head coach." However, Pittsburgh hasn't released any official statement or responded to the allegations in any way yet.
Asked directly about Rodgers' accusation that McCarthy broke down a team huddle at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles by saying, "1-2-3 Packers," McCarthy conceded that it was an "embarrassing moment." He cited working "long hours" as an explanation for the slip-up. However, McCarthy added that he and Rodgers had a "difference of opinion" about how the locker room received it.
Speaking of the locker room, Rodgers also alleged that McCarthy has made little effort to connect with the players, particularly those on defense. The Steelers coach said he met with the team's leadership council and felt like both sides came to an understanding.
"I'll just say that I came from a player council meeting," McCarthy said. "I thought it was a meeting that was very direct and very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind. Comments that brought discussion to the forefront. I'm proud of our leadership. More importantly, I loved the urgency coming out of that meeting."
McCarthy added that some of those things "should've been talked about earlier" and presented a "growth opportunity" for himself and the team.
"Probably should have had more dialogue earlier in the process when I first arrived here," McCarthy admitted. "I do respect Mike Tomlin and his career here and the things that are in place. I don't have a throw-the-baby-out-with-the-bathwater philosophy. When you have situations that create honest and direct conversation, there are good things that come out of that."
When the Steelers hired McCarthy to replace Mike Tomlin, one of the first things he did was advocate for the return of Rodgers at quarterback. At the time, McCarthy didn't hesitate when asked about the idea of re-signing the veteran quarterback.
"Definitely. I don't see why you wouldn't," McCarthy said. "I have spoken to Aaron, and so that's really where we are there. I was able to sit back and watch the games. I watched most of the Pittsburgh games on TV, and I thought he was a great asset for the team."
Once a McCarthy-Rodgers reunion was finalized, Pittsburgh hoped that duo had a little more magic left after their run to a Super Bowl XLV championship with the Green Bay Packers. Instead, the relationship has turned toxic in a matter of months.
It was bad enough when the offense was sputtering and Rodgers was arguing with McCarthy on the sideline , but that seems rather rosy compared to where things stand now. On his way out the door, Rodgers asserted that players don't respect McCarthy as Pittsburgh fights to stay in the AFC playoff race with Mason Rudolph under center.
In an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show," Rodgers teed off on McCarthy and his alleged lack of professionalism since taking over in Pittsburgh.
First, Rodgers claimed he found out about his benching through tight end Pat Friermuth. In fact, Rodgers said McCarthy still hasn't spoken to him about the decision. From there, Rodgers asserted that McCarthy was an absentee coach in the lead-up to the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting," Rodgers said. "Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room, like nothing happened. Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting.
"Friday, he doesn't come to the walkthrough. We only have a walkthrough really on Friday. Doesn't come to the first walkthrough. Doesn't come to protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes to Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn't great, and you know there were some guys early on that didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys that Mike didn't want to get another defense.
"So a lot of those guys, you know, he kind of already lost a lot of those guys. And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime."
Ultimately, Rodgers said the "nail in the coffin" came at halftime of the loss. The ex-Steelers quarterback said McCarthy went from a "rambling" speech to breaking the team down with, "1-2-3 Packers." At that moment, Rodgers said he felt McCarthy completely lost the locker room.
Now Pittsburgh is left preparing to play the Denver Broncos on a short week as the team tries to pick up the pieces from a humiliating Wednesday for the entire organization.
author: Austin Nivison

title: Cardinals extend TE Elijah Higgins for three-years
summary: This is the time of year that in the NFL, if coaches and GMs want to keep players whose deals are about to expire, they begin doling out contract extensions. On Tuesday, the Arizona Cardinals gave TE Elijah Higgins a three-year $25 million extension that will keep him in-house through the 2028 season. This new […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Elijah Higgins #84 of the Arizona Cardinals runs the balla against Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is the time of year that in the NFL, if coaches and GMs want to keep players whose deals are about to expire, they begin doling out contract extensions. On Tuesday, the Arizona Cardinals gave TE Elijah Higgins a three-year $25 million extension that will keep him in-house through the 2028 season. This new Cardinals offense requires two and three tight ends, and Higgins fit the bill. RELATED: WHO IS NEXT ON THE CHOPPING BLOCK? The new deal has $17.087 million guaranteed plus a $1.5 million signing bonus. In addition, his 2028 salary has an injury guarantee of $6 million, workout bonuses, and annual per-game bonuses. Higgins’ (6’-3”, 235 pounds) production this year isn’t great. In fact, it isn’t even good. He has played in all 11 games with 7 starts, but his receiving numbers are pedestrian. He has 21 targets with 19 receptions for 166 yards, an 8.7 yards per catch average, has converted 8 first downs, scored a single TD, 0 rushes, 122 YAC numbers, and one drop. He has played on 319 snaps, or 44% of offensive plays. He also has 155 snaps on special teams. His cap hit this year is $4.1 million. That comes out to be $213,668 per reception so far this season. Of course, that will increase beginning next year. Currently, the Cardinals have Trey McBride, Higgins, Hunter Long, and Teagan Quitoriano in their tight end room. They also have Shawn Bowman and Kenny Yeboah on the practice squad and Tip Reiman on IR. This offense plays a lot of 12 and 13 personnel. Higgins is a Stanford graduate and was selected in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Miami Dolphins. He was a last day cut to which Arizona then claimed him off waivers and has been a roster member ever since. He is very durable and played in all 17 games the past two seasons. He has 802 career receiving yards with 4 touchdowns. Originally, Higgins was a wide receiver in college and then transitioned to tight end as he got bigger. He is quick and runs a 4.54 in the 40. He is just okay in in-line blocking but is willing, and is just average on contested balls. His forte is intermediate throws and is a physical runner once it’s in his hands. Like McBride, Higgins has a large route tree. The extension is a sign that the coaching staff is preparing for future seasons, and likes his play in the tight end group. On November 15, 2026, the Cardinals posted Higgins was their “2026 Salute to Service Award” nominee.

title: Falcons’ 2024 double-dip at QB faces its reckoning in Minnesota
summary: As the Atlanta Falcons travel to face the Minnesota Vikings in Week 12, the matchup between the two quarterbacks should steal every headline. Michael Penix squares off against his former teammate and mentor Kirk Cousins, prompting a look back at the Falcons’ infamous 2024 offseason double-dip at quarterback. At the time, the Falcons felt they’d […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - DECEMBER 22: Michael Penix Jr. #9 and Kirk Cousins #18 of the Atlanta Falcons look on from the sideline during the fourth quarter against the New York Giants at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on December 22, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Atlanta Falcons travel to face the Minnesota Vikings in Week 12, the matchup between the two quarterbacks should steal every headline. Michael Penix squares off against his former teammate and mentor Kirk Cousins, prompting a look back at the Falcons’ infamous 2024 offseason double-dip at quarterback. At the time, the Falcons felt they’d solved their quarterback problems for a decade by signing Cousins to a $180 million contract and drafting Penix as his successor with the eighth overall pick. Yet two and a half years later, Atlanta is still embroiled in quarterback questions and scrapping for survival in the NFL’s weakest division while Cousins leads the Vikings as a legit playoff contender. Since leaving Atlanta this past offseason, Cousins has had a bit of a resurgence, guiding the Las Vegas Raiders to a respectable 4-5 record before returning to the Vikings at the trade deadline . Meanwhile, Penix, recovering from a season-ending knee injury in 2025, came back strong in Weeks 3 and 4, but has been mostly lackluster in his six outings since. Coming off their bye, the Falcons need to spark a late-season push for the NFC South crown, while the Vikings shake off their recent stumble in Mexico City . Sunday’s battle isn’t just for playoff positioning, but a referendum on Atlanta’s 2024 decision and their attempts to hedge with two quarterbacks compromised both, wasted precious draft capital, and left them with no clear answers at the sport’s most important position. Falcons failed to copy Packers’ blueprint The Falcons’ decision to double-dip was extremely controversial at the time because it was unprecedented. No team in NFL history had given a veteran quarterback multiple years of guarantees in free agency, only to undermine that by selecting his replacement in the first round of the draft. The Falcons dreamed of building a bridge similar to what the Green Bay Packers had with selecting Jordan Love in the first round of 2020 to sit behind Aaron Rodgers. With Love fresh off guiding the Packers to a divisional playoff loss in the 2023 postseason in his first season as a starter, it seemed like a worthwhile blueprint to follow. However, the Packers haven’t won a playoff game in the years since, and one can’t help but look back at the opportunity cost of the team’s failures to capitalize on back-to-back NFC Championship losses in 2019 and 2020 with an early-round selection that could’ve helped Rodgers and the Packers win a Super Bowl before his eventual exit in 2023. That same opportunity cost would plague the Falcons, who bypassed a glaring pass-rush need by drafting Penix, prompting a domino effect that led them to trade a future 2026 first-round pick to acquire James Pearce after already selecting Jalon Walker at the top of the 2025 NFL Draft. Pearce’s productive rookie season quieted any concerns about opportunity cost. However, after missing the first half of 2026 due to a suspension, Pearce, like the Falcons, also needs a strong finish to continue justifying the extra expenditure of draft capital for a 3-7 roster with plenty of holes . Falcons playoff drought made double-dip a gamble they couldn’t afford Not to mention, Rodgers spent over a decade in Green Bay building a Hall-of-Fame resume, and he entered the league on similar terms when he was drafted in 2005 and sat three seasons behind Brett Favre. The Packers had earned the benefit of the doubt with making such transitions, while the Falcons had not. The Falcons hadn’t cracked the postseason in six seasons before 2024, and the organization showed its hubris, assuming a return to the postseason was all but assured under Cousins, even though Minnesota had done so only twice in his six seasons there before he arrived in Atlanta. The playoffs remain elusive, and hindsight suggests the Falcons should’ve committed to one quarterback and used the remaining resources to build the rest of the team. For two years, Cousins’ bloated contract received the lion’s share of criticism, but today, the Penix pick deserves harsher scrutiny. Cousins’ steady floor is exactly what the current Falcons are missing Signing Cousins was certainly a risky overpay, given his mostly average play in both Washington and Minnesota over the preceding decade. But the veteran was a more proven commodity and offered a steadier floor, even after a 2023 Achilles injury. That injury required time to recover, time the Falcons failed to give him due to the presence of Penix breathing down his neck. The minute Cousins hit a snag , the Falcons pulled the plug and turned to Plan B. However, the further Cousins has gotten away from that 2023 Achilles rupture, the better he’s seemingly played. His veteran poise is exactly what’s missing to steady the current Falcons ship, as the team lives with the weekly rollercoaster that is developing a young quarterback like Penix. In the current under-center, play-action-based offense under current Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, Cousins would thrive. These are the exact offensive styles Cousins has spent over a decade mastering. Cousins’s downside is his relatively low ceiling. The Vikings are firmly in playoff contention, but are unlikely to do any serious damage come January with Cousins at the helm, barring their defense going on an epic run. But for a Falcons team inching towards a decade without a playoff appearance, those seem like first-world problems. Penix’s ceiling hasn’t shown up consistently yet Penix’s upside is his potential to deliver the high-tier play that could turn a team into a legit postseason contender. And while glimpses of that level of play have flashed occasionally, it hasn’t materialized consistently. Penix’s arm strength is his superpower, but it hasn’t consistently translated into big-time downfield throws. After finishing dead last in PFF’s adjusted completion percentage on deep passes in 2025, he’s bounced back to 15th in 2026. But it adds up to Penix being no better than average at his supposed best trait, raising questions about what else he brings to the table. Lately, the answer has been slow starts, panicking under pressure, and overall inconsistency. Circumstances haven’t been in his favor, as overcoming his 2025 injury derailed his development alongside coaching changes. But the Falcons knowingly ignored Penix’s significant collegiate injury history , once again showcasing incredible hubris. Now the Falcons face the real possibility of hitting reset again at quarterback this offseason, leaving the franchise with nothing to show for either investment besides wasted primes and a mountain of frustration. Penix’s 2026 finish will decide if new regime stays the course And now the clock is ticking after the team paid some of its prominent skill players, like Bijan Robinson and Drake London. They have only a few more years to maximize their primes, or they may find themselves selling off both to the highest-bidding contender, as they did with safety Jessie Bates earlier this month. The Falcons have to fix the quarterback situation sooner rather than later. Putting their hopes in Penix’s potential cost the people who selected him their jobs . Now the current decision-makers in Atlanta are struggling to retroactively justify that decision as the Falcons stare at a 3-7 record again, the same record the team had when Penix was hurt a year ago. If the Falcons can’t turn the tide over these final seven games, starting Sunday against the quarterback they ran out of town, it’ll be harder for the current regime to justify staying the course with Penix after this year.

title: Michael Penix’s fifth-year option is now a coin flip for the Falcons
summary: When Michael Penix earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors after Week 7, the debate over his future as the Atlanta Falcons’ franchise quarterback seemed settled. Yet a month later, the conversation has shifted entirely, with the pivotal decision over whether to exercise his fifth-year option before May 2027 looming. Back then, taking the […]
full_text: VALDEBEBAS, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 05: Michael Penix Jr. of Atlanta Falcons attends during the NFL Madrid 2026, week of game, between Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at Ciudad Deportiva Real Madrid on November 05, 2026, in Madrid, Spain. (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images When Michael Penix earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors after Week 7, the debate over his future as the Atlanta Falcons’ franchise quarterback seemed settled. Yet a month later, the conversation has shifted entirely, with the pivotal decision over whether to exercise his fifth-year option before May 2027 looming. Back then, taking the option seemed a no-brainer; today, his recent skid and injury history make it a much more divisive gamble. Without a strong finish to 2026, the Falcons face the harsh reality of declining Penix’s option and turning 2027 into a make-or-break prove-it year. What the option costs for Atlanta Exercising Penix’s option fully guarantees his 2028 salary, whereas declining it puts him on track for unrestricted free agency after 2027. OverTheCap currently projects the base-tier quarterback option at roughly $25.7 million, an average of the third- through 25th-highest-paid passers over the past five seasons, since Penix can no longer reach the playing-time and Pro Bowl escalators required for higher tiers. Fortunately for Atlanta, the early-May deadline comes after both free agency and the 2027 NFL Draft, allowing head coach Kevin Stefanski and GM Ian Cunningham time to explore all their quarterback options before committing to Penix. The case for: Bryce Young’s blueprint Atlanta’s division rival Carolina has already paved the way by exercising Bryce Young’s $25.9 million option this past spring. Young showed year-over-year improvement, even if modest, giving Carolina reason to think the trend would continue with more time. Penix’s trendline isn’t as neat, thanks to his recent struggles , but if you remove his awful monsoon performance in Tampa , his numbers have improved slightly in several efficiency metrics, including completion rate and passer rating, compared to last year. There’s also significant financial advantage to picking up the option. If the Falcons decline Penix’s option and he plays well in 2027, they’d have to extend or use a franchise tag, set to increase from the $50 million projection in 2027. Picking up Penix’s option could save Atlanta roughly $25 million in cap space for 2028, giving Stefanski and Cunningham greater flexibility entering a pivotal third year. The case against: Anthony Richardson’s risk However, the decision isn’t as neat and tidy due to the complications of Penix’s injury history. Five season-ending injuries over the last eight years, dating back to his freshman year at Indiana, invite risk. If Penix suffers another serious injury setback in 2027 after exercising the option, the team would be on the hook for his full 2028 salary. Atlanta only needs to look at Young’s 2023 draft companion, Anthony Richardson, as a cautionary tale. The Indianapolis Colts declined Richardson’s option because frequent injuries kept the team from fully evaluating him. Richardson missed over 50 percent of games in his first two years, and another injury derailed his 2025 camp competition against Daniel Jones. Injuries have kept Penix out of 37 percent of the Falcons’ games over the past two seasons, impeding his development. Neither Atlanta nor its quarterback can afford another health setback. No middle ground left If Penix finishes 2026 healthy and sharp, trending up on the field, the Falcons will likely throw caution to the wind and pick up the option. Anything short of an emphatic finish, however, pushes the Falcons toward declining and using their projected $100 million in 2027 cap space to aggressively pursue competition, if not an outright replacement at quarterback this offseason. Right now, the decision feels like a coin flip. Over the next seven weeks, Penix will decide which side it lands on.
author: Aaron Freeman

title: AFC North Preview, Week 12: Browns off their bye week, Steelers and Ravens reeling
summary: Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Denver Broncos, 3:00pm EST (Friday) The Steelers were upset by the Philadelphia Eagles last week, dropping their second straight game and falling to 6-4 on the season. Looking to right the ship, the Steelers made a surprising decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers for this week’s game and will […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates after running for a touchdown during the second quarter against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Updated Standings: Cincinnati Bengals 7-3 Pittsburgh Steelers 6-4 Cleveland Browns 6-4 Baltimore Ravens 4-7 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Denver Broncos, 3:00pm EST (Friday) The Steelers were upset by the Philadelphia Eagles last week, dropping their second straight game and falling to 6-4 on the season. Looking to right the ship, the Steelers made a surprising decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers for this week’s game and will start Mason Rudolph instead. Rodgers’ benching may be a disciplinary action just as much as it as performance-based, but nonetheless it represents a big shift for the Steelers’ offense. Rudolph may have a difficult time getting Pittsburgh’s offense going against an elite Denver Broncos’ defense. While Rodgers hasn’t played great recently, the Steelers’ offensive issues stem beyond just quarterback play — as their supporting cast has been underwhelming. For Rudolph to have a chance to pull off an upset in Week 12, the Steelers will need to block well up front and get a big performance from Jaylen Warren on the ground. Defensively, the key for the Steelers may be slowing down rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who has quickly emerged as the engine of Denver’s offensive attack. Bo Nix has played better at quarterback lately, but the Steelers may be able to force a turnover or two, which frankly may be necessary for them to win. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: vs. New Orleans Saints, 1:00pm EST The Bengals had their five-game win streak snapped this past Monday night by the Washington Commanders. Despite being favored by more than five points, the Bengals couldn’t get going offensively and allowed a game-winning drive at the end of the fourth quarter. They will look to quickly get back on track with another favorable matchup on hand this week against the New Orleans Saints at home. The Saints are 2-1 against the AFC North this season having been beaten both the Ravens and Browns, which account but for almost all their total victories on the season (three). All five of New Orleans’ recent games have been decided by one possession, so they have a knack for staying within striking distance. The Bengals are favored by 10 points and have the potential to explode offensively at any time. The Saints allow the 10th-most points per game defensively. Cincinnati’s defense, meanwhile, has allowed 22 points or less in three consecutive games, albeit against some softer offenses. The Saints have an inconsistent offensive attack but are not without playmakers, having recently added Travis Etienne and Jordan Tyson into the mix. The Bengals will need to prevent Tyler Shough from finding a rhythm and getting comfortable. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST It was another incomplete performance from the Ravens last week, who suffered a sixth straight loss in a 35-33 defeat against the Carolina Panthers. The Ravens could not overcome several miscues including four turnovers and multiple dropped passes. They’ll look to finally right the ship in their final game before a bye week this Sunday, taking on the Houston Texans in a road matchup. Like the Ravens, the Texans are similarly trying to claw their way back to .500 and keep their playoff hopes alive. Houston’s defensive front will challenge the Ravens’ offensive line, particularly in pass protection, where Will Anderson Jr. looms large on the edge. The Ravens will need to find a way to neutralize the Texans’ pass rush to keep Jacoby Brissett upright. On defense, the Ravens continue to struggle allowing pass production over the middle of the field. Their lapses seem to stem mostly from miscommunications in zone coverage and poor execution. Finding a way to tighten things up against the Texans will be a challenge, as C.J. Stroud and company have been a high-octane passing attack this season. Nico Collins is a difficult cover at wide receiver. Cleveland Browns Matchup: vs. Las Vegas Raiders, 8:15pm EST Fresh off their bye week, the Browns will look to keep pushing towards a playoff berth in a primetime home matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. Cleveland’s defense is in a good spot here hosting a rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, in just his third career start. However, they cannot afford to let their guard down. The Browns’ defense is allowing the sixth-fewest passing yards per game but have been more susceptible against the run, giving up over 126 yards on the ground on average each contest. Fortunately for them, the Raiders have been one of the worst rushing offenses in the league this season, although they did total 143 yards on 6.0 yards per carry last week. Expect the Browns to force Mendoza to beat the blitz and make throws against man coverage. Las Vegas’ defense is plenty vulnerable as well, setting up Deshaun Watson and company to have a good performance. The Browns have continued to struggle to sustain a good run game, as they’ve had a leading rusher exceed 50 yards just three times all season. This is a prime spot for their rushing attack to get going a bit.
