title: Bills vs. Chiefs, Week 12 preview: 5 questions for Thanksgiving game
summary: Five questions is back this week, Rumblers! All eyes are on the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs when they play, which means there’s always room to chat about the greatest current NFL rivalry. That it’s happening on Thanksgiving night is gravy. If you’ve been a Bills fan long enough, you already know the mystique […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs throws during the third quarter in the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Five questions is back this week, Rumblers! All eyes are on the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs when they play, which means there’s always room to chat about the greatest current NFL rivalry. That it’s happening on Thanksgiving night is gravy. If you’ve been a Bills fan long enough, you already know the mystique and magic that surrounds this head-to-head series between quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. But there’s so much more to these games than that alone. To get us ready for Bills-Chiefs I spoke with Maurice Elston, who writes in-depth analysis, film study breakdowns, and more for Arrowhead Pride . Here, we dive a bit further into who and what the Chiefs click in 2026. Below, Maurice and I tackle everything from the biggest differences between this year’s team and previous rosters, plus a look at Kansas City’s greatest strength and most glaring weakness. We also dive into what wide receiver Josh Downs has brought to the team since joining the team at the trade deadline. Then, Maurice explains what played into the Chiefs’ pair of losses compared to their dominant wins, and he closes with a look at what has to go right if Kansas City is to win at Highmark Stadium. Read on below for some fantastic insight from Maurice into a team you can’t ever learn enough about! 1. Catch us up with this season’s Chiefs, if you can. What’s different about them as compared to previous seasons? Maurice Elston: The biggest difference is that the Chiefs finally have an efficient running game—and a coaching staff willing to lean into it and stick with it. Kenneth Walker III has given Kansas City the dynamic running back it has lacked for much of the Patrick Mahomes era. Now, with Walker injured, fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson has demonstrated that the success of the running game can continue without him. That has made the Chiefs a much more balanced offense. They can operate from under center, use play action and stay committed to the run instead of placing the entire game on Mahomes’ shoulders. Mahomes is still capable of taking over when necessary, but he no longer has to perform heroics every week for Kansas City to win. That balance has been the defining difference between this team and the Chiefs offenses of recent seasons. 2. At 8-2, what do you see as the Chiefs’ greatest strength, and their most glaring weakness — and how might either be impacted vs. Bills? Maurice Elston: Kansas City’s greatest strength is its balance. The Chiefs can run the football effectively and build their play-action passing game from it, which is something they haven’t consistently had during the Mahomes era. Even without Walker, Johnson has rushed for 206 yards over the last two games and shown that Kansas City doesn’t have to abandon its offensive identity. The most glaring weakness is the lack of continuity along the offensive line. The Chiefs still haven’t played a game with the original starting five they envisioned entering training camp. Injuries and lineup changes have forced players into unfamiliar roles throughout the season. That will be important against Buffalo, especially with right tackle Jaylon Moore ruled out. The Bills know Kansas City will want to establish Johnson and protect Mahomes with play action. If Buffalo can stop the run without committing extra defenders and then attack the Chiefs’ backup tackles, that could disrupt the balance that has made Kansas City so successful. 3. What has WR Josh Downs brought to/done for the offense since KC traded for him? Maurice Elston: If the Chiefs were missing anything at wide receiver, it was someone who could consistently create separation against man and press coverage. Downs has brought them a polished route runner who understands how to defeat leverage, set defenders up with his releases and find openings in the middle of a defense. The production has already been encouraging. In his first two games with Kansas City, Downs has eight receptions for 112 yards and a touchdown, with six of those catches resulting in first downs. That is significant production considering how little time he has had to learn Andy Reid’s offense. His presence also helps the other receivers because defenses now have another player they must respect opposite Travis Kelce. The more comfortable Downs becomes with the playbook, the more Kansas City can expand his role. He gives the Chiefs a separation skill set that has largely been missing since Tyreek Hill left Kansas City. 4. KC’s two losses came against playoff/SB teams in the Broncos and Seahawks. What’s the real story behind those defeats — especially only putting up a single field goal against Seattle — as compared to the way they’ve played in eight wins? Maurice Elston: The two losses were different. Kansas City moved the ball and scored 24 points against Denver, but pressure and offensive-line breakdowns hurt the Chiefs in critical situations. Seattle was a complete offensive collapse. The Seahawks committed to stopping Walker, challenged Kansas City’s receivers in man coverage and generated pressure without having to compromise their coverage. Kansas City finished with only 213 yards, while Mahomes completed just six of 13 passes for 44 yards and an interception when pressured. When the receivers couldn’t separate and the offensive line couldn’t hold up in obvious passing situations, Mahomes became unsettled and the entire offense lost its rhythm. Since those losses, Downs has given the Chiefs another answer against man coverage, Kahlil Benson has gained valuable experience at left tackle and Mahomes has looked increasingly comfortable in the pocket. Those are positive developments, but the real test begins now. Kansas City’s upcoming stretch against contending teams will show whether those problems have truly been corrected or were merely hidden during the eight victories. 5. What do you see as the biggest key to success for the Chiefs, if they accomplish their main goal Thanksgiving night? Maurice Elston: As dynamic as James Cook has been, the biggest key is containing Josh Allen and eliminating the explosive plays he creates outside the structure of Buffalo’s offense. Many of Allen’s most damaging plays happen when a defense appears to have him stopped. A pass rusher loses containment, Allen escapes the pocket and suddenly turns a potential sack into a long run or a completion downfield. Kansas City’s defensive line must maintain disciplined rush lanes instead of becoming so focused on sacks that it gives Allen an escape route. When the Chiefs have an opportunity to bring him down, they must finish the play. Keeping Allen in the pocket, forcing him to operate on schedule and preventing those backbreaking second-reaction plays will be the biggest key to Kansas City leaving Buffalo with a Thanksgiving night victory. My sincere thanks to Maurice Elston for his generous time and willingness to connect with me for five questions this week. I predict we’ll get another round of questions later in winter. You can read more of Maurice’s writing over at Arrowhead Pride . Be sure to check out my turn in the hot seat answering five of Maurice’s questions, at AP!
author: Matt Byham

title: Buffalo Bills OLB Greg Rousseau single-handedly wrecking NFL offenses
summary: To say that Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau is having a career year in 2026 is quite the understatement. Rousseau leads the NFL in quarterback hits with 29, and is currently second league-wide with 10 sacks in 10 games this season. His current sack total is a new career high for Rousseau — the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - NOVEMBER 15: Greg Rousseau #15 of the Buffalo Bills during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images To say that Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau is having a career year in 2026 is quite the understatement. Rousseau leads the NFL in quarterback hits with 29, and is currently second league-wide with 10 sacks in 10 games this season. His current sack total is a new career high for Rousseau — the first time in his professional career he’s reach double-digits in that category. Rousseau deserves to be mentioned in NFL Defensive Player of the Year conversations. He seems to be a good candidate as an All-Pro selection, and is likely to receive Pro Bowl honors. His success comes following a switch this offseason to 3-4 outside linebacker after playing the previous five seasons as a defensive end in a 4-3 system. It’s the first time in Rousseau’s career that he’s played that role as an edge rusher out wide from the linebacker box. When you run through Rousseau’s stats this year, it’s easy to imagine that he’s thrilled with the position shift. In just over half a season to this point, Rousseau has set new career highs in sacks (10), quarterback hits (29), and pass defenses (8); while tying his career high in forced fumbles (3), and remains just four off his single-season-career-best of 16 tackles for loss. When new Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady hired Jim Leonhard as the team’s current defensive coordinator, many were very curious how the former Bills safety intended to implement the attack-based system he espoused. After all, Leonhard had never called a team’s defensive plays at the NFL level, and he decided to make sweeping changes while marching forward with a large group of players hand-picked by prior head coach Sean McDermott. With the benefit of hindsight, it’s now clear that Rousseau may have been miscast as a do-it-all defensive end left to battle it out in the trenches. He played well there for McDermott, of course, but the brand of game-wrecking energy now regularly seen was at best available in spurts with him so deeply tied up in close hand combat against offensive linemen. Leonhard and outside linebackers coach Bobby April III have transformed Rousseau into the sort of player who keeps other teams’ offensive coordinators up and worrying about game plans. In his new role, Rousseau uses his albatross-like wingspan and skyscraper height to out-leverage would-be blockers. His reach and hands have become a problem for most quarterbacks, sometimes to the detriment of their depth chart. Rousseau’s jump in production is staggering, quite honestly, just from a quick glance at his career numbers via Pro Football Reference : In preparing to face the Bills on Thanksgiving, Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was quick to praise the man he nicknamed “Stretch Armstrong,” adding that KC’s defense must do what it can “neutralize his strengths” and “have a plan in place, making sure that we’re putting bodies on him and keeping him off our quarterback.” It’s been quite some time since Buffalo had an edge rusher who instilled such fear among NFL teams, maybe dating back to defensive end Mario Williams. Now, Leonhard and the Bills must find a way to get better production out of the team’s other front-seven defenders. Amid all the praise for Rousseau’s game in 2026 comes a worrying trend when evaluating his defensive teammates. Though Rousseau is a 1-man wrecking machine who’s having a career season, teammates around him have failed to produce much as pass rushers. After Rousseau, there’s a steep drop in production and impact plays among the defensive line and outside linebackers. Defensive linemen Ed Oliver and Deone Walker have received praise in year one within Leonhard’s system, but the overall sack production beyond Rousseau has been dreadful. Defensive lineman T.J. Parker ranks second on the team with 3.5 sacks. Nine other players on the team have chipped in toward the sack total, however those nine defenders have only 9.5 sacks combined. Quick math reveals that Rousseau has more sacks than all Bills defenders, not named Parker, added together. Buffalo’s schedule over the next month is a gauntlet, and the defense will be tested beyond the trials early this season. Someone must step up in a complementary role as a pass rusher in tandem with Rousseau, otherwise teams may begin implementing new ways of slowing down the Bills’ best defender. In the four games since Buffalo’s bye week, the defense has played a far more aggressive brand of football. Perhaps Leonhard’s only just begun scratching the surface of the pressure package he intends to release on the NFL. A big test awaits Thursday night.
author: Matt Byham

title: Lions vs. Bears / Cowboys vs. Eagles Thanksgiving Day NFL fan discussion
summary: Thanksgiving Day is finally here, and with it comes a featured course of football all day long. First, the Detroit Lions host the Chicago Bears in a game that should have Buffalo Bills fans’ attention even through their meals this afternoon. It’s a fantastic matchup of two 8-2 teams vying to win the NFC North […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 28: Running back Jahmyr Gibbs (26) of the Detroit Lions carries the ball during a game between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Thursday, November 28, 2024. (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Thanksgiving Day is finally here, and with it comes a featured course of football all day long. First, the Detroit Lions host the Chicago Bears in a game that should have Buffalo Bills fans’ attention even through their meals this afternoon. It’s a fantastic matchup of two 8-2 teams vying to win the NFC North in what may be the NFL’s strongest division. The Bills defeated the Lions in Week 2 for Thursday Night Football , and they’ll battle the Bears in Week 15 for a Saturday spotlight game in primetime. Many see Chicago as a favorite to represent the NFC in Super Bowl LXI. The mid-afternoon game features the Dallas Cowboys hosting the Philadelphia Eagles. It’s a game with a far different vibe and two NFC East teams with losing records. The Cowboys still have a chance at the playoffs, mathmatically, but it’s bleak at best without winning their division thanks to the quality of teams in the NFC North. This evening, the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in what should be another incredible game between two of the best teams in the AFC and this era’s greatest quarterbacks in Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. We’ll of course have a separate, dedicated open thread for Bills-Chiefs in primetime this evening, but for now enjoy this space to chat all things Lions, Bears, Eagles, and Cowboys… and maybe some Turkey Day talk! We here at Buffalo Rumblings wish you all a happy, healthy, and safe Thanksgiving with your family and loved ones. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

title: 5 Kansas City Chiefs to watch at the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs on tonight, and it will be Kansas City’s first trip to the new Highmark Stadium. Unfortunately for everyone involved, the Bills won’t be able to welcome the Chiefs with nice weather, which could make for an interesting contest in this pivotal AFC matchup. For the entirety of […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 22: Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs the ball against the Arizona Cardinals during the first quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs on tonight, and it will be Kansas City’s first trip to the new Highmark Stadium. Unfortunately for everyone involved, the Bills won’t be able to welcome the Chiefs with nice weather, which could make for an interesting contest in this pivotal AFC matchup. For the entirety of the decade, Bills-Chiefs matchups have had significant impact on the AFC standings. This one is no different, as the winner of the game will put themselves in the driver’s seat for the AFC’s top overall seed. With plenty of rain, wind gusts of upwards of 40 miles per hour, and temperatures that will be at least 25 degrees cooler than those Buffalo had on Sunday, we can truly say that old-school football weather is coming for the holiday. Will that weather impact each team’s game planning? Perhaps. It is impacting this column, albeit slightly. Everyone wants to talk about Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen, so I’m going to leave them off of each respective list. We know that Allen and Mahomes are keys to success. There are plenty of other players worth spotlighting, however. Here are five Chiefs to watch this week against Buffalo. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB Emmett Johnson With Kenneth Walker III ruled out yesterday, it’s Johnson who will handle the backfield duties on Thursday. In Walker’s absence, Johnson has been excellent, totaling 206 rushing yards and a touchdown on 45 carries against the Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals. Johnson averages 4.5 yards per rush this season, but he’s done his most damage as a receiver. In the Chiefs’ last four games, Johnson has 15 catches for 236 yards and 3 touchdowns on 17 targets. He is a dynamic threat in multiple phases of the game. While Walker is obviously excellent, as he leads the NFL in yards per carry at 5.5 yards per rush this seaosn, Johnson is a stud back in his own right. Buffalo still needs to be wary of the Chiefs’ run game. WR Josh Downs The Chiefs acquired Downs from the Indianapolis Colts at the trade deadline this season, and while his numbers haven’t been eye-popping in two games with the club, he’s been exactly what Mahomes and the Chiefs’ passing offense needed. Downs has 8 receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets so far, and given that he can do damage both outside and in the slot, Buffalo has their work cut out for them in matching up with the speedy wideout. Buffalo has obviously been much better defensive since the bye week, but they also have played a string of subpar offenses helmed by mediocre—or worse—quarterbacks over that stretch. If Downs is in the slot, Dee Alford will likely be the one tasked with handling him. If he’s outside, Downs will test whichever boundary corners Buffalo has available to them. He’s a very, very good receiver who runs good routes and can pick up big yardage after the catch. Jime Leonhard and company need to have a plan to bottle him this week. TE Travis Kelce After looking like he was close to finished last season, Kelce has found new life this year. He’s averaging 14.3 yards per reception, which is a career-high for the future Hall of Famer. He has given the Bills fits throughout the years, and Buffalo’s linebacker group still isn’t what I’d call a top-notch group in coverage. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has done well to adjust and improve his grouping, but this is going to be the first big test Buffalo has faced since their post-bye week success began. Forcing Mahomes to throw the ball outside the numbers, especially in a windy, rainy day, will give the Bills a shot at some turnovers. Keeping Kelce in check over the middle is paramount to success this week. DE George Karlaftis III The 2022 first-round pick is on pace for the best season of his career. He already has 8 sacks and 26 quarterback hits, and he’s been especially good over the last month. In Kansas City’s last four games, Karlaftis has 7 sacks, 7 tackles for loss, and 11 quarterback hits. For the season, he’s also knocked down ten passes already. While Buffalo has their own breakout star in former 2021 first-round pick Greg Rousseau, Karlaftis is experiencing a similar career surge, as he’s on pace for 14 sacks this season. The Bills will need to chip him and be on the lookout for games and stunts up front, especially if Karlaftis and perennial Bills menace Chris Jones are lined up next to each other. CB Nohl Williams The second-year man is following up what was a phenomenal rookie season with an even better second act. Williams has allowed just 44.6% of the 52 passes thrown while he’s the closest man in coverage to be completed. Opposing passers have a 55.2 quarterback rating when targeting Williams, who has two interceptions and 13 pass breakups so far this season. I’m interested to see what they do with Williams. Does he merely match up with the Buffalo wideout across from him? Or is he following DJ Moore in crucial situations? Either way, Josh Allen will need to know where he is, and who he’s covering, at all times.

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in the Thanksgiving nightcap this year, and what a game it should be. The 9-1 Bills are the current No. 1 seed in the AFC playoff picture. Thanks to tiebreakers, the 8-2 Chiefs trail the 8-2 Denver Broncos in the AFC West, so Kansas City is currently […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in the Thanksgiving nightcap this year, and what a game it should be. The 9-1 Bills are the current No. 1 seed in the AFC playoff picture. Thanks to tiebreakers, the 8-2 Chiefs trail the 8-2 Denver Broncos in the AFC West, so Kansas City is currently the No. 5 seed in the conference. However, a win over the Bills would go a long way towards ensuring that the AFC playoffs run through Arrowhead Stadium. The Bills are coming off a sloppy divisional win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The Chiefs, on the other hand, thoroughly thrashed the Arizona Cardinals. Kansas City has won three games in a row; Buffalo has won six consecutive games. Unless there’s a tie, someone is going to take a loss for the first time in a long time this week. If Buffalo wants to emerge with a win over their bitter conference rival, they’ll need some big performances from their key players. While everyone wants to talk about the quarterbacks in this game, we’re intentionally leaving both Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes out of the columns this week. Those two are pretty obvious. There are plenty of other players worthy of mention, though. Here are five Bills to watch in this critical AFC contest. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB James Cook III Regardless of the weather, Cook is a tremendous key to Buffalo’s success. After a slow start on Sunday, Cook extended his streak of scoring at least one touchdown and rushing for at least 75 yards to nine games, which is a new NFL record. He had previously shared the record at eight games with John Rigging and LaDainian Tomlinson. Cook surpassed the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the fourth consecutive season, and he joins two Hall of Fame former Bills in Thurman Thomas and O.J. Simpson as the only players to achieve that feat in franchise history. The sledding won’t be easy against an outstanding Kansas Cigy tush defense that allows just 3.7 yards per carry on the season, but in a game that’s set to feature horrendous weather, finding space and keeping the offense ahead of the sticks will be of the utmost importance. TE Dalton Kincaid It’s something we’ve said ever since the Bills made Kincaid their first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. When the big tight end is healthy, Josh Allen’s life is much easier. When he doesn’t play, Allen doesn’t have nearly as much space to operate in the passing game. Last week, Allen threw for 304 yards without Kincaid, but it took 45 passing attempts and some ugly possessions to hit that milestone. If Kincaid is healthy, it gives the Bills their full cadre of pass-catchers against an elite defensive unit. Allen’s quarterback rating when targeting Kincaid was 149.2 last season. Since Kincaid joined the club, Allen has a passer rating of 99.9 with Kincaid in the lineup and 91.2 without him. Allen averages 237 passing yards per game with Kincaid in the lineup; he averages 206 passing yards per game without him. He has thrown 77 touchdowns against 29 interceptions in 47 games with Kincaid, and he’s thrown 14 touchdowns against 9 interceptions in the ten games Kincaid has missed in his career. No. 86 is a big part of Buffalo’s offense, and having him on Thursday will go a long way towards helping the Bills earn a victory. OLB Bradley Chubb Greg Rousseau is obvious. Someone else has to offer some juice in the pass rush, and while I’m tempted to spotlight rookie T.J. Parker, I think it has to be the veteran edge rusher to come in and make a play. Chubb has been pretty quiet this season, totaling just 1.5 sacks, 10 quarterback hits and 14 pressures while playing on 69% of the Bills’ defensive snaps. With the Miami Dolphins last season coming off an ACL injury, Chubb totaled 8.5 sacks, 22 pressures, and 20 quarterback hits. No matter how many good things the Bills have to say about him, they definitely expected more when they handed him a three-year deal worth $43.5 million this offseason. I expect that the Chiefs will look to double-team Rousseau, and they’ll likely leave Chubb blocked by one man. Chubb has to win that matchup and impact Patrick Mahomes in some way. DL Deone Walker The big fella doesn’t have a quarterback hit or a takcle for loss since before the bye week. He has just one sack, which he notched against C.J. Stroud during Buffalo’s Week One win over the Houston Texans. Sure, the job of the nose takcle involves doing a lot of “lunch pail” work that often goes unnoticed, but I would love to see Walker collapsing the pocket on Mahomes from the interior in the way that we’ve had to watch Chris Jones collapse the pocket on Josh Allen from the defensive tackle spot so many times over the years. Thursday night would be a nice time for Walker to dominate. It would be a great addition to his burgeoning resume in what has been a very good second professional season. S Cole Bishop With the defense settling down over the last month, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard can really start to use his chess pieces to their athletic strengths. Bishop can operate at every level of the defense for the Bills, and I would love to see Leonhard deploy him in a variety of ways. Use him to guard Travis Kelce. Use him as a deep-third centerfielder when Mahomes expects newly-acquired Amani Hooker to pkay that role. Use him as a blitzer off the edge to create pressure on the run game and the pass game. Bishop is an elite athlete who is allowing a career-low 55.8% of the passes thrown while he’s the closest man in coverage to be completed. Bishop has a chance to be eating a turkey leg on National television after this one because he can change the game in a variety of ways. Look for him to notch his first interception of the season while also collecting his second sack of the season at some point in this game.

full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 02: Spencer Brown #79 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates a touchdown scored by Josh Allen #17 during the third quarter in the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images A major test awaits the Buffalo Bills this evening. Few games carry the weight like any matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Playing in primetime on Thanksgiving night only adds to the drama. It’s a true feast for the eyes and a diabolical thief of one’s resting heart rate. Bills Mafia is well aware of the history between quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. Having played 10 times to this point between the regular season and playoffs, the all-time series is split down the middle between the two. Allen is 5-1 against Mahomes and the Chiefs in the regular season, while Mahomes is 4-0 in the postseason. By and large, it’s likely that Allen and Mahomes play key roles in the outcome of tonight’s game. However, weather is going to be a factor — and that may play very well into an expanded rushing attack. Bills fans know that may call for an enhanced featured role for running back James Cook III. It may also mean that short passes to running backs Ty Johnson and Ray Davis, as well wide receiver Khalil Shakir are the go-to for Allen while trying to combat the rain and wind. Though some see the expected foul weather as a detriment, it may actually benefit the Bills. Buffalo is a powerful, run-first offense. Part of that game plan of course involves Allen as a rusher. Last weekend, Allen didn’t attempt a single carry, but that shouldn’t repeat against Kansas City. It’s anyone’s guess as to how this game plays out. Will the Bills success against the Chiefs with Brady now in charge, and Buffalo claiming regular-season bragging right over Kansas City? We asked Rumblers to weigh in on just that, and 78% believe the Bills will defeat the Chiefs in Week 12. There’s a lot at stake on Thanksgiving night. If Buffalo wins and maintains first place in the AFC playoff race, they’d claim a major head-to-head advantage over their biggest elimination game rivals. That would improve their chances of claiming the one seed and a bye week to start the postseason. Something’s run afoul, Rumblers. The 9-1 Bills, the team currently holding the top spot in the AFC playoff race, and one that’s won six games in a row… well, they’ve somehow convinced a segment of Bills Mafia that things aren’t headed in the right direction. Buffalo has held their last four opponents to a combined nine field goals. Total. Zero touchdowns. The same defense that began the season ranked last in points allowed per game has surrendered just one touchdown since the bye week, that being a ground score early in action against running back Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens. Despite this, just 76% of fans polled gave their vote of confidence in the current direction of the Bills under head coach Joe Brady, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane. Just? Yes, it’s appropriate, considering the continued drop in fan confidence from a high of 94% two weeks ago, to 89% last week, and now seeing a further 13% loss in fan confidence Expect a major jump in either direction after Buffalo’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs this evening. Let’s quickly check in on the fan vote over at Arrowhead Pride. Just 62% of fans think the Chiefs will defeat the Bills on Thanksgiving night. However, right now, 91% of voters there are confident in the current direction of the team. One of this week’s national polls asked voters to pick the Thanksgiving game (Eve and Day) they believe will be the most entertaining. Would you be surprised to learn that Bills-Chiefs leads the way with 49% of the total vote? The only other game to garner a fair bit of the vote was Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears (40%). However, with the recent Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy soap opera, that Friday game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Denver Broncos may pick up some viewers. title: Joe Brady’s Buffalo Bills need a vintage Sean McDermott performance vs. Chiefs
summary: Some of the gameday columns I’ve written this season have centered around how Joe Brady’s Buffalo Bills need to be different than the Sean McDermott Bills. But not this one, not before this game. Because after ending the playoff drought, I view the Bills’ regular-season success against the Chiefs as one of, if not the […]
full_text: Some of the gameday columns I’ve written this season have centered around how Joe Brady’s Buffalo Bills need to be different than the Sean McDermott Bills. But not this one, not before this game. Because after ending the playoff drought, I view the Bills’ regular-season success against the Chiefs as one of, if not the crown jewel of the McDermott era. Five-consecutive wins against the Chiefs was stunning. And how Mahomes struggled vs. McDermott’s defense in those games was unfathomable. In those five losses to the Bills since 2021, these are Mahomes’ statistics: 56% completion rate 6.14 yards per attempt 8 touchdowns (none rushing) 8 interceptions 11 sacks taken Incredible, right? And, heck — the Chiefs never scored more than 21 points in any of those matchups. And how about Allen vs. the vaunted Steve Spagnuolo defenses in the five contests? 63.5% completion rate 7.8 yards per attempt 9 passing touchdowns, 7 rushing touchdowns 2 interceptions 7 sacks taken And if Brady and Co. are to draw any inspiration from a McDermott-era win over the Chiefs, there’s no need to look back into the distant past. As the 2025 regular-season victory against the Chiefs was the the finest win in the McDermott era. I genuinely believe that. Sure, the Bills had the luxury of playing at home. Other than that, the game had style points galore for Buffalo. Josh Allen went 23-of-26 for 275 yards with a touchdown pass and no interceptions. That’s a completion percentage of 88.4%, a yards-per-attempt average of 10.5, and a passer rating of 123.2. He also scored twice on the ground. James Cook had 114 yards rushing at a 4.2 yards-per-carry clip. Defensively, it was McDermott’s magnum opus against Mahomes, the type of dominant performance that certainly evaded Buffalo’s defense in playoff meetings with the Chiefs quarterback. Mahomes went 15-of-34 for 250 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. That’s a completion percentage of 44.1%, yards-per-attempt average of 7.4, and a passer rating of 57.2. The Chiefs averaged 4.0 yards per carry, but only finished with 79 yards on the ground. At one point, the Bills held a 21-10 lead. There was some semblance of Mahomes magic, as he converted a 4th and 17 in the fourth quarter that led to a touchdown drive to bring the Chiefs within one score. But the Bills were undeniably the better team from start to finish, and we had never witnessed such a sizable dichotomy between Allen and Mahomes in the same game. Tonight, in what will be a rain-soaked Highmark Stadium, Brady’s Bills need to take a page out of McDermott’s book against their most bitter rival. A sixth-consecutive win over the Chiefs would be remarkable and move Buffalo closer to something McDermott never did in Orchard Park — earning the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs.

title: NFL predictions: 4 bold takes for Bills vs. Chiefs on Thanksgiving
summary: Is there anything bold to predict about a powerhouse matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs? Sure, given enough imagination and luck. Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night is truly must-see TV. You can bet that most of the country will be tuned in this evening to see what quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 02: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball during the second quarter in the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Is there anything bold to predict about a powerhouse matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs? Sure, given enough imagination and luck. Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night is truly must-see TV. You can bet that most of the country will be tuned in this evening to see what quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have in store for Round 11. Through 10 games (includes playoffs), Allen and Mahomes are each 5-5. The key difference between them is that Allen has gone 4-1 in the regular season, while Mahomes has gone 4-0 in the postseason. That said, this is a regular season with huge stakes. Buffalo is currently 9-1 and in first place in the AFC, but this game’s winner takes the driver’s seat over the loser in the chase for the one seed come playoff time. Well that is, unless they finish in a tie. As you might expect, there are a lot of similarities between the Bills and Chiefs. Beyond the well-known star players, however, the rosters are a bit different. Where they run parallel is at quarterback — thanks to the two best players of this generation. Buffalo and Kansas City also boast nasty rushing attacks, and the Bills have the league’s top-ranked unit behind lead running back James Cook III. These are two teams that like to bleed clock, but can strike 80 yards or more down the field for six in a moment’s notice. Tonight, the recipe might involve a bit more of the running game from both sides, at least until it’s safer to attack downfield in the passing game. Here are four bold predictions I have for the Bills on Thanksgiving… James Cook sets new career high in rushing attempts You may have heard by now that the Bills are a run-first offense. That fact hasn’t necessarily limited what Allen can accomplish as a passer, but head coach Joe Brady is intent on establishing dominance in the trenches. Somewhere along the line, Cook must have been told that he’d be a fantastic runner between the tackles, despite his somewhat small size for the position. That, or his instincts know ball. Maybe it’s both, and it might also be true that Buffalo’s offensive line opens up some tasty running lanes between the tackles. Whatever the case may be, Cook is a dangerous one-cut, take-it-to-the-house runner who, in ways, recalls Terrel Davis. Last season’s rushing yardage champion has taken on an even bigger role in the Bills’ offense this season, and he’s currently second in rushing yards. I predict a heavy workload for Cook tonight, with him setting a new personal best in carries. That number to beat is 32, which he set almost one year ago against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cook has already come close to breaking that number, having totaled 31 carries against the Minnesota Vikings this season (Week 9). It may not seem like a bold prediction, given the expected weather and Cook’s role. However, if it comes to be, that may mean that the Bills thoroughly dominated the trenches and stole away the game clock. Buffalo is 14-2 in games that Cook carries the ball 20 or more times, so there’s reason to expect they lean on him in bad weather. FanDuel Sportsbook has James Cook’s rushing attempts set at over 18.5 (-138)/under 18.5 (+104). I’d be shocked if he see the ball less than 20 times. Amani Hooker gets a pick-six New Bills safety Amani Hooker has fit right in and taken every snap on defense since Buffalo brought him in via trade ahead of Week 10. Hooker has five interceptions on the season, which includes a hat trick against Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. The Bills may ask Hooker to spend a lot of time shadowing tight end Travis Kelce, which could mean ample opportunities to steal a ball from Mahomes. Kelce loves to ad-lib routes, and you can bet Hooker has studied his tendencies to see when and where jumping the route may lead to six the other way. Mahomes has thrown only four interceptions this season, and none in the past four games. He’s due. You can’t try to cash in on his odds for a pick-six at FanDuel Sportsbook, but Amani Hooker is currently listed at +1200 to record an interception. Khalil Shakir leads team in catches and receiving yards Try as they might, One Bills Drive can’t seem to shake Shakir’s role as Buffalo’s most consistently productive receiver. He isn’t always the one with the most yards or catches, but Shakir’s efficiency is nearly unmatched. If anything, Brady and Allen should be working to get Shakir more involved on game day. There were encouraging signs in Week 11 against the Miami Dolphins, when Shakir was involved early, even catching a 38-yard pass downfield while leading the team in receiving yards (101). I often refer to Shakir as The Pinball Wizard thanks to his insane agility in both space and traffic. He’s the best of both worlds as a shifty wide receiver with traits that rival the best running backs. Brady probably understands that it makes sense to attack the middle of Kansas City’s defense, and who better to lead that effort than Shakir? Maybe you prefer tight end Dalton Kincaid? Sure, that’s fair game, if he plays through a pair of injuries. Shakir is currently listed at +600 with FanDuel Sportsbook to finish with the most receiving yards among all players from both teams in the game. Again, with nasty weather expected, it seems reasonable to count on Allen looking to his most reliable receiver. Repeat after me: In Shakir We Trust. Josh Allen & Patrick Mahomes each run for a TD It’s Allen and Mahomes, and both are surgical dual-threats. You already trust that Allen’s running for at least one touchdown. You might scoff at Mahomes doing it simply because the Chiefs never use him in short-yardage situations. It doesn’t matter. Mahomes is probably going to end up keeping it himself for six from the red zone once this evening. You can get in on this as a 2 leg Same Game Parlay at FanDuel Sportsbook, which currently lists Allen and Mahomes as +995 to each score an anytime touchdown (which includes rushing or receiving). full_text: The Buffalo Bills have gotten such great ratings for Thanksgiving over the years that the NFL decided to let them host a game. If that wasn’t enough of a draw, they’ll have Kansas City coming to town to keep the Josh Allen v. Patrick Mahomes era alive and well. And if THAT wasn’t enough of a draw, KC is just one game back of Buffalo and eyeing our one seed spot. That’s quite the parade of reasons to tune in. A parade that will be rained on. Literally. The current forecast calls for rain all game. Cold November Rain. While we’ve been assured that not even this lasts forever, it’s the kind of weather that could turn even two of the game’s best quarterbacks of all time conservative. That could result in a running game slog of a contest. Which both teams are well suited for. But who is best suited? Which team has shown the better capability to win the slog? I apologize as the short week is leading me to a stats-based version of my weekly opponent preview. So let’s talk some stats. As a heads up, I don’t care about volume stats for this. There’s any number of reasons a team could amass a ton of rushing yards without being all that good at it. We’ll focus on rate stats. As is tradition. On a per play basis, the Buffalo Bills rush for 4.59 yards per attempt. That’s good for eighth best in the league which by my rule of four puts them in the “good” category. With all the emphasis on the run game for Buffalo, it’s a bit shocking that Kansas City’s offense lands in the “elite” category with their second best rate in the league. KC averages 4.88 yards per game. Right now the advantage goes to Kansas City. That said, defense matters. Which team is better at stopping the run? Kansas City allows 3.73 yards per rush, fifth best in the league or “good.” The Bills are middle of the pack with their 4.06 yards allowed and 15th spot. Advantage still goes to Kansas City. So it’s a lost cause, right? Uh, no. Part of the story will likely be injuries. As of the moment, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is looking like he’ll miss the game. Even if he suits up, he won’t have practiced for weeks as he’s been hurting his ankle in Week 9. On Buffalo’s side of things though, both Spencer Brown and O’Cyrus Torrence are both on the injury report. Defensively there’s nothing to note on the Kansas City side of things, while Buffalo’s Greg Rousseau is now on the injury report. It’s still looking bleak for Buffalo. Now let’s get to individual efficiency and see if that makes us feel better. James Cook is averaging 5.1 yards per carry. The other running backs are hitting 3.2 yards or less. Josh Allen is a dynamic threat in the run game and he’s been going for 4.4 yards per carry. Patrick Mahomes 4.o yards per carry. Non-starting running backs are averaging 4.5 yards or worse. Starting running back Kenneth Walker III is running at an absurd 5.5 yards per carry. I did forget to mention on thing though. Walker is hurt and his status is currently up in the air for this Thursday. While they’ve still managed over 100 yards per game without Walker, the efficiency should take a hit. So what’s my prediction? I like the Bills. Having the game in Buffalo should help and while Kansas City should be able to slog better than Buffalo on paper, it’s also true that those worries about the Bills schedule need to look at KC’s up to now. Mahomes and his crew shouldn’t be a pushover but it’s quite their season really starts on Thanksgiving.

title: Brian Answers: Injured/reserve slots, NFC South, Celebrity Look-a-likes, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I’ve got a special Thanksgiving edition for you today, as we wait for Monday Night Football. Make sure to check your fantasy football teams today, let’s dive right in! hollywud: How many IR designated to return spots are left […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 22: Bryce Young #9 and Corey Bullock #67 of the Carolina Panthers celebrate as time expires in the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Bank of America Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I’ve got a special Thanksgiving edition for you today, as we wait for Monday Night Football. Make sure to check your fantasy football teams today, let’s dive right in! hollywud: How many IR designated to return spots are left for the team this year? I can think of 4 spots that need to be filled, Brooks, BC, Horn & Ickey. Could that be an issue? And Thank all the staffers and commenters on Cat Scratch Reader for all the entertainment… You’re welcome! And Happy Thanksgiving! The Panthers just spent the last of their two remaining designations to return from injured/reserve on Thomas Incoom, a core special teamer. That means they will have one spot left, likely for Jaycee Horn. They’ll get two more designations if they actually make the playoffs. They allowed the 21 day return window to lapse on OL Brady Christensen, so he reverted back to IR this week. The window is still open for Jonathon Brooks. As far as OT Ikem Ekwonu goes, he’s actually still on the Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform List (PUP). So his return would not count against the 8 player maximum for Injured/Reserve. He could return at any point this season. SnarkyComet: What are your thoughts on Tremble? Like, are you going to pissed if we don’t extend him? As Mike Kaye stated in the Tweet you linked , I think Tommy Tremble is someone the Panthers have to bring back barring a huge contracts, which I don’t think he’d get on the open market. He’s finally developed into the player we thought he could be, a hugely effective blocker with receiving upside. He has a rapport with Bryce Young who will be here at least through the end of next year. No reason not to bring him back. @WTMealey: Lets play the future of QB in NFC South? 3 years from now. For each team give me a ratio same guy/different guy 90/10 50/50 you get the idea if you want to do HC that is cool as well I’d give the Saints a 50/50 on Tyler Shough and probably on their coach Kellen Moore as well. Both seem pretty solid but three years in the NFL is a long time. For the Falcons, probably 0/100 on the QB, I just don’t see them sticking with Michael Penix. Kevin Stefanski for me is a 50/50 just because this is his first year there. For the Buccaneers, I’d say 0/100 on both Baker Mayfield and Todd Bowles. I don’t see them both leaving now but I have a hard time seeing either of them with the team in 3 years. For the Panthers… I’m going with Thanksgiving optimism and saying both Bryce Young and Dave Canales are still here in 3 years, and future-us is thankful we stuck around for the ride. SmoothC: Is the defense noticeably improved under Wash? I think the defensive line certainly is. The pass rush has been more of a factor since he took over, especially Princely Umanmielen. Obviously, having a guy like Jaelan Phillips back in the fold helps the defense across the board. The secondary has been a bit more aggressive, with Will Lee having his best game as a pro last week. I’m just not sure if I attribute that to Wash as much as him just developing as a rookie. But I like the simplified defense. It is going to be tested in the coming weeks and its first major exam is going to be stopping the run against the Bucs on Monday. The Ravens did a lot of damage on the ground on Sunday, but we’ll see if a concentrated game plan to stop the run against a Tampa Bay team that will run at all costs works out. HighMiles: Is play calling holding back our offense? We seemed to be scheming T-Mac and Coker open and it made Bryce look like a superhero. Now that seems to be missing. Is it because our play calling is too predictable now, or because we are forcing our running game now as the priority, or something else entirely? I think defensive coordinators now have a better sense of what the Panthers are trying to do on offense. Remember, while this is still technically a scheme under Dave Canales’s umbrella, this was a new play caller with Brad Idzik. So I think between having some film and the offensive line struggling, the defenses have come up with a better game plan. While I love Idzik’s penchant to push the ball down field to Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, Bryce has to have the time to deliver the football. And defenses know they want to do that now. So between getting pressure and disrupting the routes in man coverage, it hasn’t been quite as explosive recently. Robholland211: I need to know am I gonna end my birthday happy due to a win or angry due to a loss? Happy Birthday Rob! I’m calling a win because the NFC South is weird and Faker Mayfield can’t throw so good anymore. Don’t bet money though, never bet on the Panthers. bulletooftony: Brian, how would you handle the LT situation? Draft one, possibly resign Icky (if he doesn’t walk), slide Freeling to LT and draft a RT, other? I’d probably bring back Ikem Ekwonu and then figure out which one on him and Monroe Freeling make the most sense at left tackle. I would also draft one, maybe not with a first round pick but any other pick would make sense. They’ll need the depth since I suspect this is Taylor Moton’s swan song either this season or next season. I’d spend the free agency capital on the interior of the offensive line since I expect center and right guard to look very different come the start of next season. Revshawn: I began my playthrough of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by standing on the branch above Saria at the start of the game and aura farming instead of going to down to meet her. Am I playing the game right? You’re playing the game wrong. It should start in Vice City with you stealing a car for Lucia’s mother. Brazilian Panther: Okay Brian, tell us to what “famous” or “celebrity” people used to compare you to. During my last year in college, The Girl Next Door came out and some chicks started saying I looked like Emile Hirsch, the main dude on that film. A taller version of him at least. Too bad I didn’t met any Elisha Cuthbert back in the day tho. Happy Thanksgiving!! Oh man, great question to end on. I’ve been compared to Michael Cera basically all of my adult life, to the point I had people actually asking me if I was the guy from Superbad. I’ve also gotten Jesse Eisenberg, which I see less. But the golden one is Machine Gun Kelly. I never would have seen it until I saw a picture of him looking like a normal person from many moons ago. That one was hauntingly accurate to the point I question the universe. That’s all for this week, Panthers fans! Enjoy your Thanksgiving, and stick with us on Monday for a hopeful beating of the Tampa Bay Bucs! KEEP POUNDING!

title: 2027 CSR NFL “Thankful” Mock Draft
summary: The NFL Draft is still five months away, but we have several things to be thankful for regardless. For example, the Panthers are leading the NFC South by two full games and are getting healthier by the week. In the spirit of Thanksgiving, I decided to make this Panthers-only mock draft fully stocked with picks […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 05: General Manager Dan Morgan of the Carolina Panthers looks on prior to the game against the Miami Dolphins at Bank of America Stadium on October 05, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL Draft is still five months away, but we have several things to be thankful for regardless. For example, the Panthers are leading the NFC South by two full games and are getting healthier by the week. In the spirit of Thanksgiving, I decided to make this Panthers-only mock draft fully stocked with picks that should warm Panthers fans hearts. Just like politics at the Thanksgiving dinner table, I have no doubt there will be some passionate arguing about this mock in the comments! Round 1 **TRADE** Detroit Lions send 1.30, 2.61, and 2028 7th to Carolina for 1.19 With plenty of options available at positions of need, Dan Morgan pulls the trigger on a trade picking up an extra second rounder to work with. Since depth is a large part of this team’s issues, more picks isn’t a bad idea. Pick 30 – Cade Pieper, iOL, Iowa I have already written a draft profile on Pieper , who is the prototypical farm-boy-turned-Iowa-offensive-lineman. Pieper is incredibly athletic with good strength and is considered one of the best run blockers in the Draft. Robert Hunt is likely a cap casualty after this season considering his play and a potential contract extension for Bryce Young. Pieper would slot right in at RG day one. Round 2 Pick 51 – Zabien Brown, CB, Alabama Brown is another player who already has a profile on CSR . Brown is a boundary corner with elite physical traits. His production leapt up last season, though it has flattened out a bit this season. Still, the flashes and tools are there, and the Panthers need more corners to avoid Akayleb Evans and Marco Wilson being the outside starters again. Pick 61 (from DET) – Kenyatta Jackson Jr, EDGE, Ohio State Jackson is a versatile edge defender with elite size. He’s already a quality run defender and has elite pass rush tools. Nic Scourton should be back next year, but Pat Jones might not be. If the Panthers move to a more 4-3 oriented front, Jackson could help solidify the edge rotation. Round 3 Pick 83 – Emmanuel Oyebadejo, DL, Florida Oyebadejo has an incredible story and even more incredible physical tools. His size/athleticism combination makes him incredibly versatile. Whether playing DT or edge, Oyebadejo has shown flashes of dominance. Learning from the likes of Derrick Brown and Jaelan Phillips could do wonders. Round 4 Pick 120 – PJ Williams, OT, SMU Williams was arrested for marijuana possession his freshman year at Texas A&M. He then transferred to SMU and has performed quite well overall. While he still has a lot of technique that needs work, he has over 30 starts in his collegiate career. Pick 126 – Suntarine Perkins, LB, Ole Miss Perkins is incredibly light (220 lbs.) but incredibly athletic linebacker. His lack of mass likely drops him to Day Three, but he could be a versatile spark plug in rotation. Round 5 No picks Round 6 Pick 199 – Rocky Beers, TE, Oklahoma Beers made his way to Oklahoma by way of FIU then Colorado State. He’s really come into his own as a receiver this season, and he has the size to play inline tight end in the NFL. Round 7 Pick 229 – Robert Fitzgerald, S, Northwestern Fitzgerald doesn’t have the athleticism that many safeties in the class do, but his production has been impressive at Northwestern. He had over 100 tackles last season and already has three interceptions this year. Pick 237 – Will Henderson III, UTSA Henderson is an undersized but insanely explosive running back who could be an excellent complement to Chuba Hubbard who could provide a spark in the return game as well. What do you think, Panthers fans? Would you be “thankful” for this draft class? Sound off in the comments!

title: Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions – Keys to a Chicago victory
summary: Happy Thanksgiving! It’s shaping up to be a great weekend for watching football while eating and spending time with family or friends. Things got off t0 a good start last night, as the Green Bay Packers lost another game, taking a massive hit to their playoff chances. Now it’s up to the Chicago Bears to […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions runs with the ball against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving! It’s shaping up to be a great weekend for watching football while eating and spending time with family or friends. Things got off t0 a good start last night, as the Green Bay Packers lost another game, taking a massive hit to their playoff chances. Now it’s up to the Chicago Bears to take control of business against the Detroit Lions this afternoon. The clash of 8-2 teams looks to be a fantastic game and will give the winner control of the NFC North heading into December. In case you haven’t heard, Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams have yet to beat Dan Campbell and the Lions in their careers. What’s it going to take to change that? Sam: Ben Johnson surely wants to avenge the two losses to his coaching mentor from a season ago. The Bears NEED to win to stay in the thick of the division. This game is, perhaps too simply, a game in the trenches. Whichever defensive line and offensive line wins is going to win the game. Stop Jahmyr Gibbs and pressure Goff, establish the run with Swift and Monangai. “Easy” as that. Jacob: The Bears need to hold up in pass protection to allow the intermediate-to-deep passes — a staple of their passing attack — time to develop. Not having to face Aidan Hutchinson should make things easier, but the Lions could take on a blitz-heavy approach to dial up the pressure against Caleb Williams. A lot of the Bears’ struggles on offense have come from the trenches, and that will need to be fixed in a critical game within the NFC North. Josh: Chicago needs to be more physical. That doesn’t just mean they need to impose their will at the line of scrimmage, but that is definitely true. They also need to make the hard tackles and they need to extend plays after contact. Dan Campbell is going to want to take Ben’s lunch money, and Chicago needs to say enough is enough and just win out of pure cussedness. TJ: The Bears need to maintain composure in all aspects of the game in order to leave with their first division win of the year. They can’t succumb to penalties, turnovers, or other dumb mistakes. On defense, stay disciplined and limit the damage done by St. Brown and Gibbs. On offense, lean on the ground game and hopefully keep time of possession in Chicago’s favor. DGooch: The key to the game, as usual, starts with the run game. The Bears need to establish the run with Guy and Swift, something they struggled to do with the Saints this past Sunday, and really for the last five weeks (3 yards per carry average). I think they should try out Jones over Bradbury, who has been pretty awful, but I doubt the Bears go that route on a short week. So – run to the Wright (see what I did there) and Jackson side–the Bears dominant run direction and where the Lions will be missing Hutch. The Lions secondary has Branch and Joseph back, but it is still their primary weakness, a weakness Caleb needs to exploit while protecting the ball. On defense, I think Allen needs to increase his blitz calls – yes he can get pressure without it now that Big Jeff is in the middle – but making Goff uncomfortable in the pocket is, well, key. And run blitzing Gibbs may limit his production. Mongo Peanut: OL play needs to be better, especially on the interior. The linchpin to this team’s success in 2025 was how good we were there. Obviously, losing a center like Dalman has been hard to replace, but the Bears are averaging under 4 yards per carry since Week 5; much of that is due to the decline in play on the interior. Caleb’s pressure rate has also spiked, largely in part due to the same issue. Fix that, and a lot of the nagging offensive annoyances go away. On defense, we just need to keep doing what we’ve been doing up front, pressure the QB, and make his life as difficult as possible. Jeffery Simmons allows a bit more leeway with how to attack Goff, which equalizes things a bit when it comes to their WRs and their ability to generate YAC. JB: Roast lion – You want to make sure that you pre-heat the oven first thing in the morning so that you’re ready to go out of the gate. No slow starts. Next, use short to intermediate cuts, letting the knife Rome through the length of the meat to unBurden its defenses. Next, take your Monangai mallet and pound the lion chunks with Swift movements until flattened and tenderized. Finally, place the lion into the oven at a Sweat-inducing 550 degrees to broil, making sure to turnover at least twice. On the stovetop, bring your gravy to a Simm ons er and top your lion for a satisfying win on Thanksgiving that the whole family will love. ECD: Offense – Get ready for a shootout and don’t let off the gas until the clock reaches 00:00. The Bears’ supporting cast on offense matches up fairly well against a Lions defense that no longer has Aiden Hutchinson. Just keep DT Alim McNeill in check as much as possible. Defense – Take the ball away any time the opportunity presents itself. You’re not going to win a foot race against Jahmyr Gibbs, and tackling has to be sure-handed with Amon-Ra St. Brown looming large. Special Teams – Do not give standout ace Trevor Nowaske any chances to make plays on the ball. Also be on alert for fake punts or field goals as they have a crafty SPC in Dave Fipp. What are your keys to the game? Drop ‘em in the comments and let us know your prediction, too.

title: 10 Things to be Thankful for with your Chicago Bears
summary: The Bears are kicking off against the Detroit Lions in a few hours, but before they do, let’s take a minute to just appreciate what the Chicago Bears have done this year and last year. Things are the best they’ve been for the beloved in a very long time, so let’s take a minute and […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears runs off the field after his team's win against the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears are kicking off against the Detroit Lions in a few hours, but before they do, let’s take a minute to just appreciate what the Chicago Bears have done this year and last year. Things are the best they’ve been for the beloved in a very long time, so let’s take a minute and be thankful for 10 things about this Chicago Bears team. 10. The Stanky Leg We could say to be thankful for “Good, Better, Best” but the Stanky Leg seems to have been an addition that everybody can’t get enough of this year. Ben loves it, and the players love that Ben’s into it. He embraces that nerd part of himself, and it just makes it a perfect addition to a victorious locker room. 9. George McCaskey You might find it wild to have George on here, who has been the target of constant criticism, including from myself, but while George has plenty of flaws, I’m not going to lie, in an environment of billionaires doing awful things to regular folks and NFL teams signing morally questionable people, George McCaskey remains a good person who runs the Bears with a level of class. It’s tough to get behind the 1% of the 1%, but George is one of the good ones. 8. Jeffery Simmons How can Big Jeff not be on here? He has completely transformed the defense from a liability to an excellent group. He’s made this team’s defense a national talking point about just how good he is, and as the Bears continue to be in the national conversation, Simmons is going to make a strong push for Defensive Player of the Year. 7. The 59-Point Burger How great was it that this is how the season started? The offense hasn’t really shown the same level of explosiveness, but this was a great way to get the season on the tracks, get the conversation started around the Bears, and just know that in Ben’s back pocket, when all things are clicking, this is what this offense is capable of. 6. Dennis Allen Dennis Allen did a lot of great things with smoke and mirrors when he didn’t have the personnel he needed earlier. He still had a defense that wasn’t the most talented in the league playing well. Now he got Jeff Simmons added into his sandbox to play with, and Allen’s defense has been elevated several notches. He’s been an outstanding DC in Chicago the last two years. 5. Jeffery Simmons Something so nice, we should be thankful for it twice. 4. Ryan Poles Wait a minute, Bill Zimmerman is putting Ryan Poles on a thankful list? Well, when you go out and do something bold like acquiring Jeffery Simmons, you need to be recognized. Plus, moves like Devin Bush are starting to reap rewards, and the Bears have some rookies contributing as well. Poles could win executive of the year this year. 3. Caleb Williams The Bears have a franchise quarterback. They haven’t really had one since Sid Luckman. Some of you might say Jim McMahon, others might say Jay Cutler, but they didn’t play enough, produce enough, or be consistent enough to be a true franchise QB. Caleb is all that. 2. Ben Johnson Great QBs don’t always grow into their potential unless they have the right coach. Ben Johnson is the right coach. Remember, the Bears interviewed Mike McCarthy, and he was going to be strongly considered if Ben Johnson went elsewhere. After hearing what’s going on in Pittsburgh, it would have been the same old Bears, even with Caleb Williams. Caleb and Ben are the pair. They are “it.” It’s awesome that it’s in Chicago. 1. The 2026 Chicago Bears I can single out Big Jeff, Caleb, Ben, and the rest of them, but let’s just be thankful for this team. The Chicago Bears are part of the national conversation. This team is dominating football games. I know some Bears fans want to see 31-13, but the fact is that the Bears keep taking leads early in games and never giving them up. This is a fun team to watch. It’s a dominant team to watch, and this team represents the best chance the Bears have had to win a Super Bowl in 40 years. Be thankful, Bears fans. The Chicago Bears are elevating all our lives this fall and winter. Now let’s watch them go out there and beat the Lions.

title: Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions: Picks and Predictions
summary: On Thanksgiving at Ford Field, the 8-2 Bears travel to face the 8-2 Lions in a battle for sole possession of first place in the NFC North. It doesn’t get any better than this, folks. Chicago arrives on a five-game winning streak behind Caleb Williams and a physical rushing attack that has slowed somewhat in […]
full_text: Nov 28, 2024; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) passes the ball against the Detroit Lions during the first half at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con On Thanksgiving at Ford Field, the 8-2 Bears travel to face the 8-2 Lions in a battle for sole possession of first place in the NFC North. It doesn’t get any better than this, folks. Chicago arrives on a five-game winning streak behind Caleb Williams and a physical rushing attack that has slowed somewhat in the last few weeks with the loss of Cole Kmet, while Detroit is rolling on a six-game run with Jared Goff and one of the league’s most explosive offenses. On defense, the Bears are as healthy as they have been all season, minus Kyler Gordon, and will feature Big Jeff Simmons for the first time against the Detroit offense. While the Lions defense has gotten back Branch and Joseph in their secondary, they have lost two Pro Bowl players in Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to season-ending injuries. Ben Johnson returns to his former home against Dan Campbell in a high-stakes divisional showdown that could shape the rest of the season. The questioning narrative that has emerged in Ben Johnson’s second season with the Bears points to his 2-6 record against the division. Can Ben and the Bears start to turn that storyline around on Thursday? What follows are our score pick, winner, and projected stat lines for this Thanksgiving classic. Thursday, November 26, 2026 , at Ford Field . Kickoff: 12:00 p.m. CT (1:00 p.m. ET) TV: CBS (Jim Nantz, J.J. Watt, Tracy Wolfson) Streaming: Paramount+ and NFL+ (local markets) Radio: ESPN Chicago (1000 AM / 100.3 FM HD2) with Jeff Joniak, Tom Thayer, and Jason McKie. WCG Picks and Predictions TJ : I do think the Bears are the better team, but Detroit has shown they are still electric on offense, and the last two outings make me nervous about Chicago’s ability to hang in a shootout if it comes to it. The Lions also appear to have Ben Johnson’s number through one year, and until the narrative changes, I’m going to give them a slight edge. 27-23 Detroit Gary Baugher Jr .: I feel like we’ve done enough on defense in 2026 to avoid getting boat raced by the elite talent the Lions have on offense, and I’m fully confident in our offense to keep pace against their defense. It might be a back and forth affair that comes down to the last possession but I’ll take the Bears by a field goal, 24-21. Josh : Detroit is a terrible matchup for Chicago. Their offense can stress all of the defense’s weaknesses, their defense can exploit the limitations of the OL, and Campbell seems to be able to win the chess match with Ben Johnson. Call it 27-23 Detroit, with a late rally falling short. Jacob Infante : I don’t think the Bears will get swept in this series like they did last year, but I personally think the Lions are playing better football right now. Chicago will get its lick back later in the season, but with this game being in Detroit and with the Bears undergoing some inconsistency on offense, I trust the Lions’ explosive offense a little bit more to get the job done, unfortunately. Lions 26, Bears 21 Sam : Detroit is playing great, while the Bears just haven’t looked themselves. I think they’ve been saving it all up for this. It’s going to be a showdown with points, defensive plays and more. I think Jahmyr Gibbs and Jared Goff edge the Bears and we endure 10 days of “Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams can’t beat the NFC North.” Detroit 31, Chicago 28 JB : Bears 34, Detroit 20. I’m convinced the Bears spent a big chunk of the bye week prepping for this game, knowing they could handle New Orleans with a simple game plan. Offense is going to go off in the dome, defense is playing great, and the Bears haven’t trailed since Caleb has returned from injury. GOOCH : I think Ben has had this one circled on the calendar for a while. He wants the Detroit monkey off the proverbial back, and what better place to do it than in Detroit on Thanksgiving. I personally buy into the theory that the Bears went vanilla against the Saints in order to keep most of the game plan under the lid for the Detroit game. I expect a revived Bears rushing attack as both Swift and Monangai establish the run game with the Guy posting a TD and over 100 yards on the ground. This grinding approach wins the Bears the time of possession (like most games this season) and keeps the explosive Detroit offense off the field. Caleb torches the Detroit secondary for 3 TD passes and over 300 yards on the fly, as Loveland and Odunze score TDs and Burden has over 100 yards recieving yards. On defense Big Jeff, Booker, and Jennings notch sacks on Goff, who is under pressure all day. The Lions settle for three field goals rather than touchdowns. The Bears control Gibbs for the most part, although he does rush for over 100 yards and a TD. Bears pick off Goff twice. Final Score: Bears 34, Detroit 23. But what do you think the final score will be? What do you predict will happen in the game? Tell us in the comments below!

title: Bengals News: Happy Thanksgiving
summary: The NFL has a full slate of games for you and yours this Thanksgiving. We here at Cincy Jungle would also like to extend a Happy Thanksgiving from all of us! You get to watch two games that have huge playoff implications between two of the top teams in their respective conferences. Then you get […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 27: Evan McPherson #2 of the Cincinnati Bengals carries a plate of turkey after an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 27, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has a full slate of games for you and yours this Thanksgiving. We here at Cincy Jungle would also like to extend a Happy Thanksgiving from all of us! You get to watch two games that have huge playoff implications between two of the top teams in their respective conferences. Then you get to eat dinner while the Dallas Cowboys host the Philadelphia Eagles in-between. The day starts off with the Detroit Lions hosting the Chicago Bears. Both teams are 8-2 just ahead of the Minnesota Vikings at 7-3. The NFC North probably will have the No. 2 seed in the conference and then two Wild Card teams. This could very well be a game that decides exactly where these teams fall in that equation. The one AFC teams will care about is the 9-1 Buffalo Bills hosting the 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs. The Chiefs are currently behind the 8-2 Denver Broncos for the AFC West, so they need to keep pace to try and get a home game or two in the playoffs. The Bills have had a bit of a cakewalk the past few weeks. It started with them playing the Baltimore Ravens the game they last two quarterbacks to injury, then a Carson Wentz led Vikings team, then the New York Jets and the Miami Dolphins, who were starting Kyle McCord. They have beaten some good teams in close games. This should be another very close game. Lets talk about all of these games down in the comments while we are either waiting to eat or digesting before an inevitable nap. Bengals News Quick Hits | Joe Burrow Keeps Throwing; D.J. Turner II’s Short Memory If there is one thing you do not have to worry about, it is the fact this offense is still going to throw the ball. If anything, it is good to get this kind of game out of the way where the defense seemed to do it a bit better than others had previously. Maybe it was just personnel, but you can bet these coaches and Burrow have reviewed that tape to find some things. Bengals Coaches Taylor, Golden Weigh In on Why Shemar Stewart Can’t See the Field At some point the excuses do not hold up. The defensive line may have felt good after a first half where they did not see the field a ton, but they were out there significantly more in the second half. It didn’t take a proffesional scout to see those linemen were gassed towards the end of the game. The team either needs to start rotating these guys in a bit more for crucial times like that or go and try and find someone they feel comfortable rotating in more. Three former Bengals advance in Pro Football Hall of Fame selection process We have talked at length about Ken Anderson and Willie Anderson being Hall of Fame caliber players. The only knock on them is they played for the Bengals most of their career. Defensive tackle Geno Atkins deserves it just as much, though. He helped revolutionize the position. He is the reason a guy like Aaron Donald was such a high pick. He showed undersized defensive tackles can wreak havoc on opposing offensive lines. His only problem is he did it all so quietly, which was more or less his trademark. NFL News Steelers cut Rodgers after QB rips McCarthy in scorched-earth interview This has been so much fun to watch as a fan of an opposing AFC North team. The Pittsburgh Steelers made their bed a long time ago. They opted for Mike McCarthy, and they banked on Aaron Rodgers deciding to play another season. Rodgers has proven he is not above this kind of thing, and now they have likely destroyed the locker room of a 6-4 team that two weeks ago was thinking they could sweep the Bengals and keep control of the AFC North. Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes renew rivalry as Bills host Chiefs The Bengals will play the Chiefs here in a few weeks, but this is a good opportunity to watch two teams the Bengals would likely have to get through in the postseason if they have any hopes of making it back to the Super Bowl. NFL QB rankings, Week 12: Brock Purdy retakes throne; Jayden Daniels hits season high Burrow drops to No. 2, which feels favorable considering his outing on Monday Night Football. He could easily bounceback, and he could probably retake the top spot if Brock Purdy is unable to go due to his ankle injury. Join the conversation! title: Why is Shemar Stewart not playing? Al Golden weighs in
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have a defensive-end problem. No, not with Boye Mafe—he’s been an incredible free-agent signing for the Bengals and is a huge part of why the Bengals are 7-3 at this point in the season. The problem is their last first-round pick, Shemar Stewart, isn’t getting on the field, and Al Golden could […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have a defensive-end problem. No, not with Boye Mafe—he’s been an incredible free-agent signing for the Bengals and is a huge part of why the Bengals are 7-3 at this point in the season. The problem is their last first-round pick, Shemar Stewart, isn’t getting on the field, and Al Golden could very much use the help after rookie Cashius Howell was placed on IR. When asked about it on Wednesday, the Bengals’ defensive coordinator took some responsibility for Stewart’s inability to get playing time. “This is a long stretch we have in front of us,” he said, per ESPN’s Ben Baby . “And whatever I have to do to help him and get him into the game and impact the game, I am committed to doing that. So I have to do a better job with that.” Reading Golden’s comments makes me think Stewart is no closer to getting on the field than Howell is at the moment. The Bengals are in great position for the division, even with the loss to the Commanders. They lost ground when it comes to the race for the No. 1 overall seed and homefield advantage in the AFC, though. They still have the head-to-head loss to the Jaguars, while the Bills, Chiefs, and Broncos all have better records. They can’t afford a lapse on the field, especially in a close game, which is why Stewart didn’t play a single snap against the Commanders on Monday night. If the Bengals are able to get out to a big lead where they can coast against the Saints, maybe we’ll see him. At this point, though, the Bengals might as well sign a free agent to help until Howell can possibly return, because Golden’s statement didn’t exactly inspire confidence in the No. 17 overall selection of the 2025 NFL Draft.
