full_text: All three AFC North teams that played this week lost by a field goal or less, while Cleveland had its bye. Pittsburgh fell 19-16 to Philadelphia, and Baltimore dropped its sixth straight in a 35-33 loss to Carolina. Division-leading Cincinnati saw its five-game winning streak come to an end Monday night when Washington kicked a field goal as time expired to beat the Bengals 22-20. Let’s take a look at the week that was in the North. Bengals collaps e in Washington Washington took over at its own 28-yard line with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Jayden Daniels needed only two completions to rookie Antonio Williams to get the Commanders to the Cincinnati 8. Daniels spiked the ball with five seconds remaining, and Drew Stevens hit the game-winning 26-yard field goal as time expired. The Bengals had taken a 20-19 lead on Evan McPherson’s 56-yard field goal. Joe Burrow’s 32-yard completion to Mike Gesicki put Cincinnati in range after Stevens had kicked a 41-yarder to put Washington ahead with 2:26 left. The Commanders sacked Burrow to push the Bengals back, leaving McPherson to make the long kick. Cincinnati had led 10-0 after Burrow found Tee Higgins for a 31-yard touchdown, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt scored from a yard out with 12 seconds left in the first half. A brief stadium lighting outage interrupted Washington’s opening drive of the third quarter, and Stevens tied the game at 10 when play resumed. Burrow answered with a 4-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young, but the Bengals managed only McPherson’s field goal the rest of the way. Burrow finished with 300 passing yards and two touchdowns, but Washington limited Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase to seven catches for 74 yards combined. The Bengals had scored at least 31 points in each of their five straight wins before the Commanders held them to 20. Cincinnati’s defense was on fire in the first half, with Boye Mafe going off for a career-high three sacks and Dexter Lawrence II adding a tackle for loss. But the second half told a different story as the Commanders scored on every single possession to drop the Bengals to 7-3. Now, the Bengals will look to rebound in Week 12 when they host the 3-7 Saints. Steelers drop second straight The Pittsburgh Steelers lost their second straight game Sunday, falling to a Philadelphia Eagles team that had dropped seven in a row. Saquon Barkley broke loose for a 38-yard touchdown run as the Eagles built a 13-0 first-quarter lead. Jake Elliott kicked four field goals, including second-half tries from 53 and 55 yards, to put Philadelphia ahead 19-9. Pittsburgh had a chance to close the gap when Carson Bruener recovered a fumble on the opening kickoff of the second half and returned it to the Philadelphia 24-yard line, but the Steelers settled for one of Chris Boswell’s three field goals. Aaron Rodgers completed 17 of 20 passes in the first half for just 95 yards and finished with 227. Philadelphia sacked him five times and held Pittsburgh to 73 rushing yards. Rodgers found Max Hurleman for a 20-yard touchdown with 1:21 left to cut the deficit to three. But Joe Milton connected with DeVonta Smith for seven yards on third-and-6 with 1:09 remaining, giving the Eagles the first down they needed to run out the clock. Pittsburgh fell to 6-4 and has now lost 12 straight road games against the Eagles, a drought that dates to its last win in Philadelphia in 1965. Now, the Steelers are moving on from Rodgers and going to Mason Rudolph for the remainder of the season . They’ll look to start a winning streak when they host the 8-2 Broncos in the NFL’s Black Friday game. Ravens fall in Carolina Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 remaining, and the Carolina Panthers held on to hand the Ravens their sixth straight loss. Fitzgerald’s kick produced the seventh lead change of the game, but Carolina didn’t seal the victory until Will Lee III deflected Jacoby Brissett’s deep pass into the hands of Tyrel Dodson with 33 seconds left. Lee also forced two fumbles, including one that went out the back of the end zone for a touchback as Justice Hill neared the goal line. Baltimore piled up 338 yards in the first half and got an 86-yard kickoff return for a touchdown from Dontez Walker. Brissett finished with 276 passing yards, including a 52-yard touchdown to Rashod Bateman on a trick play. Derrick Henry ran for 94 yards on 13 carries and put the Ravens ahead 33-32 on a 15-yard touchdown run with 6:32 left. He later left to be evaluated for a concussion and did not return. Bryce Young threw for 254 yards and two touchdowns, while Chuba Hubbard carried 27 times for 120 yards and two scores. Hubbard joined Christian McCaffrey as the only Panthers to reach 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns through the first 10 games of a season. Carolina improved to 5-5 and opened a two-game lead in the NFC South, while Baltimore fell to 4-7. The Ravens will look to keep their very slim playoff hopes alive this week when they face the 4-6 Texans in Houston. AFC North Standings for Week 12

title: 2027 Browns mock draft: Selecting a potential turkey at quarterback
summary: The Cleveland Browns have surprisingly played themselves into the AFC playoff race, sitting one game behind the Cincinnati Bengals for first in the AFC North. Playing meaningful games rather than focusing on draft position is a refreshing change of pace for the franchise. But it does not erase the reality that the Browns will be […]
full_text: (Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have surprisingly played themselves into the AFC playoff race, sitting one game behind the Cincinnati Bengals for first in the AFC North. Playing meaningful games rather than focusing on draft position is a refreshing change of pace for the franchise. But it does not erase the reality that the Browns will be rebuilding the quarterback room in 2027. Just what that remodeling will look like is still in the “to be determined” file, as the Browns could: Run it back with the current group (not at all likely). Decide it is time to unleash Shedeur Sanders as the starter on an unsuspecting NFL (literally not happening). Some mix of the always popular veteran “bridge quarterback” to pair with a rookie selected in the 2027 NFL Draft. (Quite possible, even if that bridge is current starter Deshaun Watson, which no one would have seen coming a few months ago). That final bullet point brings us to a mock draft from Nate Tice at Yahoo Sports , which, unfortunately, has the Browns embracing the Thanksgiving spirit by selecting a potential turkey at the quarterback position. Tice projects the Browns to be selecting at No. 17 (with the selection they received from the Los Angeles Rams as part of the Myles Garrett trade) and No. 20 (with their own pick). LaNorris Sellers had a man wide open… You don’t get those opportunities against Georgia often pic.twitter.com/etwPrINaGj — No Context SEC (@NoContextSEC) November 22, 2026 With that first selection, Tice embraces the “Browns is the Browns” mantra by selecting South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers : The Browns throw another dart at the quarterback position. And boy, what a chance of hitting the bull’s-eye this would be. Sellers is young (important to the Browns process) and has some of the loudest tools you’ll ever see at the position. His play has felt calmer and more decisive over the past month, but he will need more time, especially in a more conducive situation than the one he’s been in the past few years. Landing in Cleveland with the Browns’ exciting young group of pass catchers isn’t the worst place to settle, especially with head coach Todd Monken, who has gotten the most out of his quarterbacks at multiple stops. Sellers is one of the most divisive college quarterbacks, which is saying a lot given the expected draft class. While athletic, he has only completed 63.1 percent of his career passes, while most top quarterbacks surpass 70 percent. He tosses interceptions (23), which are not really balanced out by just 50 touchdown passes. Sellers is a quarterback who will have big games, like his four-touchdown performance this season against Florida – but offset that with clunkers, like completing 56 percent of his passes against Tennessee or throwing for just 87 yards against Georgia. The Browns have searched so long for a quarterback, and made a mess of it far too often, that it is hard to see how selecting a player who is going to need a year (or likely more) to develop, with no guarantee of success. Three picks later, Tice adds some depth to the defense with the selection of Notre Dame defensive end Boubacar Traore : I peeked at another offensive lineman here, despite this year’s Spencer Fano selection, and hit on the Austin Barber pick. Funnily enough, I have compared Traore to Jared Verse (but might be leaning more toward a DeMarcus Lawrence comparison). Either way, those are two strong defenders who can push the pocket, and that’s exactly what Traore brings to the table. He would be another strong edge defender to add to the Browns’ front. The Browns can always use help on defense, and in 32 career games, Traore has 88 tackles, 15.5 sacks, and 26.5 tackles for loss. His draft stock has been rising this season, and if the Irish make a run through the college football playoffs, Traore will have plenty of opportunities to showcase his talent against tougher competition than the likes of Rice, Navy, and Purdue. So there you have it. The Browns “throw another dart” at the quarterback position and add some help for the defensive line with a player who might be Jared Verse 2.0. What do you say, Browns fans? title: AFC North’s changing of the guard from Steelers/Ravens to Bengals/Browns happening fast
summary: For years- really, decades- the AFC North has seen the Cleveland Browns in the basement, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers running the show. The Cincinnati Bengals have had windows of time when they join the top two, but they haven’t had the kind of consistency that the others have. The Browns have been […]
full_text: For years- really, decades- the AFC North has seen the Cleveland Browns in the basement, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers running the show. The Cincinnati Bengals have had windows of time when they join the top two, but they haven’t had the kind of consistency that the others have. The Browns have been consistently bad, with just a couple of playoff appearances and no AFC North titles . Things have started to change during the 2026 NFL season, with Cincinnati and Cleveland at the top of the division, even if Pittsburgh had the same 6-4 record as the second-place team. Baltimore has fallen off without Lamar Jackson . Now, with the news of the Steelers benching Aaron Rodgers late on Tuesday night, after he practiced as the team’s starter the first two days of the week, the bloom seems to be off in Mike McCarthy’s first year. As our Producer at Behind the Steel Curtain said, Pittsburgh needs to reset everything in order to rebuild: It’s easy to say now, but they should have gotten rid of all the Tomlin guys. They were always going to have that “well Mike T wouldn’t have done this” about them. It’s a spoiled group. https://t.co/Q8MtftMykE — Jarrett Bailey (@JBaileyNFL) November 25, 2026 The Ravens may be looking at a similar turnover with Jackson’s contract at a point where the team either needs to try to extend him (something they’ve tried and failed to do), trade him, or release him this offseason. Given Jackson’s price tag, injury history, and limited playoff success, Baltimore’s future may not include their MVP-winning quarterback. There are many around Baltimore and Pittsburgh’s fanbases who are hoping that Jesse Minter and McCarthy are one-and-done coaches, whereas Cincinnati’s Zac Taylor was the one holdover in the division, and Todd Monken has had a positive start to his tenure in Cleveland. With the Bengals having stability at quarterback, an offensive line coming together well, great weapons on offense, and a defense coming together well, Cincinnati might be the cream of the crop in the AFC North for a few seasons. The Browns could be close behind, with a young, exciting roster of talented players all over the roster, extra draft picks over the next couple of years, and a coach who is making everything work ahead of schedule. By the time the next decade starts, we could be looking back at the 2026 NFL season as the time that the changing of the guard in the AFC North was fast-tracked, with the State of Ohio on top for a number of years. When you look at the AFC North, do you think the Bengals and Browns will takeover in the same way the Ravens and Steelers have for so many years? title: Why the Cowboys should beat the Eagles, and why they could fail
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are after history on Thanksgiving this year, looking to beat the Philadelphia Eagles on this holiday for the first time in franchise history. The Cowboys have beaten the New York Giants three times on Thanksgiving, and the Washington Commanders nine times, and proven they can beat all of these division rivals under […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are after history on Thanksgiving this year, looking to beat the Philadelphia Eagles on this holiday for the first time in franchise history. The Cowboys have beaten the New York Giants three times on Thanksgiving, and the Washington Commanders nine times, and proven they can beat all of these division rivals under Brian Schottenheimer, but need a Turkey Day win over the birds to secure their first winning streak of this 2026 season. The Eagles are the smallest sample size of division opponents on Thanksgiving, but the Cowboys are 0-2 against them. As has been a theme in this rivalry, this Thursday game will be yet another new quarterback matchup. Dak Prescott has been the mainstay in the last three meetings, with two of them coming against Jalen Hurts. The week seven meeting this year was Prescott against Tanner McKee though, and now on Thanksgiving it will be a red-hot Prescott against a passer many Cowboys fans thought would actually be Prescott’s backup this season – Joe Milton. Milton has started the last two games for the Eagles, and got them back in the win column this past Sunday off their bye, at home, against the Pittsburgh Steelers. It was an ugly win, but any type of win would do for Philly coming into that in-state battle on a seven-game losing streak. Now, the Eagles will be looking to go from beating Mike McCarthy in Week 11 to beating the coach that replaced McCarthy in Dallas in the same week. The Cowboys will be looking to keep the NFC East race alive, and getting a fifth straight Thanksgiving win would go a long way in doing just that. Let’s get to our weekly scenarios on how this game could play out. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Philadelphia Eagles if… …they stay hot in the red zone. The Cowboys are 11-12 in the red zone scoring touchdowns over their last three games, and a perfect 9-9 in the last two games – both 40+ point outbursts at home. You have to go all the way back to week six to find the last nine times the Eagles have reached the red zone, covering five games where they are 1-4. The Eagles have not scored more than 20 points since they did so against the Cowboys on that Monday night win for Dallas, and no more than those 21 points since week three when Hurts was still starting. They have only been to the red zone once in each of their last two games. They went 0-1 against the Steelers, but held them to 0-2 to continue to frustrate Pittsburgh when playing in Philadelphia and get a win. The Steelers offensive performance was so bad they’ve decided to bench Aaron Rodgers for their next game on Black Friday, in case there was any wonder about if it was more good Eagles defense or bad Steelers offense in Week 11. Coming off a game where the Cowboys scored literally every time they were trying to do so offensively, the bar is low to be able to use their offense to keep the pressure on against another opponent with a losing record. It was the passing game that was the catalyst to achieve this against the Tennessee Titans, but back in week seven it was more of the run game that helped the Cowboys beat the Eagles with McKee on the road. The Titans are also dead last in time of possession differential by a healthy margin right now, but in second to last is the next opponent for the Cowboys with these Eagles. A good blend of the run game and high percentage pass game that leads to drives ending in seven points will keep the Cowboys best players on the field deciding this game, and keep the defense playing in the positions they need to be in, rushing the passer against an Eagles offensive line that’s a shell of its former self. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Philadelphia Eagles if… …they can’t limit explosive plays. Everything we’ve covered about the Eagles so far hardly makes them look like a potent offense that’s going to create explosive plays. In a game where that may be their only chance to win though, getting such plays against the Cowboys defense is still not out of the realm of possibility. After all, of all the games they’ve played without Hurts, their best point total was against the Cowboys. They also went a perfect 3-3 in the red zone that night, and got a 29-yard run from Saquon Barkley. Barkley’s longest run in the two games immediately following playing the Cowboys was just five yards. Barkley did get back in the big play column against the Steelers with a 38-yard touchdown. Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert also had receptions of 29 and 38 yards. The Eagles missed even more big play opportunities to Devonta Smith downfield, but when the game came down to converting a 3rd-and-7 to run out the clock, they went empty out of the shotgun and trusted Milton to hit Smith right at the sticks to win the Steelers game. The Cowboys defense does not have nearly a big enough sample size under Mike Pettine yet to know what their potential is with this change of play-caller. The thought for now is that potentially it is at least sound enough to make big time performances by their own offense stand up, something they simply weren’t doing under Christian Parker. However, with both coaches on the headset, putting a cap on giving up huge backbreaking plays has not been solved just yet. Joe Milton will know the Cowboys defensive personnel well, is coming off a win, and has these home run threats in Smith and Barkley. If the Cowboys can’t keep at top on their defense against Smith getting downfield for “bazooka Joe” throws, or contain Barkley on the ground, the Eagles could pull off an upset that would send Dallas into the final month of the regular season still without back-t0-back wins.

title: 5 things to watch when the Cowboys host the Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are in search of their first winning streak of the season and desperately trying to stay alive in the NFC East hunt. On the menu this Thanksgiving are the three-win Philadelphia Eagles, who are riddled with injuries and already peeking ahead into the future. Struggling or not, the Eagles just snapped a […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are in search of their first winning streak of the season and desperately trying to stay alive in the NFC East hunt. On the menu this Thanksgiving are the three-win Philadelphia Eagles, who are riddled with injuries and already peeking ahead into the future. Struggling or not, the Eagles just snapped a seven-game losing streak on Sunday, winning their in-state battle against the Steelers, showing that these birds aren’t completely cooked just yet. For the Cowboys, collecting more wins against weaker opponents is absolutely paramount as soon as the schedule turns and it gets brutal in a hurry. Nothing will ruin a holiday weekend faster than letting a limping rival deliver a crushing blow to their playoff chances. That absolutely cannot happen. Here are five things to watch when the Cowboys host the Eagles on Thursday. 1. Pass the gravy The Cowboys offense is riding hot right now, putting up at least 40 points in each of the last two games. The passing attack has been particularly strong, with Dak Prescott carving up defenses for nine touchdown passes in that span. Meanwhile, the Eagles have major issues in the secondary, first benching Riq Woolen and now watching top corner Quinyon Mitchell deal with a hamstring injury. That vulnerability should open up a buffet of good eats with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at the front of the line. With the passing offense rolling, the Cowboys shouldn’t get complacent or take their foot off the gas. Keep feeding the playmakers until they have no more room to put it. 2. No leftovers for Milton Joe Milton III spent last year with the Cowboys, never started a game, and threw just 24 total passes before being released at roster cuts this year before being brought back to the practice squad. Now he is with the Eagles, making his third career start for them in a return trip to AT&T Stadium. Things haven’t gone smoothly for him so far, as he has yet to throw a touchdown pass and has been sacked 10 times over the past two games. Even so, he played well enough to help the Eagles beat the Steelers on Sunday. Playing against a backup quarterback cannot be taken for granted when it comes to this Cowboys defense, which already got shocked by rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels in Week 5 and Gardner Minshew in Week 8. Dallas cannot afford to serve up another holiday charity case to a guy elevated from the kids’ table. 3. Hungry pass rushers Speaking of Milton getting sacked an average of five times per game, five sacks happens to be the exact number the Cowboys defense has racked up in each of their last three home games. The defensive line is on a bit of a heater right now, thanks to what we hope is the influence of new defensive play-caller Mike Pettine. Keeping that streak alive on Thanksgiving would be fantastic. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has been feasting in the backfield lately, while lesser-known players like James Houston and Elijah Garcia are very hungry and have been bringing an appetite for destruction as of late. Against a young quarterback trying to find his footing and an offensive line struggling to keep him upright, expect Milton to have his hands full trying to stay off the turf. 4. Don’t let Saquon get seconds If there is a scenario where the Eagles pull off the upset, it starts with a running game barrage that exposes a shaky Cowboys run defense. Stopping the run remains a glaring weakness for this team, as they have been hit hard on the ground a few times this season. Philadelphia isn’t the rushing juggernaut it has been in past years, and Saquon Barkley is only averaging 46 yards per game, but that doesn’t mean he isn’t capable of breaking out. If the Eagles find a rhythm on the ground, chew up the clock, and shorten the game, they can keep the Cowboys offense chilling on the sideline and open the door for an unpleasant ending. 5. No holiday truce There is no love lost between these two franchises, and even a festive holiday won’t rekindle any tenderness. Older fans still remember the infamous 1989 Bounty Bowl, when Cowboys players were suspiciously victims of late hits all afternoon. While nobody is expecting things to go quite that far off the rails, Thursday contains all the ingredients for plenty of drama. With edgy temperaments like Jalen Carter and George Pickens, and pesky personalities like Cooper DeJean and Brevyn Spann-Ford running around, it wouldn’t take much to spark a fire. It would actually be surprising if this game didn’t feature its share of personal fouls or taunting penalties as these bitter rivals go after each other. Happy holidays!

full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Last week there was a big shakeup among the Dallas Cowboys coaching staff. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker wasn’t stripped of his title or fired, but he was stripped of his play-calling duties for the defense. Senior advisor Mike Pettine took over the play-calling, even though he’s only been with the team for a month or so. The Cowboys won their game 51-30 over the Tennessee Titans. We wanted to know how Pettine did in his first go-around calling the Cowboys defense. The fact that Tennessee scored 30 points had some wondering if the change made any difference. Others saw improvement in communication and other areas, even if it didn’t show up as much in the final score. We asked you to grade his performance, and 50% of respondents gave him a middle of the road ‘C’. The next biggest group of votes was 29% for a ‘D’ grade. Suffice it to say, most Cowboys fans came away pretty unimpressed, although a ‘C’ grade is probably as good of a grade as any defensive effort this season, so maybe there was improvement. On Thanksgiving, Pettine will get another shot against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys are 8.5-point favorites according to FanDuel. So what’s you take BTB? Was a ‘C’ grade meant as an improvement? How do you think he will do against the Eagles?

title: Cowboys vs Eagles: Writer predictions for Week 12
summary: Dallas gets its traditional Thanksgiving game with a chance to climb back to .500 and complete the clean sweep of Philadelphia this season. The Cowboys won the first meeting 38-21 and now enter at 5-6, while the Eagles are 3-7 after finally ending a seven-game losing streak against Pittsburgh. When Philadelphia has the ball Philadelphia’s […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Dallas gets its traditional Thanksgiving game with a chance to climb back to .500 and complete the clean sweep of Philadelphia this season. The Cowboys won the first meeting 38-21 and now enter at 5-6, while the Eagles are 3-7 after finally ending a seven-game losing streak against Pittsburgh. When Philadelphia has the ball Philadelphia’s best plan is to make this game about Saquon Barkley rather than Joe Milton. Milton completed only 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards against Pittsburgh, whereas Barkley produced 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. Dallas should crowd the line and make Philadelphia prove it can consistently throw the football with Milton. Dallas has produced five sacks in each of its last two games, with Quinnen Williams and James Houston both creating problems against Tennessee. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should go back to exactly what worked against Philadelphia last month. Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards as the Cowboys piled up 204 on the ground, and that balance gave Prescott clean opportunities to attack through play-action. The Eagles have struggled against the run for much of the season, allowing 1,208 yards through 10 games, so Brian Schottenheimer should make Philadelphia stop Williams before turning the game completely over to Prescott. Once Dallas throws it, there is every reason to be aggressive. Prescott is coming off 325 yards and four touchdown passes against Tennessee, while CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both topped 100 yards. Philadelphia did produce five sacks against Pittsburgh, so Dallas cannot become one-dimensional and allow Jonathan Greenard and the Eagles front to chase Prescott. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (6-5) The Cowboys need to get another win, especially after the first week of the season where all the NFC East teams won. And the three rivals all beat more impressive teams than the Titans. Both Dallas and Philadelphia need a win to keep playoff hopes alive. I’m nervous about this one, but I’ll take the Cowboys to win 34-30. Brandon Loree (8-3) You would think a Thanksgiving game vs a depleted Philadelphia Eagles squad would be a no pressure situation, but I believe this could be the game that’s makes or breaks Brian Schottenheimer’s tenure in Dallas. Why? Jerry Jones does not like to be embarrassed on national television and with the Thanksgiving game drawing a massive audience, all eyes will be on Dallas. If the Cowboys somehow lose this game, the rest of the season might be put on pilot mode until Schottenheimer will be let go. However, Dallas’ offense should give them the edge in this game and it might look similar to last week in a back and forth performance by both offenses. Give me the Cowboys win, 35-24. Dyllan Rivers (7-4) The Cowboys take care of business early, forcing Joe Milton into mistakes as he tries to keep pace with the high octane offense on the other side. We see a defensive touchdown this week as well as more fireworks from Dak Prescott and his receivers. Dallas wins 45-24 and we get to take a nice, relaxing turkey-induced nap after the game. Matt Holleran (6-5) In the Brian Schottenheimer era, just when you start to believe the Cowboys can build some momentum and go on a run they let you down. It’s no coincidence that Dallas hasn’t won back-to-back games under Schottenheimer in nearly a calendar year. Short weeks put more pressure on preparation,coaching, and execution, three things that have pained Dallas over the past two years. I sure hope I’m wrong, but I’ve seen this story before and this is the week Dallas plays a sloppy game and loses to an inferior opponent. Give me Philly, 30-24. Mike Poland (5-6) Everyone worried the Eagles beat the Steelers and thinking Philadelphia are on the rise, don’t worry about it. The Steelers haven’t beaten the Eagles in Philly since 1965. The last ten games at AT&T stadium between these two teams, Dallas has won eight, and the Cowboys have the advantage after winning earlier in the season in Lincoln Financial Field. Dallas wins 35-17.

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles: Matchups to watch in Week 12 on Thanksgiving
summary: The Dallas Cowboys got the better of the Philadelphia Eagles earlier this season with a 38-1 victory in Week 7 and are looking to repeat that success in this Thanksgiving day matchup, this time on their home field turf. Their confidence should be at an all-time high after last week’s win over the Tennessee Titans […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys got the better of the Philadelphia Eagles earlier this season with a 38-1 victory in Week 7 and are looking to repeat that success in this Thanksgiving day matchup, this time on their home field turf. Their confidence should be at an all-time high after last week’s win over the Tennessee Titans and that should help them get back to .500 on the season. To do that though, they’ll need to take advantage of certain matchups to sway the game in their favor. Cowboys WRs vs. Eagles secondary The Cowboys are currently ranked second in the league in passing yards per game (270.9) and have been absolutely lethal the past couple of weeks. Dak Prescott has thrown for over 300 yards and at least four touchdowns in each game over the two-week period, and both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens have each had 100+ receiving yard games during that time as well. Dallas’ lethal aerial attack should help lead them to victory in Week 12 against the Eagles secondary who are currently ranked 17 th in the league allowing 222.8 yards per game. Cowboys run defense vs. RB Saquon Barkley The Cowboys have struggled stopping the run all season and that hasn’t changed under Mike Petine’s play-calling so far. They recently allowed Tony Pollard to rush for 110 yards and 21 carries last week, but hopefully will be able to contain Saquon Barkley better in Week 12 on Thanksgiving. He’s been less than 100% the majority of the season and may continue to be so for the rest of the year. Despite not being at his best in their last meeting, he still managed to rush for 62 yards and a touchdown on seven carries. Limiting him could be key. DT Quinnen Williams vs. Eagles interior OL For all the problems the Cowboys defense has had this year, Quinnen Williams isn’t one of them. He’s playing at an All-Pro level and has been wreaking havoc as both a run and pass defender each and every week. We fully expect that to continue in Week 12 against the Eagles and will be paying close attention to him on a play-by-play basis. We would be at all surprised to see No. 92 sack his former teammate QB Joe Milton a couple of times this week or make several plays behind the line of scrimmage. What is your big matchup of the week for the Cowboys and Eagles?

title: Ultimate Fan: Running the ball and stopping the run will be key to success over Steelers
summary: Happy Thanksgiving, Ultimate Fans! What a weekend for football, complete with NFL drama and everything! A few short days ago we were salivating over the chance to sack Aaron Rodgers and then he went and sacked himself…making the Broncos’ game Friday more interesting to say the least. Or as our awesome UFGer noted, “more unpredictable!” […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Bo Nix #10 hands off to Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving, Ultimate Fans! What a weekend for football, complete with NFL drama and everything! A few short days ago we were salivating over the chance to sack Aaron Rodgers and then he went and sacked himself…making the Broncos’ game Friday more interesting to say the least. Or as our awesome UFGer noted, “more unpredictable!” Another huge thanks to this week’s contributor, Wrenchman1122, who’s been pulling for this team for a loooonnnnngggg time, and he’s ready for another Super Bowl run. (and since it’s Thanksgiving, let me just say a huge thanks to ALL of you — the contributors and the commenters — who come here every week to give and react to such excellent insights and fun commentary. I say it every year and I mean every time — I LOVE THIS SERIES MORE THAN ANY OTHER POST I WRITE!) But now let’s kick off this Thanksgiving football weekend with a bang! GO BRONCOS! Heading to the Steel City for #BlackFridayNFL 🍂 pic.twitter.com/WgVtzRESdt — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 26, 2026 Week 12: Broncos at Steelers MHR – Broncos are 8-2, coming off a win over the Raiders, sitting alone atop the AFC West and knocking on the door to the overall No. 1 seed in the AFC. How good is life for a Broncos fan right now? Wrenchman1122: It’s been a heck of a ride so far, especially the one-score games. Life is pretty darn good in Broncos Country right now! What I love most is that this team is winning in different ways. We have Nix who keeps growing, an offense with multiple weapons, and a defense that can make life miserable for anybody. Beating the Raiders is always sweet and with first place in the West all to ourselves and looking to catch the Bills? Even better! MHR – Big news on a short week – JK Dobbins suspended and Aaron Rodgers benched. While the Dobbins news may not impact the offense all that much, Rodgers’ decision has been…interesting. In general how do these two pieces of info impact the kind of game the Broncos should play on offense and defense? Likewise, with the short week and East Coast game, does this push Payton toward a simpler, run-heavy game plan? Wrenchman1122: I like our chances if we make them play our game. A different theory, this week – pass early to set up the run as Pittsburgh has a good run D and the secondary can be taken advantage of, especially on quick hits with Waddle in motion or Sutton bodying up the defender. And let’s keep using Engram and his speed, which was evident last week against the dreaded Raiders. The weather will play havoc with specific planning, and with Rogers being benched and ultimately released, I’d expect plenty of runs and quick throws to help Rudolph get settled. We need to stop the run…if we can stop the run, we have an excellent chance. The short week, East Coast game and weather may create a simpler game plan, but we have the advantage of a mid-season form Nix versus Rudolph who has only started a handful (19?) games. MHR – Jonah Coleman has seemed like “the guy” a few times this season and then he broke it open on Sunday. Granted, the Raiders have one of the worst run defenses in the league, but what are your thoughts on Hat Trick Coleman and making him the bell cow back? And have we seen the last of Dobbins in Denver? Wrenchman1122: I’m all in on Jonah Coleman. Sure, the Raiders weren’t exactly known for stopping the run, but you still have to go out there and do it. Three touchdowns, 111 yards rushing, and the way he ran with authority, vision, and determination tell me we’re watching something special develop. What impressed me most wasn’t just the numbers; it was how he took over when the game was on the line. That’s what you want to see from a running back. I believe Coleman has earned the opportunity to be the bell cow. Feed the hot hand! He’s physical, runs with a purpose, and seems to get stronger as the game goes on. He’s also giving this offense something it desperately needs: a dependable running game that takes pressure off Bo Nix and opens up the passing attack. As for Dobbins, I wouldn’t write him off just yet. He’s been a good player for Denver, but this is a business, and opportunities have to be earned. With the recent suspension and Coleman’s emergence, the situation has certainly changed. Here’s my bottom line – Broncos Country has been waiting for an offense that can run the ball, control the clock, and finish games physically. Coleman might be exactly the missing piece we’ve been looking for. Between Bo Nix, this defense, and a running game that’s starting to find its identity, I like what I’m seeing. (Love the Hat-Trick reference). Jonah Coleman has been named FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week for his performance in the Broncos' win. Coleman is the first rookie to take home the honor this season. pic.twitter.com/eJiPwFHp1d — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 25, 2026 MHR – The Broncos really do have a lot of offensive targets to use, and Bo Nix alluded to that after the Raiders game in talking about Evan Engram’s big day, noting that he, like many others on the team, “probably want to get the ball more.” Of all the receiving threats – Sutton, Waddle, Bryant, Engram, Mims… – who do you think are the best for this offense and is it possible to have too much of a good thing and still keep all of it? Wrenchman1122: I love this problem. When was the last time we could honestly say the Broncos had this many weapons on offense? Jaylen Waddle brings something Denver hasn’t had enough of: game-changing speed. He forces defenses to respect the deep ball and opens things up underneath for everyone else. I was impressed with Engram’s game last week. We finally were able to be reminded of what he can do. He’s a matchup nightmare for linebackers and safeties, and I want to see him become a bigger part of the weekly game plan. Defenses can’t take away everybody. Double Sutton, and Waddle can burn you. Take away the deep ball, and Engram can work the middle. Crowd the middle, and Bryant or Mims can make you pay. Add Jonah Coleman establishing a legitimate running game, and suddenly this offense becomes awfully difficult to defend. MHR – I thought the Raiders game was one of Nix’s best, even if the stat line wasn’t particularly impressive. What did you like, what should Nix and the offense build on, and what still needs work – particularly as we gear up for what could be a major showdown for the AFC with the Bills in a month? Wrenchman1122: I thought Bo showed real growth against the Raiders. What I liked most was his patience, decision-making, and willingness to take what the defense gave him rather than forcing plays. The connection with his receivers is continuing to develop, and the running game is finally giving this offense another dimension. That’s what we need to build on. What still needs work is consistency, especially on third downs, red-zone execution, and avoiding unnecessary turnovers. Against a team like Buffalo, you can’t afford to leave points on the field. I believe Bo is growing into the quarterback we hoped he would be, and I wouldn’t trade our guy for anybody. MHR – Matt Peart, not Alex Palczewski or Ben Powers, started the game at left guard, and Bo Nix got sacked just once. Payton indicated that “Powers is still important to what we’re doing” but is Peart the answer at left guard? Or was that a one-week patch? Wrenchman1122: I think Peart earned another look at left guard. The line played well against the Raiders, and keeping Bo upright has to be priority No.1. One game doesn’t make Peart the permanent answer, but I’d like to see what he can do with another opportunity. Powers remains an important piece. Not sure he’s 100% and Palczewski provides valuable depth.…

title: Davis Webb optimistic Jonah Coleman and Broncos’ rushing attack can have success versus Steelers
summary: Last Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman had a standout performance. Coleman’s 111 yards and three touchdowns earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors. There’s no doubt he was a key reason the Broncos earn their eighth victory of the season. As the regular season continues, Coleman’s […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos stands on the sidelines during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman had a standout performance. Coleman’s 111 yards and three touchdowns earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors. There’s no doubt he was a key reason the Broncos earn their eighth victory of the season. As the regular season continues, Coleman’s emergence will be essential for Denver’s offense to realize their potential. On Friday, they will face the Pittsburgh Steelers. While things appear dysfunctional based on the Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy saga, they certainly have one of the best defenses in the NFL when it comes to stopping opposing ground games. Yesterday after practice, Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb praised the rookie for his outing against the Raiders. Additionally, Webb talked about the importance of being able to establish the run against the Steelers. That’s certainly important every week, but with inclement weather in the forecast, it’ll be a must if Denver wants to escape Pittsburgh with a win. “Congrats to him. The weather on top of that, going back-to-back weeks would be awesome for a rookie to have good games. That’s a challenge to our skills blocking on the perimeter, our offensive line blocking the box and him doing back-to-back,” stated Webb. “I think he has a chance to do that. This is a very tough defense. I think they’re Top 5 in rushing against base, so our hands will be full. T.J. Watt and Cameron Heyward have been there forever, and they’re still rocking and rolling,” added Webb. The Steelers are certainly elite against the run. As Webb mentioned, the high-level play of Watt and Heyward are a big reason for that. As a group, Pittsburgh’s defense is giving up only 84 yards per contest, just over 3.6 yards per carry, and have only allowed six rushing touchdowns all season. What is even more impressive is they have been able to accomplish this without having to utilize a lot of extra defenders in the box. They rank in the bottom half of the NFL in the rate they bring up an extra defender to combat the run. Defensive Coordinator Patrick Graham has immense trust and confidence their main core up front can get the job done in the trenches. Friday’s matchup versus the Steelers will certainly be another big test for the Broncos’ offensive line and Coleman. It’s one thing to take care of business against the Raiders who have struggled all season long stopping the run. In many ways, being able to do that was highly expected. Whether or not Denver can rise to the occasion and establish a formidable rushing attack against one of the league’s best remains to be seen. Over the last four games, the Steelers have given up just 18 yards, 34 yards, 78 yards, and 98 yards on the ground. If the Broncos can establish the run, that will bolster their chances at earning their ninth victory of the season tremendously. It would also be a huge boost of confidence for them as the final stretch of the season comes up. Being able to run the ball late in the season was something Denver struggled at last year. Being able to buck that trend may be the difference in whether or not they can become Super Bowl contenders. Will Denver be able to get the job done on the ground in Pittsburgh? Tune in tomorrow and find out.

(Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos made a switch at running back on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders that ultimately paid massive dividends. full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions fans make their wat to Ford Field prior to a game between New Orleans Saints and Detroit Lions fr the opening weekend of the NFL season. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s a huge NFC North showdown to kick off the NFL’s Thanksgiving tripleheader on Thursday. The Detroit Lions are 8-2 and trying to win their third division title in four years. They’ve endured a fair share of injuries as of late, particularly on defense. Captains Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson are on injured reserve, while Detroit will also be missing defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard, defensive end DJ Wonnum, and safety Chuck Clark in this matchup. However, despite all of that, the Lions are winners of six straight. Their offense is hitting its stride, with the offensive line gelling and the run game explosive. Plus, Jared Goff is in the middle of yet another dominant year. But the Chicago Bears will be one of the toughest tests the Lions will see all season. They’re also 8-2 on the season and on a five-game winning streak of their own. The addition of Jeffery Simmons on defense has turned a good defense into a great one. And while there have been struggles in the run game, quarterback Caleb Williams has taken his game to another level. Who walks away with the W in this big NFC North game? Stay tuned right here to find out. This article will populate with updates from Ford Field, including drive-by-drive analysis, score updates, game highlights, and injury news. All you need to do is stay on this site, and hit refresh when the game kicks off and watch as the updates and news come in. By the end of the game, this will be our game recap post. Enjoy your Thanksgiving and go Lions! First quarter The Lions won the toss and elected to take the ball first, in a change of normal strategy. Detroit’s offense got off to a strong start with a 6 and 7 yard run from Jahmyr Gibbs and a 19-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Starting right guard Tate Ratledge exited the field with a limp and went straight to the blue tent. He was replaced by Miles Frazier. Ratledge was initially ruled questionable to return with an ankle and knee injury. He would return to the lineup after missing the next drive. But the Lions kept driving, and St. Brown made a ridiculous one-handed, 27-yard catch to put the Lions first-and-goal from the 9-yard line. Amon-Ra only needed one hand! pic.twitter.com/9JASlhQK13 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 However, the Lions stalled from there with back-to-back incomplete passes from Goff, and Detroit had to settle for a chip-shot field goal. 3-0 Lions. The Bears quickly drove down the field, with Caleb Williams finding a few wide-open receivers, including D’Andre Swift for 13 yards and Kalif Raymond for 12. But when they moved into the red zone, Lions rookie defensive end Derrick Moore punched the ball out of Coleston Loveland’s hands and Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the fumble for a big turnover. OUR BALL! Derrick Moore punched it out, Malcolm Rodriguez recovered it! pic.twitter.com/Fznm4bMLb5 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Detroit took over at their own 16, but quickly went three-and-out. A pitch to Gibbs was snuffed out by the Bears, turning a second-and-3 into a third-and-6. And Goff couldn’t find anyone open on third down, eventually throwing a ball off St. Brown’s fingertips for an incomplete pass. But Detroit’s defense answered the call with a forced three-and-out of their own. A nice pressure from Anthony Lucas nearly forced an interception on second down, and Luther Burden was tackled well short of the sticks on third down by safety Andre Cisco, who was in for Chuck Clark. On the drive, Bears tight end Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room. Detroit’s passing attack hit another big play—a seam route to St. Brown for 23 yards. The All-Pro receiver took a big hit, but managed to hold onto the ball to put the Lions at their own 40-yard line. Sheesh, Amon-Ra pic.twitter.com/ulmgDghxIl — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 A facemask penalty gave the Lions another 15 yards, and pushed them into Bears territory. Then a 14-yard catch from Gibbs and an 11-yard run by Jameson Williams moved the Lions into the red zone as the first quarter expired. Second quarter On a third-and-3 play, Gibbs ran up the gut for a 9-yard gain down to the Bears’ 1-yard line. Two plays later, Gibbs’ second effort pushed Detroit into the end zone for a 10-0 Lions lead early in the second quarter. Happy ThanksGIBBSing pic.twitter.com/yycv1nrD0M — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 The Bears quickly answered with an explosive run. Salvon Ahmed broke off a 46-yard gain down the right sideline and into the red zone. Salvon gets loose for 46 yards 💨 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/mqAbZN1MbH — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026 But Detroit locked them down from there. Derrick Moore picked up a sack on first down. Derrick Moore SACK 😤 pic.twitter.com/gxLRfenQP5 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Then, on third-and-long, a blitzing Roger McCreary knocked down the pass at the line of scrimmage to hold the Bears to three. 10-3 Lions. Detroit’s next drive was marred by back-to-back false starts from center Juice Scruggs. That forced a third-and-11, and Jared Goff, with all sorts of time, tried to check it down to Sione Vaki, but missed him. Chicago took over on their own 20-yard line. Caleb Williams exploited a coverage bust on third-and-3, finding a wide open Stephen Carlson for and 18-yard gain. Then Swift caught a short pass, made a few Lions miss and took it for a big 33-yard gain. D'Andre Swift down the sideline for 33 CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Evztsk1rWG — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 A few plays later, Kyle Monangai ran it in for a 1-yard touchdown, tying the game up with 4:07 left in the half 10-10. KYYYYYLE MONANGAIIIIII in the end zone again 🎶 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/ZILeJEydVn — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026 The Lions got back to work with a 28-yard strike to St. Brown on the very first play of the drive. However, disaster nearly struck on the next play, with Goff tripping, fumbling, and jumping on his own recovery. The Bears challenged the call—thinking Goff never regained possession—but there was not enough evidence to overturn it. Still, the 10-yard loss was enough to end Detroit’s drive. Goff missed Williams on a deep shot, and then he had to scramble on a third-and-20 and didn’t come close. That gave the Bears a shot to run their two-minute drill to take the lead before half. But on the first play, Williams was sacked all the way back at his 2-yard line, setting up a second-and-18 at the two-minute warning. After a 7-yard gain on second down, Williams was strip-sacked and the Lions receovered. But there was an illegal batting penalty on the Bears, giving the Lions a choice: Take the penalty, which results in a safety and possession Decline the penalty and take the ball on the Bears’ 10-yard line Detroit opted to take the safety points and the ball. 12-10 Lions. ANOTHA ONE, D-MOORE pic.twitter.com/hEvpEOIXIl — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Detroit was able to add more points on the ensuing possession. They overcame another pair of false starts thanks to a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak. Then Goff hit Williams on a bit 39-yard corner route into the red zone. 39 yards in the bucket for Jamo! pic.twitter.com/Ds7rd8QOsA — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 That gave the Lions eventually one shot at the end zone with 10 seconds left. Goff was able to hit Sam LaPorta up the seam for the score and a 19-10 Lions lead at halftime. Jared Goff perfect ball placement to Sam LaPorta for a TD before the half! CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RNd20GIm58 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026

summary: On Thanksgiving, people are surrounded by loved ones, enjoying food, and most importantly, watching Detroit Lions football. full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions warms up prior to the NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thanksgiving, people are surrounded by loved ones, enjoying food, and most importantly, watching Detroit Lions football. It’s a classic tradition across Michigan, but it doesn’t always end well, as the franchise has a losing record on the holiday. This time, though, they aim to make it a happy Thanksgiving with a win over the Chicago Bears, and what better way to do it than with some extra cash coming to you too! It was another dominant week for me on the bets last week : I went 3-0 on all my straight bets, and if the refs hadn’t called some horrible defensive pass interference penalties on the final Lions defensive possession, it would’ve been a perfect day on the bets. We also hit our first bold bet parlay, so I can’t complain too much. Stay with me here as I try to keep the hot streak going, so make room on that plate for these bets. Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Over 55.5 Points (-112) Hope you saved room for some offense because this game should have it. In their first battle last year, the Lions dominated the Bears 52-21 in Bears head coach Ben Johnson’s first game back in Detroit. Detroit won the season finale, but it wasn’t as explosive, 19-16. This year, I expect it to be more of a fight, and both offenses will be humming along. Detroit enters at 28.8 points per game, while Chicago averages 26.2. Now the Lions defense has been playing better lately, holding their last four opponents to an average of 12.7 points per game, while the Bears defense started strong but has allowed an average of 22 points per game in their last four games. I expect Johnson will want revenge from 2025, and doing so on Thanksgiving will make it that much sweeter. This is the same coach who wants to lead the NFL in all-time scoring offense . I think this game could be a high-scoring, close contest, with each team putting up at least 30 points. Each team has plenty of weapons, and as a divisional game, the stakes are higher. The winner takes control of the NFC North and, given how contested the division is, could determine how the standings fall come January. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.93 2. Jared Goff alt passing yards 300+ (+132) Since I could see this game being high-scoring, I think Lions quarterback Jared Goff will have a dominant performance against the Bears. The reason isn’t the Bears defense itself; it’s also how Goff has performed against them recently. Last season, Goff threw for over 300 yards in both games: 334 yards and five touchdowns in their dominant Week 2 victory, and 331 yards in the low-scoring season finale. Despite the Bears’ defensive line upgrades, Detroit’s offensive line is a big improvement from 2025. If Goff can throw for over 300 with that line, how can he not do it again this year? What also helps Goff this year is the Bears’ inconsistent pass defense. They’re either shutting down passing attacks, holding six teams to under 200 yards, or they’re letting them air it out, with three games where they’ve allowed over 300 yards. Goff has thrown for over 300 yards in four games so far this season, and if teams keep paying attention to running back Jahmyr Gibbs, Goff will gladly slice and dice them upfield. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $23.20 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown Over 82.5 yards (-113) It wasn’t just Goff who went off on the Bears last season; wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had some strong performances. In the first game, St. Brown had six catches for 115 yards and three touchdowns, then snagged 11 balls for 139 yards in the last game. St. Brown made it a point to go off against his former coordinator in Johnson, and as long as he’s the head coach of the Bears, I think St. Brown will try his best to play well. He’s averaging 84 yards a game this season, so I think hitting the over on this game is a must. Detroit lost its Thanksgiving game last year too, and I don’t think St. Brown wants Johnson to rain on the Detroit parade. He will do whatever it takes for Detroit to win this game, and with the offense humming, I wouldn’t put it past St. Brown to have another great performance this week. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +312 and $10 -> $41.22 Record: 17-13 Brandon’s Bold Bet If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay: St. Brown anytime touchdown (-150) Jared Goff alt passing touchdowns 3+ TD (+178) Jameson Williams anytime touchdown (+200) Speaking of St. Brown, you best believe he will want to find the end zone on Thanksgiving. If he doesn’t get as many yards as he wants, but scores at least once and comes away with the win, I think he would be content with his performance. While this game isn’t as big as the Germany game, St. Brown wants to play well when matched up against Johnson. With my expectations of this game being high-scoring, I see the passing offense taking the stage against the Bears. If Goff is throwing for over 300 yards, I think he throws three touchdowns as well. He’s done it three times this season, but he hasn’t done it at home in Ford Field. That changes when Goff put up a big performance on Thanksgiving afternoon. So far, I’ve hyped up Goff and St. Brown, but I don’t think I’ll overlook Jameson Williams for a good performance too. While his play has been up and down this season, I think he’ll find the end zone and gobble up some turkey on Thursday afternoon. Goff could throw three touchdowns to St. Brown as they did against the Bears last year, but I think he spreads the wealth and gives Williams one, perhaps on a unique trick play that catches Johnson’s defense by surprise. title: Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears preview: 4 key stats
summary: The two most recent NFC North division champions pitted against each other to kick off the NFL’s Thanksgiving spectacular. Both teams are 8-2 in loaded divisional and conference races. Dan Campbell vs. Ben Johnson. This is why the NFL is undefeated. One of the few hurdles Campbell has yet to clear is finding consistent success […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions attempts to sack Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears during an NFL football game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The two most recent NFC North division champions pitted against each other to kick off the NFL’s Thanksgiving spectacular. Both teams are 8-2 in loaded divisional and conference races. Dan Campbell vs. Ben Johnson. This is why the NFL is undefeated. One of the few hurdles Campbell has yet to clear is finding consistent success on Turkey Day. After going 1-5 on Thanksgiving as a player with the Lions and Dallas Cowboys, Campbell is just 1-4 as the Lions’ head coach in their annual spotlight game. Detroit is 1-8 on Thanksgiving over the last nine seasons, with the Chicago Bears alone going 3-1 against the Lions in that span. The Lions have endured a grueling stretch, returning from Germany and playing last week without the luxury of a bye, followed by this short four-day turnaround. However, this game carries more weight than any they’ve played since their back-to-back divisional matchups against the Packers and Vikings. As a reminder, the Lions will play all three of their road divisional games over the last four games, making it even more imperative that they take care of business at home. This week’s Lions-Bears preview will focus on both sides of the ball, with a heightened emphasis on how defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s burgeoning defensive unit can turn Bears QB Caleb Williams into a turducken. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Can’t Run Away From Your Problems The Bears’ offense this season hasn’t quite reached the heights of efficiency it attained at times last year, except Week 1, when it put together a 59-burger firework factory against the Panthers. In fact, while the Bears haven’t trailed since Williams returned to the lineup in Week 6, their offense has averaged just -0.04 EPA/play in that span, good for a clean league-average ranking of 16th. One area that’s had hiccups in that span is the run game, which has suffered from the downgrade of center Drew Dalman (offseason retirement) to Garrett Bradbury and the loss of tight end Cole Kmet to injured reserve, a rock-fighting Geodude on the perimeter. The Bears are still committed to running the football, with a 46.8% run rate (8th), but where they’re really struggling is on early downs, putting themselves behind the eight ball. Since Week 6, their 132 early-down (first- and second-down) rushing attempts have generated just 3.3 yards/rush (29th), -0.269 EPA/rush (32nd), and a 34.1% success rate (27th). That’s not the run-game wagon Ben Johnson, one of football’s better run-game architects, had rolling last year. It hasn’t mattered whether they’re facing light boxes (six defenders or fewer) or loaded boxes (eight or more defenders) on early downs, as they rank among the bottom five to 10 teams in the league in both yards/rush and EPA/rush against either defensive look. The same holds true whether they’re running from under center or shotgun, ranking in the bottom five to 10 in both metrics. Personnel-wise, it doesn’t get much better, with 13-personnel being the lone bright spot, producing numbers closer to league average. Meanwhile, the Detroit Lions’ run defense, since Week 5, leads the league with -0.20 EPA/rush, ranks third in rushing success rate allowed (34.9%) and fewest yards after contact per carry allowed (2.23), and even ranks in the top 10 in run stuff rate (23.2%). The Lions’ defense is up to the task of shutting down former Lion D’Andre Swift and second-year back Kyle Monangai, both of whom have been hobbled by lower-body ailments this season. The key matchup to watch will be the dynamic defensive tackle duo of Tyleik Williams and Alim McNeill, who should be able to push Bradbury around and will have a heavyweight clash with Joe Thuney and Jonah Jackson, two offensive guards who haven’t been quite as dominant as they were last season. Consistently putting Williams in unfavorable late-down situations will go a long way toward choking out his opportunities to operate in advantageous, low-pressure situations. Gobbling Up the Quarterback While the Lions’ defense has been selective with its blitzing since Week 5, bringing extra heat on only 20.1% of dropbacks (29th), Kelvin Sheppard may want to consider sending additional defenders at Williams on second and third downs. Against the blitz on second and third downs since his return in Week 6, Williams is just 27-of-49 passing (55.1%, 26th) for 365 passing yards, registering -0.129 EPA/dropback (21st), a 41.5% passing success rate (19th), and a 1.9% turnover rate (15th). Opposing defenses have clearly identified this vulnerability, blitzing the Bears on 43.4% of second- and third-down dropbacks, the highest rate any offense has faced since Week 6. Two defenders who could be key figures in this regard are Derrick Barnes and jack-of-all-trades defensive back Roger McCreary. Barnes has generated a 25.8% pressure rate across 31 pass-rushing snaps since Week 5, ranking 13th among 76 qualifying off-ball linebackers (min. 10 pass-rushing snaps). Meanwhile, since Week 6, McCreary has registered a 40.0% pressure rate, ranking 13th among 87 qualifying defensive backs (min. five pass-rushing snaps). The recipe for success for the Lions’ defense in getting Ben Johnson’s offense out of sync is to shut down the run on early downs and send extra rushers at Williams on subsequent downs to speed him up, rattle his cage, force mistakes, and keep punter Tory Taylor busy on Thanksgiving. Putting a Lid on the YAC Gravy Train Since Williams returned in Week 6, the Bears have relied heavily on yards after the catch (YAC), finding skill players like Luther Burden and old friend Kalif Raymond in space with room to roam. The Bears have generated 682 yards after the catch (7th) on 113 completions, averaging 6.04 YAC per completion (6th), with YAC accounting for 51.7% of their passing yards (10th). Additionally, 26 of their receptions (23.0%) have generated 10 or more yards after the catch, the fifth-highest rate in the NFL. Generating YAC has been a clear strength of their passing attack. Luckily, one of the calling cards of Sheppard’s defense is forcing offenses to fight for every yard, and nothing comes easily. The Lions are a vise grip once a pass is completed, swarming receivers and shutting down opportunities for additional yardage. Since Week 5, the Lions’ defense has allowed just 4.2 yards after the catch per reception, the second-lowest mark in the NFL over that span. Brian Branch and his boys in coverage don’t give an inch and should force the Bears’ passing offense to be more efficient downfield rather than relying on their playmakers to manufacture yardage after the catch. Feasting Downfield While the Bears’ defense under Dennis Allen, especially with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, has been a formidable foe this season, one area where they’ve struggled mightily is defending deep passes (20-plus air yards). On those passes, the Bears have allowed 17-of-35 completions (48.6%, 28th) for 697 yards, 19.91 yards/attempt (32nd), six touchdowns, and just one interception, surrendering a league-worst +1.107 EPA/dropback. It’s been a despicable showing for an otherwise formidable defense when opposing offenses have elected to test them deep. Look for the Lions to take some big shots downfield, testing the long speed of cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson and looking for opportunities to catch rookie Dillon Thieneman or backup-turned-starter Cam Lewis out of position and get behind them. The odds feel pretty high that we’re treated to another Jameson Williams explosive play on Thanksgiving.

title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 12 loss to the Rams
summary: As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports. Today we’re looking at the 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12. I don’t have metrics on the broadcast, but I can tell you with some amount of […]
full_text: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports . Today we’re looking at the 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12. I don’t have metrics on the broadcast, but I can tell you with some amount of certainty that there was less dead air in this game than any other game this season. Luke Kuechly brought some really nice insight into some of the plays, but my goodness, fellas, you’re allowed to take a breath. And stop trying to make “Thanksgiving Eve” happen. It’s not going to happen. Offense After leaning into a heavy personnel grouping last week , this week saw the Packers go back to primarily playing out of 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR). And, lest you think the numbers are skewed due to a small number of plays in the second half (and needing to catch up when they did have the ball), those full game numbers are roughly in line with the first half approach. They were primarily a shotgun-based passing attack offense in this game. For the game, they were in shotgun on 84.1% of snaps and had a pass rate of 68.2%. Again, those numbers basically align with the 1st half. They were 78.6% shotgun and 64.3% pass in the 1st half. As we’ve seen them do all year, they switched up their run game approach in this game. After going with a power-heavy approach against the Vikings, they were back to a zone-based attack this week. Inside Zone didn’t work overly well for them, but they did well with Outside Zone and Power. I’m curious to dig a little deeper into that when the film hits. Was that a matter of a smaller sample size, or was that something they could have leaned a bit heavier into if they wanted to? Jordan Love had a pretty rough day in the stat sheet. He went 17/29 for 198 yards, 1 TD and 2 INTs for an EPA per Play of -0.31. That would go down as his worst game of the year by EPA per Play (behind the -0.22 he posted against the Vikings last week). As I mentioned at the top, I thought Kuechly did a nice job breaking down what Love was expecting on that 1st INT, and the second INT certainly seemed to be a case where Bo Melton cut off his route. So there are certainly things to consider (and things we’ll certainly be breaking down this week), but, right now, the numbers are the numbers and the numbers are bad. Love did seem to have a little more time to throw in this game, but, as with every game this season, time is relative. The average time to pressure against Love was 2.3 seconds, 0.26 seconds below the NFL average. His average time to throw of 2.62 seconds seems downright functional, and would make this his 5th longest time to throw in a game this year. It’s still 0.08 seconds below the NFL average. So protection was better, but still below average. Still, it felt functional in a way it certainly did not against the Vikings. Love came into this game shredding Man coverage, and the Rams came into the game playing one of the highest rates of man coverage in the league. Love continued playing well against man, but the zone stuff is ugly. We don’t know how long Christian Watson will be out, but it sure would be nice if Tucker Kraft could find his game a little bit. He clearly is not all the way back from his injury (whether that’s physical or mental, I don’t really know), but the offense won’t really have a chance if he can’t find a way to turn it on. Defense Micah Parsons played limited snaps in his return to the field , but he was impactful while he was there, notching a 21.4% pressure rate and an average time to pressure of 2.47 seconds. Welcome back, @MicahhParsons11 ! 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/YLmftoOBeY — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Parsons posted a pressure rate of 20.2% and an average time to pressure of 2.76 seconds last season, so he looked like Micah Parsons while he was on the field. That was certainly encouraging. With Parsons back, I was certainly hoping for more from Lukas Van Ness, but we didn’t really see that. He had a pressure rate of 6.7% and an average time to pressure of 2.6 seconds. With as run-heavy as the Rams were (66.2% run rate for the game, 81.4% in the 2nd half) it’s hard to glean too much in terms of how the pass rush will look with Parsons back. Something to keep an eye on going forward. Chris McClellan turned in a nice game with 4 assisted tackles, 4 solo tackles and 1 tackle for loss. I’m excited to take a look at him when the film comes out. Albums listened to: Jay-Z – The Blueprint 2: The Gift & The Curse

title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 12 vs. the Rams
summary: On Thanksgiving Eve, the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams faced off in a game which had heavy impact on the playoff chances for both teams. RG Kevin Zeitler made his first start for the Packers. EDGE Micah Parsons made his long awaited return after sustaining a torn ACL during the 2025 season. It […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thanksgiving Eve, the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams faced off in a game which had heavy impact on the playoff chances for both teams. RG Kevin Zeitler made his first start for the Packers. EDGE Micah Parsons made his long awaited return after sustaining a torn ACL during the 2025 season. It was also another chapter in the Matt LaFleur vs. Sean McVay saga, and, for the first time since the two both became NFL head coaches, McVay and the Rams came out victorious, 26-13. Let’s take a look at what worked, and what didn’t. Winner: Micah Parsons It feels so good typing these words right now. After wondering what the heck was taking so long with the return of the Packers star edge rusher after a December 2025 ACL tear, it was revealed that the damage was much more severe than many of us realized . Last night, finally healthy, Parsons made his first start of the 2026 season, playing about 37% of total defensive snaps. And he looked…great! Parsons nearly got to QB Matthew Stafford a few times, and then just before halftime, we all got to see the sack we’d been waiting 346 days for. With how things have been called all year for the Packers, I was certain this would be flagged for roughing the passer. Parsons finished the night with 1 sack and 2 QB hits, and was credited with 4 pressures on 26 snaps. Good stuff, and it’ll only get better. Welcome back, @MicahhParsons11 ! 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/YLmftoOBeY — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Winner: Christian Watson WR Christian Watson was the only reliable pass catcher for the Packers last night, and he was knocked out of the game in the first half after taking a nasty blow to the helmet, which saw Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected. Prior to the hit, Watson was the only one able to hold onto the ball or…do anything right, really. The routes were nice. The hands were strong. He finished the night catching all 4 targets for 65 yards and 1 TD. His concussion status will be one to monitor as the Packers head into their next game next Sunday. CHRISTIAN. WATSON. 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/wXV7uZYgFw — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Loser: Tucker Kraft The Packers have had a problem with TE Tucker Kraft all season, and now, it’s got me begging them to stop giving him the ball. Kraft has had some pretty egregious drops this year, has played like he’s scared of getting hit, and has just been generally BAD. Last night, he logged his second fumble of the year, and the Rams were able to turn it into 3 more points. Kraft finished the night catching 3 of 5 targets for 24 yards. They don’t really have any other options at TE, so I guess we just hope for the best? And cry a little? Landman PUNCH. Rams force a turnover. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/Rc7QYWZ47f — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Loser: Matthew Golden Last night was the first time I’ve seen QB Jordan Love visibly angry, and it came on the heels of an interception that seemed to have been caused by WR Matthew Golden running the wrong route. Golden has been great this year. He even showed flashes of that last night with his big 39 yard gain, but this error killed any sort of momentum the Packers were developing. Golden finished the night with 1 catch on 5 targets for 39 yards. Shannon Sharpe calls out matthew golden pic.twitter.com/6XsPpO7422 — NBA Hoops (@Thechat101) November 26, 2026 Loser: Bo Melton It may not be a good idea to stop running and then just watch as the defender intercepts your quarterback. Rams get a pick off Love again. Defense is COOKING. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/JjAiSSCGb3 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Loser: Brian Gutekunst We can blame the quarterback (not really), we can blame the offensive line, we can blame the receivers, we can blame the run defense, we can blame the head coach! At the end of the day, this goes back to GM Brian Gutekunst, who put the team together. Now—there are things he can’t control, like the drops, and the injury bug flying through the locker room. But the poor depth at offensive line has been the catalyst for almost all of the bad things to happen to the Packers offense this season. Jordan Love has been running for his life. He’s being hit while throwing. The RB room doesn’t stand a chance. The receivers have had almost no time to get open. An even mediocre offensive line fixes a lot of this. By failing to put together an o-line group that can sustain any sort of run game, any sort of passing game other than “sling it and hope for the best”, Brian Gutekunst has bungled the 2026 roster. The 6-5 Packers make their next appearance next Sunday, December 6, against the 3-7 New Orleans Saints. The game is at 1 pm ET/12 pm CT, and yes, that’s a threat.
