title: Thanksgiving Day games will impact NFC North, AFC top seed races
summary: It’s not every year that the NFL ends up with elite matchups on Thanksgiving Day that will have enormous impacts on the league’s playoff races. Part of this is due to the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys being involved every year, as the two franchises have been hit-or-miss in terms of their playoff impacts over […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-November 28: Detroit Lions fan cheers during the second half of an NFL Thanksgiving Day football game between the Chicago Bears and the Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Thursday, November 28, 2024. (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images It’s not every year that the NFL ends up with elite matchups on Thanksgiving Day that will have enormous impacts on the league’s playoff races. Part of this is due to the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys being involved every year, as the two franchises have been hit-or-miss in terms of their playoff impacts over the past few years, as well as the league often finding random pairs of teams to match up in the night game. For example, last year’s Thanksgiving games ended up having one big game: the Packers’ 31-24 win over the Lions, which was an obviously important game heading into the day. The two teams were within a game of the NFC North lead at the time — the Packers coming in at 7-3-1 and the Lions at 7-4 — and Green Bay’s win ended up keeping them ahead of Detroit for the NFC’s final playoff spot at the end of the season. However, the Cowboys-Chiefs game saw both teams sputtering a bit heading into the game, while the night game between Cincinnati and Baltimore was a bit of a dud. 2024 was even less exciting from a national perspective. The Lions hosted the Bears, but Chicago was 4-7 heading into the holiday and was mired in a five-game losing streak; Cowboys-Giants featured teams with a combined six wins ahead of the game; and Packers-Dolphins was a cross-conference game that had little rivalry juice. Thanksgiving Day in 2026 is a very different story, however. The power balance in the NFL’s best division and the race for the top seed in the AFC are both on the line today, providing an exceptional pair of matchups in the early and prime time games that should keep NFL fans riveted. Two of today’s games feature a pair of teams with at least 8 wins each, something that has never happened before, according to my research. In fact, the only other time that Thanksgiving had two games pitting teams with even 7 or more wins each was way back in 2014 with Eagles-Cowboys (both 8-3) and Seahawks-49ers (both 7-4). It’s a perfect year to schedule dinner for around kickoff of the afternoon, ensuring that the football fans in your household can watch an impactful game before food, then eat and get a nap in before grabbing some leftovers to chow down with a big night game. Game 1: Bears vs. Lions (12 Noon CT, CBS) This is the big one in the NFC North. Like the Packers and Bears a year ago, Chicago and Detroit enter the later stages of this season as the top teams in the league’s best division with two games to play against one another in the final handful of weeks. The two teams come into the holiday at 8-2, one game up on the Vikings and two up on the Packers in the NFC North standings. They’re also on equal footing in a number of areas — their point differentials are almost equal (+68 for the Lions, +65 for the Bears). If one team needs this game more than the other right now, it’s the Bears. Chicago is 0-2 in the division, while the Lions are 2-0. If the two teams split the season series and tie for the division lead, the tiebreaker will go to the team with the better division record; therefore, Chicago is in a tougher spot and really cannot afford to go a game down and lose the first half of the season series plus yet another divisional game. The winner of this one will stake a strong claim to the division and will stay within striking distance of the one-loss 49ers for the NFC’s top spot overall. The loser can make up the difference in these teams’ rematch in Week 17, but there will be work to do before then. As for the Packers, they would probably benefit more from a Bears win here, since Green Bay has one head-to-head win over Chicago already. The division isn’t entirely lost to the Packers yet, but they’ll have lots of ground to make up no matter the result of this game. Game 2: Eagles vs. Cowboys (3:30 PM CT, FOX) Here’s your mealtime/naptime game. The NFC East is a bit of a mess this season, with the Eagles in particular struggling with a new offensive coordinator and no Jalen Hurts. They come in at 3-7, while the Cowboys continue to ride an explosive offense (and equally explosive defense) to a 5-6 record. There could be some fun firepower in this game, but it doesn’t move the needle in terms of a matchup that has a major impact on the playoffs. Eat up, rest up, and recharge for a big night game. Game 3: Chiefs vs. Bills (7:20 PM CT, NBC) Here’s the dessert for football fans: yet another thrilling matchup between elite quarterbacks. The Bills sit atop the AFC at 9-1 and they are running away with the AFC East. They are the second-highest scoring team in the NFL, and their defense surprisingly ranks in the top ten in scoring. That’s largely due to schedule, however; the Bills have allowed fewer than 10 points per game on average over their last four games, but those performances have come against the Ravens, Vikings, Jets, and Dolphins, quarterbacked by Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Geno Smith, and Kyle McCord, respectively. The Chiefs are a different story this year than last, when they scuffled even before Patrick Mahomes’ injury. He’s back off a torn ACL though, and the Chiefs have found an elite running game with Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson as a 1-2 punch. These two teams have put together quite the rivalry of late. The Bills have won each of the last five regular season meetings between the franchises, dating back to 2021, but the Chiefs have taken each of the four playoff matchups that have matched up the two elite quarterbacks. The 8-2 Broncos are in the mix right now as well, but don’t be shocked if the team that wins this game ends up as the AFC’s #1 seed and earns a bye in the first round of the playoffs. Between the rivalry and the playoff impact this game could have, it should make for an excellent matchup to cap off a big day of football around the NFL.

title: Packers Snap Counts: Micah Parsons played less than 40 percent of snaps
summary: Micah Parsons made his 2026 debut tonight, and he was certainly on a pitch count. Let’s take a look at every player who saw action (or didn’t) in the Green Bay Packers’ 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams tonight. As a reminder, the scratches today were running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Ziare Franklin […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Micah Parsons made his 2026 debut tonight, and he was certainly on a pitch count. Let’s take a look at every player who saw action (or didn’t) in the Green Bay Packers’ 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams tonight . As a reminder, the scratches today were running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Ziare Franklin (shin), offensive lineman Donovan Jennings, offensive lineman Jager Burton and offensive lineman Mekhi Becton (all three were healthy scratches to get down to a 48-man game-day roster). Quarterback Jordan Love: 45 snaps Tyrod Taylor: 0 Running Back Kaleb Johnson: 23 Chris Brooks: 19 MarShawn Lloyd: 3 The Packers’ top two backs in this game were Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks, after there was a three-way split last week. Johnson was given a more all-around back role, as he was targeted twice and ran the ball eight times. Last week, Johnson was the runner, Brooks was the blocking back and MarShawn Lloyd was the route-runner. When Josh Jacobs returns to the lineup, assume that Lloyd is going to get knocked down to being a healthy scratch. The Packers haven’t ever had more than three backs up on the 48-man game-day roster, even when they held five players at the position on the 53-man active roster. Receiver Matthew Golden: 38 Savion Williams: 34 Christian Watson: 26 Bo Melton: 16 J. Michael Sturdivant: 7 Skyy Moore: 1 Receiver Christian Watson dropped out of the game with a concussion, which is why Savion Williams jumped him in the pecking order this week. Williams actually started the game as the slot receiver, a role that Skyy Moore was playing until Moore’s ankle got injured earlier in the year. In his two weeks back from injury, Moore has only played one offensive snap. Tight End Tucker Kraft: 45 Mark Redman: 8 Jonnu Smith: 5 Tucker Kraft played every single snap of the game, and the Packers only played 1.3 tight ends per play, a big difference from their game plan against the Minnesota Vikings last week. Last week, the team heavily leaned into multiple tight end looks, while this week featured a lot more three-receiver sets, even when Christian Watson went down. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan: 45 Laken Tomlinson: 45 Sean Rhyan: 45 Anthony Belton: 45 Kevin Zeitler: 24 Aaron Banks: 21 John Williams: 0 Travis Glover: 0 The starting offensive line in this game was Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, Sean Rhyan, Kevin Zeitler and Anthony Belton (left to right), a lineup that had never played together before. Zeitler dropped out of action in the middle of the game, though, which pushed Aaron Banks, who had been benched in recent weeks, into a guard spot. Defensive Line Chris McClellan: 45 Karl Brooks: 42 Anthony Campbell: 35 Devonte Wyatt: 30 Jordon Riley: 28 Earlier in the season, rookie third-round pick Chris McClellan was a reserve defensive lineman, but because of injuries, the nose tackle played the most snaps of anyone in the unit against the Rams. Devonte Wyatt, who appeared to be on a pitch count in the first half (he hasn’t looked right coming off his ankle injury this year), also dropped out of the game due to injury. It will be interesting to see if the team tries to get Warren Brinson, who is currently on the injured reserve, up to the active roster soon. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness: 47 Micah Parsons: 27 Barryn Sorrell: 25 Brenton Cox Jr.: 25 Dani Dennis-Sutton: 24 Micah Parsons’ return to action featured him playing 39 percent of the defensive snaps in this game, about half of his playing time rate in 2025. For the most part, the snaps for Parsons, Barryn Sorrell (who got injured in this game, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani Dennis-Sutton split snaps about evenly behind Lukas Van Ness. Linebacker Isaiah McDuffie: 70 Ty’Ron Hopper: 69 Nick Niemann: 0 Kristian Welch: 0 With Zaire Franklin still out, Isaiah McDuffie played the Mike spot and Ty’Ron Hopper was the Will. When Franklin comes back, which should be soon, he should be playing the Mike. When Franklin was last healthy, McDuffie and Hopper split the Will position. Cornerback Brandon Cisse: 70 Keisean Nixon: 70 Kamal Hadden: 1 Benjamin St-Juste: 0 The only notable nugget here is that Kamal Hadden played one snap in the slot when Javon Bullard was getting looked at for an injury. Otherwise, Brandon Cisse played right cornerback and Kamal Hadden played left cornerback, as usual. Safety Evan Williams: 70 Xavier McKinney: 70 Javon Bullard: 22 Kitan Oladapo: 0 Because the Rams played such heavy personnel on offense, it forced the Packers to play their 3-4 base defense often. The result of that was Javon Bullard, the team’s slot defender, only playing 31 percent of the defensive snaps today. “Nickel is the new base” is a fun catchphrase for NFL analysis right now, but it all depends on what the opposing offense puts on the field. Unfortunately, the Packers didn’t get many three-receiver looks today, in part because of how the game got out of hand for them in the second half. That left Bullard on the bench for more than two-thirds of the plays tonight.

title: NFC Playoff Picture: Packers fall out of postseason position with loss to the Rams
summary: After a pitiful second half against the Los Angeles Rams, the Green Bay Packers lost grip on a 13-13 tie with the help of a struggling offense and a defense that couldn’t stop the run. Ultimately, the team fell 26-13 to Los Angeles, which has now jumped past the Packers in the wildcard race. In […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a pitiful second half against the Los Angeles Rams, the Green Bay Packers lost grip on a 13-13 tie with the help of a struggling offense and a defense that couldn’t stop the run. Ultimately, the team fell 26-13 to Los Angeles, which has now jumped past the Packers in the wildcard race. In the second half, Green Bay averaged just 3.1 plays per drive, compared to Los Angeles’ 9 plays per drive. If you can believe it, the Packers’ defense, which was seemingly on the field for the entire second half, ended up wearing down. The Packers can’t hold onto the ball, in part because they can’t run the ball. Since the merger in 1970, only two teams have had worse rushing yard outputs than Green Bay through 11 games: the 2019 Miami Dolphins (which went 2-9) and the 1991 Indianapolis Colts (which went 1-10). With the loss behind us now, let’s look to the future. Currently, here’s how the NFC playoff race is playing out. NFC playoff standings 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 2. Detroit Lions (8-2, 2-0 NFCN) 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) 5. Chicago Bears (8-2, 0-2 NFCN) 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 7. Los Angeles Rams (7-4) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Green Bay Packers (6-5) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (4-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7, 1-0 vs ATL+NO) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7, 1-1 vs TB+NO) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7, 0-1 vs TB+ATL, 1-5 NFC) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7, 1-6 NFC) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) Yes, we’re two spots behind the last playoff spot. Hopefully, the Seattle Seahawks lose to the San Francisco 49ers this weekend, so we at least can have a tied record with them. The Rams being a full game ahead of the Packers and having the head-to-head tie-breaker over Green Bay is going to be a major factor in the playoff race moving forward. According to The Athletic’s playoff simulator , the Packers only have a 25 percent chance to make the playoffs right now, and their opportunity to win the division is essentially zero. title: Packers-Rams Final Score: Blake Corum takes control in 26-13 Rams win
summary: The Green Bay Packers’ playoff hopes are officially on life support. The team needed a win over the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday of Thanksgiving week to stay in the NFC’s 7th and final playoff position with six games to go in the 2026 regular season. Instead, another offensive collapse in the second half doomed […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 25: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against Isaiah McDuffie #58 and Brandon Cisse #2 of the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on November 25, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers’ playoff hopes are officially on life support. The team needed a win over the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday of Thanksgiving week to stay in the NFC’s 7th and final playoff position with six games to go in the 2026 regular season. Instead, another offensive collapse in the second half doomed the team, as Jordan Love and company ran just eight plays, held the football for barely three minutes, and picked up no first downs between the start of the second half and the midpoint of the fourth quarter. Over that time, the Rams took a lead and extended it out to ten points, which was too much for Green Bay to overcome. Blake Corum ran the football more than 20 times in the second half as the Green Bay defense wore down, and the Rams running back finished with over 180 yards on the ground and scored the go-ahead touchdown early in the third quarter to help the Rams coast to a 26-13 win. Micah Parsons’ return for the Packers saw him record a sack, but it was spoiled by his teammates’ inability to stop the run and the Packers’ offensive miscommunications. Jordan Love threw two interceptions, both of which appeared to be partially due to receivers running the wrong routes. Tucker Kraft committed an early fumble as well, giving the Packers three turnovers for the second straight game. And all told, the Packers had fewer than 20 minutes of possession in the game and ran just 44 plays on offense. The unit certainly suffered after Christian Watson left the game with an apparent concussion, while right guard Kevin Zeitler injured his ankle in his first start as a Packer. But the Packers’ issues were well beyond any injury issues, and they once again point to more fundamental problems with this team as a whole. With the Rams getting the win — going up by a game in the standings and earning a big tiebreaker with the victory — the Packers’ likelihood of making the postseason is now awfully slim. The Packers went 3-and-out on the game’s opening drive, and the Rams immediately took advantage of a bad call, with Brandon Cisse getting flagged for a long pass interference penalty. That put them in field goal range quickly, but Xavier McKinney snuffed out a swing pass on 3rd down to force a 3-point attempt from former Packer Brandon McManus, who hit from 43 yards out to give the Rams an early lead. Despite a running game that lost six carries on its first two carries, the Packers offense got moving on their second drive. Jordan Love hit Kaleb Johnson for 19 yards out of the backfield for the initial first down of the game, but after he found Tucker Kraft for another first down, the tight end coughed up the football as Nate Landman forced a fumble for the game’s first turnover. Another inexplicable penalty on the ensuing drive helped the Rams drive deep into Packers territory, as Devonte Wyatt was called for an absurd roughing the passer penalty. Micah Parsons made his presence known for the first time with a pressure on Matthew Stafford, however, helping to limit the Rams to another field goal. After another run for negative yardage by Johnson, Love hit Watson for a big 25-yard gain on a crossing route over the middle to get the Packers quickly across midfield. Trey Smack cut the Rams’ lead to 6-3 a few plays later, hitting a bomb from 54 yards out to get Green Bay on the board. The Rams responded with a touchdown drive, picking apart the Packers’ secondary with short and intermediate. Stafford went 5 of 6 for 60 yards on the drive, with his longest play going to Konata Mumpfield for 24 yards, but it was Kyren Williams who finished it off, finding the end zone from seven yards out for a score. That gave them a 13-3 lead early on in the second quarter. Love came up with back-to-back explosive plays on the first two snaps of the next drive, however, as the Packers answered. An end-around flea flicker from Savion Williams back to Love went for a gain of 21 to Watson, then Love hit Matthew Golden for a catch-and-run of 39 yards. A Chris Brooks run of 4 yards and a Love scramble for 7 set up goal to go and two plays later from the 7, Love drifted back and found Watson crossing left to right for a touchdown. Watson’s 8th score of the season brought Green Bay back to within three points. After forcing the Rams to punt for the first time all game, the Packers drove into field goal range once again. They did so thanks to Savion Williams picking up a 3rd-and-short on a dive when lined up as a tailback and Jordan Love finding MarShawn Lloyd for a nice gain out of the backfield for another first down. Matt LaFleur kept the offense on the field for a 4th-and-1 at the 30-yard line, and it proved to be a costly decision. Love lofted a good pass to Watson up the right sideline for a gain of 15 yards, but Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a hit to Watson’s head. Watson walked off on his own power, but the penalty and the catch were erased, offset by an offensive pass interference penalty on Matthew Golden. Watson walked to the locker room under his own power, but he would not return to the game. Instead of sending the offense out again, Trey Smack came on for a 48-yard field goal attempt and he hit it, tying the game with just under two minutes left in the first half. Micah Parsons then got his first sack of the season on first down of the Rams’ next drive, scuttling any real chance for Los Angeles to score before the half as the game went into the break tied at 13. sheeeeeeeesh pic.twitter.com/GoF3dq0YrB — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Coming out of the break, the Rams got cruising on the ground. Blake Corum picked up chunks of yardage as Stafford found Mumpfield for a couple of 3rd down conversions to get inside the Packers’ 10. On 3rd-and-2, Mumpfield appeared to have a touchdown, but he was ruled to have bobbled the ball and the play was ruled incomplete. That appeared to set up a 4th down attempt, but instead the Packers were called for defensive holding on the play anyway, giving the Rams a 1st-and-goal from the one. After Corum got stopped on his first rushing attempt, he barely snuck over the goal line on second down to give the Rams a seven-point lead. The Packers’ offense got bailed out on the next sequence with the game hanging in the balance, but then gave the ball right back. After going three-and-out following the Rams’ 8-minute drive, Los Angeles looked to put together a long drive again but Ty’Ron Hopper dropped into zone coverage and intercepted a Stafford pass, setting up Love and company in a great spot. However, he and Matthew Golden were not on the same page; Golden appeared to run the wrong route and Love’s deep pass to the middle of the field got picked off near the goal line to return the favor. Corum continued to run the ball effectively into the early fourth quarter, even as they saw a pair of starting offensive linemen and tight end Tyler Higbee leave the game with injuries. Finally, however, the Packers managed to get a stop with the Rams at the 40-yard line, leading to a surprising punt rather than a long field goal attempt. The Packers still could not move the chains, however, failing to pick up a first down for the third time in three second half drives. Tucker Kraft came up a yard and a half short on 3rd-and-9, and Matt LaFleur called for a punt from deep in Rams territory. Corum gave the Packers a big jab on 2nd-and-long with a 13-yard reception, then delivered a knockout blow with a 35-yard run up the gut on 3rd-and-1. That set up another McManus field goal, making it a two-possession game at 23-13. Green Bay finally started to mount a bit of a rally, picking up their first first downs of the second half with under six…

title: Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected; Packers WR Christian Watson evaluated for concussion
summary: In the second quarter of the Green Bay Packers-Los Angeles Rams game, Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and leading with his helmet on a tackle attempt on Packers receiver Christian Watson. You can find video of the play below: Initially, a cart came out for Watson, but the receiver was […]
full_text: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the second quarter of the Green Bay Packers-Los Angeles Rams game, Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and leading with his helmet on a tackle attempt on Packers receiver Christian Watson. You can find video of the play below: Christian Watson gets CRUSHED and is down injured pic.twitter.com/U0etpi9e8G — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 26, 2026 Initially, a cart came out for Watson, but the receiver was able to leave the field under his own power. The Packers are currently listing Watson as questionable to return and say that he’s being evaluated for a concussion. To be honest, it looks like the biggest hit he ended up taking was when his head hit the turf on the way down, not necessarily Kinchens’ blow to Watson’s facemask. Green Bay was not awarded a first down on this play due to offsetting penalties. Packers receiver Matthew Golden was called for offensive pass interference (you can only set a pick within a yard of the line of scrimmage), so they simply replayed the fourth-and-one play. After not getting a man coverage look with their running back’s motion, like they had on the play that Watson was injured on, head coach Matt LaFleur called a timeout and elected to kick the football, setting up a 17-17 tie going into halftime. We’ll keep you updated when we hear more news on the Packers’ injury situation. — Update: The Packers have now officially ruled Watson out with a concussion.

title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 12): Colts fan confidence rebounds, but doubts remain about Richardson
summary: The latest SB Nation Reacts survey shows a surprising rebound in confidence among Indianapolis Colts fans, with 31 percent now believing the franchise is headed in the right direction. That’s a significant 19-percentage-point increase from last week’s 12 percent, ending a month-long decline that saw fan confidence fall from 47 percent to its lowest point […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Anthony Richardson #5 of the Indianapolis Colts runs off the field during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest SB Nation Reacts survey shows a surprising rebound in confidence among Indianapolis Colts fans, with 31 percent now believing the franchise is headed in the right direction . That’s a significant 19-percentage-point increase from last week’s 12 percent, ending a month-long decline that saw fan confidence fall from 47 percent to its lowest point of the season. While the majority of fans remain unconvinced, the latest results suggest that some optimism may finally be returning to Indianapolis. The improvement comes following one of the biggest organizational decisions of the season, as the Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones after another disastrous offensive performance against the Houston Texans. Jones had struggled considerably throughout the past several weeks, and Thursday’s 26-3 defeat appeared to be the final straw for an organization that had remained committed to him despite mounting criticism. With Jones now gone and Anthony Richardson returning as the starting quarterback, the Colts have at least demonstrated a willingness to move in a different direction rather than continue with an approach that clearly wasn’t working. However, the decision to move on from Jones is unlikely to be the only reason for the increase in confidence. Indianapolis has already made significant changes throughout the organization, including the firing of general manager Chris Ballard and the trades of several established veterans. While those decisions have left the current roster considerably weaker, they have also provided the franchise with additional draft capital and an opportunity to begin building toward a more sustainable future. With a new general manager expected to take over during the offseason, fans may finally be starting to see some direction emerging from what has been an incredibly disappointing season. There is still plenty of work ahead, and 31 percent is hardly a number worth celebrating. However, considering where fan sentiment stood just a week ago, the improvement is an encouraging sign that the fan base hasn’t completely lost hope in the organization’s future. Colts fans aren’t particularly optimistic about Anthony Richardson While confidence in the overall direction of the franchise has improved, fans remain considerably more skeptical about what Anthony Richardson can accomplish over the remainder of the season. According to this week’s survey, 72 percent of respondents believe Richardson will finish with a losing record as the Colts’ starting quarterback , while just 16 percent expect him to finish above .500. The remaining 12 percent believe he will split his six starts evenly, finishing 3-3. Those results aren’t particularly surprising given Richardson’s previous struggles and the current state of Indianapolis’ offense. The former fourth-overall pick hasn’t started a regular-season game since December 2024 and has yet to demonstrate the accuracy or consistency necessary to establish himself as a dependable NFL quarterback. He will also be working with a significantly weakened receiving corps and an offensive line that has struggled considerably throughout the season, hardly ideal circumstances for a player attempting to revive his career. However, Richardson’s return should provide Indianapolis with an opportunity to evaluate whether he has made any meaningful progress over the past two years. His athleticism and rushing ability could introduce a different dimension to Shane Steichen’s offense, particularly with Jonathan Taylor still leading the backfield. Even if the Colts continue losing games, seeing Richardson demonstrate improved decision-making, better accuracy and a greater understanding of the offense would represent a positive development. For now, the latest Reacts results suggest that Colts fans are beginning to regain some confidence in the franchise’s direction, even if they aren’t convinced that Richardson will be the quarterback leading the organization into its next competitive window. title: Jaguars Open Patrick Mekari’s 21-Day Practice Window
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars took a major step toward getting a starting offensive lineman back on Wednesday, as the team announced it has opened the 21-day practice period for 2025 starting guard Patrick Mekari, who has been on injured reserve since the start of the season. Under NFL rules, a player placed on injured reserve with […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mekari #65 of the Jacksonville Jaguars looks on at the end of a game against the Los Angeles Chargersat EverBank Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars took a major step toward getting a starting offensive lineman back on Wednesday, as the team announced it has opened the 21-day practice period for 2025 starting guard Patrick Mekari, who has been on injured reserve since the start of the season. Under NFL rules, a player placed on injured reserve with a designation to return can resume practicing once he is eligible. That begins a 21-day clock. Within it, the team must either activate him to the 53-man roster or leave him on IR for the rest of the season. Counting from today, that clock runs into mid-December. Similarly, defensive end BJ Green’s 21-day window was also recently opened, with his hopeful activation still looming from injured reserve. How We Got Here Jacksonville signed Mekari as a free agent to a three-year, $37.5 million contract with $20 million guaranteed during the 2025 offseason. The money alone makes his return to the lineup a notable one for an interior line still struggling for an identity. With left tackle Anton Harrison on IR, center Robert Hainsey reportedly week to week, and swing tackle Walker Little exiting the Week 11 matchup with injury, Mekari’s versatility, if healthy, could be a boon to this Jacksonville offensive line. With an ability to play center and either guard or tackle position, Patrick would allow a variety of starting line combinations, or at minimum, functional depth at all five spots. Also, should the team decide that Cleveland or rookie Emmanuel Pregnon needs more time, they could plug Mekari there. Offensive Penalty Yard Leaders 1. JAX Emmanuel Pregnon: 82 yards (11 penalties) 2. PIT DK Metcalf: 76 (8) 3. BAL Ronnie Stanley: 69 (9) Brock Purdy being #5 with his FOUR intentional grounding penalties is hilarious. pic.twitter.com/UGinFtWNy7 — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) November 25, 2026 A Timely Return Mekari started at right guard in all 14 games he appeared in for Jacksonville last season. He was part of an offensive line that did not allow a sack in five games, tied for the most in the league. It also allowed no QB hit in two games, the most in the NFL in 2025. He has played 102 career games (67 starts) with Baltimore (2019-24) and Jacksonville (2025-present). However, Mekari has consistently struggled with back issues since signing in Jacksonville. This culminated in the veteran OL undergoing back surgery in mid-August. He was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return, with Ezra Cleveland starting at right guard in his absence. After being listed on the injury report throughout 2025 with the back injury, Mekari’s final injury came in Week 16 against the Denver Broncos, which kept him out of the Week 17 game against the Colts. He was later cleared to play in the wild-card game against the Bills, with the offseason surgery to follow. It’s easy to say that Jacksonville fans have yet to see a consistently healthy Patrick Mekari. If healthy currently, the benefit for the recently struggling offensive line may be right on time. Head Coach Liam Coen noted on Wednesday that it was great to get Mekari going, stating that the 305-pound lineman has “worked his tail off to get back,” as another experienced veteran in the fold to give the team depth and competition. He stated Mekari is “as strong as he’s been in a long time.” What’s next Opening the window doesn’t guarantee he plays, as there is no guarantee that a player will be activated from injured reserve simply because their practice window is opened. During the 2025 season, then rookie defensive end Jalen McLeod 21-day window was opened on December 16th and subsequently expired on January 7th with the rookie unable to make it back. Once the 21-day window expires the player is required to spend the remainder of the season on IR with no ability to return during that season. The coaching staff will watch how his back responds to practice before deciding on activation. Any updates on his status will likely come through the weekly injury reports. Stay tuned.

title: Chiefs-Bills: 5 questions with Buffalo Rumblings ahead of Week 12
summary: Tonight, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills in a week 12 Thanksgiving’s night showdown. We welcome Matthew Byham of Buffalo Rumblings— our sister SBNation site covering the Bills— for Five Questions with the Enemy. full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tonight, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills in a week 12 Thanksgiving’s night showdown. We welcome Matthew Byham of Buffalo Rumblings— our sister SBNation site covering the Bills— for Five Questions with the Enemy . Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Buffalo Rumbling s community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 12 matchup! 1. Buffalo converted only two of its five red-zone possessions into touchdowns against Miami and now faces the NFL’s top-ranked red-zone defense. What must the Bills improve inside the 20-yard line to finish drives against Kansas City? It wasn’t all that surprising to me that Josh Allen and the Bills struggled to convert red zone trips into touchdowns. The Miami Dolphins under Jeff Hafley field a top-10 defense and they put together a great game plan. Unfortunately, their surprising talent is overshadowed by the mess on offense. Divisional matchups are always unpredictable, no matter any lack of familiarity (i.e., Dolphins having new coaching/roster overhaul). The team would never admit it, but I also have to wonder if Buffalo was holding some things back a bit with a very important game only a few days later. Not necessarily in an effort to hide plays (because at this point there’s a lot of tape on every team), but rather pacing themselves for the marathon ahead. Not to take anything away from a Dolphins team that seems to be on the right track, but the Bills never trailed in that game. Head coach Joe Brady probably felt that even accumulating field goals might be too much for Miami’s offense to counter. As to your question about what the Bills need to improve? First and foremost, it would be great if tight end Dalton Kincaid (questionable w/thumb, ankle) were able to play in this one. He missed last week, and it’s pretty evident that Brady’s offense is vastly superior with Kincaid involved — especially as a red zone target. But drilling down further, the Bills struggle to gain separation on routes, and it’s magnified in the red zone. Buffalo would also do well to leverage their running game more near the goal line in this one. Sometimes I believe Brady gets a bit cute trying to outsmart a defense when, time and again, they’ve proven almost impossible to stop in the trenches this season. I’d like to see Brady roll out with two running backs near the goal line. It’s rare for him to do that anywhere on the field, even though Ty Johnson is the team’s most reliable pass catcher. Pairing Johnson with James Cook III in goal-to-go situations, while accounting for Allen’s dual threat, could create real havoc for a defense. Brady just has to be willing to shift out of a few 13-personnel plays, while finding the shortest path from point A to B. 2. Josh Allen did not record a rushing attempt against Miami, marking the first full game of his career without one. How aggressively should Buffalo use Allen’s legs against a Chiefs defense that has historically struggled to contain his extended plays? Allen should run as instinct instructs, nothing more, nothing less. I wouldn’t expect Brady to confine him to one thing or another, aside from asking him to avoid arm punts in a game like this, and with weather that’s going to be suspect at best. Allowing Allen to play free from constraint is the best move, while giving him options to abort anything risky. It is interesting that Allen didn’t rush a single time versus the Dolphins, but I’m left wondering if that was to protect him from any potential injury. Early on, Buffalo’s offense faced 4th & 1, and they ran a traditional handoff to Cook, who went right. It was a complete paradigm shift from what we’ve known of the Bills’ short-yardage offense. I expect him to have at least a few carries in this game, both in short- and long-yardage situations. 3. James Cook has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards and has recorded at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown in nine consecutive games. How important will establishing Cook be in the expected cold and rainy conditions Thursday night? James Cook is vital to the Bills’ success on offense. You could place bets on Buffalo leveraging Cook early and often, even if the weather was trending pleasant. Buffalo is 14-2 when Cook carries 20 times or more in a game. Under Brady, the Bills now employ a smash-mouth brand of football where they’ll remain committed to the run game even if it’s only getting a few yards a clip in early action. Outsiders have begun to catch on that Brady’s system is heavy on the run, despite having Allen at quarterback. Somehow, Cook seems to be fairly overlooked in many circles despite leading the league in rushing last season and roughly 30 yards out of first place this season. Cook is slight by typical NFL standards, but he’s proven tough between the tackles and moves like a hummingbird in traffic. With Cook and the maulers along the offensive line, Buffalo has been able to wear out defenses in a four-quarter battle of attrition. 4. Buffalo has not allowed a touchdown in three consecutive games and could regain several injured defenders against Kansas City. Is the Bills’ recent defensive improvement sustainable against a Chiefs offense that has scored at least 34 points in three straight games? That’s the question everyone wants answered right now. It’s fair to say that Buffalo hasn’t faced the NFL’s best quarterbacks in the last four games, but there’s reason to be optimistic about their trajectory. That’s due to confidence, which is so important in this sport. Early in the season, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s group was often out of position and visibly confused pre-snap. The pass rush was the only thing working, and mostly because Greg Rousseau has been a revelation as a 3-4 outside linebacker. The secondary has played well of late, especially since moving on from safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (first to Damar Hamlin and now Amani Hooker — the latter via trade). Cornerback Christian Benford has been elite, working to almost completely shut down tight end Brock Bowers and wide receiver Justin Jefferson, and holding wide receiver Zay Flowers to zero burger on the stat sheet. Make no mistake, this is a huge challenge. Kelce will always be Kelce, right (he’s always so open!)? It seems like this may be the most productive group of pass catchers KC’s had since Tyreek Hill wore red. Will they hold the Chiefs under their 34-point average in the last three games? It’s impossible to know, but at the same time the Bills are a different caliber of team compared to the New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons (what an epic defensive drop this season), and Arizona Cardinals. It’s similar to Buffalo, where the Chiefs are either more complete or far better than the Baltimore Ravens, Minnesota Vikings, Jets, or Dolphins. I think we find out a lot more about both teams Thanksgiving night. 5. Buffalo has won five consecutive regular-season meetings against Kansas City, and the winner will take control of the AFC’s No. 1 seed. What is your prediction for how this Thanksgiving night matchup unfolds, including the final score? I know that many Chiefs fans like to say that the regular-season matchup means little, and that Buffalo has yet to defeat Mahomes and company in the postseason. However, this is a massive game simply because of the playoff bye that’s at stake. Allen and the Bills have never earned the one seed, which I believe harmed prior rosters as it relates to injury recovery/availability in the playoffs under McDermott. Currently in control of the one seed, I’d venture to guess that Allen and company are going to be…

full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts , a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here . And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence Whether fans’ overall confidence in the team stays as high as it is right now will depend on how the Chiefs perform at Highmark Stadium. I don’t think l the Chiefs have to win in order for fans to stay confident in the teams direction, but they do have to play well. If Kansas City’s pass rush looks ineffective or they make boneheaded errors on special teams, then fans are liable to lose a little bit of their gusto for this team’s direction. But if KC comes out with their hair on fire and moves the ball well and play sound football, then win or lose I think most fans will feel okay about the team’s direction. I will say, one caveat to this is that the only teams the Chiefs have beaten with a winning record this season are the Broncos and the Raiders (at the time they played). At some point, you would like to see them beat a good team. Can the Chiefs finally beat the Bills when it doesn’t matter? There are a few reasons to be hopeful that the Kansas City Chiefs can walk out of Highmark Stadium with a victory on Thanksgiving night. The Bills have allowed opposing teams to score 30 points or more on four different occasions this year. The Chiefs have the second-best scoring defense, allowing just 16.3 points per game. The Chiefs also have the best red zone defense, allowing opposing teams to score a touchdown on just 36% of red zone visits. Really, this game is going to come down to a few things. Can Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs keep up the offensive tear they have been on? Will Josh Allen make dumb decisions and turn the ball over? Allen already has 9 interceptions this season, compared to just 4 picks for Mahomes. Can Emmett Johnson continue to prove that he is the best offensive rookie in the NFL and run all over the Bills? Can the Chiefs stop Josh Allen from running the ball? You know it’s coming, but he is a big dude and not easy to bring down. Bottom line, this is going to be a tough game and fingers crossed the good guys come out on top. Click here to see other recent survey results.

Two months later, with the draft set to begin, the Chiefs were focused. Chiefs gear up for miserable weather conditions in Buffalo on Thanksgiving | The Kansas City Star “You just have to go out there and play football,” Mahomes said. “I try to just do whatever I can to be the best version of myself no matter where you’re playing or what the weather is. “I want (Andy Reid) to have enough trust in me to call the game exactly the same, no matter the circumstance, and I think we’ve done a great job with that throughout my career.” Bills-Chiefs score predictions: Why our experts are split on Mahomes vs. Allen on Thanksgiving | The Athletic Another obvious worry for the Chiefs is limiting Allen. Defensive coordinator that he hasn’t exactly cracked the code on how to slow down Allen in their previous meetings, though that’s understandable given the QB’s run-pass ability. Without an obvious answer for Allen and while projecting the Chiefs offense to struggle somewhat in a chaotic setting, I could definitely see the Bills extending their regular-season win streak to six games over the Chiefs. It’s the longest such streak by Kansas City since the 2021 season. Kansas City has also won each of its last three games by at least 21 points, doing so for the first time since the 1997 campaign. ‘It’s always a challenge’ | How the Bills are preparing for a high-powered Kansas City Chiefs offense | Buffalo Bills Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is ready for the challenge, leaning on his experience coaching against Mahomes as a member of the AFC West over the last two seasons. “Fortunately, I’ve been able to game plan against them a number of times in the last few years, and it’s always a challenge,” Leonhard said. “You take a very highly skilled group of athletes, and you’ve got the trigger man in Mahomes who is able to just disperse the ball all over the place.” Around the NF L Steelers release Aaron Rodgers following stunning appearance on ‘The Pat McAfee Show’ | NFL.com McCarthy held a news conference hours after Rodgers’ “McAfee” appearance and declined to get into specifics regarding the QB’s claims as he said he was focused their upcoming game against the Broncos. title: Chiefs-Bills: 5 Things to Watch in Week 12 matchup
summary: The (8-2) Kansas City Chiefs will clash with the (9-1) Buffalo Bills in the highly anticipated Thanksgiving night matchup. The game kicks off at 7:30 Arrowhead time from New Highmark Stadium in Buffalo and will be broadcast on NBC. This game has become the league’s premier rivalry and will be played on the biggest stage […]
full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The (8-2) Kansas City Chiefs will clash with the (9-1) Buffalo Bills in the highly anticipated Thanksgiving night matchup. The game kicks off at 7:30 Arrowhead time from New Highmark Stadium in Buffalo and will be broadcast on NBC . This game has become the league’s premier rivalry and will be played on the biggest stage imaginable for a regular-season game. Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen are deadlocked at 5-5 since their first meeting in the 2020 NFL season, with Allen holding a 5-1 regular-season advantage and Mahomes going 4-0 in the playoffs. This game could shape the rest of the season and drastically alter the AFC playoff picture. There is never a dull moment when these teams meet, and this week should not be any different. Here are five things to watch 1. Mahomes vs Allen For the past six seasons, Mahomes and Allen have played at the highest level, and they’ve saved their best for when they play each other. Patrick Mahomes will face Josh Allen for 11th time as starting QBs in regular season or playoffs. Only QBs to meet more in non-division games: Tom Brady vs Peyton Manning 15 (plus 2 more when both in AFC East) Brady vs Ben Roethlisberger 12 — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) November 25, 2026 This season, Allen has thrown for 2,572 yards and 14 touchdowns, while Mahomes has thrown for 2,709 yards and 22 touchdowns. This season, Mahomes holds that advantage over Allen and will likely start to garner more MVP attention as the season progresses. This week, the game should be exciting, and the quarterback play should be top-notch. Mahomes vs Allen 🍿 Chiefs vs Bills 📺 Inject this game right into our veins 😤 pic.twitter.com/f4Bi1R96EQ — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 31, 2025 2. Winning with the run game The quarterbacks will get the attention this week, but the game will flow through the trenches and the ground game. The Bills rank second in the NFL, averaging 146 rushing yards a game, while the Chiefs rank fifth, averaging 134 per game. The Bills’ rushing attack has been largely led by All-Pro running back James Cook, who is second in the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1060 yards through ten games and ten touchdowns. James Cook has reached 1,000 rushing yards ✅ Season Stats: 209 Car | 1,060 Rush Yds | 10 Rush TD Season Pace: 355 Car | 1,802 Rush Yds | 17 Rush TD #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/BDlpuytQo9 — PaceBall (@paceball__) November 23, 2026 Bills quarterback Josh Allen has also added 290 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns this year. The Bills rely heavily on Cook and Allen to move the ball on the ground, while the Chiefs’ ground game has only become more dynamic through the past three weeks. Kenneth Walker remains fifth in the NFL in rushing yards with 872 and seven touchdowns, but he will miss a third consecutive game with a groin injury this week. His backup, rookie Emmett Johnson, has dazzled, and with 317 rushing yards on the season and two touchdowns, it has become clear the Chiefs’ running back room may be the best in the NFL. Walker won’t play this week, but it gives Johnson another chance to show what he can do. Run defense will be at a premium this week as well. Both teams rank in the top ten in rushing yards allowed per game. For the Chiefs, the front seven will face its toughest test yet. Johnson reading Nourzads block well to find a nice gain. The 4i returns inside, Nourzad keeps him on his inside shoulder, allowing Humphrey to overtake. Once he passes it off he climbs to LB level. Johnson hits the cut hard and finishes the run. pic.twitter.com/zR4djivI1f — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 23, 2026 3. Forcing turnovers Despite their success this season, the Bills sit at -1 in the turnover differential, due to a whopping 16 turnovers, which puts them at 24th in the NFL. By comparison, the Chiefs sit at a +6 margin, the fourth-best in the NFL, and have turned the ball over only seven times, tying for the second-best in the league. The Bills’ turnovers haven’t caught up with them yet, but their two biggest stars have been responsible for most of the issues. Allen has thrown nine interceptions so far this season, and Cook has fumbled the ball four times. By comparison, Patrick Mahomes has thrown four interceptions, and the only running back fumble this year was Johnson’s, and the offense recovered it. Josh Allen, Where Are We Throwing The Ball, Bro? Right Before The Half, He Gets Intercepted By Zayne Anderson. Not The Way You Want To Head Into The Locker Room. pic.twitter.com/AMUDb2G3Se — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 22, 2026 No Chiefs pass catcher has given the ball up either, and this efficiency has kept them on track for big plays and long scoring drives. The Bills defense is one of the best in the NFL at forcing turnovers, so the offense will need to continue their mistake-free football. On the opposite end, a few takeaways could give the Chiefs the spark they need to gain momentum against the Bills. There was no broadcast replay, so here is #Bills Josh Allen’s scrap/fighting against #Dolphins corner Chris Johnson after his first interception via the All-22. #BillsMafia @BuffTrenchTalk pic.twitter.com/5txJ85EpiA — Carson Hayek (@CarsonHayek) November 23, 2026 4. Pressures and containment on Allen Josh Allen is among the most difficult quarterbacks in the NFL to defend in the pocket. His ability to create on the fly rivals only Mahomes, but if you leave him in the pocket, he has the velocity to pick teams apart. This week, the Chiefs’ front four will have the tall task of ensuring he doesn’t run wild if containment breaks down, while also finding the balance to keep him from getting comfortable in the pocket. Karlaftis goes wide up the field and tries to bend the arc. Jones goes back inside the B-gap but gets washed down. This, along with the mesh concept opens a massive lane for Allen to operate. Bad angles from the rest of the LB's, and he crashes in to seal the game. pic.twitter.com/OLjLKL40qY — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 18, 2024 George Karlaftis, Chris Jones, Ashton Gillotte, R Mason Thomas, and Peter Woods will all play key roles in containing/ pressuring Allen, as well as Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill. The secondary could also play a big role in containing Allen if the Chiefs choose to spy. The Chiefs could disguise Chamarri Conner or L’Jarius Sneed in the slot, then shift to spy Allen and contain him in the pocket. “I don’t want you to play anymore, I want you to retire” – Chiefs DC Steve Spagnuolo to Josh Allen following the Bills 28-21 win last year Josh Allen currently holds a 5-1 regular season record over the Chiefs heading into Thanksgiving night #buffalobills #billsmafia #JoshAllen pic.twitter.com/rKoSpoNPnG — Caleb Carr (@caleb_carr) November 25, 2026 Allen’s turnovers have been up this season, and the front seven can help contribute by making him uncomfortable in the pocket. 5. The weather For the first time all season, the elements could be in play. Some changes to the Bills forecast! Rain becomes widespread tomorrow PM and continues into the evening. However, the latest model run is hinting at slightly drier skies during the game. It's far from a guarantee, but there's at least a little hope! @news4buffalo #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/u4jVD1CmEn — Mike Doyle (@wx_MikeDoyle) November 25, 2026 Multiple weather outlets have predicted heavy rain and cold temperatures, with high wind gusts through the Buffalo area on Thursday night. The rain and cold conditions will not be pleasant, but will be manageable. The wind, however, could change things. Not only will we have to worry about rain for the game tomorrow, wind will be another factor. Winds will be gusting up to 30-35 mph at times, especially early on in the game. pic.twitter.com/A7v5bT8tkz — BuffaloWeather (@weather_buffalo) November 25, 2026 It will be worth watching early on how both coaching staffs handle the conditions and whether they affect how the ball is thrown downfield. I…

title: Chiefs-Bills Week 12 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, our writers predicted the final score and result. The NFL’s marquee rivalry for the last half-decade sees the Chiefs entering with a 8-2 record, having already exceeded […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, our writers predicted the final score and result. The NFL’s marquee rivalry for the last half-decade sees the Chiefs entering with a 8-2 record, having already exceeded last season’s disappointing win total by two victories. At 9-1, the Bills are tied for the best record in the NFL. Both teams face major questions after facing some of the league’s worst teams over the past month. Thursday night is an opportunity for each team to prove their record to be legitimate. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Bills as slight 2.5-point home favorites. The Chiefs are coming off of a dominant 34-7 blowout of the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11, while the Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins by a 26-9 margin. Both teams faced off against backup quarterbacks last week. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) For most of the season, I’ve assumed that I would be picking Buffalo to win this one. And the Chiefs have some major questions to answer about how good they are after a trio of dominant wins over minimal competition. However, the same can be true for Buffalo, who has faced a laughable stretch of opposing quarterbacks since their Week 7 bye. Based on expected rainy and cold weather, I am going to pick the Chiefs to come out on top in a game where pounding the rock will prove crucial. This would have been a nice game to have Kenneth Walker available to alternate with Emmett Johnson. But Johnson has been as hot as any player in the league this month and will have a nice chance to make a Rookie of the Year case before a national audience. Chiefs 24, Bills 20 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) Ding, Ding. The best rivalry in the NFL will pit two of the top contenders in football against one another this week. While the Chiefs and Bills both won in blowout fashion on Sunday, it should be noted that a poor performance from Josh Allen caused Buffalo to have to scrap all the way to the finish line. Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes and company played mostly backups in the second half. As usual, this game will come down to Mahomes or Allen holding the ball in critical situations. The Chiefs must find answers for stopping the Bills pass rush, but a well-balanced running game will be needed for a Chiefs win. The two teams mirror each other, and the game will come down to who can win late. Bills 28, Chiefs 24 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) Chiefs-Bills has become one of the defining rivalries of the Patrick Mahomes era, and this Thanksgiving matchup has me torn. Buffalo has James Cook to complement Josh Allen, but I think Kansas City’s running game can make the difference this time. The Chiefs have found ways to run against Buffalo before, but this backfield gives them a stronger opportunity to sustain drives without asking Mahomes to do everything. In a game that could come down to the final possession, being able to grind out first downs late in the fourth quarter and keep Allen on the sideline could be the deciding factor. Defensively, I trust the Chiefs’ cornerbacks to compete with Buffalo’s receivers and limit explosive plays. Containing Allen is another challenge entirely, and Kansas City will need to finish possessions without letting him escape pressure and create something out of nothing. I expect another tense game between these two teams, but I’m betting on the Chiefs’ ground game helping them close it out. My mind says Buffalo, but my heart says Kansas City—and I’m following my heart. Chiefs 28, Bills 24 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) The Chiefs will beat Buffalo because they have Patrick Mahomes, and there’s nobody I trust more when the stakes are elevated. As great as Josh Allen is, Mahomes’ ability to manipulate defenses, extend plays and deliver in the biggest moments is what separates him from every other quarterback in football. He’s thrown 13 touchdowns without a single interception over his last four games, and I expect the best player on the planet to remind everybody why the AFC still runs through him. Chiefs 22, Bills 20 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) The regular season game of the year, and the Super Bowl of this and every Bills season is on Thanksgiving night. It should be the most-watched, highest scoring game of 2026. But, with the weather looking cold and wet, it could be the team with the best running game and defense that holds up– and this season, that’s your Kansas City Chiefs. Josh Allen is a problem for both teams at times– his ability to run can move the chains in big moments, but he’ll also give the Chiefs defense a chance at a couple turnovers. Spagnuolo’s crew is quietly among the best in the NFL, but don’t expect a flurry of sacks this week, they’ll need to focus on stopping Cook and containing Allen. It’s weird to say, but I like Emmett Johnson over James Cook on Thanksgiving. I also suspect Mahomes’ competitive nature can overcome mother nature. Chiefs 24, Bills 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I’ve talked myself into it. This is the year. The Bills can’t ever make it to the Super Bowl, and so each regular season matchup against the Chiefs becomes their Super Bowl. This is the year they lose their Super Bowl. Patrick Mahomes is quietly playing at an MVP level and the Bills’ defense can be had. I love the matchup of the Chiefs’ rushing attack against the Bills. Our defense has played better the last few weeks, but I’m really curious to see how they play against a more quality opponent. This is always one of the best games of the year, and a potential AFC Championship preview. The Chiefs win and remain competitive in the race for the AFC West crown and home field advantage. Chiefs 27, Bills 24 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Kansas City Chiefs are coming in hot off beating three terrible teams in a row. Now it’s time to get back into the deep end and swim with the sharks. This game is by far the biggest of the Chiefs’ season. A victory on Thanksgiving night changes the complexion of this entire season. Luckily, the Bills’ defense is nothing to write home about. This is the team that gave up 31 points to the Houston Texans and 30 points to the Las Vegas Raiders. The issue is, they have scored over 30 points in five games this year. So the defense will have their hands full playing on the road at the new Highmark Stadium, but to heck with it, I’m riding with my team, and I believe in these boys. Chiefs 28, Bills 24 Nate Christensen The Chiefs have not beat the Bills in the regular season since 2020. The Bills have typically come off a heartbreaking loss to the Chiefs in the playoffs and get revenge for it in the regular season. This year, I do think the Chiefs get the win. I think the Chiefs are able to slow this game down with a run game Buffalo won’t be able to stop. The defense will give up some points and yards, but I think they create more stops that let the Chiefs win. Chiefs 27, Bills 24 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) After an afternoon loss on Thanksgiving last year that ruined my favorite holiday, I am fired up for the Chiefs to be the nightcap, after I can enjoy my mother’s cooking all day and not have my appetite ruined by a potential loss. But I see myself and the rest of Chiefs Kingdom eating their pies in happiness through the night, celebrating with family and friends that Kansas City looks to be back in control of the AFC. The Chiefs have built themselves to beat the Bills, whether intentional or not, and it starts with one of…

full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 12, the Chiefs play the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Here is the Chiefs’ final official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website . After Monday’s practice estimates, Tuesday’s report showed the teams on the field preparing for the game. Chiefs Running back Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out after being upgraded to a limited participant and practiced Tuesday for the first time since injuring his groin before the Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons . Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was ruled out after he did not participate in practice again and hasn’t since leaving the Week 9 game against the New York Jets in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was ruled out after he was a limited participant in practice all week for the third consecutive week. He was activated from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list last week. Tight end Noah Gray (rib) is questionable after he was upgraded to a full participant in practice after missing on Monday after leaving the game against the Arizona Cardinals late with the injury. Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) has no game designation after he was a full participant in practice again; he appears set to return after entering concussion protocol during the first quarter of the Week 10 game. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) is questionable to play for the first time since leaving the game injured against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Bills Starting cornerback Christian Benford (groin) is questionable after being upgraded to a limited participant on Tuesday and missing last week’s game. In eight games played this season, Benford has 33 tackles and eight passes defended. In his career against Kansas City, Benford has 2 passes defended, one sack and a forced fumble. Starting tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is questionable after he was a limited participant in practice on Tuesday and limited on Monday. He missed last week’s game and has been banged up for a few weeks. This season, Kincaid has seen the second-most catches on the team (32) and has 487 yards and two touchdowns; Kincaid has one touchdown in his career against the Chiefs. Starting right guard O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle) is questionable after being a l imited participant in practice this week; he has not missed a start this year. Starting linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) is questionable after he was a limited participant in practice this week after missing last week’s game. This season, Williams has 61 tackles (5 for loss), one sack, two interceptions and four passes defended.

title: Chiefs-Bills Madden Simulation Week 12: Happy Thanksgiving
summary: On Thursday, the (8-2) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road to New York to take on the (9-1) Buffalo Bills. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. Note: Madden simulation is 8-2 this season, predicting the outcome. First quarter The Chiefs opened with the ball but managed just one first […]
full_text: On Thursday, the (8-2) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road to New York to take on the (9-1) Buffalo Bills . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: Madden simulation is 8-2 this season, predicting the outcome. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here . First quarter The Chiefs opened with the ball but managed just one first down, coming on an 18-yard pass to Xavier Worthy. The drive stalled after Deone Walker sacked Mahomes on third down, forcing Kansas City to punt. James Cook flipped the field with a 33-yard gain, followed by a 22-yard run that moved the Bills to the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. Kansas City’s defense stood tall, forcing Buffalo to settle for a field goal on its opening drive. Tyler Bass put the Bills on the board. Trey Smith exited the game with an apparent injury. Emmett Johnson caught a Texas route near midfield and turned it into a 21-yard gain to the Bills’ 26-yard line. End of first quarter: Bills 3, Chiefs 0 Second quarter On third-and-10, Patrick Mahomes tossed a pass to Travis Kelce on a tight end screen gaining eight yards. Opting to go for it on fourth-and-two, Mahomes went back to Kelce, but the pass was knocked down, and the Chiefs turned the ball over on downs. The Bills quickly went three-and-out. Kansas City then connected on a 20-yard catch-and-run to Rashee Rice, reaching the Bills’ 47-yard line. However, the drive stalled, and the Chiefs punted the ball back to Buffalo. The Bills picked up a first down on a 19-yard pass to Dalton Kincaid before crossing midfield and facing fourth-and-six. Josh Allen rifled a pass to a streaking James Cook, who picked up the first down and more, reaching the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. Kincaid snagged a pass in the end zone for the game’s first touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the quarter. The Chiefs managed to steal some points before halftime, as Harrison Butker drilled a field goal. End of second quarter: Bills 10, Chiefs 3 Third quarter Wide receiver Khalil Shakir caught a corner route for 25 yards before being stopped at the Chiefs’ 23-yard line. Shakir followed that up with another catch to move Buffalo to the 12. James Cook found the end zone on a comeback route along the goal line for a receiving touchdown. Patrick Mahomes took off for a first-down run, gaining 18 yards to reach the Chiefs’ 45-yard line. Mahomes then connected with Josh Downs on a streak route to move Kansas City to the Bills’ 35. A Bills defender knocked away another third-down pass intended for Kelce. Butker then missed a 52-yard field goal attempt. Shakir caught a wide-open pass over the middle for a 29-yard gain, setting up another scoring opportunity for Buffalo. Cook reached the end zone once again, this time on the ground, with a 19-yard run to the right side for another touchdown. End of third quarter: Bills 24, Chiefs 3 Fourth quarter The Chiefs started the quarter with the ball at the Bills’ 40-yard line. Ed Oliver got to Mahomes for a seven-yard loss, but Mahomes responded by finding a streaking Worthy behind the Bills’ secondary for a 47-yard touchdown in the back of the end zone. James Cook continued to take over the game, gaining 36 yards on the drive, including a 10-yard touchdown run for his third touchdown of the game. Coming out of the two-minute warning, Jalen Royals caught a slant from Mahomes and reached the Bills’ four-yard line. The Chiefs couldn’t capitalize, failing to score a touchdown and turning the ball over on downs. Final score: Bills 31, Chiefs 10 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 29 for 42 passing, 316 yards, 1 touchdown, 2 rushing attempts, 20 yards Emmett Johnson: 4 rushing attempts, -1 yard, 6 receptions, 50 yards. Josh Downs: 9 receptions, 81 yards. Xavier Worthy: 5 receptions, 84 yards, 1 touchdown. Rashee Rice: 3 receptions, 47 yards. Travis Kelce: 3 receptions, 29 yards George Karlaftis: 4 tackles for loss, .5 sack. Chris Jones: 2 tackles for loss, .5 sack. Felix Anudike-Uzomah: .5 sack Josh Allen: 16 for 22 passing, 187 yards, 2 touchdowns James Cook III: 15 rushing attempts, 135 yards, 2 touchdowns, 3 receptions, 38 yards, 1 touchdown. Khalil Shakir: 7 receptions, 87 yards. Dalton Kincaid: 5 receptions, 57 yards, 1 touchdown Ed Oliver: 1 sack Deon Walker: 1 sack Joe Andreessen: 1 sack Next week, the Chiefs are once again playing Thursday Night Football, this time taking on the Los Angeles Rams. Until then, we will see how it plays out inside the EA Universe.

title: Week 12 AP NFL Power Rankings: Chiefs climb to Top 3 ahead of Thanksgiving matchup
summary: Somehow, it’s already Thanksgiving. I don’t know how we got here, but here we are. It’s almost 2027, folks. full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Somehow, it’s already Thanksgiving. I don’t know how we got here, but here we are. It’s almost 2027, folks. In my opinion, Thanksgiving weekend is the second-best weekend of football after the Divisional Playoff weekend. This Thanksgiving is shaping up to be no different. Each game scheduled for Wednesday-Friday could have major playoff implications. Yes, we are being treated to a Thanksgiving appetizer with a “Thanksgiving Eve” game on Wednesday night between the Packers and Rams. This is followed by a huge NFC North matchup between the Bears and Lions on Thanksgiving, an NFC East battle between the Eagles and Cowboys that afternoon, leading up to the nightcap of the AFC rivals Chiefs and Bills. Finally, Black Friday will bring us the Broncos versus Steelers as both teams are fighting to maintain their playoff positions. Before this feast of football on Thanksgiving week, let’s take a look back at Week 11 and where each team stands in this week’s edition of the Arrowhead Pride Power Rankings. In honor of Thanksgiving, and to perhaps stir up even more debate, we’ll tier-rank the teams according to the best Thanksgiving side dishes. As I think we can all agree—the best food on the Thanksgiving table, and what makes a Thanksgiving dinner worth having—are the side dishes. Biggest riser: New York Giants +4 Biggest fallers: Cincinnati Bengals and Arizona Cardinals -4 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . Turkey stuffing tier The Thanksgiving plate is not complete without it, and it’s so good you go back for seconds. 1. San Francisco 49ers (1st) Right now, they’re the class of the NFL. The unanimous number one overall team by the AP staff. 2. Buffalo Bills (2nd) This team remains high in the power rankings, but Josh Allen continues to try and give the ball away to his opponents. 3. Kansas City Chiefs (6th) They took care of business in the three-game stretch against inferior opponents. Now we find out what the Chiefs are truly made of. 4. Chicago Bears (5th) A win on the road in Detroit on Turkey Day would give the Bears the definitive edge in the NFC North. Huge game upcoming. 5. Denver Broncos (8th) Running back Jonah Coleman adds a whole other dimension to this offense. 6. Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd) They looked like the Jaguars of old on Sunday. 7. Detroit Lions (9th) The quietest 8-2 record of any team—ever? 8. Cincinnati Bengals (4th) Their lack of a rushing attack could be a major problem in January. Potatoes Tier Mashed, sweet, baked, au gratin—these teams are quality but can look vastly different from week to week. 9. Minnesota Vikings (7th) Outclassed in Mexico City in all phases. Kirk Cousins was great last week, but didn’t do much to help this team against the current top-ranked team. 10. New York Giants (14th) Well coached, great pass rush, serviceable play from the quarterback position. Cam Skattebo could blow it at any moment. 11. Seattle Seahawks (10th) They desperately need to figure out a way to win in San Francisco on Thanksgiving weekend. They will have the rest advantage coming off their bye week, while the 49ers are returning from their second international trip of the season in Mexico 12. Los Angeles Rams (11th) Now is the time for the offseason champs to turn it on and make their postseason run. As it stands currently, they’ll be in Cancun come January. 13. Green Bay Packers (12th) This offensive line has looked porous, and a matchup against Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald is not the Thanksgiving appetizer they were surely hoping for. Rolls tier At times, great and can be game-changing. But if not homemade, it’s not worth having on the table. 14. Cleveland Browns (13th) With the Bengals bungling their Monday night contest, the Browns only sit one game back for the AFC North crown. 15. Houston Texans (15th) Their hopes at a postseason berth hinge on the continued collapse of the Steelers. 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (16th) 4-0 at home and 2-4 on the road. Black Friday at home against the Broncos…so there’s a chance? Casseroles tier The “mid” tier. It can fill you up, but you don’t always know what you’re eating. 17. Carolina Panthers (18th) One week Bryce Young will look like an MVP candidate, and the next he’ll look like that confused rookie we once knew. 18. New England Patriots (17th) Is Daniel Jones a future New England Patriot? 19. Dallas Cowboys (21st) The only team in the NFC East to not have a win against a team with a winning record. 20. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (20th) This roster seems more talented than the product on the field we are seeing. Todd Bowles’ days in Tampa seem numbered. 21. Las Vegas Raiders (19th) Fernando Mendoza may be the real deal. But they are currently only an average football team. 22. Washington Commanders (23rd) Huge win on Monday night. They avenge some of their own late-game management blunders. 23. Atlanta Falcons (22nd) We’ll see if the bye week is the reset this team clearly needed. Bijan, my fantasy team needs you. 24. New Orleans Saints (24th) Jordyn Tyson cooled off, while Chris Olive had a big day receiving. Alas, it still was not enough. Cranberry sauce tier This can be left off the Thanksgiving menu. 25. Baltimore Ravens (25th) The Ravens are in the midst of a six-game losing streak. Their point differential in those six games? 96 points for and 175 points against. 26. Philadelphia Eagles (28th) They won the Pennsylvania Bowl but still sit in last place in the NFC East after all four teams won this week. Mathematically, they are still in the running for the NFC East with their third quarterback of the season. 27. New York Jets (26th) Playing the Los Angeles Chargers is like passing go and collecting $200 in Monopoly. 28. Tennessee Titans (29th) 30 points against the Cowboys’ defense is nothing to write home about. Head coach Robert Saleh still called it “disgusting football.” 29. Indianapolis Colts (30th) This franchise makes no sense…offered a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones, only to decline the offer and then release him for peanuts a week later. 30. Miami Dolphins (32nd) Did the Dolphins’ defense actually expose Josh Allen? 31. Arizona Cardinals (27th) Seeing Trey McBride battling on such a poor roster reminded me of the days of Tony Gonzalez with the Chiefs. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (31st) Jim Harbaugh looks totally lost and confused—on the sidelines and in his press conferences.
