title: Rams PFF grades: Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett turn back clock
summary: The first NFL pre-Thanksgiving game brought a delicious victory for the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. LA defeated the Green Bay Packers 26-13 to move to 7-4 on the season. After starting 2-4, winning five-straight didn’t seem to be in the cards. Their fortune seems to be shifting even in the face of injury. […]
full_text: The first NFL pre-Thanksgiving game brought a delicious victory for the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. LA defeated the Green Bay Packers 26-13 to move to 7-4 on the season. After starting 2-4, winning five-straight didn’t seem to be in the cards. Their fortune seems to be shifting even in the face of injury. Who stood out on an individual level from this game? Let’s review the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades and data in order to lean into some analytical takeaways. *Final grades are not currently available as of the writing of this post. Due to the Thanksgiving holiday I am going to run with the data still under review. Close enough. Top five grades on offense 1 – Konata Mumpfield, WR: 77.0 Mumpfield was the Rams’ passing offense on Wednesday night. He earned 69 yards on four catches and provided the only threat vertically. The next closest pass catchers in terms of yardage were Blake Corum at 21 and Kyren Williams at 19. Xavier Smith was the only other receiver to catch a pass and his solo reception went for four yards. Is that a reliable way to play offense and win games? Not really. The Rams must find better answers from their receiver group. They cannot rely on Davante Adams to completely reverse their fortunes on his own, especially coming back from a significant injury this late into his career. Gorgeous route from Mumpfield. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/IgMO6MGy9y — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 2 – Justin Dedich, LG: 76.2 Dedich filled in for the injured Bill Murray who had replaced Steve Avila in the starting lineup. Dedich always seems to fare well in terms of PFF grading, and it’s encouraging to see him pickup where he left off after suffering an injury this summer that has limited his availability. Dedich is undersized. That may prevent him from ever becoming a full-time starter. He still has value in a reserve role. 3 – Tyler Higbee, TE: 75.2 Veteran tight end Tyler Higbee’s most important contributions came as a run blocker where he earned a mark from PFF of 70.2. He added one catch for 14 yards and came close to another big play. Higbee played roughly half the game before suffering an injury and being ruled out. Davis Allen was also ruled out. The statuses of both are worth monitoring moving forward. 4 – Blake Corum, RB: 71.6 What more is there to say about Blake Corum’s performance not just Wednesday night but over the last seven weeks? Against the Packers he grinded out 184 yards and a score for an average of 5.80. PFF credited the back with 103 yards after contact (3.22 average). The offensive line was road grading as well, as they generated 2.58 yards before contact on Corum’s carries. Not a bad day at the office. BLAKE CORUM COMING THROUGH. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/vxYuIWEU93 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 5 – Beaux Limmer, C: 70.9 It would be a welcome development—given the amount of players across the Rams’ roster that need new contracts—if Limmer could takeover the starting center job on a going forward basis. Injured starter Coleman Shelton is approaching the end of his 2025 free agent deal. Limmer has one year left on his rookie contract. He continues to excel in pass protection in the middle of the offensive line. Other notes on offense Matthew Stafford finished 17th in grades out of the 19 players who appeared on offense. PFF graded him at a mark of 54.2. The outlet did not credit the veteran quarterback with a single big-time throw. He had one turnover-worthy play that resulted into an interception that could have proved costly; however, Jordan Love made a mistake of his own just two plays later. Stafford has now thrown an interception in all but two of 11 games this season. He’s at 11 on the year, so averaging one per game in the aggregate. If the Rams are going to be limited offensively and lean into ball control into order to constrict the opposition into submission, one requirement of that is taking care of the football. Can the Rams trust Stafford in this area? His track record so far this year suggests not. Rams fans are waiting for Stafford to turn his season around. It hasn’t happened yet. He’s still the 21st-graded quarterback by both offensive grade and passing grade. It’s clear he has taken a major step back this year. The end could be nearer than expected. It’s difficult to say anything other than 2027 seems to be Ty Simpson’s year to takeover. Matthew Stafford with a meatball sub One of the WORST INTs of the season. pic.twitter.com/D56tKeTSDy — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) November 26, 2026 Top five grades on defense 1 – Aaron Donald, DT: 93.5 Donald and Garrett each had five total pressures on Jordan Love even though neither finished with a sack. The Rams only brought down Love once (Bryon Young), although the pressure did ultimately force three turnovers by the Pakcers’ offense. Love easily could have finished with at least five interceptions—including dropped picks by Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie and a takeaway by Kam Curl that was reversed because of penalty. 2 – Kamren Kinchens, DB: 90.5 Kinchens forced a major collision along the sideline with receiver Christian Watson that dramatically altered the rest of the game. Kinchens was ejected, which resulted in controversy. Watson entered concussion protocol and was ruled out for the second half. The Rams seemingly had no answers for the dynamic receiver up to that point, and the Packers had little going through the air in the second half without Watson. Closer look at the hit that Kamren Kinchens was ejected for pic.twitter.com/SZERA2rlI0 — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 26, 2026 3 – Myles Garrett, EDGE: 90.2 4 – Nate Landman, MLB: 89.9 Make it another hallmark punch out for Nate Landman. He stole the ball away from tight end Tucker Kraft for a key takeaway. The veteran linebacker played just 25 snaps. Omar Speights had 10. Shaun Dolac played seven. The roles of these players are changing as Lake took over the green dot duties. That isn’t necessarily a bad thing. The defensive line is limiting opposing rushing attacks on their own. The Rams are able to pivot more towards additional safeties to focus on tightening up through the air. It’s working. Stick with it. 5 – Quentin Lake, DB: 89.4 Lake finished with the second-highest coverage grade on the defense (87.0) behind only Landman (90.5). He dropped an interception that likely would have scored and put the Packers away even earlier. In total he finished with two pass breakups. Other notes on defense The Packers went after reserve corners Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes often with mixed results. Each had four targets into their coverage. Wallace allowed three receptions for 15 yards and the touchdown to Watson. Forbes gave up three catches for 79 yards (36 after the catch) and he caught the interception that effectively sealed the game. While their PFF marks were low relative to the other members of the defense (18th and 19th out of 20), these coverage numbers aren’t something that will get you beat. The standard is not perfection for these players as they look to replace injured starter Jaylen Watson. There will be negative moments. The Rams must hope that the positives—like Forbes’ interception—outweigh the bad.
author: JB Scott

title: Blake Corum is the Rams’ best running back
summary: Blake Corum was incredible for the Los Angeles Rams in their Week 12 win over the Green Bay Packers. He was nearly unstoppable as he gashed through the Green Bay defense, carrying the offense in a 26-13 victory. Not only was Corum the best player in the game, he solidified himself as RB1 for the […]
full_text: Blake Corum was incredible for the Los Angeles Rams in their Week 12 win over the Green Bay Packers. He was nearly unstoppable as he gashed through the Green Bay defense, carrying the offense in a 26-13 victory. Not only was Corum the best player in the game, he solidified himself as RB1 for the Rams going forward. Los Angeles has the luxury of rotating between two starting-caliber running backs in Corum and Kyren Williams. If you don’t think that’s an enviable place to be, go look at the Rams’ opponents from Wednesday night, whose leading rusher was a wide receiver in a losing effort. Williams has been a positive contributor for the Rams for years and still is right now. But when push came to shove in the biggest game of the season so far , Sean McVay put his faith in Corum. Blake Corum celebrated his 26th birthday with the best game of his NFL career against Green Bay. 32 CAR, 184 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 2 REC, 21 REC YDS. With a rushing attack like this, the Rams have everything they need to make a Super Bowl run. https://t.co/ihXa9lX4LH pic.twitter.com/LF8VibPU0E — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 26, 2026 Clearly, he was rewarded for his belief. This season, Corum has tallied more yardage on fewer carries than Williams, and he was the go-to option in a game the Rams truly could not afford to lose. The third-year pro posted 33 carries for 184 yards in the win over the Packers; that’s the highest number of carries for a Ram since Zac Stacy in 2013, and it’s the most single-game yardage for a Ram since Todd Gurley in 2018. It should be noted that Corum was doing this behind a depleted offensive line, too, with a pair of starters out (not to mention the holes due to injury across the rest of the offensive roster). Part of that is the Packers’ porous run defense, which has now given up the two highest individual rushing totals of the season, but still, it’s not as if he had wide-open running lanes all night. According to Next Gen Stats, Corum had 150 yards after contact on Wednesday night. The Rams becoming a successful service academy offense with multiple backup offensive linemen just because Blake Corum just doesn’t go down at first contact is so wild — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 26, 2026 There’s something to be said for riding the hot hand, and that’s definitely part of what went into Wednesday’s Corum-heavy second half. After all, Ronnie Rivers had a turn being the workhorse last time out in a win over the Arizona Cardinals. But this is back-to-back weeks that Corum has out-touched Williams. And, as mentioned above, his full-season stats have been even more efficient while scoring at a nearly identical clip (Corum has six rushing touchdowns, Williams has seven after Week 12). Most rush yards in a game this season Bijan Robinson 194 (Week 3) Blake Corum 184 (Week 12) ⬅️ Kenneth Walker III 177 (Week 4) Kenneth Walker III 173 (Week 1) Bucky Irving 170 (Week 8) pic.twitter.com/Cwo2yfFgQU — PFF (@PFF) November 26, 2026 Williams should still play plenty of snaps down the stretch, obviously. He’s still a good player, it’s not like he’s chopped liver compared to Corum. And by splitting the snaps between two backs, you’re ideally keeping both a bit fresher for a potential postseason run. Just ask the Seattle Seahawks and Kenneth Walker III about how much of a boon it is to have a fresh running back in January and February. But as things stand today, the best running back the Rams have is Blake Corum. For a running game that is not just efficient but can also completely take over a game like we just saw, the focal point right now should be Corum, no matter what the other back in the rotation has accomplished before.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: RAMalytics: 3 stats that defined Rams’ win over Packers
summary: A 26-13 win isn’t exactly a blowout. Then again, the Los Angeles Rams completely suffocated the Green Bay Packers by dominating time of possession—especially in the second half. Blake Corum was the boa constrictor. He amassed over 200 total yards on the game with at least 180 and a score on the ground alone. The […]
full_text: A 26-13 win isn’t exactly a blowout. Then again, the Los Angeles Rams completely suffocated the Green Bay Packers by dominating time of possession—especially in the second half. Blake Corum was the boa constrictor. He amassed over 200 total yards on the game with at least 180 and a score on the ground alone. The Rams’ rushing attack was productive despite Davis Allen, Tyler Higbee, Warren McClendon, and Bill Murray all leaving the game due to injury. The Rams can hang their hat on this impressive victory, although the slate does not let up any time soon. Before we turn the page, these are 3 stats that defined LA’s win over Green Bay: #1 – Defense is leading the way Sure, it helps that across LA’s five-game winning streak the first four victories came against middling-at-best competition. Still, in their last six outings, the Rams allowed just four touchdowns. Myles Garrett wasn’t available for that full stretch. Trent McDuffie either. They are still finding a way to get the job done. The biggest tell that LA dominated Jordan Love and company? The Packers offense finished with 244 total yards while Corum accumulated 205 himself. Kyren Williams added another 65 yards and a score. #2 – Blake Corum’s takeover It was jarring to see Corum open the game in the backfield. I’ve grown accustomed to seeing Kyren Williams earn the start, even if running back workload has been fairly split in recent years. The Rams have come to understand that Corum gives them a more dynamic option on the ground. When they needed an offensive spark this season, Corum provided that while very little else is working. LA is taking the path of least resistance and leaning on their best playmaker. The most impressive part of Corum’s performance? He finished with 99 yards after contact against the Packers. If those were all of his yards on Wednesday night, that is a strong individual performance. He broke tackles and created yardage that wasn’t readily there to a final output of 184 rushing yards. According to SumerSports, Corum had an EPA per rush of +0.19. It’s rare to see an EPA per rush that isn’t negative across the NFL. #3 – Dominating time of possession For the full game, the Rams held the ball for 40:40 versus the Packers’ 19:20 . On the surface that lends itself to winning. When you split the time of possession by half (23:45 to 6.55) , you realize Green Bay really had no opportunity to mount a comeback. Corum and the Rams were playing keep away. The defense was also able to force turnovers even when Love and the Packers offense was on the field. Green Bay’s offense largely watched their demise from the sidelines. The Rams similarly dominated the second half against the Arizona Cardinals last week. This is their second-straight game—and only the second game across the entire NFL season so far—where a team accumulated more than 24 minutes of possession in the second half. You can’t win if you can’t score. By playing complimentary football, the Rams aren’t even giving opposing offenses a chance to do so.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams-Packers takeaways: Shake & Blake!
summary: The Los Angeles Rams made a statement on Thanksgiving Eve, taking down the Green Bay Packers 26-13 in a dominant performance on both sides of the football. With the regular season entering its most important stretch, the Rams delivered the type of complementary football that can make them a dangerous team come January. There were […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 25: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against Isaiah McDuffie #58 and Brandon Cisse #2 of the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on November 25, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams made a statement on Thanksgiving Eve, taking down the Green Bay Packers 26-13 in a dominant performance on both sides of the football. With the regular season entering its most important stretch, the Rams delivered the type of complementary football that can make them a dangerous team come January. There were plenty of reasons to be thankful for this performance, but two things stood out above the rest: a powerful running game and a defense that made life miserable for Jordan Love and the Packers’ offense. Blake Corum helped lead the charge on the ground, while the Rams’ defensive stars made sure Green Bay never found much rhythm. Let’s break down the biggest takeaways from a Thanksgiving Eve victory. 1st Down: The Rams know their identity In 2025, the Rams identity was to let Matthew Stafford cook. They rode the arm of the veteran quarterback and he turned in an MVP season. But with a slew of injuries to the offense and Stafford not quite playing up to par in 2026, Sean McVay adapted the offense; using 20 and 13 personnel. McVay has leaned into the running game – working Kyren Williams and Blake Corum to wear down defenses. 44 running plays tonight! On the other side of the ball, Chris Shula’s defense just continues to stifle offenses. The defensive line pressure on the quarterback and the secondary’s suffocation of perimeter options leaves little weakness on the defensive side of the ball. 2nd Down: Shake & Blake! If you did not think there was a new RB1 for the Rams yet, you have to believe now. The Rams fed Corum to the tune of 32 rushing attempts. Happy Birthday to Blake Corum for a historic game and Thanksgiving Eve player of the game! Blake Corum now up to 184 yards rushing 😳 pic.twitter.com/xOJ3Oa2ejO — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 3rd Down: Special Teams are … Back?! Brandon McManus connected on all 4 field goals. Ronnie Rivers averaged 25.5 yards per kickoff return. Xavier Smith had a 15 yard punt return. Ethan Evans had a punt inside the 20. The Rams simply won the field position battle with quality execution with their special teams. Perhaps they have turned a corner? 4th Down: Fearsome White Another second half shutout by the Los Angeles Rams defense. Incredible. That’s how you honor the 1960s Fearsome Foursome unit. In addition, the Rams did not give up a first quarter touchdown for the 12th consecutive game. Wild time of possession this half. pic.twitter.com/HspcdfOYGF — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026
author: Steven Ridings

title: Two more tight ends hurt in latest win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams saw tight ends Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen leave their win over the Green Bay Packers early due to injury. The Rams, like many NFL teams, have had a hard time staying healthy, but somehow the Rams are finding ways to win. L.A. has won five games in a row to […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams saw tight ends Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen leave their win over the Green Bay Packers early due to injury. The Rams, like many NFL teams, have had a hard time staying healthy, but somehow the Rams are finding ways to win. L.A. has won five games in a row to rise toa 7-4 record. The Rams are in the playoff race, but they’ll need to keep winning to stay there. Will the Rams be able to keep winning with all their injuries? Fair question. The Rams get some time before their next game against the Kansas City Chiefs to get healthy. Parkinson quiet despite losses of Higbee, Allen (nbcsports) “Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. The Rams have some things to figure out given the sheer number of bodies missing after also losing two offensive linemen in the game. The long week hopefully affords them enough time to return to health ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Chiefs. – Mark Garcia ” Rams ride Blake Corum to Thanksgiving Eve win over Packers; Jordan Love throws 2 INTs with Christian Watson out (sports.yahoo) “A pair of highlight-reel plays thrust Green Bay right back into the thick of things. LaFleur turned to trickery initially, with wideout Savion Williams taking a handoff and throwing the ball back to Love, who went on to fling a pass downfield to Watson. His toe-tapping 21-yard reception was followed by a 39-yard catch and run from another receiver, Matthew Golden. Watson was the one who found pay dirt, reeling in a 6-yard touchdown pass from Love midway through the second quarter. That score cut the Packers’ deficit to 13-10. Watson’s night came to a premature end on Green Bay’s next drive. LaFleur rolled the dice on fourth-and-1 from the L.A. 30-yard line, and it originally looked like that decision was going to be rewarded. Love located Watson for what would have been a chains-moving pickup, except the pass was broken up by a brutal blow from Kinchens near the sideline that leveled Watson.“ NFL Urged to Suspend ‘Dirty’ Rams Player After Ejection From Packers Game (sports.yahoo) “Kamren Kinchens Facing More Punishment After Ejection From Rams Game Others defended Kinchens, noting that it might not have even been worth a flag, let alone an ejection. The decision was not made solely by the officials on the ground, though, which is an important note. “I spoke with Wald Anderson in New York, and he said the defender leaves his feet, he launches and makes forcible contact to the head and neck area–using his helmet–to the opponent,” Netflix’s Terry McAulay said during the broadcast. “But the final decision-maker is the executive vice president of football operations, Troy Vincent, and he determined this was flagrant and that No. 5 should be disqualified.” The Rams win their biggest game of the year over the Packers (usatoday) “Packers star receiver Christian Watson took a big hit in the first half by Rams safety Kamren Kinchens and did not return. Kinchens was also ejected from the game as a result of the hit. The game featured the home debut of Myles Garrett and the return of Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons . Parsons had not played since tearing his ACL on December 14, 2025. Here’s everything else you may have missed from the “Thanksgiving Eve” game.“ Rams Fall Victim to Another Controversial Call With Kam Kinchens Ejection (si.com) “According to the Netflix broadcast, rules analyst Terry McAulay noted that because Kinchens left his feet and hit Watson in the head with his helmet, the play warranted an ejection. While the hit was violent, it seems excessive for him to have been ejected. While players will get ejected for targeting at the college level, that’s not something that’s seen very often in the NFL. Players can be ejected for two qualifying unsportsmanlike conduct penalties. However, this was Kinchens’ first penalty. Officials also have the option of disqualifying a player for a flagrant act. Kinchens’ hit was deemed to be flagrant” Rams Week 12 rooting guide: 3 games that can help LA’s playoff odds (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams handled their business to start Thanksgiving week, taking down the Green Bay Packers in a 26-13 win on Wednesday night. Now, they wait and see if they get any help from other teams around the league on Thursday and Sunday afternoon. According to The Athletic , the Rams have a 47% chance to make the playoffs after Wednesday’s win. There are three games that can swing their odds a few percentage points if the results go Los Angeles’ way. Here’s a rooting guide for the rest of Week 12.“ Packers-Rams on Wednesday night: What We Learned from Los Angeles’ 26-13 win over Green Bay (nfl.com) “ Rams make a statement . Entering this game, it was fair to expect the Packers could prevail as part of their playoff push. The Rams were playing with an offense held together by duct tape and chewing gum and had defeated a quartet of opponents (the Raiders, Chargers, Commanders, Cardinals) that weren’t exactly the NFL’s version of The Expendables . In terms of reputation, the Packers entered Wednesday night with more respect for their potential than the opposition could boast. The Rams decided to shove that skepticism right back in the direction from which it came Wednesday night by leaning deeper into their new identity, riding the running game to dominate time of possession and grind the Packers down to a pulp. Matthew Stafford only needed to complete 16 of 23 passes for 140 yards, threw an interception that could have been pivotal, and ended up not worrying about it for more than roughly 55 seconds. The Rams won the physical battle in the trenches against the Packers’ beleaguered offensive line, shut down Green Bay’s offense entirely in the second half and walked away with a resounding win that not only moved them to 7-4, but will likely make the rest of the NFL take them seriously again.“ Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett & Blake Corum Reflect On Week 12 Win Over the Packers (youtube/rams) “Los Angeles Rams press conference with head coach Sean McVay, quarterback Matthew Stafford, outside linebacker Myles Garrett, and running back Blake Corum following Wednesday’s 26-13 Week 12 win over the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium.” Game Recap: Blake Corum’s 184 rushing yards, defense’s timely playmaking lift Rams to 26-13 win over Packers on Thanksgiving Eve (rams.com) “INGLEWOOD, Calif. – Behind a career performance by running back Blake Corum and timely playmaking by their defense, the Rams defeated the Packers 23-13 Wednesday night at SoFi Stadium to extend their win streak to five games. Corum led Los Angeles in rushing with 32 carries for 184 yards and one touchdown, the rushing yards a new single-game career high. Meanwhile, running back Kyren Williams added 12 carries for 46 yards and one touchdown. Including the two carries by wide receiver Xavier Smith , and excluding Stafford’s one scramble, the Rams finished with twice as many rush attempts (46) as a team as pass attempts (23).“ Nate Landman, Kyren Williams & Kamren Kinchens Recap Fifth Straight Win After Beating the Packers (youtube.com) “Los Angeles Rams inside linebacker Nate Landman, running back Kyren Williams, and safety Kamren Kinchens recap the Rams’ fifth straight win after beating the Green Bay Packers 26-13 in Week 12 at SoFi Stadium.” Comment(s) of the day: Feed post(s) of the day:

title: Trent McDuffie proved worth in win over Packers
summary: The defense led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Chris Shula’s unit forced three takeaways and allowed just 13 points to an opposing offense that can put up points in a hurry. One of the stronger individual performers? Trent McDuffie, one of LA’s prized offseason acquisitions. […]
full_text: The defense led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Chris Shula’s unit forced three takeaways and allowed just 13 points to an opposing offense that can put up points in a hurry. One of the stronger individual performers? Trent McDuffie, one of LA’s prized offseason acquisitions. SumerSports charted 26 passing plays where McDuffie was matched up directly with a Packers receiver. You can’t realistically expect nor ask for better results. 11 plays vs Matthew Golden: 2 targets, 0 catches allowed 6 plays vs Christian Watson: 0 targets, 0 catches allowed 4 plays vs Tucker Kraft: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 3 plays vs Savion Williams: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 2 plays vs Bo Melton: 1 target, 1 catch for 12 yards While the Rams overall had trouble slowing down Watson, who accumulated four first-half receptions for 65 yards and a score before missing the second half due to injury, McDuffie was one of the defenders able to slow down his momentum. Kraft is one of the NFL’s top tight ends and the Rams held him to just three catches for 24 yards. Nate Landman punched out a fumble shortly after one of those receptions for a key defensive takeaway. All-in-all, Jordan Love finished with just 17 completions on 29 passes (59%) for 198 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 62.1. This was an impressive outing for the Los Angeles defense. They limited Love and company even without the team’s other high-profile offseason addition at cornerback, Jaylen Watson. Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace were also stingy in coverage, and that is a positive sign for the remainder of the season. Watson will not return in 2026. Even more positive is the fact the Packers had very little production on the ground. Savion Williams was the most efficient with two carries for 18 yards. Kaleb Johnson was held to 13 yards on eight carries (1.6 average). Byron Young and Myles Garrett each made notable tackles for loss that put Green Bay behind the chains. The Rams have now won five-straight games. Their previous four wins were against weaker competition. The defense is demonstrating they can get the job done even when facing superior quarterback talents and overall stronger opponents. Whether that is true for the offense remains to be seen. What is obvious is that the Rams are a defensive-led team in their current state. On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie proved his worth to a defense that is performing at a high level.

title: Rams Winners & Losers: LA beats Packers to bolster playoff odds
summary: It’s no secret that Wednesday’s pre-Thanksgiving matchup between the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers carried immense weight for both teams’ playoff chances. The Rams took care of business behind Blake Corum’s big rushing day on his birthday. They dealt a near-death blow to Green Bay’s postseason odds. The schedule to get to the […]
full_text: It’s no secret that Wednesday’s pre-Thanksgiving matchup between the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers carried immense weight for both teams’ playoff chances . The Rams took care of business behind Blake Corum’s big rushing day on his birthday. They dealt a near-death blow to Green Bay’s postseason odds. The schedule to get to the playoffs is still long and littered with stiff competition. That is a tomorrow problem. For today, let’s take inventory of all the individual contributions that led the Rams to their most important win on the season yet. Winners Blake Corum, RB Corum made it seven-straight games with a touchdown. He has officially taken the starting running back job from Kyren Williams and continues to outshine his counterpart in terms of production. The third-year back rushed 32 times (!) for 184 yards (5.8 average) and a touchdown. He also added two catches for 21 yards through the air. The Rams have needed an offensive spark nearly all season. It’s clear that Corum has been the answer and is someone the team must rely on moving forward in order to make due on their sky-high expectations. Blake Corum now up to 184 yards rushing 😳 pic.twitter.com/xOJ3Oa2ejO — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Aaron Donald & Myles Garrett Jordan Love is not a quarterback that gets sacked often, even if his pass protection is often porous these days. Donald and Garrett were key to generating pressure. Love was only brought down a single time by Byron Young. The pressure helped force Love into some very curious decisions—of which resulted in key takeaways by the defense. Donald and Garrett are as advertised , even if they are hitting their stride later into the season than originally expected. MYLES GARRETT WITH THE TFL! #RamsHouse |📺 @NetflixSports pic.twitter.com/u5kylwSvFS — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 26, 2026 Perseverance on offensive line You don’t rush for 241 yards without a strong performance from the big guys up front. The Rams got the job done even with injuries that caused linemen to play out of position. Warren McClendon, Bill Murray, Tyler Higbee, and Davis Allen all dealt with injuries at some point. Rookie Keagen Trost, Justin Dedich, and David Quessenberry all played parts in relief. The perseverance from this group in an all-important game was impressive. Konata Mumpfield, WR With no Puka Nacua for the rest of the season and Davante Adams’ return to health timeline currently uncertain, the only pass catcher who seems interested in stepping up is second-year receiver Konata Mumpfield. He added four receptions for 69 yards on Wednesday night. He also snagged a ball at the goal line that was originally called a touchdown and later reversed to incomplete. It was probably at least a completion even if the touchdown call was borderline and the ball short of the end zone. Mumpfield’s step forward is an encouraging sign for the offense. Their passing game is not where it needs to be. Mumpfield’s production with Adams back in the fold should help matters. Terrible Call: #Rams WR Konata Mumpfield had this catch Ball doesn’t move 2 feet in and controls it through the ground. Just rule it a catch MY GOSH pic.twitter.com/epNJ5WTuPQ — FirstDownMedia (@FirstDownMediaa) November 26, 2026 Josaiah Stewart, OLB Wesley Bailey and Josaiah Stewart are still playing sizeable rotational roles on defense. Last week Bailey snagged an interception. Against the Packers, Stewart made multiple key plays in coverage to prevent big gains. You won’t see Garrett in coverage often—the Rams want him moving towards the quarterback. Someone has to do the dirty work and play the linebacker role. Stewart did an excellent job in this facet versus Green Bay. Losers Matthew Stafford, QB With the Rams up one score late into the third quarter, Matthew Stafford threw an inexplicable first-down interception right to a Packers defender. It was a chance for Green Bay and Love to regain momentum, although Love made an even worse throw for a turnover just two plays later. The Rams stubbed their toe. The Packers let them off the hook. It’s still an open question whether the Rams have enough juice in the passing game to keep up with the likes of the Chiefs, 49ers, Cowboys, and Seahawks—all teams they will see in the coming weeks. Stafford must be better both in terms of production and in his decision making. It’s tough to win games when your leading rusher has more yards than your quarterback (184 versus 140). First Stafford throws an Int… pic.twitter.com/rRiARSbN25 — MyBookie – Bet With The Best (@MyBookie) November 26, 2026 Passing game But the passing game struggles do not rest entirely on Stafford’s shoulders. The receiving corps aside from Mumpfield is not inspiring confidence. The injuries at the tight end position from this game spell concern moving forward. Sean McVay’s play calling leaned more towards “don’t lose” then “go for the win”. LA was reliant on screen passes that often went for minimal gain and there were a few close laterals that could have resulted in disaster. Something needs to change. Do the Rams have the right players in order to turn things around, or will the passing attack be the reason they fall short of Super Bowl expectations?

full_text: The Los Angeles Rams won on Wednesday night to move to 7-4, and they are now officially in a playoff spot for the first time this season after five straight wins. They came into Week 12 tied with the Seattle Seahawks and the Green Bay Packers, but the previous tiebreakers favored Seattle so L.A. was on the outside losing in. The win over the Packers knocked Green Bay down and L.A. is a half-game ahead of Seattle — for now. The Seahawks play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. If Seattle wins, they would move back ahead of the Rams based on their superior division record. The Minnesota Vikings at 7-3 are just a half-game in front of the Rams at this point, too. If they win, they stay ahead of L.A., as well. If either Seattle or Minnesota lose, the Rams hold onto their playoff spot. The Seahawks would fall to 6-5 and a game behind the Rams. A Vikings loss would drop them to 7-4 in a tie with the Rams but also give them their third NFC loss, meaning the Rams would be ahead of them in the conference record tiebreaker. If both outcomes happen, the Rams would jump from ninth in Week 11 all the way to sixth after Week 12. title: Rams vs. Packers final score: L.A. wins their biggest game of the year
summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers by a final score of 26-13 in the first ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL Game. Blake Corum powered the Rams to this win with 184 yards on the ground with 32 carries. It was an incredible performance by the third-year player. L.A.’s defense also forced a fumble […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers by a final score of 26-13 in the first ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL Game. Blake Corum powered the Rams to this win with 184 yards on the ground with 32 carries. It was an incredible performance by the third-year player. L.A.’s defense also forced a fumble and two interceptions to support their offense, and notch this crucial win for the Rams and their playoff odds. The Rams jumped out to a 6-0, and then 13-3 lead in the second quarter when Kyren Williams found the endzone for the first touchdown of the day, but the Packers scored 10 unanswered point of their own to tie the game at 13-13 going into halftime. Christian Watson was on pace for a massive game with four receptions for 65 yards and score, but a hit by Kam Kinchens ended Watson’s night with a concussion. Kinchens was ejected for the hit on Watson as both players saw their nights end early. The Rams drove down the field to open the second half and when Blake Corum found the endzone for his first touchdown of the day, the Rams had a 20-13 lead after the extra point. L.A.’s defense forced a Green Bay punt which gave the Rams a chance to take a two-score lead, but Matthew Stafford threw an interception to give life back to the Packers. Jordan Love then threw an interception of his own to give the Rams the ball back, but the Rams failed to add any points off the turnover, keeping the score 20-13 and a one possession game. With about six minutes to go in the fourth quarter, L.A. tacked on their third field goal to take a 23-13 lead and a two-score lead. With under four minutes to go, and with the Pack driving, Love threw his second interception of the game setting up the Rams to chew clock and forcing the Packers to burn timeouts as L.A. tried to put the game away. The Rams added a final field goal to take a 26-13 lead with 30-seconds remaining in the contest, and that was enough for the Rams. Sean McVay beat Matt LaFleur for the first time in his career. L.A. earned their most impressive win of the 2026 season, and now they get some time off before they get back to work and look to move their win streak to six games when they face the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday Night football.

Tough at home and in the fourth quarter: The Browns have had six fourth-quarterback comebacks and they are a perfect 4-0 at home. title: Raiders offense gets back on track without Brock Bowers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders offense, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza and a running game that featured Ashton Jeanty, got back on track. Nearly overcoming a horrendous start and without offensive weapon Brock Bowers causing mass disruption and chaos. The discrepancy of penalties was so severe it prompted head coach Klint Kubiak to tell a […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Tafoya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders offense, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza and a running game that featured Ashton Jeanty, got back on track. Nearly overcoming a horrendous start and without offensive weapon Brock Bowers causing mass disruption and chaos. The discrepancy of penalties was so severe it prompted head coach Klint Kubiak to tell a sideline reporter at the half that the referees “need to call it both ways.” The rook Usually, numbers come first in a review of play such as this; however, the heart and grit of a champion were on full display in the young rookie. The first-quarter statistics were so bad that if he had gone into a shell and played like a dog, no one would have blamed him. But rather than do what so many Raiders quarterbacks have done over the years, he weathered the storm, found his rhythm and got busy. In his second start, Mendoza threw for over 250 yards (267) and three touchdowns. Only Joe Burrow, Jared Goff and Trevor Lawrence are the other No.1 overall quarterbacks to do so within their first two starts in NFL history. Placing him in amazing company. However, that is just the tip of the iceberg; the 88.5 quarterback rating against arguably the best secondary he will face all season without Bowers is phenomenal. He laid out a perfect pass to Jeanty coming out of the backfield on a wheel route, singled up against a defensive end for a 68-yard catch-and-run, hit Jack Bech for a 7-yard out route and got Ian Thomas for a 19-yard score. The play to Thomas was a play-action pass featuring one of the coldest play fakes of the year. The fake was so good it fooled not only former NFL defensive player of the year Patrick Surtain II, but it fooled the cameraman too. At the end of the game, coming out of the two-minute warning, Mendoza made his first glaring mistake, which cost them the game. An ill-advised slant to Tucker was pounced on by Ja’Quan McMillian, who sold out on it from the jump and returned it 35 yards to the house. Boosting Denver’s lead to 38-24 and essentially ended the game. On the ensuing possession Mendoza came out with every intention to score quickly, but ultimately succumbed to a Broncos defense that smelled blood, hit him on his final three passing attempts and sacked him twice consecutively to turn over possession. Running backs For the first time as a team since Week 3, the Raiders topped the 100-yard rushing mark as a team. Averaging 6.0 yards per carry for the league’s second-worst rushing attack was a huge deal. Doing so against a vaunted Broncos defense, which was a top-ten scoring defense. Even the quarterback, Mendoza, ran four times for 22 yards and averaged 5.5 yards per carry. Jeanty played arguably his best game of the year, rushing for 79 yards on 11 carries and catching five passes for 90 yards including a 68-yard touchdown catch out of the backfield. Jeanty would take over possession of the longest run of the season on a 46-yard scamper stemming from utilizing good vision and making a great cut on a draw play. Mike Washington Jr. got in on the action and was a steady contributor and spell back in the run game as he added 42 yards of his own on nine carries. Carrying the load through the middle quarters, Washington was just as intricate to the Raiders 17-straight point comeback effort. Wide receivers Jack Bech, whom we can safely call Brock-lite, turned the offense into a third-down-converting machine. Finishing the game with the most receptions and second-most yards: eight receptions on nine targets and 88 yards with one touchdown. Bech and Mendoza have a chemistry that was on full display as they continued to move chains in critical situations. Jalen Nailor, the offseason’s three-year, $35 million acquisition, finished the game with a single recorded catch for 16 yards. A stat line drastically misleading as he was on the receiving end of not one, but two Mendoza touchdown passes that were negated due to penalties. Tre Tucker had a game to forget; whether it was drops, the turf monster, or flat-out giving up on routes, bad things happened when the ball came his way. Drops were a key factor in this game. When playing with a rookie quarterback who needs help from veteran receivers those types of things can be detrimental to their confidence. Final thoughts Hanging 370 yards and 24 points of offense against the division-leading Broncos was no small feat. Mendoza threw five touchdown passes against the vaunted pass defense, but only three counted. The running game neared 150 total yards; both running backs averaged over 4.5 yards per carry. The bounce-back was marvelous, and the reality is the Broncos’ defense is likely the toughest they will see for a month (3 games). Until they meet again on December 20 and then the last game of the season against the Kansas City Chiefs. That gives the Raiders a real opportunity to keep improving and maybe even stack a few wins.

title: Jermod McCoy shows promise during 1st start for Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11 vs. Denver Broncos
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have been searching for answers at cornerback throughout the season, often deploying a three-man rotation between Darien Porter, Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy at one of the two starting spots on the perimeter this season. However, in Week 11 against the Denver Broncos, the coaching staff decided to let McCoy take […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have been searching for answers at cornerback throughout the season, often deploying a three-man rotation between Darien Porter, Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy at one of the two starting spots on the perimeter this season. However, in Week 11 against the Denver Broncos , the coaching staff decided to let McCoy take all of the reps, for better or worse. According to Pro Football Focus , the numbers on the fourth-round pick’s first start were a mixed bag. He was targeted five times and gave up two catches (one drop) for 55 yards while recording a pass breakup. So it was far from a perfect outing, but the Tennessee product showed promise on tape where the stats leave out some context. With that in mind, let’s dive into the film. Jermod McCoy 1on1 with no safety help vs. Jaylen Waddle Love the patience at the LOS in soft press & is in a good spot to defend against Waddle's speed, just a tick late to recognize the curl and ends up running by. Tough assignment for the rookie #Raiders pic.twitter.com/835Z2flNMN — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 23, 2026 Let’s get the negative reps out of the way to end on a high note. And while the result here is bad, this is far from a terrible rep. The problem is that when the Broncos motion the slot receiver across the formation to get into a three-by-one set, the Raiders respond by getting into a single-high coverage that leaves McCoy one-on-one with Jaylen Waddle, who has a reputation as one of the best deep threats in the NFL. Still, the rookie corner does a decent job of staying patient at the line of scrimmage by not completely opening his hips until Waddle commits to the outside release. Then, McCoy uses his inside hand to help slow the receiver down a bit and run with the receiver stride for stride, meaning this is perfect coverage against a go route. However, it isn’t, and the problems begin at about the 50-yard line. That’s where Waddle starts to tip his route by picking his shoulders and head up to hit the breaks on the curl route. But McCoy doesn’t, or is late to see that, and ends up running right by his man, giving up plenty of separation for a 19-yard catch. To cut the fourth-round pick some slack, especially with no safety help over the top, this is a tough assignment with Waddle’s speed. However, he can still use this rep to build confidence, knowing that he was able to run with Waddle. This can be a learning moment for McCoy, recognizing that he can trust his speed and look for the route indicators that receivers give him moving forward. Similar rep here, just against Troy Franklin (4.41 speed) McCoy gets turned around a bit at the LOS (though he's still in decent position) and it looks like he panics, getting too handsy with Franklin. That slows him down and leads to him getting beaten deep pic.twitter.com/aufeUKkkBQ — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 23, 2026 This is a similar rep, just against Troy Franklin, who can also fly with a 4.41-second 40-yard dash time at the 2024 NFL Combine. Again, McCoy shows decent patience at the line of scrimmage to avoid opening up the gate and getting burnt. But he does get turned around a bit with Franklin using an outside jab step to set up his inside release. Still, McCoy isn’t out of position initially by using his hands to help stay in phase. The issue is he holds on too long, which slows him down and leads to the receiver breaking free later in the route. Luckily, the wideout had one of the more comical drops of the season, with the ball doinking off his helmet for an incompletion. So, the corner gets away with this one. Also, it looks like he was supposed to have some sort of help over the top. The Raiders are running a unique coverage here, where the outside corners (McCoy and Eric Stokes at the bottom of the screen) are playing man while the four other defensive backs (Hezekiah Masses, Treydan Stukes, Jeremy Chinn and Taron Johnson) are executing a pattern match zone coverage. Notice how both Johnson and Chinn converge on the receiver in the middle of the field despite the pass going over the top of the defense. It’s impossible to know for certain without having the exact play call and coverage rules, but I’d imagine one of those two is supposed to help against the deep route. Flea Flicker vs. Jermod McCoy What's frustrating is he isn't fooled by the play call and executes the switch release to pick up the wheel route and be in a decent spot to cover it. He just trips right before the ball arrives, and Chinn can't get there in time to help #Raiders pic.twitter.com/zTS8QNDMvn — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 23, 2026 This is a rep that goes down as a negative one on the ledger since the Broncos get an explosive play out of it, but it isn’t nearly as bad as the scorebook shows for McCoy. Not only does Denver run a flea flicker, but they also have the outside receiver (Marvin Mims, who runs a 4.38-second 40-yard dash) motion across the formation for a wheel route while executing a switch release with the receiver at the top of the screen. But the rookie isn’t fooled, staying at his landmark in the Cover 4 call and passing off the outside receiver to pick up the wheel route. McCoy is in a good spot to defend the route, squeezing the receiver toward the sideline and staying in the receiver’s hip pocket throughout the rep. However, he starts to stumble around the 12-yard line and trips right before the ball arrives, while Chinn can’t get there in time to help, resulting in the big gain that set up a Broncos touchdown. What’s most encouraging about this play is that in previous games, McCoy had a lot of issues against these types of concepts in zone coverage. In his limited playing time prior to this past Sunday, he often looked confused or like he was thinking too much and unsure who to cover when playing zone, especially against route combinations where he had to pick up and pass off receivers. So, despite this being a big gain, the rookie is showing growth here. He just needs to be better at staying on his feet to finish the play. While the incompletion is a result of Sutton running into Johnson, this is solid coverage from Jermod McCoy on Sutton against the mesh concept #Raiders pic.twitter.com/sXvxZGziFu — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 23, 2026 Moving onto the positive reps, while the incompletion here is a result of Bo Nix making the wrong read and Courtland Sutton running into Johnson, it’s still solid coverage from McCoy. Denver dials up a mesh concept, where Sutton is working across the field on a deep drag or over route to set a pick for the slot receiver (No. 13 Pat Bryant). That’s a good play call by Sean Payton because it catches Las Vegas in man coverage and Bryant is open, which is where Nix should go with the ball. But from McCoy’s perspective, he’s in a perfect position to defend the over route, avoiding any contact on the pick and running stride-for-stride with Sutton. In fact, the corner might get an interception if the receiver’s route doesn’t get cut short. It’s the difference between his eyes being on his man (which is where they should be in man coverage) and on the quarterback, making it more difficult to adjust to the ball in the air. As a side note, Klint Kubiak went viral for saying at halftime that the referees needed to call the game both ways. Kubiak has a good point with this play because if Cody White was called for offensive pass interference in the end zone — a penalty that wiped away a touchdown — then Sutton should get flagged here, too. While the incompletion is a result of Sutton running into Johnson, this is solid coverage from Jermod McCoy on Sutton against the mesh concept #Raiders pic.twitter.com/sXvxZGziFu — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 23, 2026 Here, we’ll get another rep from McCoy in press coverage against Franklin on a go route. This time, he does an ever better job of…

title: Brock Bowers returns to practice
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders began the practice week to prepare for Sunday night’s crucial game at the Cleveland Browns with some good news. Superstar tight end Brock Bowers was present at the start of practice according to media reports. That is a good sign Bowers, barring a setback should be in line to play at […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders began the practice week to prepare for Sunday night’s crucial game at the Cleveland Browns with some good news. Superstar tight end Brock Bowers was present at the start of practice according to media reports. That is a good sign Bowers, barring a setback should be in line to play at the Browns. Bowers missed Sunday’s loss at the Denver Broncos with an ankle injury that kept him to 11 snaps in a home loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He practiced on a limited basis Thursday and Friday last week before being ruled out. Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak said after the Denver game that the team was hopeful Bowers could play against the Browns. Wednesday, Kubiak said Bowers was limited in practice and the team remains optimistic he will play at Cleveland. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) was back at practice Wednesday after missing the Denver game. Kubiak said he was limited and the team thinks he should play Sunday as well. The only two Las Vegas players who didn’t practice Wednesday were defensive tackles Tim Keenan (knee) and Adam Butler (concussion). They were both hurt at Denver. Also, defensive end Patrick Johnson was at practice, which begins his 21-day practice window from being removed from the injured reserve.

title: Ashton Jeanty, Jack Bech answer the bell
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 84 percent of the snaps and had 79 yards rushing on […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 84 percent of the snaps and had 79 yards rushing on 11 carries, including a 46-yard run. He also had a 68-yard touchdown catch. He needs to keep this explosion going. Jack Bech: The second-round pick played a career 55 snaps and had eight catches for 88 yards on nine targets, also a career high. He has finally made an impact and he was Fernando Mendoza’s security blanket with star tight end Brock Bowers out. With Bowers coming back, Bech needs to find a way to make an impact moving forward. Darien Porter: The third-round pick was a starter as recently as Week 9. At Denver, Porter didn’t play one defensive snap and played just three snaps on special teams. It will be interesting if he plays any cornerback at Cleveland. Caleb Rogers: The benched starter played just four special teams snaps. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, played four special teams snaps. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, has been on the 53-man roster for four games and he was inactive for all four games. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick missed Week 11 due to an injury. The team is hopeful he plays at Cleveland. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was injured in the fourth quarter at Denver. He will be monitored through the week. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 29 snaps on special teams, which is his norm. He has played just three defensive snaps this season.

title: Fernando Mendoza is having issues throwing to his left
summary: Fernando Mendoza has been living up to expectations after his first two starts. His last one against the Broncos displayed why he could be the Raiders’ franchise quarterback. His three-touchdown performance after falling behind 17-0 showed toughness and grit. He helped lead a comeback that just fell short with a heartbreaking pick-six that put the […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fernando Mendoza has been living up to expectations after his first two starts. His last one against the Broncos displayed why he could be the Raiders’ franchise quarterback. His three-touchdown performance after falling behind 17-0 showed toughness and grit. He helped lead a comeback that just fell short with a heartbreaking pick-six that put the game out of reach. One area where Mendoza has struggled is his accuracy. He missed a few throws he should have had against the Broncos. When you deep-dive into the numbers, you realize it is too one-sided. Mendoza was 1/4 for 39 yards, throwing 10-plus yards to his left. When throwing to his right, he was 5/7 for 135 yards and a touchdown. Mendoza throwing 10+yards vs the Broncos To his left 1/4 39 yards To his right 5/7 135 yards 1 touchdown. Most of his misses were to his left. — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) November 24, 2026 What’s interesting is that in college it was the opposite. He had issues throwing to his right over throwing to his left. Elijah Sarratt lined up to his left side for his beautiful back shoulders, which helped build his name in the scouting community. Of course, Mendoza’s leap in throwing downfield was big from Week 10 to 11. Expect Mendoza to keep this going and improve in this area as well.

title: Top-5 Thanksgiving Day plays in Miami Dolphins history
summary: Thanksgiving Day means a few things to most Americans: food, family and football. And while the Miami Dolphins won’t be playing on this year’s Turkey Day, they’ve had some very memorable moments for the franchise on Thanksgiving in the past. The Dolphins have played eight times on Thanksgiving — winning five of those contests. And […]
full_text: Thanksgiving Day means a few things to most Americans: food, family and football. And while the Miami Dolphins won’t be playing on this year’s Turkey Day, they’ve had some very memorable moments for the franchise on Thanksgiving in the past. The Dolphins have played eight times on Thanksgiving — winning five of those contests. And in those games, they’ve had their fair share of incredible plays, including one of the most infamous blunders in the history of the National Football League. So before Mom busts out the gravy and stuffing, before Dad cracks open his first cold one of the day, and before the kids break out the ol’ pigskin in the backyard, let’s rank the top-5 plays in Miami Dolphins’ Thanksgiving Day game history. 5. Bob Griese throws 45-yard touchdown to Paul Warfield (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 1973) On November 22nd, 1973, the defending Super Bowl Champion Miami Dolphins faced a very good Dallas Cowboys team on Thanksgiving Day. Early on in the contest, future Hall-of-Fame quarterback Bob Griese hit future Hall-of-Fame wide receiver Paul Warfield for a 45-yard touchdown in a game that would eventually end in a 14-7 Dolphins victory. 4. Sammy Knight returns interception 70-yards (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 2003) On a day that saw the Dolphins’ defense sack Cowboys’ quarterback Quincy Carter five times and intercept three of his passes, Sammy Knight’s pick and subsequent 70-yard return was one for the highlight reels. Knight joined Patrick Surtain and Zach Thomas as beneficiaries of errant Cowboy Carter throws that afternoon, and the Dolphins went back to South Florida with a 40-21 victory. 3. Jason Taylor returns fumble for 34-yard touchdown (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 2003) Sammy Knight wasn’t the only Dolphins defender with a signature play during Miami’s win over Dallas in 2003. Hall-of-Fame defensive end Jason Taylor also thrilled fans of the aqua and orange that Thanksgiving with a 34-yard scoop and score after a Quincy Carter fumble. Dressed in throwback uniforms that day, the Dolphins defense dominated Dallas en route to a big Turkey Day victory. 2. Keith Byars runs for 77-yard touchdown in the snow (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 1993) One of the most memorable plays in NFL history would come later in this contest, however, without Keith Byars’ 77-yard touchdown scamper through the Texas snow earlier in the game, we may have never seen it. After Byars crossed the goalline in Dallas, he would celebrate by making a snow angel on the Texas Stadium turf in Irving. 1. Leon Lett fumbles, Dellenbach recovers, Dolphins win (Dolphins vs. Cowboys – 1993) The most famous play in Thanksgiving Day history came in the Dallas snow in 1993. With Miami trailing 14-13 in the closing seconds of the tilt, Dolphins kicker Pete Stoyanovich attempted a 40-yard field goal for the win. The Cowboys blocked the kick — seemingly securing the victory for the home crowd. However, in a blunder for the ages, Cowboys defensive lineman Leon Lett inexplicably attempted to recover the loose football, but slipped on the slick turf, knocking the ball forward. Dolphins center Jeff Dellenbach would jump on the fumble near the Cowboys’ goalline, giving Stoyanovich another opportunity to make a field goal from a much shorter distance. He would nail the kick and Miami would win the game by a score of 16-14.

title: Jacob Rodriguez coming for Dolphins record held by Zach Thomas
summary: Great linebacker play has been a staple of the Miami Dolphins throughout the history of the franchise. From Nick Buoniconti, A.J. Duhe, John Offerdahl and Bryan Cox, all the way up to Zach Thomas, Junior Seau, Joey Porter and now Jordyn Brooks, Dolphins fans have been blessed to witness the play of some of the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins is introduced prior to a game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Great linebacker play has been a staple of the Miami Dolphins throughout the history of the franchise. From Nick Buoniconti, A.J. Duhe, John Offerdahl and Bryan Cox, all the way up to Zach Thomas, Junior Seau, Joey Porter and now Jordyn Brooks, Dolphins fans have been blessed to witness the play of some of the greats of the game. Keeping with tradition, the season that 2026 second-round pick Jacob Rodriguez is having is giving the youngster a chance to possibly etch his name in the record books. During his rookie season in 1996, future Hall-of-Fame linebacker Zach Thomas finished his first campaign as a professional with 154 combined tackles. That mark set a rookie record for Miami — one that has yet to be broken… yet. However, that record is in danger of being surpassed by Rodriguez this season. Through ten games, Rodriguez ranks 8th in the National Football League with 93 combined tackles — 9.3 per game. If Miami’s sensational rookie can avoid injury and the daunting “rookie wall,” he’ll finish the year with roughly 158 tackles — four more than Thomas had in the greatest rookie year a Dolphins’ linebacker has ever had. The accomplishment would be a bright spot in an otherwise difficult year for the South Florida franchise. Now, it’s worth noting that Thomas’ record was set when the NFL played just 16 regular season games before the playoffs started — one less than the 17 games the league currently plays, so if Rodriguez wants to lay claim to the record without an asterisk, he’ll need to average a little over 10 tackles per game from here on out. Can he do it? Absolutely, but the achievement won’t come easy. In a season that has seen the team secure just one single victory, Rodriguez’s development — plus his potential to set a new Dolphins record — is something fans of the franchise can cheer for as the year nears its conclusion.

(Photo by Yuri CORTEZ / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images This Sunday’s game at U.S. Bank Stadium between the Atlanta Falcons and the Minnesota Vikings will feature Kirk Cousins’ return to the Twin Cities as the Vikings’ quarterback to take on the team he left Minnesota for before the 2024 season. It’s one of the more interesting storylines of Week 12 of this NFL season, and a pretty significant chunk of the country will be able to see it on over-the-air television. The folks from 506 Sports have released their broadcast maps for this Week 12, and the FOX map for this week is below. The Falcons/Vikings game is represented by the red area. As you can see, the portion of the country that will get Falcons/Vikings is pretty large, encompassing most of the western and northern United States, as well as a decent portion of the south. This will also be the game being shown to viewers in Alaska and Hawai’i. The other two games in the early window on FOX are the New York Giants at the Indianapolis Colts (represented by the blue area) and the Tennessee Titans at the Jacksonville Jaguars (represented by the green area). Because of all the other games that have been interspersed throughout this Thanksgiving week, there will only be six games in the Sunday early window between FOX and CBS (and only three in the late window, so pray for Scott Hanson’s sanity, Red Zone viewers). That could also play a role in why the viewing area for Falcons/Vikings is as wide as it is. There’s your broadcast coverage map for Week 12, folks. Hopefully there are quite a few of you who are in the red area on the map for this week’s game.

title: Week 11 Observations: Don’t Despair
summary: I waited all day for Sunday night. I should have finished raking the leaves.   The Minnesota Vikings played poorly in every aspect of the game and took a well-deserved, convincing 35-10 thrashing at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. With that, dreams of the coveted #1 seed and the bye are gone. […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images I waited all day for Sunday night. I should have finished raking the leaves. The Minnesota Vikings played poorly in every aspect of the game and took a well-deserved, convincing 35-10 thrashing at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. With that, dreams of the coveted #1 seed and the bye are gone. The NFC North remains within reach. It’s now about taking our medicine, learning from the lessons, and improving over the final seven games of the season. Regrets? I Have a Few (Anatomy of a Bad Prediction) With apologies to Ol’ Blue Eyes, I will mention them. IT WASN’T PURPLE BIAS, BUT I DROPPED THE BALL In hindsight, my prediction of a close 27-24 victory was well-informed enough to avoid dismissing it as letting my wishes father my thoughts. Kevin O’Connell was 2-0 vs. Kyle Shanahan as a head coach, and Shanahan was 0-5 when Brian Flores was on the opposing sideline. Our defense handled Brock Purdy well enough in previous meetings that I didn’t expect the near-perfect performance we saw Sunday night. Looking back to the second half of last season, the defense held its own against high-powered NFL offenses, including several dominant performances. This year, we’re coming off games in which we held a Lions team averaging over 30 points to just 19 at home. We did about as well as we could have against the Bills, given that we didn’t have a functional offense and that it felt like the defense was on the field for 50 minutes. The 49ers just came out of a game in which they allowed 40 points to the Cowboys. In previous outings, they gave up 29 to the Seahawks, 29 to the Falcons, and 30 to the…Cardinals (?!). They haven’t been able to get the quarterback all season. It was not unreasonable to expect 27 points while holding the 49ers to 21-24. I SHOULD HAVE PUT MORE STOCK IN KOC’S PRIMETIME ISSUES Yeah, I should have taken a more skeptical “I’ll believe it when I see it” approach here. Doing so would have made me more open to this kind of disastrous outcome. My bad. The Vikings are 6-12 in primetime games under Kevin O'Connell. They're 2-6 since the calendar flipped to 2025, with losses by 22 (Lions), 18 (Rams), 16 (Falcons), 27 (Chargers), 17 (Bills), and 25 (49ers). — Will Ragatz (@WillRagatz) November 23, 2026 While I’ve already seen the predictable, tired “Kirk Cousins in primetime” social media posts after this one, the record actually shows he’s 10-6 in those games since 2020. This includes a 5-1 record as a member of the Atlanta Falcons when the lights were brightest. Yes, I get it. A team plays in primetime because the competition is stronger. The NFL doesn’t plan to showcase many 49ers vs. Titans games to a nationwide audience when it builds out the schedule in the spring. But it’s no longer debatable: Kevin O’Connell’s approach to these high-profile games must change. Enough is enough. I should have been on guard for a letdown, given the emotional high from last week’s win over the Packers in Cousins’ return. It felt like the week after we won that exhilarating OT game in Buffalo in 2022. We were the talk of the shows on ESPN/FS1/national sports talk radio: “What if Vikings are for real?! Look out, NFC!” Then what happened the following week? A 40-3 drubbing at home by the Dallas Cowboys. A similar dynamic unfolded this week after Cousins returned from a four-day break and led the Vikings to a win in Green Bay: “The Vikings are a real threat in the NFC now! They have an offense that can complement the defense!” A 25-point loss later, all the previous excitement was wasted in record time and quickly forgotten, replaced by the familiar feeling of: “Here we go again.” The worst part? We didn’t even have to win! If we had lost in the final seconds on a FG or even a late touchdown, this week’s feelings would have been completely different. Not being competitive is the only thing that could have thrown a wet blanket over it all. KOC has way too many wet blankets at his disposal, and it’s now become an issue that’s impossible to hide or explain away. I DIDN’T TAKE MY OWN ADVICE ABOUT COUSINS Last week, I cautioned against thinking Cousins would come in here and pick up where he left off in 2023. It would take a few weeks, and the idea was that what mattered was that the offense was rounding into shape as we got into December and really took off in early January heading into the playoffs. I should have listened to that incredibly insightful, learned, and handsome gentleman. There’s a reason you have OTAs, minicamps, and training camps. Familiarity with the scheme or not, reps matter. Chemistry with your receivers matters. The timing you develop and perfect all offseason matters. Not every receiver breaks into routes at the same speed, depth, or angle. A few inches off in tight coverage can turn a clean reception into an interception. Cousins didn’t have any of that to work with, and it showed against the 49ers. His chemistry with Tai Felton looked off all night. And the split second longer it took him in the pocket probably cost us a touchdown when T.J. Hockenson broke free wide open in the end zone. He hesitated, and the ball was tipped, or he was hit as he threw, causing the pass to sail short. Oh, and this didn’t help either. If you had swapped this game’s timing with the Jets on the Week 17 schedule, could it have been different? Maybe. That’s six more games and weeks of practice. The Cousins from last week in Green Bay would likely have been good enough against the Jets on Sunday. Against the 49ers? Nope. But we played the 49ers when we played them, and I should have listened to my own advice. Do Not Despair (Redemption’s in the Air… Hopefully) Listen, I’m as jaded as the next diehard Vikings fan. I’m old enough to wear the scars from nearly every heartbreak and disappointment of the post-Bud Grant era. That said, some of the dread and doom I read in the game and postgame DN threads were even too much for me. And it wasn’t confined to those threads. People are ready to proclaim the Kevin O’Connell era over, at 7-3, with seven games to go. I’ve always said it. This is an enormous season for KOC. He needs postseason success, or his seat will get hot at ludicrous speed. History wouldn’t be on his side if he reached a Super Bowl for the first time after his fifth season with the same team. Since 1990, there have been just two: Andy Reid with the Eagles and Jeff Fisher with the Oilers/Titans. That’s it. The 2026 quarterback room disaster and the fact that we needed to parachute Kirk Cousins in midseason to save us are totally on KOC. Who else shoulders the blame? Oh, I see J.J. McCarthy beat the 7-2 Jaguars. Wonderful. Fantastic news. Sarcasm is my own. But it’s not even December, and we’re 7-3. Look at how the narrative shifted for this team… in one week . There’s still a lot of football left. Let’s hold off on the dire pronouncements for now. PAST DOES NOT HAVE TO BE PROLOGUE Don’t despair. This isn’t 2022 or even 2024. The defense stunk in 2022. We’re two years further in, with a level of familiarity with Flores’ scheme we didn’t have in 2024. We haven’t yet seen Jordan Addison’s impact with Cousins back. I truly believe that (for now). Let’s have hope and optimism. Oh, and don’t forget perspective. They’re all our friends. Unless you think the most talented offensive minds in the world just figured out that the quick passing game is an effective counter to the blitz, that a light just went on in Kyle Shanahan’s head, or that Brian Flores forgot how to coach defense, well, that’s fine. But count me out. ESPN’s Ben Solak had a great video explaining how condensed formations and the 49ers’ unique ability to use them exploited vulnerabilities in the Vikings’ scheme, especially in…

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Christian Darrisaw #71 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and Atlanta Falcons released their first injury reports in advance of their matchup on Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium. Here they are: Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Donovan Jackson* LG Knee DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Jordan Addison* WR Thumb DNP Christian Darrisaw* LT Shoulder DNP Jalen Redmond* DT Ankle DNP Isaiah Rodgers* CB Thigh DNP Harrison Smith* S Thigh DNP Tai Felton WR Hip LP Kyler Murray QB Hamstring LP Myles Price* WR/KR Knee/Groin LP Atlanta Falcons Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation James Pearce Jr. DE Back LP Matthew Bergeron* G Back DNP Billy Bowman DB Hamstring DNP Zachariah Branch WR Hamstring DNP Jahan Dotson* WR Hamstring DNP DeMarcco Hellams S Foot DNP Za’Darius Smith DE NIR-Rest DNP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, they held a walk-through on Wednesday with several starters listed as DNP, which doesn’t bode well for Sunday. Hopefully some/most of these will be upgraded to limited or better tomorrow and Friday. I doubt Jordan Addison will be active on Sunday, however. And when Christian Darrisaw is a DNP with an injury, his track record is he doesn’t play that week. We’ll see. Kyler Murray has also been upgraded to a limited participant, so he could end up being the primary backup to Kirk Cousins at some point. For the Falcons, the more significant names on the list are starting guard Matthew Bergeron and starting wide receiver Jahan Dotson. Neither practiced on Wednesday so something to keep an eye on the rest of the week. We’ll have updates tomorrow and Friday with injury designations. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford
