summary: Losing games sucks! No two ways about that. : It triggers a lot of emotions and there is a large segment of fans that want to see the Vikings move on from KOC. : I think many of these same fans would like to see BFlo promoted. : If the team could get a first […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 14: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons is sacked by Dallas Turner #15 of the Minnesota Vikings during the second quarter in the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Losing games sucks! No two ways about that. : It triggers a lot of emotions and there is a large segment of fans that want to see the Vikings move on from KOC. : I think many of these same fans would like to see BFlo promoted. : If the team could get a first round pick for KOC while promoting BFlo then, as a Hipster Draft Doofus, I would love it. It is still hard for me to imagine the Wilf’s moving on though. : 50-28 is impressive, : 2-8 vs winning teams in Primetime or the Playoffs is not good. Season : Game / Slot : Opponent : Result : Starting QB 2022 : Week 2 (MNF) : Philadelphia Eagles : L 24-7 : Kirk Cousins 2022 : Week 12 (TNF) : New England Patriots : W 33-26 : Kirk Cousins 2022 : Wild Card : New York Giants : L 31-24 : Kirk Cousins 2023 : Week 2 (TNF) : Philadelphia Eagles : L 34-28 : Kirk Cousins 2023 : Week 7 (MNF) : San Francisco 49ers : W 22-17 : Kirk Cousins 2023 : Week 17 (SNF) : Green Bay Packers : L 33-10 : Nick Mullens 2024 : Week 18 (SNF) : Detroit Lions : L 31-9 : Sam Darnold 2024 : Wild Card : Los Angeles Rams : L 27-9 : Sam Darnold 2026 : Week 9 (MNF) : Buffalo Bills : L 23-6 : Carson Wentz 2026 : Week 11 (SNF) : San Francisco 49ers : L 35-10 : Kirk Cousins You could probably blame the defense in 2022 and the backup QBs in other games but for the most part, they did not get it done. Teams like Detroit and the 49ers do better as they should. Since Campbell took over the Lions he has had Goff as his starter and Shanahan has had Purdy starting since Dec of 2022 although he missed 8 games last year. Goff has only missed 3 games back in 2021. Sure would be nice to have some stability at QB no? Yeah, JJ was supposed to be the one but the injuries more than likely soured the team on his long term viability. Maybe it will come back to haunt them? Who knows? I only hope the young man is able to stay healthy and continue to develop. I think after every loss we will hear the same refrain from some fans which is cool. I just cannot see the team doing it is my position. Looking ahead to the Dirty Birds, Michael Penix Jr. has struggled heavily when pressured in 2026—posting a league-worst 40.5% catchable throw rate and completing just 31% of his passes (1 TD, 4 INTs) under duress. This obviously leads to the belief that the Falcons will lean heavily on Bijan Robinson to test the Vikings run defense. Robinson has 951 rushing yards, 5.1 yards per carry in 2026. He also has 35 receptions for 256 receiving yards and 1 touchdown. I imagine the Falcons will try to emulate what the 49ers did by trying to hit those seam routes to Pitts and maybe London. I think it will be close. Minnesota Vikings News and Links O’Connell Describes Vikings Demeanor After Returning from Loss to 49ers in Mexico https://www.vikings.com/news/oconnell-demeanor-49ers-loss-mexico-week-11 That international adventure could have been disheartening, especially after a game that defied what the Vikings defense achieved through the first nine, and the promise that Minnesota’s offense displayed in a key divisional win in Week 10. The team’s spirits are intact, though. It’s a testament to the culture that Head Coach Kevin O’Connell has supported during his five seasons leading the franchise. The coach met with reporters on a Zoom Monday afternoon and expounded on the excitement of playing five of the final seven regular-season games at home. He also shed light on what it was like in the aftermath of the trip across the border. “What I was taken back by was just the immediate response of the team, the locker room, our leadership, the energy in there, you know, the idea that we didn’t even need to get all the way back to the locker room and you could hear [the confidence],” O’Connell said. “It was a pretty [long] walk back to the locker room and you could hear it within the guys on the team, and then when I was able to kind of put a bow on it for the group, there was just a ton of positive energy and obviously everybody accepting the fact that we were going to give the Niners credit in a game that we obviously wanted to go [win], and we didn’t get it done. “I think the energy and the resiliency of the group will be applied, obviously, in the immediate, which was great to see,” O’Connell continued. “But what I’m most encouraged about is how we’ve been able to apply that in what we do in regard to our preparation, what we do in regard to the conviction and the focus and knowing that our players are very excited to get back home and get to play a lot of games at U.S. Bank Stadium. We knew kind of coming into the season — when you look at the schedule — that this point in the year, we wanted to be in a good place to hopefully play our best football.” The coach added, “The idea of having the healthiest, best version of your team as we get into the end of November and into December is something we’re very much looking forward to attacking and trying to make come to life because we’re going to need to with how competitive the NFC is.” Vikings’ Brian Flores has humble reaction to getting carved up by Brock Purdy, 49ers https://clutchpoints.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/vikings-news-brian-flores-reaction-loss-brock-purdy-49ers “They’re a very good team, and they had a really good game plan. They executed that game plan. I think Brock made some great throws in some tight windows. They made some tough catches in some tight windows, and they played really well,” said Flores. Brian O’Neill opens up about Kirk Cousins screaming at him on Vikings sideline https://bringmethenews.com/minnesota-sports/brian-oneill-opens-up-about-kirk-cousins-screaming-at-him-on-vikings-sideline “Me and Kirk have the kind of relationship built up over the years that he can say whatever he wants to me, and I’m not going to be offended. I’d rather have him be direct and be clear with what he’s feeling and what he expects from us than just be quiet, just sit there and just keep playing with the way it had been going,” O’Neill said. “I certainly don’t think into it that much. I didn’t think it was that big of a deal. He’s mild-mannered off the field, but on the field he’s always intense. That kind of interaction, although it doesn’t feel good, is probably necessary. That’s probably the reason he is who he is, because he can clearly take charge and run the huddle and run the sideline.” O’Neill was charged with allowing three pressures in 47 pass-blocking snaps. “We gotta be better for him, and we will,” O’Neill added. Why the Vikings should still be optimistic, even after major letdown against 49ers https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7810080/2026/11/25/vikings-optimistic-kirk-cousins-49ers-playoffs/ The Vikings still have a 92 percent chance of making the postseason, according to The Athletic’s NFL Playoff Simulator. There are also multiple reasons to think better performances are ahead. … Perhaps the segment of the game that best captures his impact is on third down. In the first nine weeks of the 2026 season, the Vikings ranked near the bottom of NFL offenses in third-down conversion rate and efficiency in third-and-long situations. In Cousins’ two games, the team has faced 25 third downs, the most in the NFL. The Vikings have earned first downs at a 52 percent clip in those spots, about 20 percent higher than in their first eight games. … Replicating San Francisco’s approach will require several ingredients. The opponent must have a quarterback resolute enough to decipher the defense and make smart and accurate throws. It must also have an experienced and talented offensive line capable of walling up against the Vikings’ interior pressure. Even tight end George Kittle held up one-on-one against edge rusher Dallas Turner. ……

title: Vikes Views: Thankful for These Vikings
summary: The holidays are upon us, and there likely won’t be many of you bored at work reading this post. I hope you all enjoy some time with family, football, and whatever else makes this time of year special. As we sit two-thirds of the way through the season, here are a few Vikings I’m thankful […]
full_text: Irving Texas Thursday 11/23/00 Minnesota Vikings at Dallas Cowboys----Vikngs Randy Moss celebrated his first touchdown catch over Dallas in the 3rd quarter on Thanksgiving at Texas Stadium(Photo By JERRY HOLT/Star Tribune via Getty Images) | Star Tribune via Getty Images The holidays are upon us, and there likely won’t be many of you bored at work reading this post. I hope you all enjoy some time with family, football, and whatever else makes this time of year special. As we sit two-thirds of the way through the season, here are a few Vikings I’m thankful for this year. Dallas Turner Turner has stepped up into the starting role and thrived this season. He’s playing 80% of the defensive snaps so far and has already tied his career high with eight sacks. Jonathan Greenard was a key part of this defense and Turner was able to fill those shoes perfectly. Brian Flores The architect of the best defense in the NFL had a rough outing this past Sunday. However, I am still very thankful for Flores. The defense is the only reason this team is relevant this season. Harrison Smith I am thankful for Smith’s entire career. He’s been a Viking for every snap of his career. Joining the 40/40 club this year cements him as a first ballot Hall of Famer. This isn’t just a farewell tour, he’s still playing 55% of the defensive snaps this year. He’s no longer “starting”, but he is making an impact in year 15. Jalen Redmond Redmond has been the most consistent player on the Vikings. He has the second-highest run-defense grade amongst Interior Defensive Lineman and fourth-highest overall grade. Much like Flores, Redmond didn’t have the best night against the 49ers. I am convinced he’s going to bounce back strong. Redmond is playing 81% of the defensive snaps on the line. That’s a lot of work I know his teammates are thankful for. Kirk Cousins I think most of us saw the writing on the wall with the QB room prior to Kirk’s return. The team isn’t the best in the NFC right now, but Kirk gives us fans some hope heading into the holidays. It’s never likely any team is going to win the Super Bowl (1 every 32 years is average by my calculation). There is a chance this year, and that’s largely because of the improved quarterback play we expect going forward. I am thankful for so many more. Our cornerbacks are both really good. Andrew Van Ginkel, the rest of the front seven, and all of the backups have stepped up throughout the season. Aaron Jones continues to carry the load on offense week after week. Justin Jefferson, thank you for not being a diva. Will “The Thrill” Reichard is still one of the best kickers in the league. I hope everyone enjoys the holidays, and thank you for reading my posts. To Packers, Bears, and Lions fans: I hope your turkey is dry and your beer is warm.
author: Craig Williams

title: Patriots rooting guide for Thanksgiving weekend
summary: Happy Thanksgiving weekend, everybody. While the rest of us are going to enjoy some days with family and food, the NFL is quite busy: a total of 16 games will be played between Wednesday and Monday, with at least one game on on five of the next six days. One of those will be played […]
full_text: Happy Thanksgiving weekend, everybody. While the rest of us are going to enjoy some days with family and food, the NFL is quite busy: a total of 16 games will be played between Wednesday and Monday, with at least one game on on five of the next six days. One of those will be played by the New England Patriots, who are going to take on the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET. There are no questions about who to root for in this specific game, but how about the others? Let’s take a look. Once again, a quick explainer: as long as the Patriots are still theoretically alive in the race for a playoff spot, we will root with that possibility in mind. Thursday 1 p.m. ET Chicago Bears (8-2) at Detroit Lions (8-2) : Go good game! The Patriots lost to both teams already this year, so this really makes no difference whatsoever. | CBS 4:30 p.m. ET Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) at Dallas Cowboys (5-6) : Go good game! Two NFC East rivals going against one another with no impact on the Patriots. Time to enjoy a second slice of pie. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Buffalo Bills (9-1) : Go… Bills? Okay, stay with us here. If we are being honest with ourselves, the Patriots can probably kiss their dreams of defending the AFC East title this season goodbye. However, the playoffs are still a possibility. Other teams are more realistic candidates to drop behind New England — looking at you, Pittsburgh — but if the Chiefs have no games on their schedule where it would be essential for us to root for rather than against them. So, in an ideal scenario, they kick off a losing streak on Thursday night that might just allow the Patriots to overtake them further down the road. Of course, the chances of that actually happening are fairly low, but one can dream. | NBC Friday 3 p.m. ET Denver Broncos (8-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers ( 6-4 ) : Go Broncos! Now this is a game that truly matters. The Steelers are the current seventh seed in the AFC and as such the Patriots’ closest rival in the race for a postseason spot. In fact, if they lose to the Broncos and New England wins in L.A. then the Patriots are suddenly ahead of them in the standings. Luckily for the Patriots, the Steelers are doing their best these days to at least play their part in that. | Prime Video Sunday 1 p.m. ET New Orleans Saints (3-7) at Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) : Go Saints! Somebody has to win the AFC North, and the Bengals are the best bet right now. That said, it would be good if they had to fight for playoff positioning until the very last week of the season, just in case the Patriots need them to beat the Browns in Week 18. With. that in mind, we are rooting for the Saints in this one. | CBS Baltimore Ravens (4-7) at Houston Texans (4-6) : Go Ravens! Another somewhat important game from a Patriots point of view. Neither team is currently in the playoff picture, but the Texans have seemingly started hitting their stride and a loss to the moribund Ravens would help break their momentum and make a late push harder. | CBS New York Giants (6-3-1) at Indianapolis Colts (3-8) : Go Colts! Indianapolis entering the playoff race seems like a long shot, meaning that this can be a game where we root with draft position in mind. Don’t forget: the Jets earn the Colts’ first-rounder next year. | FOX Tennessee Titans (1-9) at Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) : Go Titans! With games against the Steelers and Texans still on their schedule, the Patriots will want the Jaguars to have to bring their A-game in both contests. Maybe some heat applied from a loss to their division rivals can help with that. | FOX New York Jets (3-8) at Miami Dolphins (1-9) : Go Dolphins! We are rooting for the worse-positioned AFC East team in this one, once again from a draft perspective. | CBS Atlanta Falcons (3-7) at Minnesota Vikings (7-3) : Go Vikings! Four words: strength of schedule tiebreaker. Will it matter? Unlikely. Is it better to be safe than sorry, though? Absolutely. | FOX 4:25 p.m. ET Washington Commanders (4-5-1) at Arizona Cardinals (3-8) : Go Commanders! We would rather see top draft picks end up with an NFC team like the Cardinals over, for example, the Dolphins or Jets. Sorry, Arizona, it’s nothing personal. | FOX Seattle Seahawks ( 6-4 ) at San Francisco 49ers (9-1) : Go Seahawks! Once again, strength of schedule makes the difference here. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) at Cleveland Browns ( 6-4 ) : Go Raiders! A big one for the Patriots on Sunday night. New England has a clear edge over Las Vegas, but is looking up in the standings to the Browns. A Raiders win would therefore be important for two reasons: it would drop Cleveland to 6-5 and also give them a negative result in a common game with the Patriots. title: The Buttfumble is still worth remembering 14 years later
summary: Happy Buttfumble-versary, everyone! I can’t believe it has been 14 years since we all bore witness (or should I say bare witnass) to the single worst play in NFL history. It simultaneously feels like forever ago and last year. The world was a very different place on November 22nd, 2012, when we all sat down […]
full_text: Happy Buttfumble-versary, everyone! I can’t believe it has been 14 years since we all bore witness (or should I say bare witnass) to the single worst play in NFL history. It simultaneously feels like forever ago and last year. The world was a very different place on November 22nd, 2012, when we all sat down post-feast to watch what was supposed to be a contested matchup between two teams vying for control of the AFC East. But (or should I say Butt) contested it was certainly not, as the Patriots stuffed the Jets like a Thanksgiving turkey to the tune of a 49-19 beatdown that was over before halftime. Tommy B went 18 of 27 for 323 yards and three touchdowns. The Patriots put up 153 yards on the ground. The Jets fumbled five times, losing four of them. The Patriots scored both a defensive and a special teams touchdown. New England scored three times in 52 seconds. It was 35-3 at the end of the second quarter. It’s the kind of game where, unless you were a Patriots fan or a particularly masochistic (or should I say ass-you-kissed-it. OK, that one was a reach. I’ll stop now) Jets fan, you willingly succumbed to the 300 CCs of tryptophan coursing through your system and went to bed early. Most of that matchup has been forgotten by the rest of the world, as over 3,800 games have been played since that fateful Thanksgiving night. Most people can’t tell you the final score or remember the Joe McKnight kickoff fumble or the Shane Vereen wheel route to the house. But what most certainly hasn’t been forgotten, though, is a certain sequence of events that took place with a little over nine minutes to play in the second quarter, when quarterback Mark Sanchez collided with Brandon Moore’s ample posterior and fumbled the ball right into safety Steve Gregory’s waiting arms. Gregory waltzed right into the rear end zone to put the Patriots up 21-0, a score that would hold for all of six seconds before Julian Edelman found the end zone again on the ensuing kickoff debacle. I keep thinking that, with each revisit of this play every Thanksgiving, maybe this is the year where it gets less funny. This is the year where I’m finally able to appreciate the Buttfumble, but not belly laugh every time I watch it. And that day may very well come. But as Aragorn, Son of Arathorn once said before leading a significantly more successful charge than the one Sanchez tried to lead, it is not this day. I mean just look at the image below. How funny is that? And it happened to the Jets, against my favorite team, on my favorite day of the year. We really had it so damn good. I know I’m technically a little late to the party with the actual anniversary being this past Sunday. But just as Thanksgiving is on a different day every year, so is the celebration of the Buttfumble. Because it’s not a November 22nd thing; it’s a Thanksgiving thing. So, as we all sit down at our respective tables tomorrow to take a break, be thankful for what we have, and keep tabs on how many Bud Drys Uncle Lou has sucked back so you can make yourself scarce when he starts getting political, let’s all take a moment to once again appreciate the Buttfumble and count our blessings that we aren’t Jets fans. In case it has been a little while since you last watched the play, here you go: On this date in 2012, one of the most infamous plays in NFL history happened … the Butt Fumble. 😂 pic.twitter.com/VCdSEWjkXa — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 22, 2026 Laughing burns calories, which are about to be in excess. So it’s good for your health, Have a great Turkey Day, everyone. And a Happy Buttfumble-versary to all.
author: Alec Shane

title: Josh McDaniels draws on past experience as Patriots turn to Tommy DeVito
summary: This is not Josh McDaniels’ first rodeo with a backup quarterback. Throughout his coaching career, McDaniels has called plenty of games with a backup under center. Perhaps most notably, he was the offensive coordinator in 2008 when Matt Cassel took over for Tom Brady after the quarterback tore his ACL. Now, McDaniels is leaning on […]
full_text: This is not Josh McDaniels’ first rodeo with a backup quarterback. Throughout his coaching career, McDaniels has called plenty of games with a backup under center. Perhaps most notably, he was the offensive coordinator in 2008 when Matt Cassel took over for Tom Brady after the quarterback tore his ACL. Now, McDaniels is leaning on those experiences as his offense prepares to hand the reins to Tommy DeVito. “There’s always a way to win, and you have to,” McDaniels said Wednesday. “Right now, the challenge is the formula may be slightly different when you change quarterbacks. But that’s our job, is to try to find the right formula for this group, given our current situation, which we have a lot of confidence in.” McDaniels said the first two days of practice have gone well with DeVito filling in for the injured Drake Maye. The 28-year-old has brought energy and confidence to the position, while McDaniels and the offensive coaching staff have worked to build a game plan around what the new starter is most comfortable executing. “I think the biggest thing you can do is focus on the person that’s going to play now and not worry about the things that maybe you’ve been doing or don’t have as much repetition in. What you have to do is now put a plan together that you have confidence in and he has confidence in, most importantly,” McDaniels said. “Being fluid is important, and making good decisions along the way in the process of each week is going to be an important part of our operation and making sure when we get to Sunday, whatever it is we’re calling, whatever it is we’re trying to execute, we know he has full faith in doing it and the team does, too.” After Maye suffered a fractured fibula in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions, DeVito struggled in relief. He completed just 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Head coach Mike Vrabel and DeVito have expressed confidence that the quarterback will be better with an opportunity to prepare as the starter. McDaniels shares that optimism, particularly now that he has experience calling a game with DeVito and additional time to prepare coming out of the bye week. “There’s a lot of things Tommy does well,” McDaniels said. “We have a week or two weeks to plan. We have repetitions. We have things that we can correct in practice. We have things that we like. We have things that maybe we don’t like as much. We’ll hold that for next week. So it’s a totally different process now that you’re going to go into the game this way. “But he’s delivered the ball well all year. He’s thrown the ball well in the spring. He threw it well in training camp. Arm strength is not a problem, as you know and the guys know. He’s made plays with his legs. He’s a smart guy, and he’s a competitive guy. So we like all those things about him.” The Patriots face an uphill climb moving forward after back-to-back losses in which their defense surrendered 80 combined points, compounded by the injury to Maye. Still, with seven games remaining, New England sits just one game out of a Wild Card spot. The opportunity to make a playoff push remains in front of the Patriots, but doing so will require DeVito and the rest of the roster to elevate their play. “I know this, the energy has been fantastic and it should be,” McDaniels said. “It’s just the 11th game of the season. We have a lot to look forward to, a lot to play for, and we have a lot of confidence in the guys that are in the huddle.”

title: Aaron Rodgers has been released. Should the Patriots go after him?
summary: Last week, when the Indianapolis Colts released starting quarterback Daniel Jones, we took a deep dive into the why or the why not he should end up getting signed by the New England Patriots. Ultimately, our verdict was that Jones coming to Foxborough appeared unlikely to happen for a variety of reasons and, lo and […]
full_text: Last week, when the Indianapolis Colts released starting quarterback Daniel Jones, we took a deep dive into the why or the why not he should end up getting signed by the New England Patriots. Ultimately, our verdict was that Jones coming to Foxborough appeared unlikely to happen for a variety of reasons and, lo and behold, it looks like the team agreed with that assessment: it continues backing Tommy DeVito as the starting quarterback with Drake Maye sidelined for the foreseeable future with a fractured fibula. However, a new challenger has now emerged — and it’s a big one: Aaron Rodgers, a former Pro Football Hall of Famer and one of the best quarterbacks the NFL has ever seen. Rodgers was unceremoniously cut by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday after his relationship with the team and head coach Mike McCarthy in particular had soured, to put it mildly. With the expectation being that he will go through waivers unclaimed due to the nature of his contract, the 43-year-old could be on the open market by Thursday afternoon, ready to be picked up for a fraction of the cost. The initial assessment of Rodgers as a Patriots candidate ranged from “no” to “hell no,” but there have been some vocal advocates both among local media circles, former Patriots players, and our little community here. Could it therefore be that the initial reaction was too harsh? Let’s put on our analytical hazmat suits and find out. Why the Patriots should sign Aaron Rodgers He is no longer the elite passer he was in the 2010s and the early 2020s, but Rodgers has still played some serviceable football during his one and a half years in Pittsburgh. This season, for example, he has completed 60.9% of his pass attempts for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions. That second number, and his career-long ball security as a whole, might be key from a Patriots perspective. Rodgers’ 1.7% interception rate this year is 11th-best in the NFL, and would be a clear improvement over Drake Maye’s 4.0% and backup Tommy DeVito’s 3.1% (even though the latter’s number needs to be taken with a grain of salt given the limited sample size). No, he wouldn’t challenge Maye’s status as QB1; at this point in their careers and despite his recent ball security issues, the third-year passer’s ceiling is significantly higher than Rodgers’. That said, he could be a suitable stop-gap and help settle down a unit whose biggest issue besides injuries has been turnovers. The real question in that regard would be whether or not the Patriots would trust Rodgers more than DeVito to lead the offense for the next few weeks, and put the team in position for a playoff run. Historically, that wouldn’t even be a question; we are talking about four-time league MVP Aaron Rodgers. The gap between him and a backup has shrunk significantly from his peak. Nonetheless, one could still make the argument that even a player ranked 29th among qualifying quarterbacks with -0.022 expected points added per play would be the best available option for a team like New England. And if that player is one with the experience of 22 NFL seasons, the argument tilts even further in his favor. Why the Patriots shouldn’t sign Aaron Rodgers Rodgers having lost a step is something the Patriots would have to live with; they probably wouldn’t be too worried about that in a vacuum. The same is true about him having to learn a new system and building chemistry with an unfamiliar supporting cast. If they believed in him, they probably would find a way to adjust accordingly and make it work for the handful of weeks he would be needed to. The anti-Rodgers argument, however, has little to do with his play or lack of in-system experience relative to Tommy DeVito. It is all about him and his impact on the culture Mike Vrabel has been trying to build since his arrival as head coach in January 2025. Rodgers has been a divisive figure for a while now, but what happened before his release on Wednesday was unprecedented even by his or the NFL as a whole’s standards. Appearing on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show less than 24 hours after being informed that he would be benched for backup quarterback Mason Rudolph, he aired his grievances pretty much unfiltered. A few hours later, and to nobody’s surprise, he was cut. Since then, additional details have come out, including Rodgers threatening to quit the team unless he was allowed to call Pittsburgh’s offense himself. Other details revealed by him have been confirmed to be true, but him presenting them on national television is an unprecedented development. Now, let’s switch back to New England. The Patriots inviting that into their building, especially with a 5-5 record and some pressure already bubbling inside the team, would reek of desperation — desperation a team that played in the Super Bowl less than 10 months ago and has the pieces in place to remain competitive for years to come, shouldn’t feel. Yes, Tommy DeVito might be a downgrade from him, but he would be no live grenade tossed into the locker room that could explode at any moment if things doesn’t go its way. Sure, there is a chance that won’t happen again and that Rodgers lands somewhere between repentant and out to prove people wrong, but would taking this chance be worth it for a bottom-third starter? Verdict The Patriots won’t sign Aaron Rodgers as a free agent, nor should they. It’s as simple as that, and as noted above is not about his diminished abilities as a quarterback or inexperience in a Josh McDaniels system. It is, however, as simple as this: signing Rodgers after Wednesday’s events would go against every message the supposed culture-building head coach Mike Vrabel has preached for the last year-plus. Every phrase about putting the team first or holding oneself accountable was tossed out the window by him, and while it might only have been a spur-of-the-moment event in the aftermath of significant in-team disagreements, adding him would still not be worth the gamble. You can’t build a culture in six weeks, but you sure can start tearing one down. And Rodgers, well, he is a sledgehammer. What do you think about Aaron Rodgers? Should the Patriots pursue him, or steer clear of him? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts or visit this Feed post by Pats Pulpit community member BBREBOZO .

title: What Romeo Doubs returning to practice means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots offense is still missing some of its most important players, including quarterback Drake Maye, due to injury. However, in the last three days, it saw two starters return to practice: after left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker made his comeback on Monday, wide receiver Romeo Doubs was back in action on Wednesday. Both […]
full_text: The New England Patriots offense is still missing some of its most important players, including quarterback Drake Maye, due to injury. However, in the last three days, it saw two starters return to practice: after left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker made his comeback on Monday , wide receiver Romeo Doubs was back in action on Wednesday . Both have now officially been designated to return from injured reserve and are eligible to rejoin New England’s active roster as soon as this week’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. How else does this impact the team, though? Let’s find out. Window open We will speak about the on-field impact of a potential Doubs return to the Patriots’ 53-man roster as soon as it happens. For now, however, let’s focus on the return designation and what it means for the team As noted above, Doubs has now been designated to return from injured reserve to New England’s active roster. He is allowed to carry that status for 21 days, and he can be activated at any point during those three weeks. If the Patriots opt against that move by December 16, however, he will have to return to IR and stay there for the remainder of the season. Given the limited nature of return designations — more on that topic shortly — the Patriots would not have brought Doubs back to practice if they didn’t feel good about his ability to return to the 53-man team and eventual game day squad. There are still questions about the timing, especially given that he will have only two practice opportunities this week due to the Thanksgiving break on Thursday. At least theoretically, however, an activation could happen as soon as this week. Roster crunch Given those aforementioned questions about Doubs’ return, the Patriots might opt to play things safe and keep him on injured reserve until next week. If so, they would h ave bought themselves some extra time to find what will have to be two open roster spots at one point. Besides Dubs, after all, the aforementioned Alijah Vera-Tucker is also in line to return. Given that he already was back at practice on Monday, his activation appears to be closer than his teammates’. Either way, at one point the Patriots will have to create two roster spots to bring both starters back into the mix. How they will do is anybody’s guess, but there are options. Drake Maye, for example, might be a candidate to be moved to injured reserve himself given that his fractured fibula is expected to keep him out at least six weeks — longer than the four-week minimum stay on IR. Offensive lineman Walter Rouse, who remains in concussion protocol two weeks after first entering it, is another player to watch. In addition, the Patriots also might decide to simply cut some back-end-of-the-roster players. One spot left We’ve been seemingly speaking about it ad nauseam this season, but that is the nature of the Patriots’ 2026 campaign. So, here it goes again: NFL teams are permitted to return eight players from injured reserve during the regular season, plus two more if they qualify for the playoffs. Leaving those two extra spots to the side for now, the Patriots are now down to their final return spot. Doubs, after all, has become the seventh player to be brought back off IR, joining fellow wideouts A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, fullback Reggie Gilliam, and offensive linemen Marcus Bryan, Greg Van Roten and Alijah Vera-Tucker. With one spot remaining, only one of RB TreVeyon Henderson, RG Mike Onwenu, ED Quintayvious Hutchins, LB Khalil Jacobs and S Dell Pettus will be able to return during the regular season. Of course, should Drake Maye join that list, he would be the top candidate to be brought back both in status and expected length of recovery. For the time being, though, we have one spot and at least five players vying for it — if they are physically possible to return in the first place.

title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: Cincinnati Bengals
summary: Another week and another disappointing showcase for Kellen Moore and the offense. Not only have the New Orleans Saints suffered back-to-back losses, but it’s also now been back-to-back games in which Tyler Shough has looked like a shell of himself. This week is not going to present an easy opportunity for the Saints to get […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints is pressured by Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another week and another disappointing showcase for Kellen Moore and the offense. Not only have the New Orleans Saints suffered back-to-back losses, but it’s also now been back-to-back games in which Tyler Shough has looked like a shell of himself. This week is not going to present an easy opportunity for the Saints to get right, as they will have to make those plays happen for themselves when they face a team that is considered to be one of the favorites to win it all in the Bengals. The Saints’ inept rushing offense is at least remaining consistent in its struggles. This is another game where an improved rushing attack would be a major help against one of the best passing defenses in the NFL, considering the Saints currently field the 28th-ranked rushing offense. The Bengals rank 11th in the NFL in passing defense, allowing only 216.2 yards per game. Their rushing defense is not that great, but it’s better than what the Saints’ offense has been able to produce. They allow 123.9 rushing yards per game, which ranks 21st overall. The Bengals’ defense also ranks 21st in total defense, allowing 361 yards per game. The advantage the Saints could have would be on third down, as the Bengals have one of the worst third-down defenses, ranking 30th in the league and allowing opponents to convert 46.5% of their opportunities. New Orleans needs to run the ball with consistency at some point. In the games the Saints have lost, the offense has been one-dimensional. And this matchup is not easy at all. They struggled with the interior presence of Jeffery Simmons against the Bears. Well, the Bengals will be bringing Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen into this game on Sunday. Given the way the interior offensive line has played for the Saints, this does not inspire much confidence heading into this matchup. DJ Turner and Bryan Cook will occupy the secondary for the Bengals, and the priority for this elite pass coverage unit will be to slow down Chris Olave. The Saints will need to stay ahead of the chains and establish a better rhythm in their play-calling. If the Saints can stay in manageable third-down situations, they have shown the ability to convert. They currently rank seventh in the NFL in third-down conversions on offense. The Saints need to get close to 125 rushing yards in this game. This will help keep the Bengals’ explosive offense on the sidelines, open up passing opportunities for Shough downfield, and give the Saints more scoring opportunities. This will be a difficult matchup, but this is the beauty of the NFL. On any given Sunday, any team can win, and any team can lose. The Bengals will also be playing on a short week, as they played on the road on Monday night. Will the Saints be able to take advantage? That remains to be seen. How do you think the Saints’ offense will match up against the Bengals’ defense on Sunday? .

title: Is it time for the Saints to make a change at the top?
summary: The New Orleans Saints have spent the better part of the last several years trying to find their footing following Sean Payton’s departure, and the results are impossible to ignore. While they have undergone multiple changes at head coach and quarterback, Mickey Loomis remains the man in charge after 25 years, leaving questions about whether […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 18: Executive Vice President/General Manager Mickey Loomis of the New Orleans Saints looks on prior to the start of an NBA game between the New Orleans Pelicans and the Boston Celtics at Smoothie King Center on November 18, 2022 in New Orleans, Louisiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints have spent the better part of the last several years trying to find their footing following Sean Payton’s departure, and the results are impossible to ignore. While they have undergone multiple changes at head coach and quarterback, Mickey Loomis remains the man in charge after 25 years, leaving questions about whether the Saints need a fresh and modernized voice to lead the way at general manager. Loomis’ track record with Payton is undeniable. The two helped transform New Orleans into one of the league’s most consistent contenders, including a Super Bowl and NFC South titles. However, the results since Payton left the building have painted a completely different picture. Loomis is now 58-84 (.408) in games without Payton at the helm. That includes Dennis Allen’s 18-25 record and Kellen Moore’s 9-18 record since taking over in New Orleans. The Saints haven’t been to the playoffs since 2020 and it’s only gone downward since. That kind of sustained disappointment raises legitimate questions about how much of the organization’s success was tied to Payton rather than Loomis’ ability to construct and manage a competitive roster, especially considering how Payton has turned the Denver Broncos around. Loomis deserves credit for the success the Saints have had in the past, but eventually, previous accomplishments can’t continue to outweigh present results. New Orleans has spent years attempting to return to their winning ways and simply just can’t get over the hump. With Kellen Moore’s future in jeopardy, it’s fair to question whether Loomis’ seat should be hot as well. If New Orleans wants to change their current trajectory, it may be time to seriously consider significant changes. That starts with the NFL’s longest tenured general manager.

title: 5 things the NY Giants can be thankful for on Thanksgiving
summary: The New York Giants are in first place in the NFC East. On this Thanksgiving Day, let’s talk about some of the things the Giants and their fans should be thankful for. full_text: John Harbaugh | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants are in first place in the NFC East. On this Thanksgiving Day, let’s talk about some of the things the Giants and their fans should be thankful for. John Harbaugh All the good things that have happened to the Giants so far this season emanated from the hiring of Harbaugh. He is not a perfect coach, no human being is perfect. Harbaugh, though, was the perfect coach for the Giants at this time. Besides, the fact that they hired Harbaugh means they avoided any chance of Mike McCarthy sleeping through meetings in the Meadowlands! John Mara getting to enjoy this The Giants’ owner is 71 years old, and has been fighting a lengthy battle with an unknown form of cancer. Media sees him on occasion, but understandably never gets to speak with him. Sometimes he looks good, and sometimes you can see his struggle. Mara has taken a lot of abuse from fans over the years. He has certainly made mistakes, but no one cares more about the New York Giants than John Mara. I am thankful that he is getting to see and enjoy the Giants being good again. Roaring crowds at MetLife Stadium For years now, we have watched Giants fans head for the exits long before games ended. Sparse crowds that were either silent or unhappy had become the norm. This season has awakened Giants’ fans, and it is fun to hear the crowd during Giants games again. harbaugh noticed during Sunday’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. “It was awesome, it was fun. They were into it from the very beginning. They were loud the whole game,” he said. “I thought our fans were fabulous, tremendous, and the highest level of loud. And man, we can keep building on that, make it even louder and make it even better. But these are some great fans. These are some high energy fans here in New York. It was a sight to see. It was great.” Minnesota’s mistake I don’t want to open up a Jaxson Dart vs. J.J. McCarthy debate. If you have been paying attention, you know where I stand on the Giants’ future at quarterback. Whatever happens beyond this season, though, the Giants should send Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings a nice fruit basket or a poinsettia or something for gifting them McCarthy. I don’t know what happened between McCarthy and O’Connell, or why it didn’t work for McCarthy in Minnesota. I do know he looks every bit like one of the best 32 quarterbacks in the NFL and it is stunning that the Vikings gave him away without giving him a real chance this year. Thanks, Vikings! Arvell Reese and Abdul Carter Go back through Giants history, and the best Giants teams have always been defense-first teams that were built on toughness and got just enough contributions from their offense and special teams groups. This Giants team is trending in that direction, and it has two young star players in Reese and Carter as the foundation.

title: NFL predictions, Week 12: Giants facing must-win game against struggling Colts
summary: Will the New York Giants take care or business against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 12? Below, what the Big Blue View staff thinks of that game, and the rest of our picks for Week 12. Chris Pflum This is a game the Giants absolutely should win. In another year, with another team and another […]
full_text: Will the New York Giants take care or business against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 12? Below, what the Big Blue View staff thinks of that game, and the rest of our picks for Week 12. Chris Pflum This is a game the Giants absolutely should win. In another year, with another team and another coach, I would say that this is a potential trap game. However, I think these Giants know how precarious their season has been and how hard they’ve had to fight for every win since starters began dropping to injury. I also believe that John Harbaugh has used the loss to Washington as a wake-up call and will have the team taking the woebegone Colts seriously. I think every game from here on out will tell us something about the 2026 Giants, and this game I’m looking to see if they can take care of business. The competition is about to ramp up dramatically and it will be great to see the Giants take care of business and play a complete game before playing the 49ers and Seahawks. Pick: Giants Tony Del Genio The Colts are in a full rebuild, having traded Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, and Josh Downs and released Daniel Jones. Their best deep threat, Alec Pierce, has been out since early in the season. Starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee) are questionable, though Gardner has returned to practice. The same is true for tackle Bernhard Raimann (concussion). The bottom line: This is a depleted team playing out the string for an organization in chaos. Elite running back Jonathan Taylor is still there, but the Giants should win, and win easily. That said, the Giants have not had an easy win all season, even against bad teams. I’d like to think that last week’s stirring victory over Jacksonville was a coming-of-age moment for this group, and that they will now regularly dominate inferior teams and put up a good fight against contenders. We just don’t know yet. One wild card is the Colts’ new starting quarterback Anthony Richardson. In his one season as a mostly starting QB (11 starts), 2024, he showed that he is simultaneously (1) not an accurate passer (47.7% completion rate, worst among starters), (2) a dangerous deep passing threat (12.3 ADOT, more than 2 yards higher than any other starting QB), (3) a dangerous but risky runner (499 rushing yards and 6 TDs, but 9 fumbles). Two years later, who knows how much he’s developed, but given that he could not displace Jones as starter when Jones was playing poorly, the answer is probably: not much. Part of becoming a contender is learning how and having the discipline to dominate poor teams. Early in the season, the Giants could only squeak out victories over bad teams. Have they learned how to beat bad teams easily, or have they spent too much time this week basking in the sudden glazing they have received by the national NFL media? I’ll take a guess that John Harbaugh has their heads in the right place. Pick: Giants David Hartman The Giants proved something last week. They got their biggest win of the season when they knocked off the first-place Jaguars, and despite some stomach-churning moments near the end, they got key first downs when they needed them to close it out – something they couldn’t do the week before. It’s nice when a team gets an immediate opportunity to execute something it recently failed at. This week the G-Men travel to Indianapolis to face another AFC South team. This game was supposed to showcase Daniel Jones going against his old squad, but the Colts released him after their Week 11 loss, which was the latest in a long line of failures and missteps that have plagued this team since it got off to a very surprising 8-1 start last season. That feels like a decade ago. New York is a 6.5 point road favorite. The 3-8 Colts are going nowhere, and now have Anthony Richardson under center. He’s a gifted athlete who hasn’t grown into the player the Colts envisioned when they took him with the fourth overall pick in 2023. They still have Jonathan Taylor, but they don’t have any proven receivers. This isn’t a team that should be able to hang with the Giants, whose defense is playing at a high level. I’ve learned to not get overconfident with this team. New York’s next two games after this one are against the 49ers and Seahawks, so this has trap game (and letdown game) written all over it. No matter how dysfunctional and broken they are, Big Blue needs to not look past the Colts. I don’t see John Harbaugh allowing that. New York is better at just about every position on the field except running back and kicker, and needs to focus and finish. They will. Pick: Giants by two scores. Valentine’s View The Giants can see a finish line that includes the franchise’s first NFC East title since 2011. They can also smell the stinking, rotten, hot breath of the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders trying to chase them down. Playoff simulators give the Giants roughly a two-in-three chance to win the division, but the reality is the situation is not that comfortable for New York. There is work to be done. That includes winning games you are supposed to win, like this one. I can’t imagine John Harbaugh will allow his team to take the Colts for granted. title: NY Giants’ Abdul Carter named the NFC Defensive Player Of the Week
summary: New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter has been named the NFC Defensive Player Of the Week for his incredible performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Carter had an absolutely dominant game against the Jaguars, notching 12 quarterback pressures, 6 of which were quick pressures, 2.0 sacks, 5 QB hits, 4 tackles, and 2 tackles for […]
full_text: Abdul Carter rushing the passer Sunday night. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter has been named the NFC Defensive Player Of the Week for his incredible performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Carter had an absolutely dominant game against the Jaguars, notching 12 quarterback pressures, 6 of which were quick pressures, 2.0 sacks, 5 QB hits, 4 tackles, and 2 tackles for a loss. He was the only player across the NFC with multiple sacks and five quarterback hits in Week 11. Carter is beginning to truly break out and is becoming the player the Giants envisioned when they took him 3rd overall out of Penn State. Carter told doubters to stand back and watch his game against the Jaguars prior to Week 11. He said that he’d have a big game, then backed it up by terrorizing Trevor Lawrence. “He’s been saying the same thing to me,” coach John Harbaugh said after the game. “But more than that, he’s been practicing that way. So to see him break out and get the sack and the quarterback hits, it was great.” “Twelve pressures, did he? Twelve pressures,” Harbaugh added. “Should have given him two game balls, I guess.” Carter said after the game that he and the rest of the defense answered the call to shut down a good Jaguars team. “These are the games that all of our best players got to play their best,” said Carter. “We’ve got a team like that. You are what your record says you are. They’ve got a great record, they’ve got a great team. We proved we’re that, too.” Carter, 23, has already become one of the most feared and disruptive pass rushers in the NFL despite this beeing just his third season at outside linebacker. Per NFL NextGenStats, this was just the fourth time this season a player put up those types of numbers without an unblocked pressure. So far this year, Carter ranks : 1st in the NFL in Time To Pressure (2.17 secondsj) 2nd in Pass Rush Win Rate (28 percent) 1st in Quick Pressure rate (76 percent) After the game, RT Jermaine Eluemunor credited Carter’s elite get-off for his disruptiveness and compared him to truly elite company. “There’s a lot of guys in the NFL that are really talented but don’t have that get-off,” Eluemunor said “Just anticipating the snap count, but then also being able to have that get-off. Because there are a lot of guys that jump the snap count, but they don’t have that first explosive step that he has. That explosive step that he has is really rare in this league. Only a couple of guys have it. Micah Parsons has it, Myles [Garrett] has it, Will Anderson has it, and those are three of the best in the NFL. He can anticipate the snap count, but then he also has that explosiveness to help with that.” “[Abdul] thinks he’s the best and he’s going to start playing like that,” Eluemunor added. “He’s been playing like that, but I think that in this game, you truly got to see the hard work and the film study that he’s been putting in and just the emphasis he’s put on just trying to be that player. I think that’s the first of many games he’s probably going to have like that this season.” It’s also an increasingly common occurrence to see a Giant be recognized for their play. All told, this is the 6th time this year that a Giant has earned Player Of The Week or Month honors. S Jevon Holland was the NFC Defensive Player Of The Month for September. WR Malik Nabers earned NFC Offensive Player Of The Month for October. CB Deonte Banks was named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week for his game Week 4 against the Cardinals. LB Arvell Reese was named NFC Defensive Rookie Of The Week in Week 4 as well. Reese was also named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week for his Week 9 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Abdul Carter has been named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week for Week 11.

title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 12 preview — Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 12 of the NFL season, and Happy Thanksgiving! The NFL is doing its part to keep marriage counselors in business. Your Thanksgiving weekend schedule: A game on Wednesday night, a triple-header on Thanksgiving Day, a game on Black Friday, and then the usual Sunday-Monday schedule with the remaining slate. Saturday is a […]
full_text: Unstoppable! | Getty Images Welcome to Week 12 of the NFL season, and Happy Thanksgiving! The NFL is doing its part to keep marriage counselors in business. Your Thanksgiving weekend schedule: A game on Wednesday night, a triple-header on Thanksgiving Day, a game on Black Friday, and then the usual Sunday-Monday schedule with the remaining slate. Saturday is a day off, but there are wall-to-wall college rivalry games. Eat, drink, and watch football. Then watch more football. What could possibly go wrong? Game of the Week: There are a few good choices but it has to be Chiefs at Bills on Thanksgiving night. Fun fact: It’s only the second time in NFL history that two teams are coming into a game having won three straight contests by 17 or more points. Mahomes! Allen! Enjoy this one with your second piece of pumpkin pie and a nightcap. The line: BUF -3. There are four weeks left before the fantasy playoffs start in most formats. Still time to make a move, so read on! St ats of the Week Every team in the NFC North is over .500, while no team in the NFC South is over .500. The Bills ’ defense has not allowed a touchdown across 43 straight possessions. The flip side: Across Weeks 10 and 11, the Cowboys’ offense had a stretch of nine straight possessions that resulted in a touchdown. Each of the Cowboys’ last two games had more than 80 total points scored. In all three of their games since trading away DT Jeffery Simmons, the Titans have allowed 40+ points. Seven different 49ers players who are 30 or older have caught a TD pass this season, the most in NFL history. In the first half against Philadelphia, Aaron Rodgers averaged one half of an air yard per pass attempt (the lowest total for a half of football since they began tracking air yards in 2006). Rodgers has been benched for Mason Rudolph. Dak Prescott was the No. 1 fantasy QB this past week, and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were the No. 1 and No. 2 fantasy wide receivers. Bye Weeks: NONE Week 12 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start CeeDee Lamb . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with a lot more hits than misses throughout. Ride of the Week Tony Pollard went over 100 yards rushing but didn’t score or do anything in the passing game, so that’s a bit of a miss. Fade of the Week Tyler Warren had one catch. Sleeper of the Week Justin Herbert was the QB4 on the week, with two passing TDs, a rushing TD, and no picks. You can check my work here . *** Ride of the Week: Bucky Irving (vs. CAR). Bucky is on one. He’s recorded six straight games with at least 18 carries and racked up six TDs across his last four outings. For what seems like the hundredth time in the last two seasons, Baker Mayfield is playing hurt – and he can’t do his usual Baker stuff. Plus, without Mike Evans he’s not the same QB. Tampa is pounding the ball and playing solid defense, and this is a home game, in primetime, that they absolutely must have. Irving should once again feast, in a plus matchup. Carolina has allowed the second most fantasy points per game (FPPG) and the most rushing touchdowns (14) to opposing backs. ATop-3 RB finish this week is realistic. Fade of the Week: Jaylen Warren (vs. DEN). Don’t look now, but Warren has reverted to a timeshare back on a sputtering offense. After an epic run before the bye, it’s been back-to-back stinkers (a total of 16 carries for 43 yards). He does have seven catches in those two contests, and that’s the path to success this week – doing a little of what Ashton Jeanty did to the Broncos catching passes out of the backfield a week ago. It’s viable, as Denver has allowed the most receiving yards to opposing backs. I’m not buying it. Mason Rudolph isn’t likely to check it down as much as Aaron Rodgers. It’s getting ugly in Pittsburgh. I’m out. Sleeper of the Week: I’ll preface all sleeper discussions by saying it’s harder to find sleepers this week, with no teams on bye. Managers are less likely to need to reach. With that said, I’ll go with Deshaun Watson (vs. LV), who I think is a good start this week in 2-QB formats. Watson has been OK for fantasy this season (QB19 in FPPG). He’s starting to run a little more and has some very good young weapons to throw to. The Raiders have allowed the fifth most FPPG and the second most TD passes (23) to opposing QBs, and Cleveland is a tough place to visit. Watson is ranked as the QB15 this week and I think a Top-12 (QB1) finish is in play. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen , Patrick Mahomes, Dak Prescott, and Joe Burrow ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Three QBs ranked in the Top-10 this week who I think will outperform projections: Jayden Daniels (@ARI), Trevor Lawrence (vs. TEN), and C.J. Stroud (vs. BAL). All have good matchups. Lawrence is coming off a rough outing at New York and gets a very soft landing against what is now the NFL’s most generous defense this side of Dallas. Daniels is starting to look like he did in his rookie year (and is again pulling games out of his you-know-what), and Stroud has been humming for weeks and gets a team whose season effectively ended on Sunday. Ride these three with confidence. Other Rides in the Top 15: Kirk Cousins (vs. ATL, in a bit of a revenge game) and Jared Goff (vs. CHI in the game with by far the highest Vegas total of the week – 55.5). Sleepers: J.J. McCarthy (vs. IND) has been steering the ship and limiting his mistakes. The Colts are probably the NFL’s hottest mess right now, and McCarthy should find little in the way of resistance. Indy allows the tenth most FPPG to opposing QBs, but they’ve been worse during their recent collapse. Joe Milton (@DAL) has done little to inspire confidence since he became the Birds’ starter a few weeks ago. A date with Dallas on Thanksgiving is his best opportunity to show off that rifle arm and running ability. I wouldn’t start him over any of the really good QBs, but I like his chances to finally put up decent QB2 numbers. Dallas has allowed the second most points in the NFL, and the fourth most FPPG to opposing QBs. Other QB2-types to consider if you need it: Geno Smith (@MIA), Sam Darnold (@SF), and Justin Herbert (vs. NE, assuming he plays). Fades: I don’t have a ton of confidence in either Jordan Love (@LAR) or Matthew Stafford (vs. GB) in the Wednesday night game. The defenses in this game rank sixth and seventh in terms of FPPG allowed to opposing QBs, and with Micah Parsons set to make his season debut, both QBs could be under constant pressure from very good defenses that can get to the QB. Love has weapons but his team can’t run the ball. Stafford is missing his go-to receivers. This game has a Vegas total of 44.5 and I think it’ll go under. QB2s who managers could be considering, but who I’d avoid if I could: Anthony Richardson ( vs. NYG, who have been making QBs pay lately), Michael Penix, Jr. (@MIN, in an awful road matchup), Jacoby Brissett (@HOU), Bryce Young (@TB), Tommy DeVito (@LAC), and Fernando Mendoza (@CLE). Running back: Elite options this week – Jahmyr Gibbs, James Cook, Bijan…

title: Jets Thanksgiving Game History
summary: The Jets have played eight times on Thanksgiving in the past. They are an even 4-4 in those games. Below we will take a look at them. November 24, 1960: New York Titans 41 Dallas Texans 35 The American Football League played games on Thanksgiving, and the Jets played on Turkey Day in each their […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - JANUARY 03: Brad Smith #16 of the New York Jets runs in a touchdown in the second quarter against Frostee Rucker #92 of the Cincinnati Bengals at Giants Stadium on January 3, 2010 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets have played eight times on Thanksgiving in the past. They are an even 4-4 in those games. Below we will take a look at them. November 24, 1960: New York Titans 41 Dallas Texans 35 The American Football League played games on Thanksgiving, and the Jets played on Turkey Day in each their first three years of existence. They were called the Titans at that point. Playing against the future Kansas City Chiefs , Don Maynard caught 10 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown, while Art Powell added 8 catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. November 23, 1961: New York Titans 21 Buffalo Bills 14 Al Dorow threw for 223 yards and a touchdown, and Dick Felt returned an interception 55 yards for a touchdown to provide the Titans with the winning margin at the Polo Grounds. November 22, 1962: New York Titans 46 Denver Broncos 45 A wild game in Denver saw the Titans blow a 24-7 lead and then overcome a 45-32 fourth quarter deficit on Johnny Green’s fourth and fifth touchdown passes of the game, one to Dick Christy and the other to Art Powell. November 23, 1972: Detroit Lions 37 New York Jets 20 Entering the fourth quarter, the Lions led 23-20, but they blew the game open with a field goal and touchdown runs by Greg Landry from 6 yards and Altie Taylor from 38. November 28, 1985: Detroit Lions 31 New York Jets 20 Eric Hipple threw four touchdown passes, three to Leonard Thompson as the Lions jumped out to a 24-3 lead and never looked back. November 22, 2007: Dallas Cowboys 34 New York Jets 3 It was an ugly afternoon in a lost season for the Jets. The Cowboys owned a 21-3 lead at halftime on a Marion Barber touchdown run, a Jason Witten reception from Tony Romo, and a Terrence Newman interception off Kellen Clemens returned for a score. November 25, 2010: New York Jets 26 Cincinnati Bengals 10 In the third meeting between these teams in eleven months, the Jets erased a 10-7 halftime deficit. Brad Smith was the star with a 53 yard touchdown run in the first minute of the second half and an 89 yard kickoff returned for a score in the fourth quarter. November 22, 2012: New England Patriots 49 New York Jets 19 This game is best remembered for the Buttfumble. What people don’t remember was that was part of a 52 second span where New England scored an offensive touchdown, a defensive touchdown, and a special teams touchdown to turn a 7-0 lead into a 28-0 rout.

title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
summary: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did […]
full_text: Detroit Lions fans dress for Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, Thursday, Nov. 28, 2019 at Ford Field. Detroit Lions fans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary. (He was a driving force behind other innovations like instant replay, the flags on goal posts, the NFL-AFL merger, and too many others to name). He jumped at the opportunity. The Cowboys hosted their first Thanksgiving game in 1966. They kept the game annually until the 1970’s when the league hatched a plan to alternate between the Cowboys and the then St. Louis Cardinals . The Cowboys were to host the second game in even years and the Cardinals in odd years. The Cardinals only hosted two home Thanksgiving games, however, which took place in 1975 and in 1977. The games weren’t competitive, and attendance was relatively poor. Then commissioner Pete Roselle put an end to the experiment, and made a deal with Schramm that the Cowboys would keep the game from then on. Dallas has hosted the second Thanksgiving game ever since. With two permanent Thanksgiving hosts, why does the third game rotate? In 2006, the NFL added a third game in primetime. The Chiefs defeated the Broncos that night. By this time, a Thanksgiving game had become a desired timeslot. Unlike the experiments in Dallas and Detroit decades earlier, the 30 other teams in the league would probably all love to become the permanent host of the primetime Thanksgiving game. Since everybody wants it, the league has not given the game to a single team. The matchup changes every year and in recent years has usually been a division rivalry (although not this year). The last major change to Thanksgiving games came in 2014 when the NFL’s current TV deal kicked into effect. CBS and FOX both get to broadcast one game on Thanksgiving afternoon. Prior to the current TV contract, CBS could only show games where an AFC team was on the road. That meant one AFC team had to play at either Detroit or Dallas every Thanksgiving. The league’s new TV deal allowed AFC road games to be flexed to FOX and NFC road games to be flexed to CBS. The new arrangement allowed for greater scheduling flexibility. Both Detroit and Dallas could be given NFC opponents, and one of the afternoon games could be flexed to CBS. In theory either the Detroit or Dallas game could also be flexed to prime time, but that has yet to happen. This year the NFL added a game on Thanksgiving Eve. Since 2023, there has also been a game on Black Friday so the number of marquee games this weekend has continued to rise.

title: NFL Week 12 games: Eagles rooting guide
summary: The twelfth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 12 games. EAGLES GAME The 3-7 Eagles have a 0.3% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy. Their betting odds to make the postseason are listed at +6800, which means […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates as he scores a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The twelfth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 12 games. EAGLES GAME The 3-7 Eagles have a 0.3% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy . Their betting odds to make the postseason are listed at +6800, which means you can bet $10 to win $680 if it happens. In other words, it’s time to be interested in the Eagles maximizing their positioning in the 2027 NFL Draft. Current draft order of non-playoff teams via Tankathon : The Eagles beating the Cowboys on Thanksgiving would certainly be a delicious short-term outcome. However, the best things for the Birds in the bigger picture is for them to lose this game. I know that’s not very fun to think about or admit. So, root for the Birds to beat the Cowboys, because you always do. And if they win, it’ll feel great! But take solace in knowing that the Eagles stand to benefit in the form of improved draft position if they don’t beat Dallas. With a loss, there’s potential for the Eagles to move as high as the No. 4 overall pick. NFL DRAFT CONSIDERATIONS GREEN BAY PACKERS defeated by LOS ANGELES RAMS: The Eagles would’ve preferred to see a Packers win on Wednesday night since the Dallas Cowboys own Green Bay’s 2027 first-round pick. That selection is currently set to be No. 17 overall and will only move up the board if they continue to lose. If the Packers make the playoffs, the pick owed to the Cowboys won’t be any more favorable than No. 19. Packers lost, unfortunately. CHICAGO BEARS at DETROIT LIONS: The Eagles want the Packers to win the NFC North since Green Bay owes their 2027 first-round pick to the Cowboys. With the Packers already having a win over the Bears and a loss to the Lions, it’s better for the Bears to win here because GB has an easier path to catching up to them. Root for da Bears. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS at BUFALLO BILLS: The Bills play the Dolphins in Week 17 and the Jets in Week 18. It could be good for Buffalo to wrap up their playoff positioning early so that they rest starters in those games, giving those teams wins that could allow the Eagles to move ahead of them in the draft order. Root for the Bills. DENVER BRONCOS at PITTSBURGH STEELERS: With the Eagles owning the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, they should want Jacksonville to miss the playoffs. That much seems unlikely since they’re the best team in their division. But in the event that Jacksonville slips up and falls into wild card territory, the Eagles want other teams to box them out of those spots. With that in mind, a Steelers win is most beneficial since they’re in that wild card territory. Root for the Steelers. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at CINCINNATI BENGALS: The Saints are currently one spot ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. The Eagles need them to win to move ahead of them. Root for the Saints. NEW YORK GIANTS at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS: The Colts’ first-round pick owed to the Jets is currently ahead of the Eagles’ selection in the draft order. As an added bonus, you get to root against the G-Men. Root for the Colts. NEW YORK JETS at MIAMI DOLPHINS: The Eagles probably can’t catch the one-win Dolphins in the draft order. It’s better, then, for the Jets to lose so that the Birds can move ahead of their selection. Root for the Jets. ATLANTA FALCONS at MINNESOTA VIKINGS: The Eagles are currently picking ahead of the Falcons in the draft order but these two teams have the same record. Would be good to see that change. Also, a Vikings loss is good for the Packers. Root for the Falcons. TENNESSEE TITANS at JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS: Two reasons to root for the Titans: 1) a Titans win gives the Eagles a better chance (though still unlikely) to move ahead of Tennessee in the draft order and 2) thanks to the Jordan Davis trade, the Eagles own the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Jags to lose as much as possible. Root for the Titans. BALTIMORE RAVENS at HOUSTON TEXANS: The Eagles want a non-Jags team to win the AFC South. The Texans have the best chance to take it from Jacksonville. As an added bonus, thanks to the Cam Jurgens trade, the Eagles own Baltimore’s fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Ravens to lose as much as possible (while staying behind the Eagles’ first-round selection still, of course). Root for the Texans. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS: Thanks to the A.J. Brown trade, the Eagles own the more favorable of either New England’s or Chicago’s 2027 fifth-round pick. Also, a Chargers win gives the Eagles a better chance (though still unlikely) to move ahead of the Bolts in the draft order. Root for the Chargers. WASHINGTON COMMANDERS at ARIZONA CARDINALS: The Cards are currently ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. The Eagles need them to win to move ahead of them. As an added bonus, you get to root against the Commies. Root for the Cardinals. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS at SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS: The Eagles want the Packers to make the playoffs. The Seahawks losing helps Green Bay more. Root for the 49ers. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at CLEVELAND BROWNS: The Raiders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Raiders. CAROLINA PANTHERS at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS: The Bucs are currently ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. The Eagles need them to win to move ahead of them. Root for the Buccaneers.

title: Eagles at Cowboys Week 12 prediction
summary: The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season has not been very fun. That being said, the Birds have a chance to give their fans a really fun moment in time by beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Will it happen? Probably not. The Eagles won in Week 11, yeah, but it’s hard to feel like that victory […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles carries the ball during a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season has not been very fun. That being said, the Birds have a chance to give their fans a really fun moment in time by beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Will it happen? Probably not. The Eagles won in Week 11, yeah, but it’s hard to feel like that victory could’ve aged any worse. The Pittsburgh Steelers are clearly an absolute mess . The Eagles beating them probably said more about Pittsburgh’s dysfunction than it did Philly turning a corner. Case in point: the Eagles’ offense was still pretty awful despite undergoing some stylistic changes. It’s difficult to envision this unit keeping up with the Cowboys’ scoring pace. That said, the Dallas defense is bad. They might be less bad now than Mike Pettine is their play-caller … but last week’s win over the Tennessee Titans hardly proves as much. The path to an Eagles victory involves the offense capitalizing on the Cowboys’ defensive struggles … and Vic Fangio’s defense really rising to the challenge. With 11 sacks and 21 tackles for loss over their last two games, the Eagles’ defensive line has shown signs of life. It’s time for Jalen Carter to step up and deliver in a big way, especially given that the Cowboys will be without starting right guard Tyler Booker. If the Eagles win this game, it’ll be the most satisfying possible victory in a lost season. If they lose, well, they’ll be 3-8 and much closer to being officially eliminated from playoff contention.
