title: Eagles News: Where does Joe Milton fit in Philadelphia’s future?
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles news and links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! We’ll learn more about Joe Milton and how the Eagles value him (or not) over the rest of the season. He’s set to be a restricted free agent after the season. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Joe Milton III #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles news and links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! We’ll learn more about Joe Milton and how the Eagles value him (or not) over the rest of the season. He’s set to be a restricted free agent after the season. If they’re of the mind he can legitimately contend for QB2, they could offer him a right of first refusal tender valued around $3.8 million. Other teams would then have the ability to beat that price to sign him to an offer sheet, which the Eagles could then decide to match or not. Or they could try to sign him to an extension to avoid the RFA process altogether. What do you make of how he’s played thus far and do you have interest in him being back in 2027? A strong showing in a win over the Dallas Cowboys today would certainly help his case. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … In Roob’s Eagles Observations: Why tanking doesn’t make sense in the NFL – NBCSP JOE MILTON PART I: Joe Milton has not been great so far, but considering his lack of practice time in this offense and with these receivers and behind this offensive line and also considering his lack of NFL experience, I think he’s done as well as you could expect. What’s interesting to me is where he fits into the Eagles’ future. He’ll be a restricted free agent after the season and I would expect the Eagles to sign him to a bargain contract extension to make sure he’s here next year, get him a full offseason in whatever offense whoever the head coach and offensive coordinator are running and begin 2027 with him as Jalen Hurts’ backup … assuming Hurts is healthy and ready to go. Obviously, the Eagles like Milton more than Tanner McKee, and McKee will be unrestricted anyway and will likely be somewhere else in 2027. It doesn’t feel like Cole Payton is going to be ready to be No. 2 next year so Milton makes the most sense. And I’d like to see what that looks like with OTAs, summer throwing with the WRs, training camp and a preseason. The kid clearly has talent. He just needs time on task. Will be interesting to see what he looks like when he’s not coming in cold in the middle of a season with a bunch of guys he doesn’t know. Eagles’ offensive changes produced less than encouraging results – BGN There were significant changes on how the Eagles ran their offense, from pre-snap motion, to when they snapped the ball, and the formations they used. Since Joe Milton became the starting quarterback, the Eagles were trending in this direction. The results, unfortunately, have been more of the same. The Eagles can’t control the clock, they’ve been unable to stay on the field, and struggle to score points. This was with Saquon Barkley healthier (for a half at least) and DeVonta Smith back. Sean Mannion’s offense still failed to score 20 points and gain 250 yards. This was with the changes made — and how Philadelphia has been trending in that direction — over the last two weeks. There have been some positives with the changes, but the results have been what we’re accustomed to. NFL Week 12 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we’re hearing – ESPN Still no coaching changes? Where do things stand for head coaches on the hot seat? Graziano: Well, it’s not like no team has done anything. The Colts fired their GM weeks ago. The Panthers fired their defensive coordinator. The Cardinals fired their defensive coordinator. The Cowboys didn’t fire their defensive coordinator, instead demoted him and kept him around to suffer with everyone else. But you want to know about head coaches, so fine. Situations I’m watching for potential change at the end of the season include the Jets, Buccaneers, Colts, Eagles and maybe Commanders, though Dan Quinn seems to be turning things around in D.C. NFL Week 12 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Bobby picked the Cowboys: The Eagles mercifully got off the schneid in Week 11 against the Steelers, ending a seven-game losing streak, but the way they won doesn’t seem replicable against a scorching Cowboys squad. Philadelphia downed Pittsburgh by scoring 13 first-quarter points and then holding on for dear life for a 19-16 win. That likely won’t cut it against Dallas, considering Dak Prescott has accounted for 10 touchdowns over the past two games while leading the offense to 91 points. Joe Milton III hasn’t performed consistently enough to keep up with any scoring output remotely similar to that, and the Cowboys already proved capable of such an onslaught while carving up the Eagles earlier this season for 38 points and 416 yards (204 of which came on the ground) in a 17-point win. That emphatic victory took place in Philadelphia. Now, the Cowboys get their NFC East rivals at home. Eagles-Cowboys predictions: Dallas scored 91 points in two games. Why are our writers split? – The Athletic Berman: The Eagles defense demonstrated improvement in recent games. The Cowboys offense is scorching — 91 points in two games! — and I’m focused less on the Eagles defense in this matchup and more on the offense. Can the Eagles score points? They haven’t scored more than 24 points this season. They’ve averaged 15 points in five games without Jalen Hurts. I don’t see them winning 19-16, and I’m not sold on this team scoring into the high 20s and 30s. That makes me lean toward the Cowboys, who are 8.5-point home favorites. Is there a chance Milton has a career day on national television and Saquon Barkley explodes for 100-plus yards, a la LeSean McCoy on Thanksgiving in 2014? Sure. But I’m not predicting it. Cowboys 28, Eagles 20 […] Kubena: I put more stock in the Cowboys putting up 40 points on the San Francisco 49ers than I do in the 51 they hung on the Tennessee Titans, who are reaching new lows after trading All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (who played against the Eagles in Week 2). I also thought the Eagles showed progress offensively against the Steelers. They scored on their first three drives, and Milton’s second-half misses were the main reasons that game didn’t become a blowout. I expect the Eagles to build on Milton’s third start (and second with DeVonta Smith in the lineup) and field their first game with a positive offensive EPA since — you guessed it — they played the Cowboys in Week 7. Eagles 24, Cowboys 21 NFL Week 11: 32 teams, 32 observations – PFF Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas Goedert has hauled in eight of his 11 contested targets this season. His 72.7% contested-catch rate ranks third among the 17 tight ends with at least eight contested targets. The young quarterback makes his third NFL start after beating the Steelers and again making positive strides. What is the next step for Milton, who has used his legs to make plays as well as his impressive arm? Could the Eagles design some running plays for Milton to break down the Dallas defense? “I think Joe’s skill set is unique in terms of his athletic ability. I think both within truly schemed plays, and then he made a nice off-schedule play on a third-and-long,” Offensive Coordinator Sean Mannion said. “So, I think it’s an asset for us. Some of it might be with the QB run game and some of it might look a little bit differently. So, it’s a weekly challenge each week. He’s got an athletic skill set both in the scripted opportunities with true QB runs and then also with the off-schedule.” Game Review – PHI 19, PIT 16 – Iggles Blitz Drew Mukuba had a solid game. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced three roster moves ahead of their Week 12 Thanksgiving game against the Dallas Cowboys. Here’s an overview: DT Gabe Hall was signed from the practice squad to the active roster. EDGE Mason Reiger and S Cole Wisniewski were temporarily elevated from the practice squad to the roster. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. GABE HALL The Eagles previously temporarily elevated Hall for their Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Despite playing just eight snaps on defense, Hall logged one sack (potentially making him the last player to ever sack Aaron Rodgers) and one tackle for loss. One can wonder if Hall’s performance caught attention from other teams, prompting the Eagles to put him on their roster so that he couldn’t be poached from the practice squad. The Eagles now have five defensive tackles on their roster: Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young, Ty Robinson, and Hall. They also still have Leki Fotu and Zion Wilson on the practice squad. MASON REIGER With Arnold Ebiketie ruled out, the Eagles elevated Reiger to have more edge rusher depth. Reiger will likely only play on special teams, just like he did the last time the team temporarily elevated him. He has one remaining elevation this season, as does fellow rookie edge defender Keyshawn James-Newby. COLE WISNIEWSKI This marks Wisniewski’s third and final elevation for the 2026 season. He’s set to contribute on special teams in addition to providing depth at safety.

title: The Eagles have OWNED the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Both times!
summary: It’s not a long tradition, but Thanksgiving Day for Eagles fans is a glorious one. When the Birds take the field in Dallas against the Cowboys this afternoon, they will seek to continue their utter Turkey Day dominance. Sure, it’s only been two games, but their 1989 Bounty Bowl beatdown and Chip Kelly-led 2014 shellacking […]
full_text: Photo by Andrew Dieb/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s not a long tradition, but Thanksgiving Day for Eagles fans is a glorious one. When the Birds take the field in Dallas against the Cowboys this afternoon, they will seek to continue their utter Turkey Day dominance. Sure, it’s only been two games, but their 1989 Bounty Bowl beatdown and Chip Kelly-led 2014 shellacking in Dallas made for some memorable holiday viewing. The Eagles have outscored Dallas on Thanksgiving 60-10 in their illustrious two-game history. So before you sit down for your turkey dinner with all the dressings (or if you’re in Philly, your Italian godmother’s lasagna), enjoy a special BGN Memories looking back at these two signature victories. The Bounty Bowl As an impressionable 13-year-old boy, the 1989 Bounty Bowl was a seminal moment of my childhood. I think all late-stage Generation X Eagles fans would say the same. After dominating the sport, and the Philadelphia franchise as “America’s Team” for the better part of three decades, the Cowboys had fallen to depths they’d never seen before. And at long last, the Eagles were finally the better team. Dallas was on its way to a 1-15 record, while the Eagles were establishing themselves as a playoff contender. Under Buddy Ryan, they had established themselves as one of the dirtier, nastier teams in the league, with a ferocious defense that either pummeled opposing quarterbacks into oblivion, or lost by giving up a ton of huge plays. The scoreboard at the end of the day read 27-0. but there was much more to the story than that. After the game, Cowboys head coach Jimmy Johnson accused Ryan of putting “bounties” on opposing players’ heads, including Troy Aikman and a $200 bounty on former Birds’ kicker Luis Zendejas. The rivalry had grown nasty a couple years prior when, during the players’ strike of 1987, Tom Landry’s Cowboys had multiple starters play against a team of Eagles’ scabs and ran up the score by using trick plays on Ryan’s beleaguered group. Ryan wasn’t coaching the scabs anyway (he wanted to remain in solidarity with his striking players and refused to engage with the replacement players), but he took Landry’s actions personally. A few weeks later at Veterans Stadium, the Eagles were putting the finishing touches on a hard-earned 30-20 victory. Randall Cunningham was expected to execute the kneel-down at the end of the game but instead faked the knee and threw a deep pass to wide receiver Mike Quick. Caught by surprise, Dallas defenders interfered with Quick, and the Eagles got the ball at the one-yard line. Keith Byars punched in a final rub-in-the-face touchdown to make the final score 37-20. Fast forward two years later, and the bad blood festered with Johnson in his rookie season. Aikman, who like Johnson was also a rookie, completed just seven of his 24 pass attempts for just 54 yards and two interceptions. In contrast, Cunningham and the Eagles offense had an efficient afternoon, but it was the extra curricular activities that left the most lasting impression. During the second half kickoff coming out of halftime, Zendejas was seen having trouble getting off the field following a hit by linebacker Jessie Small. It was an odd play, as the action was on the other end of the field and Zendejas was no threat to make a tackle. Before the game, Zendejas had told players that Ryan would routinely offer cash rewards to players who leveled big hits on that week’s opposition, including kickers and punters. On the broadcast, analyst John Madden said, “The Eagles sent someone after Zendejas.” It was patently obvious. After that play, tensions continued to rise. There were minor skirmishes and fights, some late hits, and you could tell things were coming to a head. Finally, late in the fourth quarter, a massive fight broke out after a late hit on Aikman. Two weeks later, the Cowboys had to travel to Philly and play the Eagles in the immediate aftermath of a big snowstorm. Not surprisingly, the Eagles whipped up on the Cowboys for a second time on the field and, equally unsurprising, Eagles fans whipped ice balls at Johnson and Cowboy players as the game ended. For Eagles fans, it’s one of the most memorable games in NFL and, more specifically, Thanksgiving history. For Cowboys fans, they likely remember the three Super Bowls they won in four years right after. The Mark Sanchez Game No, no one in Philadelphia really calls it this, but it was the game that Mark Sanchez, one of the least impressive quarterbacks to ever start a professional football game for the Eagles, outplayed Tony Romo. And most impressive of all, no one got stabbed or anything. The 2014 season was a weird one for the Eagles in Chip Kelly’s second season, and this 33-10 victory on Thanksgiving would be the high water mark of a season that ultimately ended in bitter disappointment. Both teams entered Thanksgiving at 8-3 and the Cowboys had the seeming advantage at QB. But from the opening kickoff, this game was all Birds. Sanchez went 20-29 for 217 yards and a touchdown, but it was running back LeSean McCoy who dominated. He piled up 159 yards on the ground with a touchdown, wideout Jeremy Maclin hauled in eight passes for 108 yards, and Jordan Matthews added a 27-yard touchdown pass from Sanchez in the first quarter to build a 14-0 cushion. Romo and the Dallas offense never got on track. The defense forced four turnovers, including two Romo picks, and the Eagles dominated the Cowboys from wire-to-wire. Honestly, it was a marvelous game in the moment that now feels a little hollow knowing that it was the last good moment the team had in ‘14. Following their win on Thanksgiving, Kelly’s Birds lost three straight, including two straight at home and one of them to these same Cowboys, who went into the Linc and put up a 38-27 revenge win. The Eagles won their final game of the season to improve to 10-6, but lost a series of tiebreakers and missed the playoffs. Dallas and Romo would advance to the NFC Divisional round but fell to the Packers 26-21 and missed out on their first return trip to the NFC Championship Game since 1995. Kelly would not make it through the following season as coach. Later today, Nick Sirianni and the 3-7 Eagles will look to make it three Thanksgiving wins in a row against Dallas. What will they do for an encore?

title: Steelers President Art Rooney expresses full confidence in Mike McCarthy
summary: Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy. Among the issues Rodgers put on blast were McCarthy routinely falling […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy. Among the issues Rodgers put on blast were McCarthy routinely falling asleep in meetings, being late for walkthroughs and meetings, not knowing the gameplay, and breaking down a team huddle vs. the Eagles by saying, “1-2-3 Packers.” Several insiders have noted that players have backed up these claims made by Rodgers, which led many to believe McCarthy’s days in Pittsburgh could and should be numbered. However, Team President Art Rooney II expressed faith in the Steelers’ head coach. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said via Gerry Dulac . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” The Steeles will face the Broncos on Black Friday in their first home game since they defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 to secure a 6-2 record. Oh how much has changed since then. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! ‘1,2,3 Packers’: Aaron Rodgers details baffling Mike McCarthy halftime moment Aaron Rodgers says he won’t return to Steelers Aaron Rodgers claims Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meetings Aaron Rodgers, several Steelers ‘frustrated’ with Mike McCarthy Steelers players not happy with Aaron Rodgers benching

title: Steelers-Broncos preview: What to expect from Denver’s offense, defense in Week 12
summary: Despite a dramatic exit from starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers that has catapulted the Steelers into becoming the NFL’s biggest story ahead of Thanksgiving, Pittsburgh still has a game to play on Friday against one of the league’s best teams: The 8-2 Denver Broncos, currently the No. 2 seed in the AFC. If the Steelers can […]
full_text: Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images | Getty Images Despite a dramatic exit from starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers that has catapulted the Steelers into becoming the NFL’s biggest story ahead of Thanksgiving, Pittsburgh still has a game to play on Friday against one of the league’s best teams: The 8-2 Denver Broncos, currently the No. 2 seed in the AFC. If the Steelers can stay focused on their Black Friday matchup amid the drama, as McCarthy said the team would, what kind of opponent can Pittsburgh expect in Week 12? What to expect from the Broncos’ offense Rushing YPG: 95.6 (25th) Passing YPG: 189.1 (25th) PPG: 23.6 (13th) If they squint their eyes, Steelers fans might find a lot of similarities between their own struggling offense and this Broncos unit. Mike McCarthy and Sean Payton’s offensive systems have plenty of overlap, including an affinity for 11 personnel groupings and a passing game that relies heavily on the quick passing game to the short areas of the field. The Broncos might have had more luck in the scoring department (23.6 PPG) than the Steelers (21.4 PPG), but Denver has actually been more ineffective by some traditional and advanced metrics alike. It’s been a tumultuous season for Denver, who started the season with new offensive coordinator Davis Webb as a play caller, but then, all too predictably, had Sean Payton reclaim those duties in Week 5. Denver has struggled mightily on the ground this season. They’ve eclipsed 100 yards rushing in a game in just four games, and rushed for 82 or less in six others. Philosophically, they don’t favor one rushing scheme heavily, instead dabbling pretty equally in man (25%), gap (20%), outside zone (23%), and inside zone (20%) concepts. J.K. Dobbins — who Steelers fans should be familiar with from his time in Baltimore — started the season as Denver’s lead back, but has significantly lost playing time over the last month. His share of offensive snaps fell to 23% in Week 7 and has gone down each week since, to the point that he took only one snap in Week 11. This despite the Broncos placing R.J. Harvey on injured reserve ahead of their Week 8 contest. Now Dobbins is suspended, with Payton announcing the suspension just 24 hours after telling reporters: “J.K. is going to be super important for what we’re doing in this stretch.” While Dobbins and the Broncos game hasn’t performed particularly well, part of why Dobbins’ playing time began to decrease was the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman. Dobbins still holds the team lead in rushing yards (324) entering the week, but Coleman has nearly caught him (302) in just six games played. Jonah Coleman has very good vision. Going to be one of the better singles and doubles hitters. pic.twitter.com/JesVhyUioV — Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 23, 2026 Coleman is a relatively sound blocker in pass protection and has decently reliable hands for a running back, which has allowed him to stay on the field in passing situations. On the ground, Coleman is a decisive, violent runner who is able to break tackles with his impressive contact balance. He has more lateral quickness than speed, but he has good vision and seems advanced in his reads for a rookie runner. He’s coming off his most productive game as a pro, rushing 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns and adding four receptions for 18 yards in Week 11. It’s worth noting this game against the Raiders, the second-worst rushing defense in the league, but he’s the type of runner who wears down a defense and makes it hard to get off the field late in the game. Jonah Coleman – Week 11 – every touch https://t.co/Z133p6dsWh pic.twitter.com/ImyS5GxBcH — Jacob Gibbs (@jagibbs_23) November 23, 2026 That is easily the most exciting element of the Broncos’ offense. In the passing game, Bo Nix is one of the more frustrating quarterback watches in the league. Nix has played somewhat similarly to recently released Aaron Rodgers. QB Completion % Passing Yards TDs INT Yards Per Attempt Avg. Depth of Target EPA/Dropback Big Time Throw Rate Bo Nix 59.9% 1,955 12 5 6.1 7.5 -0.03 3.4% Aaron Rodgers 60.9% 2,241 16 6 6.2 7.6 -0.17 3.4% Like in Pittsburgh, Denver’s wide receivers are struggling to fill up the stat sheet. The team traded a first-round pick (No. 30), a third-round pick (No. 94), and a fourth-round pick (No. 130) in the 2026 NFL Draft to acquire Jaylen Waddle from the Miami Dolphins — and then signed him to a three-year, $84.8 million extension — but have not worked him into the game plan in a way you’d expect, having surrendered that much capital. Waddle does lead the team in receptions (33), targets (58), and yards (398) through 10 games, but those are fairly disappointing per-game averages considering the team gave up assets like they were acquiring one of the league’s most dynamic weapons. Perhaps Steelers fans can relate given D.K. Metcalf’s struggles since arriving. Jaylen Waddle.. 1st round pick 3rd round pick 4th round pick pic.twitter.com/U3XNsufjXQ — Michael🇲🇽 (@RespectMyCos) November 24, 2026 But it isn’t just Waddle. No Bronco is averaging more than Waddle’s 39.8 receiving yards per game, and only tight end Nate Adkins (3) has more touchdowns than Waddle (2). Receivers Courtland Sutton (266 yards), Pat Bryant (221), and tight end Evan Engram (243) have had moments, but no Broncos pass-catchers are producing consistently. Bo Nix has simply been that bad. Per Next Gen Stats, Nix has averaged the NFL’s lowest completion percentage (42.9%) and yards per attempt (4.5) against blitzes in the NFL. His 14 turnover-worthy throws ranked eighth-most in the NFL. Nix has thrown multiple touchdowns in a game just three times this season, never exceeding two in a game. He’s failed to reach 200 yards passing in four games this season, and has exceeded 222 passing yards just three times. Bo Nix over his three seasons: EPA per dropback 24: 0.03 25: 0.10 26: -0.14 Air Yards/Attempt 24: 7.3 25: 7.3 26: 4.9 % of attempts going < 2 air yards 24: 37% 25: 36% 26: 44.4% % going 10+ air yards 24: 30% 25: 28% 26: 20.6% — JJ Zachariason (@LateRoundQB) October 16, 2026 Nix also isn’t running as much as he has in previous years. That’s likely due to the ankle injury he suffered in last year’s playoffs, but it’s still a remarkable turn. After scrambling 83 times across his first two seasons, Nix has scrambled just nine times this season. Overall, he has 121 rushing yards on 43 attempts and just two touchdowns, on pace to be the least effective rushing season of his career. He’s also fumbled nine times this season, after fumbling just six times across the two prior seasons. Still, much like this current version of Rodgers, Nix can still unleash an impressive throw during the course of a game. He is exactly the type of quarterback who can put a drive together late if an opponent’s offense doesn’t put the Broncos away late and lets them hang in the game. Bo Nix dropped a DIME pic.twitter.com/b34bySOKTJ — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) November 22, 2026 The Broncos’ offense is mostly bad. Can the Steelers’ offense, now turning to Mason Rudolph, put up enough of a fight against Denver’s defense to win this game? To be determined. What to expect from the Broncos’ defense Passing YPG allowed: 230.3 (24th) Rushing YPG allowed: 126.2 (22nd) PPG allowed: 21 (11th) RB: The Bronco defense’s poor yardage numbers don’t really mesh with their strong reputation and status as a near-top-10 unit in points allowed. It’s an imperfect group, sure, but still a dangerous defense to face late in the year — especially if you’re a Steelers team that’s been going through some, uh, issues as of late. Denver hasn’t allowed a 30-point game since Week 1, with a defense that has closed out a number of tight games in a six-game winning streak. title: Steelers’ Nick Herbig still limited ahead of Broncos game
summary: With Aaron Rodgers’ televising his exposé on the Steelers and eventually being released Wednesday, it’s easy to forget that Pittsburgh still held a team practice ahead of a Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos. In the Steelers’ Wednesday injury report, outside linebacker Nick Herbig remained limited in practice for the second straight day as […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images With Aaron Rodgers’ televising his exposé on the Steelers and eventually being released Wednesday, it’s easy to forget that Pittsburgh still held a team practice ahead of a Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos. In the Steelers’ Wednesday injury report, outside linebacker Nick Herbig remained limited in practice for the second straight day as he recovers from a hip/ribs injury that caused him to miss Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Notably, the Steelers had several new names join the availability report, with safety DeShon Elliott (knee) and linebacker Cole Holcomb (ankle) appearing as limited. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers, now off the team, was unsurprisingly a non-participant for “personal” reasons; veteran defender Cam Heyward was also given a rest day. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (ankle) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) did not participate for the second straight practice on Wednesday. Still in their 21-day return windows from injured reserve, wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie guard Gennings Dunker continued to log full practices. #Steelers Week 12 Wednesday Injury Report pic.twitter.com/YfbJJfw21s — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 25, 2026 As for Denver, safety Taylor Rapp (limited; quadricep) and defensive end Sai’vion Jones (DNP; hamstring) were listed as out, but the rest of the team appears healthy. Running back Tyler Badie, who has logged full practices this week, is expected to be activated from IR at some point with the Broncos’ JK Dobbins serving a one-game team suspension this week. The Steelers have not yet released game designations for Black Friday’s game.

title: The Aaron Rodgers, Steelers breakup is the weirdest NFL story in a long time
summary: Of course Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Steelers — and possibly his entire NFL career — would end in a midweek episode of The Pat McAfee Show. How did we not see this coming? It all started with a bizarrely-timed team announcement from the Steelers. At 11 p.m. EST on Tuesday, team spokesman Burt Lauten […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images Of course Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Steelers — and possibly his entire NFL career — would end in a midweek episode of The Pat McAfee Show. How did we not see this coming? It all started with a bizarrely-timed team announcement from the Steelers. At 11 p.m. EST on Tuesday, team spokesman Burt Lauten released a statement saying that backup quarterback Mason Rudolph would start against the Broncos in Week 12, and that Rodgers wouldn’t just be benched, but inactive. pic.twitter.com/F2qo4OawcY — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 Sure, Rodgers wasn’t exactly playing at the level of an un-benchable quarterback, but everything about the move screamed that there was something else brewing behind the scenes. Why was the statement from Lauten and not head coach Mike McCarthy? More importantly, why was it late on a Tuesday night before the Steelers played the Denver Broncos on a short week Friday — and in a game with sizable implications in the AFC playoff picture? Sure enough, the other shoe dropped the next day, with Rodgers joining The Pat McAfee Show — where he’s filmed many a controversial segment over the last few seasons — on Wednesday to share his thoughts in a half-hour segment. And the future Hall of Fame quarterback didn’t hold back in a series of stories about alleged dysfunction under McCarthy’s leadership that would result in the team waiving Rodgers hours later. While the story is still unfolding, both Rodgers, and later McCarthy, spoke of an ultimatum between the two that came to a head with the quarterback’s release on Wednesday. “This has been months of conversation leading up to the last few days,” Rodgers said of his benching, adding that he found out about the decision not from the team, but from a phone conversation with teammate Pat Freiermuth. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy later disputed Rodgers’ claims, saying the team tried to reach out to the veteran quarterback several times. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the Steelers’ organization is supporting McCarthy with no plans of making an “immediate” coaching change following Tuesday and Wednesday’s events. McCarthy said he’s still the right person to lead the Steelers. “I know how to win. And that’s the facts,” he told the media in a Wednesday press conference . Rodgers told McAfee that he had talked “for a long time (in) the last few days” with McCarthy, later confirming that the two had met as late as 6:15 p.m. Tuesday without the topic of benching ever coming up. Rodgers said he still hadn’t heard from the team by midday Wednesday; he also said he had been taking starting reps through Tuesday. Rapoport reported that players were “surprised” by the benching. Then, Rodgers pivoted, saying he wanted to talk through his last week to explain “some of the issues I’ve been dealing with that ultimately led to where we’re at now.” Rodgers started with the Steelers’ Wednesday quarterback meeting before the Week 11 loss to the Eagles, saying that McCarthy was late and then had fallen asleep within 10 minutes of entering the meeting. Then, he woke himself up and promptly fell asleep again, later waking and leaving the room “like nothing happened.” Rodgers claimed that he and Steelers general manager Omar Khan have joked about McCarthy sleeping in meetings. McCarthy did not directly deny the claims of sleeping in meetings in his Wednesday press conference. “Thursday, (McCarthy) misses an offense meeting. Friday, he doesn’t come to the walkthrough,” Rodgers said, later adding that missed meetings have been a problem since training camp. “Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don’t have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason.” Rodgers went on to accuse McCarthy of “not wanting to get to know the defense,” despite prompting to get to know the players better. “(McCarthy) had already lost a lot of those guys,” Rodgers said. Rodgers said that “the nail in the coffin” was the 63-year-old head coach breaking down the team on “1, 2, 3, Packers” at halftime against the Eagles amid “weird rambling.” “We’re all looking around, like ‘What the f—-, what’s going on? Where’s his head at?’” Rodgers said. “We’ve had the conversations for months now — it began as a concerned friend, about someone who is unhealthy. If you’re sleeping in meetings, you’re unhealthy. … I could go week by week throughout the season on stuff that’s going on. This guy is calling the plays!” McCarthy confirmed to the media on Wednesday that he mistakenly did say “Packers” at halftime against the Eagles in an “embarrassing moment.” Rodgers recalled saying that the team needed a change on Monday, adding that “really, the entire team” agreed with the sentiment. “Everybody knows what’s going on,” he said. Then, on Tuesday, Rodgers said that McCarthy was behind on watching film and had only viewed clips. “There’s already a first- and second- and third-down install at this point,” Rodgers said, later saying that it was a repeat issue. “You’re unwell,” Rodgers said of McCarthy. “What’s best for the team is you give it up to somebody and you take care of yourself and work on your health.” Rodgers indicated that he had wanted McCarthy to continue acting as head coach but have quarterback coach Tom Arth call the plays. “We don’t have to tell anybody,” Rodgers recalled. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported early Wednesday that the team had been considering the move. From @gmfb : The #Steelers were set to make a change to their play-calling process, with QB coach Tom Arth to relay plays in to Aaron Rodgers at the behest of Rodgers. Hours late, the team announced Rodgers would be benched. More 👇🏼 pic.twitter.com/CXpJK2uHi9 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 25, 2026 Steelers insider Gerry Dulac later reported that Rodgers, on Tuesday, said he wanted to call plays for the team moving forward, telling the team to release him if not. “They called his bluff and released him,” Dulac posted . “This has been a conversation for weeks and weeks and weeks,” Rodgers said of his frustrations with McCarthy. “And every time I bring these things up, he just denies it.” In his press conference Wednesday, McCarthy said it was his decision to bench Rodgers, saying, “There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of (Rodgers’) job description.” The coach declined to “get into specifics.” Rodgers repeatedly said that others on the team and staff would agree with his claims. PennLive Steelers beat reporter Nick Farabaugh posted Wednesday that players hadn’t corroborated Rodgers’ statements on the record, but many in the organization have “backed up the claims Rodgers said about McCarthy.” ESPN’s Brooke Pryor also wrote that “multiple league sources corroborated Aaron Rodgers’ account of Mike McCarthy’s actions – sleeping in meetings, breaking down the huddle with ‘1,2,3 Packers’ (to ESPN).” “I don’t think (McCarthy) knows the plan,” Rodgers said. “He learns the plan during the week.” While Rodgers spent much of the segment with McAfee airing his grievances with McCarthy, the quarterback did say that he played a role in bringing the veteran coach, who at one point coached Rodgers in Green Bay, to the Steelers. “I did vouch for (McCarthy) to Omar,” Rodgers said of the Steelers’ head coaching interview process ahead of the 2026 season. “I’m not a victim; I’m accountable to this.” Rodgers claimed that McCarthy still blames him for getting fired from the Packers in 2018, something McCarthy denied in his Wednesday press conference. Rodgers added that McCarthy’s alleged issues have occurred throughout the latter’s time with the Cowboys and Packers. He said he had thought McCarthy would be different in 2026 knowing it was his quarterback’s last year in the NFL. Why haven’t more things come to light? Rodgers said players and coaches worry about job security. “I can (tell the truth) because what are the repercussions for me?” the veteran quarterback said. “I don’t care about…

title: Mike McCarthy has support of Steelers organization amid Aaron Rodgers saga, per report
summary: Speaking to the media for the first time since Aaron Rodgers was officially waived by the Steelers on Wednesday, head coach Mike McCarthy pushed back on many of his former quarterback’s claims about dysfunction in the organization. At the same time, it appears the team still has faith in its veteran head coach, with NFL […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images Speaking to the media for the first time since Aaron Rodgers was officially waived by the Steelers on Wednesday, head coach Mike McCarthy pushed back on many of his former quarterback’s claims about dysfunction in the organization. At the same time, it appears the team still has faith in its veteran head coach, with NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport posting Wednesday during McCarthy’s press conference that the coach still “has the full support of the organization.” #Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, the subject of Aaron Rodgers accusations today, has the full support of the organization, sources say. They are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes. pic.twitter.com/bRBqzmMlgc — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 25, 2026 “(The Steelers) are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes,” Rapoport wrote. With seven games remaining on the 2026 regular season schedule, it appears Pittsburgh will not be unseating McCarthy at head coach despite claims from Rodgers that he was missing and sleeping through meetings, behind in film study, and refusing to connect with defensive players on the roster. According to Steelers Now’s Alan Saunders , McCarthy said he had a meeting with the team’s leadership council, saying he still has the support of the locker room. “It was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind,” the coach told the press Wednesday. “I’m proud of our leadership.”

title: Marshawn Lynch, Richard Sherman, among former Seahawks advanced in Pro Football Hall of Fame voting
summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame has announced the 52 players who’ve advanced in the voting process for the Class of 2027. Of the 52 players, there are multiple with ties to the Seattle Seahawks. Running backs Shaun Alexander, Marshawn Lynch, and Ricky Watters, cornerback Richard Sherman, safety Earl Thomas, and defensive tackle, Kevin Williams […]
full_text: The Pro Football Hall of Fame has announced the 52 players who’ve advanced in the voting process for the Class of 2027. Of the 52 players, there are multiple with ties to the Seattle Seahawks. Running backs Shaun Alexander, Marshawn Lynch, and Ricky Watters, cornerback Richard Sherman, safety Earl Thomas, and defensive tackle, Kevin Williams have all advanced in the voting process. Of the six players listed, Sherman is in his first year of eligibility for the Hall of Fame. A few other players who had a cup of coffee with the Seahawks also advanced, including offensive lineman Jahri Evans and running back Adrian Peterson. Unfortunately for Alexander, Lynch, and Watters, they may have to wait at least another year. With the likes of Adrian Peterson and Frank Gore included in the 52, it would be tough to see any other running back advance too much deeper. The same could be said for Williams at defensive tackle. Defensive tackle has some other studs who could take the flowers away from Wiliams this year, including Haloti Ngata and Vince Wilfork. As for Thomas, despite his impressive career, the off the field issues and anticlimactic end to his career with the Baltimore Ravens may be cause to have him wait another year. Although his dominant play with the Legion of Boom should still give him a good shot at at least advancing to the next round of voting. The likeliest of the players listed above to make it all the way is Sherman who, along with Thomas and Kam Chancellor, helped lead the Seahawks to their first Supe Bbowl title in the 2013 season. Although fans can argue who was the biggest difference maker in the LOB between Sherman, Thomas, and Chancellor, nobody can deny that Sherman had the biggest moment of the three when he made the famous pass breakup against Michael Crabtree in the 2013 NFC Championship game against the San Francisco 49ers. That tip led to an interception by Malcolm Smith, paving the way for the Seahawks to make the Syoer Viwk. The other positive for Sherman is that he is still heard by national viewers (and the Hall of Fame selection committee) every week as an analyst and co-host for Amazon Prime Video’s Thursday Night Football (TNF) broadcast coverage. That should not matter to voters, however staying vocal (which Sherman is very good at) and in the news can only help your case. This is a stark contrast to how Thomas unfortunately has been since retiring. Although he did not make the final 52 players, I would be remiss not to express frustration as to the third Legion of Boom member, Kam Chancellor not being amongst the final 52 nominees. For those who remember watching the LOB, Chancellor was the tone setter for that defense. His physicality was what other teams feared, it is what made opponents lean towards making business decisions rather than fighting for another yard. Outside of the Sherman “tip” against the 49ers discussed above, Chancellor may have the second most memorable play by the LOB: The huge hit on 49ers tight end, Vernon Davis . That hit exemplifies the physicality that Chancellor brought to the Seahawks defense, and team as a whole. The knock on Chancellor may just be his short career, and lack of interceptions that Thomas and Sherman both bring to the table. Regardless, although this may not be Chancellor’s year, it may just be the year for the other Seahawk hopefuls. The Hall of Fame selection committee will reduce the list to 25 candidates in two weeks. The list of players will eventually be reduced to 13 to join Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft in the final 15 candidates. From there, the committee will reduce the list from 15 down to seven. Selectors in the committee can then vote for six of the seven remaining candidates. Any candidate receiving 80% approval will be elected to the Class of 2027.

full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have fallen in the NFC West standings as a result of the Los Angeles Rams’ 26-13 Thanksgiving Eve win over the Green Bay Packers, but there is a silver lining here for the reigning Super Bowl champions. Green Bay has dropped to 6-5 after losing its third game over the last five weeks. Seattle is now (temporarily, at least) ahead of the Packers in the Wild Card chase. While the Seahawks are behind the Rams by a half-game, they currently own the division record tiebreaker on their fierce rivals. This means that the Seahawks control their Wild Card fate, starting with Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. NFC playoff standings with Rams win Wednesday night 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 2. Detroit Lions (8-2, 2-0 NFCN) 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) 5. Chicago Bears (8-2, 0-2 NFCN) 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 7. Los Angeles Rams (7-4) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Green Bay Packers (6-5) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (4-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7, 1-0 vs ATL+NO) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7, 1-1 vs TB+NO) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7, 0-1 vs TB+ATL, 1-5 NFC) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7, 1-6 NFC) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) If the Seahawks defeat the 49ers, Seattle is the 7-seed heading into Week 13. title: Seahawks-49ers Wednesday injury report: Sam Darnold practices in full
summary: Coming off two consecutive wins and their bye, there’s plenty working in favor of the Seattle Seahawks as they head into a pivotal matchup against the NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but Wednesday’s injury report wasn’t exactly promising. Seahawks Nov. 25 practice report Did not participate: Limited participant: Full participant With the status of […]
full_text: (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off two consecutive wins and their bye, there’s plenty working in favor of the Seattle Seahawks as they head into a pivotal matchup against the NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but Wednesday’s injury report wasn’t exactly promising. Seahawks Nov. 25 practice report Did not participate: LB Demarcus Lawrence (shoulder) OT Abraham Lucas (ankle) QB Jalen Milroe (illness) OG Quenton Nelson (knee) DT Jarran Reed (toe) Limited participant: OG Anthony Bradford (knee, illness) QB Drew Lock (right elbow) OT Charles Cross (ankle) LB Ernest Jones IV (knee) TE Nick Kallerup (ankle) WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) DT Leonard Williams (stinger) Full participant QB San Darnold (quadricep, ribs) LB Patrick O’Connell (toe) With the status of backups quarterbacks Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe up in the air, a full practice for Sam Darnold certainly bodes well for his return to come against the 49ers. During Monday’s press conference, head coach Mike Macdonald refused to make any officials declarations regarding the Super Bowl winning quarterback, but said Wednesday’s practice would be a big indicator of whether he’d be able to suit up, and it appears he’s trending in the right direction. Macdonald has not yet confirmed Darnold as the starter, but stated he remains the team’s go-to guy when healthy and a quarterback change is not being contemplated. Although Lock’s right elbow tendinitis has lingered since October, he’s suited up the past two weeks and his limited practice merely appears cautionary. Regarding Milroe, whether he’s able to particpant in any capacity over the next two days will likely determine his availability against San Francisco, but the team has recently signed QB Adrian Martinez on their practice squad should he be sidelined this weekend. Regardless of who’s under center, they’ll face an additional challenge with OG Quenton Nelson and OT Abraham Lucas ruled out, a move announced by Macdonald this afternoon . Josh Jones is set to draw the start in place of Lucas, with Anthony Bradford in line to suit up at right guard — if he’s cleared. Despite having played in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, the fourth-year pro was limited with a knee injury that forced him to practice in a limited capacity leading up to the game, and it appears to still be lingering. Bradford previously missed five weeks while on injured reserve as he dealt with a knee injury originally suffered in Week 2. Should he be unable to go, rookie Beau Stephens would be in line to draw the start. Arguably the two most troublesome absences’ are that of DT Jarran Reed and LB Demarcus Lawrence. Reed originally suffered a toe injury against the Raiders but later returned to the game. It remains unknown if the team’s decision to hold him out is cautionary or because it worsened, but his status tomorrow will definitely be an indicator for Sunday. As for Lawrence, there hadn’t been an indication he was dealing with an injury and the severity remains unclear. Although DT Leonard Williams’ limited practice is an improvement, WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and LB Ernest Jones IV not participant in a full capacity is alarming. However, the veteran linebacker previously popped up on Seattle’s practice report for Week 3 and 9 with separate injuries and went on to play — so his status downgrade shouldn’t be flagged just yet. The same goes for Smith-Njigba, who was flagged for an ankle injury prior to the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Denver Broncos and went on to play without an injury designation. Further updates should come tomorrow when Seattle holds their second practice of the week as well as when they release their official injury designations on Friday.

title: It’s separation week for the Seahawks and the NFL
summary: Happy Thanksgiving to all, and to all, holy catfish, do we have some amazing football this week! Not only do we have four days of NFL action starting today, but we have some absolutely epic matchups while we’re stuffing our faces. Not only are there some incredible matchups (ignore the Sunday morning matchups), but many […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving to all, and to all, holy catfish, do we have some amazing football this week! Not only do we have four days of NFL action starting today, but we have some absolutely epic matchups while we’re stuffing our faces. Not only are there some incredible matchups (ignore the Sunday morning matchups), but many of these matchups will bring clarity to the hierarchy of contenders as this season heads into the final six weeks. On the appetizers level, Cleveland should absolutely be rocking on Sunday Night Football , as they look to bury the Raiders dim playoff hopes, and take a stranglehold on a playoff spot of their own. In case you didn’t hear the spectacular news, Mike McCarthy gets the last laugh, benching Aaron Rodgers and potentially ending one of the weirdest QB/coach relationships in NFL history. Instead, we’ll watch the Broncos try to keep pace in the AFC West race, while we’re forced to go through the Mason Rudolph experience. The last of our appetizers will be on Monday Night Football , as the Panthers look to put the pathetic NFC South to bed, as a road win in Tampa could have Carolina actually getting above .500 and locking up a second straight division title. From a Seahawks perspective, there’s a path where Seattle may find themselves traveling to Charlotte for wildcard weekend, so even if Joe Buck and Troy Aikman are miserable throughout, this game could play a pivotal role in the Seahawks season. Now, onto the main courses. Wednesday night we have the Green Bay Packers coming to Los Angeles to take on the Puka-less Rams. Returning to the Packers is superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons. I thought that the Packers looked like a Super Bowl contender at points last year, with Parsons. If he could improve the Green Bay defense even marginally, then the Pack become much more of a threat to stealing a playoff spot from Seattle. While the Rams continue to be wounded, they’re still 6-4 and seemed to morphed into a ground and pound team that is getting better each week defensively. This isn’t a loser goes home game, but the loser falls behind a game behind the winner, but also loses the tiebreaker. I may regret what I’m about to say, but I want the Rams to win. The Seahawks need to keep winning, and they control their destiny with two matchups still to come against the Rams, whereas they have no control over what the Packers will do here in the second half. We may have arguably the greatest duo of games in Thanksgiving history as we’ll see potential conference championship previews in both the NFC and AFC. In the 10am window, we have the titans of the North meeting in Detroit as the Lions take on the Bears. Seattle fans have seen what the Bears are capable of, while the Lions continue to win despite continuous stupid injuries. I really think this is arguably the best and biggest matchup of the week. The Lions are so difficult at home, so I wouldn’t be surprised if they win and take the lead in the division race. If the Bears win, that’d be their second statement win on the road, and the NFC could really start to feel like a two team race with the 49ers. With the Bears already defeating the Seahawks, the rooting guide calls for hoping Chicago wins. The third and final game is another duel between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. Who would’ve guessed before the season started that Patrick Mahomes would be the one playing at an MVP level, while Josh Allen has been far from his superstar standard, but that has not kept Buffalo from their best 10 game start since 90’s super Buffalo years. With Cincinnati and Jacksonville taking brutal losses on Monday night, the winner of this game will become the favorite for the #1 seed in the AFC. I can already hear the Switfies and league offices assembling their army for one last Super Bowl run. Speaking of Super Bowl runs, there may be no better chance than now for the San Francisco 49ers to finally get over the hump. Another dominating win in a different country, Kyle Shanahan’s squad looks like the class of the NFL as Brock Purdy has ascended to legit MVP frontrunner and Fred Warner has returned to being arguably the best defensive player on the planet. They look really tough, but that doesn’t mean they’re not vulnerable in the biggest game of the week for the Seahawks, and arguably Seattle’s biggest game of the season. The Seahawks are rested, in better shape health wise, and we may be seeing the healthiest version of San Darnold, paired with a running game and defense that seems to be flexing its muscle more and more each week. The 49ers are coming off a weeklong period that saw them win a shootout against the Cowboys, prepare for the Mexico City altitude in Colorado Springs, and then beat the snot out of the Vikings in Azteca. If there’s ever a moment where rest and desperation meet a tired team that is sitting pretty with its and comfortable in its current standings, this is it. There’s no dancing around it, this is the defining separation game for the Seahawks. A win with either quarterback likely settles what debate is left between Sam Darnold and Drew Lock, and you could then conceivably make a real case that Seattle, despite a worse record, was the better team in their two matchups vs San Francisco. They’d jump ahead of either the Rams or Packers for the final wildcard spot, and they’d be nipping at the heels of the NFC North contenders for that coveted #5 seed which is the NFC South door all wildcard teams would prefer. At 7-4, with wins over the Chiefs and 49ers in the past five weeks, I think Seahawks fans should feel good about dreaming big again, even if the path to Super Bowl 61 means a month-long road trip. A loss on Sunday, and reality really begins to set in. Seattle would then fall into the position of nearly needing to win out, just to get into the playoffs as a No. 7 seed. I’m sure a loss would create more questions about the quarterback position, and having been swept in three games by the Bears and 49ers, you have to wonder about the future of this team’s contention window. Either way, we have an incredible week of football and should get some real clarity about the Seahawks, and the league after this weekend.

title: Chargers claim former Seahawks corner who was traded to Seattle 3 months ago
summary: The Seattle Seahawks gave up a draft pick to get cornerback Avery Smith from the Los Angeles Chargers, and now the Chargers have both the pick and Smith back. Per the NFL transaction wire, Smith was claimed off waivers by the Chargers, who sit at 1-9 and are otherwise dealing with depth issues at cornerback. […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks gave up a draft pick to get cornerback Avery Smith from the Los Angeles Chargers, and now the Chargers have both the pick and Smith back. Per the NFL transaction wire, Smith was claimed off waivers by the Chargers, who sit at 1-9 and are otherwise dealing with depth issues at cornerback. Smith was traded to Seattle for a 2027 sixth-round pick , having had a solid preseason as an undrafted rookie. Seattle’s uncertain cornerback room settled in quite nicely, with Nehemiah Pritchett having the best year of his young career, while veteran Trevon Diggs has also played 36 defensive snaps as an extra corner. Smith ultimately did not play any defensive snaps in his brief time with the Seahawks. He had a couple of healthy scratches (including Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders) and was limited to special teams, recording five total tackles and two penalties. Smith did notably struggle handling punt return gunners in Week 9 versus the Arizona Cardinals. Needless to say, while it’s only a Day 3 pick given up for Smith, this trade didn’t work out all that well for the Seahawks. They kicked the tires on a young corner (while already having two corners, Andre Fuller and Michael Dansby, on the practice squad) and he neither got on the field on defense nor contributed all that positively on special teams. Three months later, he’s back with his original team.

full_text: (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are set to release their first injury report for Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers, but we can already rule out a couple of players before Wednesday’s practice is even completed. Mike Macdonald told reporters that left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle) are both out. Macdonald described Nelson as “close” to returning from his recent procedure , whereas Lucas’ ankle injury suffered in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders is not severe enough to land him on injured reserve. He considers Lucas’ timetable in the range of “days to weeks.” Josh Jones, who started for Charles Cross at left tackle when Cross was out with his own ankle injury, will slide over to right tackle in Lucas’ absence. Cross is expected to be back at left tackle after a two-game absence. It’s worth noting that right guard Anthony Bradford (knee) will be limited on Wednesday, although that was what transpired for the Raiders game before he had full participation status on Friday. Seattle signed Bobby Hart from the practice squad earlier this week to serve as additional swing tackle depth, while Chase Lundt was poached off the Buffalo Bills practice squad for guard/tackle versatility. Stay tuned for Seattle’s initial injury/practice report later this afternoon.

title: Rams versus Packers live discussion: We’re all cheeseheads tonight
summary: The seventh-seeded Green Bay Packers take on the 9th-seeded Los Angeles Rams. full_text: The seventh-seeded Green Bay Packers take on the 9th-seeded Los Angeles Rams. That is not something you would have thought would be true about these two teams at this point in the season if somebody had told you that in August. The Packers hold the tiebreaker over the Rams, thanks to a better conference record. This is a matchup the Packers have dominated. Against the Rams, Green Bay is 20-2 in their last 22 games. They are 10-1 in the last 11. When you own a team to that extent, it’s no longer a trend. It’s domination. Green Bay has fared pretty well in their last dozen contests against the NFC West in general. It’s odd, but it can’t be ignored. The Rams are without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. That hasn’t slowed down the Rams during the past month, as they still rank sixth in the league in EPA per play and success rate. But they’ve faced the Cardinals twice, the Commanders, Chargers, and Raiders since Week 6. The last time they faced a top offense was in Week 5, and the Bills scored 37 points. To their credit, the Rams have been stingy defensively. Only one team has scored more than 18 points since the Bills game. They’ve dictated much of the game, but this will be an offense that can truly challenge the Rams in ways they haven’t been all season. The Packers are one of those “all-or-nothing” kind of offenses. They can go multiple drives without scoring, and then hit on a big play or three to flip the scoreboard. This should be a lower-scoring game. It probably won’t be fun to watch. History says the Packers will win. Micah Parsons is back, and that should make it a living hell for Matthew Stafford, who has been off all season. Packers 24, Rams 21.

title: 49ers injury report: Brock Purdy suffered an ankle injury
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have a huge division matchup with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took the podium to update the media on injuries and player statuses heading into the game. The obvious news is that right tackle Colton McKivitz is placed on injured reserve, but the big news […]
full_text: (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have a huge division matchup with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took the podium to update the media on injuries and player statuses heading into the game. The obvious news is that right tackle Colton McKivitz is placed on injured reserve , but the big news is Brock Purdy’s ankle injury, which happened in the second quarter of Sunday night’s win over the Vikings in Mexico City. Shanahan said Purdy won’t practice on Wednesday with the ankle injury, and he was aware of the injury during the game on Sunday night. When asked if there was any concern about the injury moving forward, Shanahan said: “We’ll see.” The injury happened in the second quarter against the Vikings, and Shanahan said it didn’t affect his play in the game and was checked out and deemed “fine.” Shanahan said it’s possible he won’t go on Sunday, but the injury isn’t a high ankle injury, and Purdy will be day-to-day. It’s hard to diagnose how the week will progress or take anything from Shanahan’s statement, which was very matter-of-fact. For now, fans will have to take the news as it comes, but shouldn’t panic that Purdy will miss on Sunday. The other updates were that Deommodore Lenoir, Upton Stout, Austen Pleasants, and Carver Willis were limited today in practice with different ailments. Dre Greenlaw and Siran Neal both missed today’s practice. Shanahan was asked about Vederian Lowe and stated that he will be the new starter at right tackle, and Pleasants has actually been healthy for a few weeks and, with the obvious situation, will be activated to the roster. Lowe was praised by Shanahan, who said he played really well, especially against Minnesota, and this situation is why he was brought in as the swing tackle. Pleasants has a chance to be activated and serve as the swing tackle moving forward. The 49ers are an injury away from rookie Enrique Cruz taking the field. Pleasants would give the team a veteran presence.

title: 49ers activate veteran cornerback from the IR; Brandin Cook joins the practice squad
summary: The San Francisco 49ers announced a couple of transactions on Wednesday. The 49ers activated cornerback Nate Hobbs from the injured reserve list. The 49ers needed to make the move, or Hobbs’ season would have ended because his practice window had closed. Where Hobbs fits in will be worth monitoring. Throughout his career, Hobbs has rarely […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced a couple of transactions on Wednesday. The 49ers activated cornerback Nate Hobbs from the injured reserve list. The 49ers needed to make the move, or Hobbs’ season would have ended because his practice window had closed. Where Hobbs fits in will be worth monitoring. Throughout his career, Hobbs has rarely played special teams. Unless he’s part of Raheem Morris’s sub packages or rotating with one of the cornerbacks, Hobbs’s main role with the 49ers would be on special teams. The corresponding move was to place right tackle Colton McKivitz on the injured reserve. The 49ers also brought back wide receiver Brandin Cooks to the practice squad. Cooks joins Khadarel Hodge, Will Pauling, and Wesley Grimes on the practice squad at receiver. Given his veteran experience, it makes you wonder whether the 49ers will lean on Cooks come playoff time. Perhaps in an emergency situation, if one of the younger players slips up over the next month and a half.

title: Why the first matchup between the 49ers and Seahawks was so strange
summary: The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, 32-29. To say it was a strange game is an understatement. It was also thrilling and exhilarating. Wins are wins in the NFL, but this win was particularly odd given how it played out. The 49ers’ defensive line was excellent. The secondary was exceptional. […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, 32-29. To say it was a strange game is an understatement. It was also thrilling and exhilarating. Wins are wins in the NFL, but this win was particularly odd given how it played out. The 49ers’ defensive line was excellent. The secondary was exceptional. The offense converted in the red zone, as they have done so effectively this season. So, what made this game so odd? Despite the score, this was the highest-scoring defensive struggle I may have ever seen. How can you call it a defensive struggle with over 60 total points? Let me explain. The 49ers scored a touchdown on a George Holani fumble before halftime. The Seahawks scored points on the back of a Jacob Cowing muffed punt. Deebo Samuel popped his hamstring and fell flat on his face, and the ball came loose for another turnover on the plus side of the field for Seattle. In fact, the initial touchdown for the 49ers started with a Renardo Green interception deep in Seattle’s territory. Now, the reason I point this out is that turnovers were the story of this game. Seattle’s offense likely doesn’t score much without turnovers. The 49ers certainly capitalized on their turnovers, and the biggest drive of the game was a drive that started from the Seattle 26 in the fourth quarter, which was punctuated by a seven-yard touchdown catch by Brandin Cooks. The reason I point all these things out is that it’s hard to expect this type of scenario and, at times, sloppiness from both teams again. Turnovers will be a major part of the story on Sunday as Sam Darnold returns, and if he continues the trend of turning the football over, it will hinder Seattle’s chances. With Darnold as the quarterback, the only stretch of football he has played without turning the football over was from Week 18 (against SF) through the playoffs with a Super Bowl win. That’s a four-game stretch. I’m willing to bet he’s going to make some mistakes on Sunday. Seattle’s defense is still elite, in a much different way than Minnesota is, but if turnovers happen and Seattle is backed up defending their own end zone, that’s a recipe for success for the 49ers. Week 5 was filled with chaos and jaw-dropping scenarios. I expect Sunday to be far more composed and just as tight a matchup.

title: Brandon Aiyuk joins the Commanders’ practice squad
summary: The least surprising transaction to happen on Tuesday was former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk visiting the Washington Commanders. While Aiyuk has yet to sign officially, it was a move that was the most predictable outcome. The Commanders need a wideout. Former 49ers general manager Adam Peters now runs the show in Washington. […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The least surprising transaction to happen on Tuesday was former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk visiting the Washington Commanders. While Aiyuk has yet to sign officially, it was a move that was the most predictable outcome. The Commanders need a wideout. Former 49ers general manager Adam Peters now runs the show in Washington. Aiyuk’s college quarterback, Jayden Daniels, just so happens to be under center in DC. During a radio appearance on Wednesday, Peters called Aiyuk one of the “hardest workers on the team” when he was with the 49ers. “One of the things that I don’t think anyone can dispute is his work ethic. That’s how he became an All-Pro-type player. He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He’s a guy who’s a tough cover; he’s great after the catch. There’s a lot of great things about him on the field. It wasn’t just that he was the most gifted guy; he’s self-made too. There’s a lot of positives.” The caveat “on the field” is doing a lot of work here. While the 49ers may have had some buyer’s remorse after his injury, Aiyuk put on a clinic of what not to do for the past year and a half. That’s why he was released . Peters, who hasn’t spoken to Aiyuk in “a couple years,” continued. “I can’t speak on all what happened between him and the 49ers. What I do remember is he’s a very motivated player.” Maybe there was no resolution to be had. But you’d think if Aiyuk had any kind of motivation left, he would’ve swallowed his pride and gone to work for the team with the best record in the conference. Doesn’t winning on the big stage have to mean something? Again, there was likely no coming back from whatever the “situation” was, but Aiyuk had every reason to be motivated last year, when we saw him running routes in August in a preseason game with the team. Then, as the year went along, a No. 1 receiver never emerged. Aiyuk could’ve been the top target for a playoff team. The motivation is different now. It’s been two years since Aiyuk played in the NFL. Unless he’s training against NFL defensive backs on the side, he hasn’t gone against the best competition in the world since a season-ending knee injury. Expecting anything close to the 1,300-yard receiver feels like a long shot. We’ll keep a close eye on whether Aiyuk signs to Washington’s practice squad and where the two sides go from there, but this story is far from over. Kyle’s update, 10:00 am PT : ESPN’s Adam Schefter tweeted that Aiyuk finished up his visit with the Commanders, but there won’t be a deal today. Here’s Schefter’s quote from Drew Rosenhaus: “Discussions are ongoing and positive. Probably no decision today.” Aka, we could not agree on terms today. Kyle’s update, 10:20 am PT: So much for that. About twenty minutes later, Aiyuk is joining the Commanders’ practice squad. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026

title: Malik Mustapha wins his appeal; NFL rescinds fine for hit on Jaxon Smith-Njigba
summary: Over a month ago, when the San Francisco 49ers were in Seattle, the NFL fined safety Malik Mustapha for a “hit on a defenseless player.” It was on the final drive of the game that Mustapha hit Jaxon-Smith Njigba. Raheem Morris calls it the “strike zone,” which is above the belt and below the neck. […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over a month ago, when the San Francisco 49ers were in Seattle, the NFL fined safety Malik Mustapha for a “hit on a defenseless player.” It was on the final drive of the game that Mustapha hit Jaxon-Smith Njigba. Raheem Morris calls it the “strike zone,” which is above the belt and below the neck. That’s where Mustapha hit JSN, yet the NFL still felt the need to step in. The league fined Mustapha $6,998. Mustapha will be happy to get those funds back. More importantly, from the 49ers’ perspective, it means Mustapha no longer has one strike to his name. This year, three violations of specific offenses equal a one-game suspension. Upon appeal, the NFL rescinded the $6,998 fine it assessed to 49ers S Malik Mustapha for this hit earlier in the season on Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Jordy Nelson was the hearing officer. The 49ers and Seahawks play again Sunday. pic.twitter.com/S0IU2KwFiw — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 Mustapha came close against the Cowboys. The kind of force Mustapha plays with, he’ll always come close to what’s deemed “unnecessary” in today’s NFL. So, getting one strike back could pay dividends in the second half of the season. Back in Week 5, Mustapha had another collision where he de-cleated Rashid Shaheed. It was clean and in the strike zone, but a lot of these flags, and eventually penalties, stem from the result or how a player peels himself off the turf. There were a couple of those in Week 5. Malik should not change who he is. He made a difference the last time these two teams met. Hopefully, he won’t be fined for tackling again.

title: Do the Titans need to sign another big-money CB this offseason?
summary: The Tennessee Titans entered this past offseason with no starting cornerbacks on the roster. Mike Borgonzi inherited the L’Jarius Sneed nightmare from the previous regime, and released him when it became financially plausible. He also traded Roger McCreary and Jarvis Brownlee during the 2025 season. Both players haven’t done much since leaving. Marcus Harris was […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TN - NOVEMBER 15: Tennessee Titans cornerback Joshua Williams (25) and cornerback Alontae Taylor (24) run onto the field prior to a game between the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars, November 15, 2026, at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Matthew Maxey/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Tennessee Titans entered this past offseason with no starting cornerbacks on the roster. Mike Borgonzi inherited the L’Jarius Sneed nightmare from the previous regime, and released him when it became financially plausible. He also traded Roger McCreary and Jarvis Brownlee during the 2025 season. Both players haven’t done much since leaving. Marcus Harris was viewed as the nickelback, but the defense had zero starters on the boundary. When free agency opened, in collaboration with head coach Robert Saleh, Borgonzi signed Alontae Taylor and Cor’Dale Flott to three-year contracts. Taylor earns $19 million annually, while Flott is paid $15 million per year. The results have been fairly disappointing . The Taylor acquisition has especially been a drastic mistake. The Titans signed him to play cornerback, but abandoned that mission after five weeks. They’ve since moved Taylor to nickel, his more natural position, while benching Harris, who was playing well. It’s painfully obvious they are attempting to salvage an ill-advised contract. Flott hasn’t been as bad as this fanbase suggests. He’s played quite decently in some games. If the Titans could field any semblance of a pass rush, you’d likely be surprised with how effective Flott is as this defense’s CB2. The issue is Taylor and his contract. There’s no logical escape route next offseason. In all likelihood, the Titans will absorb the Taylor blow through next season, and release him the following offseason (2028). The Taylor mistake likely puts the Titans back into the market for a starting cornerback this coming offseason. They cannot enter 2027 with Joshua Williams or Micah Robinson as a starter. Unless they draft Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore with a top-five selection in the 2027 NFL Draft, they’d be asking a lot of a late first-or-second-round cornerback to start immediately in Week 1, especially in Saleh’s complex defense. The Titans may have to consider signing another veteran cornerback to start opposite Taylor. Ideally, it would be a highly-drafted rookie, but free agency poses another avenue. Some of the known cornerbacks on expiring contracts include Joey Porter Jr., D.J. Turner, Tyrique Stevenson, Tariq Woolen, and Marlon Humphrey. Brandin Echoles, who played for Saleh in NY, is also a pending free agent. Saleh would probably love to get someone like D.J. Reed, who is under contract with the Detroit Lions (but may be available?).
