title: Washington Commanders officially sign Brandon Aiyuk to practice squad
summary: UPDATE: The Commanders have officially announced the signing of receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad. They also added cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, and released receiver Malik Heath from the practice squad in a corresponding move. It’s clear that Aiyuk will need some time to get used to the Commanders’ offensive system […]
full_text: UPDATE: The Commanders have officially announced the signing of receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad. They also added cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, and released receiver Malik Heath from the practice squad in a corresponding move. It’s clear that Aiyuk will need some time to get used to the Commanders’ offensive system and to get into NFL game shape, and he’ll also need to help run the Washington scout team. His activation will come in time and try to help the Commanders down the stretch in their attempt to win the NFC East. We have made the following roster moves: – Signed WR Brandon Aiyuk and CB Ambry Thomas to the practice squad – Released WR Malik Heath from the practice squad — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 26, 2026 The Commanders have signed receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday. The free agent, who was released by the San Francisco 49ers and formally cleared waivers, met with the Commanders at the team’s complex on Wednesday . Per Schefter, Aiyuk signed contract to join the team’s practice squad. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 This move was telegraphed somewhat, with the Tuesday release of running back Craig Reynolds to open up a spot. Aiyuk will have an opportunity to work himself back into game shape after more than two years on the shelf. The Commanders can elevate him when ready, or they can sign him to the active roster at a time of their choosing. He can be elevated three times before Washington has to formally activate him. Washington has been Aiyuk’s preferred destination, a point that was clear when he started wearing Commanders gear in social media posts over the summer. Some quick background: The 49ers drafted Aiyuk in the first round back in 2020 and then inked him to a four-year, $120-million contract in 2024. Then things got messy. Aiyuk suffered a serious knee injury during the 2024 campaign and didn’t play after that. The 49ers took issue with Aiyuk’s choice to rehab away from their facility, and it created a schism and a rift that was never repaired. The 49ers voided Aiyuk’s guarantees and placed him on the exempt/did not report list. Then Aiyuk went on a social media tirade, torching 49ers GM John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. He also took some shots at Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels – Aiyuk and Daniels were good friends and teammates at Arizona State – and his mother. They have reportedly mended fences, which set the stage for this signing. Commanders GM Adam Peters was also involved in the Aiyuk draft pick when he was in San Francisco. Aiyuk had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023, shockingly his last full season in the NFL. There’s no doubting Aiyuk’s talent, though it has been some time since that has led to production. How long it takes for Aiyuk to get ready is to be determined, but Washington needs him to get prepared fast to keep this good thing going. It’s hard to imagine he’ll be ready for Sunday’s road game against the Arizona Cardinals, especially with his need to catch up learning the Commanders system. And there’s great shape and football shape, which are two totally different things. Let us know your thoughts about this Brandon Aiyuk signing in the article comments below:

If Aiyuk is anything close to the player he was in 2023, when he earned second-team All-Pro honors and, in Peters’ words, “was a true No. 1 receiver,” Washington will have added a first-round talent at a bargain rate. If Aiyuk appears to have lost a step after two-plus years out of the game or otherwise does not work out, Washington can easily cut ties at minimal cost; he’s not taking a spot on the active roster and he’ll be paid a minimal weekly salary. If the Commanders elevate him for as many as three games, the limit for a practice-squad player, his total salary for the rest of the season would max out at roughly $306,000, a bargain rate for a player viewed as a No. 1 receiver and a far cry from what he was slated to earn in the remainder of his deal with the 49ers. Any further elevations would require that they sign him to the active roster. Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told reporters earlier this month that the veteran receiver is fully healthy after suffering a multi-ligament knee injury in 2024. But Aiyuk hasn’t played a snap, in a game or practice, since Oct. 20, 2024 — 766 days to be exact. Aiyuk will likely need a significant ramp-up period to get back into football conditioning and get acclimated to the Commanders’ offense, and as a practice-squad player, he’ll be afforded fewer practice reps than the receivers on the active roster. title: Stats and Snaps – 2026 Week 11, Commanders vs Bengals
summary: The story of the Commanders’ season has been playing up to the level of the best teams in the league and playing down to the level of some of the worst ones. Until Week 9, they had struggled to find ways to win close games. For the second week in a row, the Commanders pulled […]
full_text: The story of the Commanders’ season has been playing up to the level of the best teams in the league and playing down to the level of some of the worst ones. Until Week 9, they had struggled to find ways to win close games. For the second week in a row, the Commanders pulled off a game-winning drive after the two minute warning. While it may be too early to pronounce a turnaround to the disappointing 2026 season, fans who have kept hope alive for a return to 2024 form would have recognised the calm determination and surgical precision Jayden Daniels showed as he led the team into field goal range on a drive that began with 39 seconds remaining. Over the past few games, the Commanders’ identity has finally started to come into focus. In addition to a magician at QB, Daronte Jones’ aggressive defense is emerging as a strength. The Bengals rank 4 th in total points. Prior to facing the Commanders, they were averaging 30.9 point per game. The Commanders are one of only three teams to hold them to under 27 points, along with the Jaguars and Texans. That level of defense, and a quarterback who is up to any challenge, can allow Washington to compete with the best teams in football, if they can just stay out of their own way. Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal with time expiring sealed the Commanders’ first back-to-back wins since the divisional round of the 2024 playoffs. They need to keep stacking the wins to catch up with the division-leading Giants and keep their playoff hopes alive. Fortunately, they only need to equal the Giants’ win total to win the division, thanks to the Week 10 win giving them the advantage of the head-to-head tiebreaker. The Commanders only play two opponents with winning records in the seven remaining games, while the Giants have yet to run the gauntlet of the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions. Hopefully the Cowboys stay out of the mix. But the Commanders may have the opportunity to settle the matter if Jerry’s boys are still keeping it close by the time of the Week 18 rematch. There is still a lot of football left to play. Against the 7-2 Bengals, the Commanders did what they needed to do to keep their season alive. They will need to keep building on the winning formula of aggressive defense, ball control and executing when it matters to get off of life support and hit the post-season with momentum. Fans who still have doubts just need to rewatch the final two minutes of Monday night’s game. To drive that message home, let’s take a look at who stood out – it’s a long list – whose play left room for improvement – shorter list – and where they all lined up in the Commanders’ 22-20 upset of the Cincinnati Bengals in primetime. Technicalities: Stats were sourced from the official NFL gamebook via NFLGSIS, Pro Football Reference (PFR), Pro Football Focus (PFF) and ESPN’s total QBR. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). Where differences in advanced stats result from judgment calls (eg. Coverage yards allowed, broken tackles) I have gone with a modified consensus approach. When there is fundamental disagreement between sources, the stats won’t be reported. Minor differences between sources that support the same conclusion are reported. If advanced stats are reported without attribution of source, it means there was consensus. As always, official NFL stats override conflicting data from other sources. 2026 reference ranges for the advanced metrics used in the Stats and Snaps were published in the Week 10 Stats Roundups ( Offense , Defense ), to help readers get a sense of what are good or not so good numbers for the different positions. BIGGEST PLAYS OF THE GAME These plays had the largest impact on teams’ scoring potential within a drive, as judged by Expected Points Added (EPA). Threshhold: EPA = +/- 2.20 Biggest Plays for Commanders Q4, 0.23, 2 nd and 10 at WAS 50: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep middle to Antonio Williams for 42 yards. EPA 3.66 Q4, 6:48, 2 nd and 20 at WAS 25: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep middle to Stefon Diggs for 29 yards. EPA 3.15 Q2, 0:54, 2 nd and 7 at CIN 38: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep middle to Chig Okonkwo for 32 yards. EPA 3.12 Q3, 13:44, 1 st and 10 at WAS 39: Jayden Daniels scrambles up the middle for 47 yards. EPA 3.12 Q1, 1:03, 4 th and 1 at CIN 45: Joe Burrow left end for no gain (tackle by Frankie Luvu). EPA -2.2 Biggest Plays for Bengals Q2, 3:02, 3 rd and 11 at CIN 22: Joe Burrow pass complete short middle to Samaje Perine for 44 yards. EPA 4.2 Q2, 2:00, 2 nd and 7 at WAS 31: Joe Burrow pass complete deep left to Tee Higgins for 31 yards, touchdown. EPA 3.82 Q2, 8:34, 4 th and 2 at WAS 37: Joe Burrow pass complete short middle to Mike Gesicki for 11 yards. EPA 3.05 Q1, 3:52, 3 rd and 9 at CIN 19: Joe Burrow pass complete short right to Samaje Perine for 17 yards. Samaje Perine fumbles, ball out of bounds at CIN-36. EPA 2.37 Q4, 0:50, 4 th and 14 at WAS 37: Evan McPherson 56 yd field goal good. EPA 2.21 OFFENSE JD5 completed 23/35 (65.7%, ADOT 7.8 yds) for 289 yds, with no TDs or INTs, while taking 3 sacks for 11 yds. Two of Jayden’s completions for 64 yds occurred on the the final drive, with 39 seconds remaining, to set up the game-winning field goal. It was his second game-winning drive of the season. According to PFF, he faced pressure on 35.7% of dropbacks. He ran the ball 6 times for 55 yds (9.2 Y/A) and 2 first downs, with a long of 47 yds (33.3% success rate 33.3%). Jayden’s effort was good for a 58.6 total QBR, ranking him 13 th among starting QBs in Week 11. While not used extensively, the two backs given opportunities were well above the league average of 2.2 YBC/att this week. Not surprisingly, both were at or near the top of the league in rushing success rate in Week 11. Jacory Croskey-Merritt was just behind Jayden in total yardage, with 54 yds on 13 att (4.2 Y/A), 1 TD, and 4 first downs. He achieved a healthy 2.5 YBC/att on his carries. Bill’s 76.9% rushing success rate was the highest among all NFL players with more than 10 rushing attempts in Week 11. He also caught 2/3 targets for 23 yds, with a long reception of 18 yds. All 23 yards were gained after the catch. He led the team at an impressive 11.5 YAC/rec, and was the Commanders’ second-most productive receiver at 2.30 Y/RR. Ekeler found plenty of room to run, averaging 4.1 YBC/att. Ekeler caught 2/3 targets for 3 yds. Rachaad White did not touch the ball. Antonio Williams earned a Pepsi Rookie of the Week nomination for his best game as a pro, catching 9/11 targets (81.8% rec, ADOT 8.7 yds) for 122 yds, including receptions of 22 and 42 yards, constituting the game winning drive. He was the Commanders’ most productive receiver, at an impressive 3.05 Y/RR. Williams gained 63 yards after the catch, for a whopping 7.0 YAC/rec. He caught his only contested target. title: Washington Commanders vs. Cardinals Week 12: Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) scrambles out of the pocket against the Cardinals linebacker Zaven Collins (25) during a game at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Sept. 29, 2024. | Patrick Breen/The Republic / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: The 4-5-1 Washington Commanders go on the road this week following an impressive last-minute win over the Bengals on Monday night. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals’ season is all but over at 3-8 , following a blowout loss to the Chiefs on Sunday and wholesale personnel and coaching changes. While the odds of Washington securing their third consecutive win seem good, Dan Quinn made it clear earlier in the week that the Commanders are not in a position to overlook anyone. A lot has changed since Bill-in-Bangkok previewed this matchup back in July, with starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett traded to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9. His current replacement should look familiar to Commanders fans, as 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson is expected to make his second start of the season, with backup Gardner Minshew on season-ending injured reserve and rookie Carson Beck still not practicing on Wednesday . Johnson went 18 of 31 for 155 yards with one touchdown on Sunday while being sacked three times. The Cardinals also traded 2024 No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans before the trade deadline, while wide receiver Michael Wilson joined several of his teammates on season-ending injured reserve a couple of weeks ago. Arizona currently lists undrafted rookie Harrison Wallace III on their depth chart as the starter at the “X” position opposite veteran Simi Fehoko. The No. 3 overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, running back Jeremiyah Love, is still on injured reserve along with Trey Benson. That leaves the Cardinals with a committee backfield of Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier , who have averaged 5.6 and 4.0 yards per carry, respectively. Paired with the constant carousel at the quarterback position, Arizona’s offense has been outscored 85-16 over their last three games while averaging just 175 yards of total offense per game. The Cardinals best offensive weapon is Trey McBride , who leads the team in receiving and could be a problem for a Commanders defense that has allowed 9 receiving touchdowns and 804 receiving yards to tight ends across their first 10 games. Trey McBride juggles it around and scores the TD! @DETvsARI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/G8aLJwlZEA — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The Cardinals defense is also currently undergoing changes, following the firing of defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday. Rallis has been replaced by interim defensive coordinator Teryl Austin , who was a long-time assistant and former defensive coordinator for the Pittsburgh Steelers, and interviewed for the same role with the Washington Commanders back in January. Congrats to former Steelers DC Teryl Austin on being named Arizona's interim DC. Under Austin (2022-25): • 1st in takeaways • T-6th in scoring defense • 8th in run defense Never got enough credit in Pittsburgh. Rooting for him. pic.twitter.com/tClW72KoRj — TomlinBurgh (@TomlinSteelers) November 24, 2026 Austin takes over a group ranked #29 in pass defense and #28 in run defense and, according to ESPN, ranked #26 in overall defense. The squad has also suffered several key injuries on the defensive side of the ball, including their best pass defender in Will Johnson, one of their best tacklers, safety Andrew Wingard, and rookie defensive tackle Kaleb Proctor, who was supposed to help anchor the middle of the defensive front. Edge defender Josh Sweat is having a down year; both he and Zaven Collins only have 3 sacks through 11 games. Safety Budda Baker turned 30 before the season started, and the Cardinals have allowed the highest number of passing TDs (25) in the league and are #31 in passing yards per completion (8.4). Expect Austin to carry on Rallis’ defensive philosophy, which centers around a versatile 3-4 alignment that relies on pre-snap disguise and simulated pressures, but focus on simplifying the defense to get more disciplined play. As BiB also outlined, head coach Mike LaFleur comes from the Shanahan-West Coast tree and will look to dig deep into his creative playbook to get something going on offense. While the Washington Commanders are clearly ascending and the Cardinals are continuing their march towards an early selection in next April’s draft, head coach Dan Quinn and his team would be wise to not look past an Arizona team that could end their playoff hopes just when they are starting to get off the ground. Betting Lines: Oddsmakers have established the home team as the solid underdog for this matchup. Point Spread : Commanders -7 Game Total (Over/Under) : 41.5 points Bill-in-Bangkok’s original preview published July 12th: Date: November 29, 2026, 4:25 p.m. ET Location: State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona The Cardinals finished the 2025 regular season with a 3–14 record, placing last in the NFC West and missing the playoffs for the fourth consecutive year. After starting the year with wins in Weeks 1 & 2, the team lost 14 of its final 15 games, including a 9-game losing streak to close out the ‘25 schedule. The defense struggled throughout the second half of the year, allowing 37 or more points in 6 of those final 9 matchups. Following the conclusion of the season, the front office sacked head coach Jonathan Gannon and parted ways with quarterback Kyler Murray. Expectations remain low for the 2026 season under new head coach Mike LaFleur. Most national publications project the team to win four or fewer games as the franchise enters yet another rebuilding period. As mentioned above, the schedule features a difficult opening stretch, with six of the first nine games on the road and five matchups against 2025 playoff teams. With veteran Jacoby Brissett expected to manage the offense, external expectations focus primarily on evaluating young roster talent rather than competing for a postseason spot. While national expectations are not very high for the Commanders this season, most analysts expect Washington to occupy a tier above the Cardinals, who are expected to be in contention for the top pick in the 2027 Draft. While there are no easy games in the NFL, this appears, from the perspective of the offseason, to be the most favorable matchup of Washington’s 2026 schedule, and Commanders fans are likely to believe that the burgundy & gold will enter the season with the more talented roster of the two teams. By Week 12, it is very possible that the Cardinals will be thinking more about the draft than the playoffs, while Washington, barring an embarrassing meltdown reminiscent of 2025, should still have hopes for a possible playoff spot. From USA Today: Six NFL quarterbacks who could lose starting jobs in 2026 Jacoby Brissett, Arizona Cardinals Brissett was a more-than serviceable fill-in for former Cardinals starter Kyler Murray after Murray’s injury in 2025. In 12 starts, he set career highs in passing yards (3,366) and touchdowns (23). Brissett’s 64.9% completion rate was also his best in any season with at least 25 pass attempts. In the offseason, the 33-year-old veteran requested a multi-year extension that would pay him starting quarterback money. Instead, the Cardinals repaid him with a likely future replacement when they selected University of Miami (Fla.) quarterback Carson Beck in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. full_text: The Commanders are operating on a short week. That’s a sharp contrast to the last couple of weeks, where Washington has been afforded some extra time. That eliminates some recovery time. So we’ve got a situation where the Commanders must deal with some tough truths. We’ll see how they end up at the end of the week, but there are some things to monitor. Cornerback Amik Robertson was a DNP with an ankle injury, a troubling development but not a deal breaker unless we get through the week with him in the same state. Receiver Stefon Diggs was another non-participant, but his absence was of a personal nature. Defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (rib) and receiver Treylon Burks (foot) were limited. title: Jayden Daniels: Happy for Brandon Aiyuk, he’s passionate, competitive

full_text: Jayden Daniels spoke to the media after the Washington Commanders completed their first practice of the week. They’re preparing to travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals on Sunday, but everyone wanted to know about the reported signing of WR Brandon Aiyuk. There was a lot of social media activity during the offseason as Aiyuk feuded with the 49ers trying to get his release. Those antics eventually involved Daniels, Aiyuk’s former college QB at Arizona State. A deal looked like it would never happen at that point, but the two friends have since mended their relationship. Daniels said Aiyuk has looked out for him since he was 18, and even though they haven’t played together in years, they still stay in contact and discuss personal and professional business. “I’m a grown man, he’s a grown man. Things happen you know.” General manager Adam Peters had his weekly radio interview this morning, and got a bonus media appearance after Daniels held his official presser. Peters talked about the player Aiyuk was in San Francisco, and the team’s decision to add him late in the season. title: NFL Week 12 uniforms: Rams debut alternates, Cowboys rock Thanksgiving throwbacks
summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 12, led by an alternate uniform for the Los Angeles Rams.
full_text:
The NFL on Thanksgiving is a classic tradition, and the uniforms are as much a part of the games as a celebratory turkey leg. But, this year a game will be played on Thanksgiving Eve for the first time. And it's only right that the matchup included the debut of a uniform, too. 

 

 The Los Angeles Rams  wore their "Fearsome White" threads against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday. The all-white look is inspired by the Rams' "Fearsome Foursome" defensive line from the 1960s and early 1970s. A modern "Rams Royal" lid includes white horns, white facemask, new 3D bumper logos and "Rams" on the front. Royal blue stripes run over the shoulder to mirror the curve of the helmet horn, alongside accenting sleeve numbers.

 The fifth annual John Madden celebration will be held on Thanksgiving, and a patch featuring a silhouette of Madden will be included on the jersey of each player at all of the Wednesday and Thursday games.

 

 A Thanksgiving tripleheader means throwback threads, led by the Dallas Cowboys rocking their 1960s-era uniforms against the Philadelphia Eagles . Dallas brought this combination back in 2022 following a nine-year hiatus. The navy and white look includes a clean lid with a navy star on the side and a stripe down the middle. 

 On Black Friday, the Pittsburgh Steelers are dressing for the occasion with their color rush threads against the Denver Broncos . The all-black look includes gold numbers and stripes on the sleeves, with a similarly colored stripe down the pants. Pittsburgh owns a 9-3 record in the uniform.

 The holiday slate isn't the only place to find uniform heat. The Los Angeles Chargers are wearing their "Super Chargers" all-navy ensemble against the New England Patriots . It's color rush week for the New Orleans Saints with an all-white combination versus the Cincinnati Bengals . The Cleveland Browns are rocking their all-brown "Alpha Dawg" look against the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football."

title: NFL Week 12 arrivals: Jeffery Simmons leads arrivals ahead of Bears-Lions
summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
The Thanksgiving menu includes an extra helping of NFL style, with Week 12 arrivals getting started before the turkey hits the table.

 
 The Green Bay Packers visited the Los Angeles Rams on a warm Wednesday in Inglewood, California. Thursday brings the Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions together in Detroit, and morning temperatures in the 40s could lead to giving statement coats their moment. The Philadelphia Eagles visit the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, where a sunny afternoon in the 50s calls for sweater weather.

 The Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night in Orchard Park, New York, to close out the tripleheader with temperatures in the 30s and rain in the forecast. Friday's meeting between the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh brings another opportunity for layers, with temperatures around the low 40s and possible showers.

 Sunday offers a little of everything: jacket weather around the Great Lakes, warmer conditions in South Florida and potential rain in the Bay Area. Whether players are bundling up or keeping things breezy, there's plenty of room to serve a look.

 Here are the standout arrivals from Week 12.

 

 Thanksgiving threads 
 Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons embraced fall fashion in a camel-colored coat with plush shearling-style lapels, layered over a plum plaid suit and matching turtleneck. 
 
 
 Wednesday's looks 
 Aaron Donald kept it sleek in a black zip-up jacket and matching pants, accessorizing with gold-tinted shades and a checkered designer pouch. His blue, white and yellow sneakers added a pop of Rams colors to the look.

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
summary: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

title: How upsets in the 2026 NFL season have upended survivor pools
summary: Why spend up to nearly $80,000 in order to win a survivor contest over halfway through the NFL season?
full_text:
Paul Jager was browsing the marketplace for Splash Sports' Survivor World Championship on Friday, Nov. 20, when one specific entry caught his eye ahead of Week 11. The seller had other entries listed and hadn't yet listed this one, but Jager found it and was in awe at the teams used to get it to this point. He knew he had to have it.

 Jager purchased the entry on the marketplace for $133,000, the largest transaction that Splash has facilitated since it launched its flagship contest this season. Upon taking ownership of it, he made his Week 11 pick: the Pittsburgh Steelers to defeat the Philadelphia Eagles. 

 "If I can get through with the Steelers, this entry is set up to win the whole thing," Jager told ESPN of his mindset at the time. "I was like, 'I'm going to take one chance, and if Pittsburgh wins, I am literally set.' I knew five minutes into the game, I was regretting taking Pittsburgh."

 The Steelers lost to their in-state rivals, ending that entry's hopes of winning at least a share of the $21 million grand prize. But Jager wasn't out of the running. The investor by trade in Kansas City, Kansas who dabbles a lot in sports betting, currently has six entries alive at Splash and two in Circa Sports' famed Survivor contest, which features a prize pool of over $25 million this season.

 

 Jager's experience is part of what's shaping up to be the new normal for players in high-stakes survivor contests. It fits perfectly into the new look for a sports betting world that is increasingly taking a more stock market-esque approach.

 When Splash announced its completely online contest before this season, it was with the goal of expanding the space on top of the remarkable bedrock Circa (which requires in-person registration and proxies) has built since 2020. That included a built-in marketplace that allows players to buy and sell whole or partial tickets within the app using their connected payment methods. So far this season, Splash has already facilitated more than $4 million in transactions.

 Circa also launched its own official marketplace by partnering with online platform Survivor Sweat. Circa Sports director of operations Jeff Benson says that the partnership "has driven significantly more engagement and activity than in previous years."

 Gabe Patgorski, a former Circa champion, current contestant and founder of the research website Survivor Atlas, describes the contest as more "portfolio-style," given that there is no limit to the number of entries each player can have. Contestants can be more liberal with their selections, knowing that the quantity of entries they keep alive will just increase each's value, if nothing else.

 It's a whole new branch of strategy in a game with over 21 sextillion possible combinations throughout the season. And when the stakes are as high as $1,000 per entry, players are looking for any edge they can get to ultimately come out profitable.

 "The marketplace is a really cool way to turn any static entry you have in a contest to a tradable asset that you can get out of, or take some chips off the table at any time in the year, or buy back in. And so we've actually seen way more activity than I would've expected," Splash co-founder and co-CEO TJ Ross told ESPN. 

 Some of the trade activity comes after a particularly brutal first seven weeks of the season whittled down the fields to a fraction of the original entries. Over that span, favorites of seven points or greater -- the teams toward which many survivor contestants gravitate -- lost eight games straight-up, marking the first time since 1972 in which each of the first seven weeks of the season featured such an upset, according to ESPN Research.

 

 Those results had an extensive impact on survivor contests: Following Week 7, Circa Survivor had lost 97.4% of its field (24,357 of the 25,017 entries). Entering Week 12, Circa Grandissimo, the $100,000 entry contest with a $7.7 million prize pool, is down to just three players from the 77 who started.

 "In short, 2026 has combined the largest field Circa has ever seen with a run of upsets concentrated on the most popular survivor selections," Benson told ESPN via email after Week 7. "The absolute carnage is record-setting in scale; the underlying dynamic (chalk getting eliminated in bunches) is a familiar and defining feature of the format, just playing out more dramatically this year."

 Though the raw volume of eliminations seems shocking, the early portion of the 2026 season was actually not the most carnage the contest has experienced by percentage. That honor belongs to the infamous 2024 season , which saw 99.5% of the field eliminated going into Week 8. The 2022 campaign had 98.0% of its field gone by the same time, which ultimately produced only two winners that year, the fewest in the contest's history. 

 The favorites have been more reliable since Week 7; the top four most-picked teams in Circa Survivor have won each week and favorites of at least seven points have gone 16-1 straight up from Week 8 through Sunday's games. Week 11 featured an average point spread of 8, the third-largest for any week (excluding the final two weeks of the season in which playoff positioning can dramatically affect spreads) in the last 50 years, per ESPN Research. 

 Players in the high-stakes contests must now brace for the holiday season. In the Circa pool, each entry must choose a team playing in one of the five Thanksgiving-adjacent games and one of the four Christmas-adjacent games, in addition to the usual games on Sunday and Monday. In Splash, each entry must choose two teams in Weeks 12 through 16, as well as in Week 9, regardless of when they are played.

 "It's felt like a normal survivor season to me so far, very different from last year but similar to 2024 and 2022 in terms of pace of eliminations," 2025 Circa Survivor champion Jason Somerville told ESPN over text. He has one entry still alive in Circa. "It never feels real to me 'til Thanksgiving anyway, so fingers crossed I have some decisions to make in December."

 

 The way this season has played out supports the notion that this could be a much more generous holiday season for the contestants than usual, especially with how things shook out at the NFL trade deadline. 

 Patgorski noticed that many of the already bad teams got worse at this season's deadline, and teams that began the season with high hopes -- like the  Indianapolis Colts and  Philadelphia Eagles -- became big sellers. There are also teams dealing with injured or underperforming quarterbacks, like the  Baltimore Ravens ,  Los Angeles Chargers and  New England Patriots , for whom the bottom has fallen out.

 "The path to the end seems a lot easier for almost everyone," said Patgorski. "Every week there are so many big favorites where people are going, 'Oh, that's a lock. That's a free square.' And it's a pretty big shift from a few weeks ago where people thought, 'Okay, this contest has a big chance not to go to the end.' And now, everyone's thinking, 'Oh, there's going to be 50 winners. It's so easy to get to Christmas now. It's so easy to get to the end.'"

 Philadelphia presents a juicy opportunity for Circa players given it is one of the few teams playing in both the Thanksgiving and Christmas mini-weeks ... but that in itself creates a paradoxical dilemma unique to high-end survivor contests. 

 As of Tuesday, the Eagles are 8.5-point road underdogs to the  Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving according to DraftKings, easily the largest spread between the five games that make up the Wednesday-through-Friday slate. Patgorski estimates that 60-70% of the field will pick Dallas. 

 "The math says you're supposed to avoid that just because randomness happens often enough to pop that bubble. I think a lot of players have a sense of that, but of course you have to weigh that against, 'Well, maybe it's worth joining the crowd because my entry is strong enough where I'm fine just getting…

title: 2026 NFL Thanksgiving preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
summary: Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills are still on deck. We have the top storylines, bold predictions, stats to know, fantasy/betting nuggets and more.
full_text:
Holiday football is here, and the NFL started  this season 's Thanksgiving week slate a day earlier than normal. On Wednesday night, the Rams beat the Packers . But we have three great Thanksgiving Day games, too.

 The Lions and Packers kicked it off, and an NFC East showdown between the Eagles and Cowboys is up next. And to conclude Thursday's games, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will visit  Josh Allen  and the Bills in the first clash of NFL MVPs on the holiday, per the Elias Sports Bureau.

 Ahead of the matchups, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside each locker room with key storylines and a look back at each team's history playing on Thanksgiving. ESPN Research provides optimistic stats for every team, and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. Plus, analytics writer Seth Walder makes bold predictions and fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and three analysts -- Maldonado, Moody and Walder -- give us final score picks for the games.

 

 

 Eagles (3-7) at Cowboys (5-6) 
 Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET | Fox | DAL -8.5 (47.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Eagles:  With edge rusher  Jonathan Greenard getting healthier and counterpart  Nolan Smith Jr . continuing his surge, the Eagles have racked up 11 sacks and 15 QB hits over the past two games. "I've been telling you guys that it would come, but you didn't believe me," defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said of the pass rush. "But the guy we're playing this week [ Dak Prescott ] I think is the hardest guy in the league to sack." The cornerback room took some hits with Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) and Jonathan Jones (ankle) getting injured against Pittsburgh. Jones is expected to be sidelined against Dallas, but Fangio indicated Mitchell should be OK to play. Either way, if Philadelphia has any shot of slowing down Dallas, the front seven will have to continue its high level of play.  -- Tim McManus 

 What we're hearing on the Cowboys:  The Cowboys are not out of the NFC East picture yet, but they need to keep winning to apply pressure against the Giants. The Cowboys have not posted back-to-back wins since last Thanksgiving, and ex-Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton would love nothing more than to show off against a team that did not believe he was worthy of the backup job to Prescott. But the holiday game has been kind recently to the Cowboys, who have won four in a row. The last time they had a Thanksgiving winning streak that long was from 1980 to 1985. -- Todd Archer 

 Stat the Eagles are thankful for:  In their Week 11 win over the Steelers , running back Saquon Barkley recorded a season-high 61 rushing yards before contact. He also increased his touchdown streak to a career-high four straight games.

 Stat the Cowboys are thankful for: Prescott has recorded at least 300 passing yards and five touchdowns in each of his past two games. He is the fourth QB in NFL history to post both of those marks in consecutive games, joining Tom Brady in 2007 (three straight), Ben Roethlisberger in 2014 (two straight) and Daunte Culpepper in 2004 (two straight).  -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams will record multiple sacks for the second straight week. He is scorching hot, with seven sacks in his past six games. When the Cowboys played the Eagles earlier this season, Williams had a sack, recorded a 40% pass rush win rate and notched a 33% pressure rate. -- Walder 

 

 Injuries: Eagles | Cowboys 

 Fantasy nugget: Eagles WR DeVonta Smith returned from a hamstring injury in Week 11 and led the team with 12 targets while playing 81% of the snaps. He finished with only 9.1 fantasy points, but his workload was encouraging. Smith has a favorable matchup against the Cowboys, who are allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers. See Week 12 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: Since coach Brian Schottenheimer was hired in 2025, Dallas games are 21-7 to the over -- the best in the NFL ahead of Baltimore (19-9). Against a potentially injured Eagles secondary, Prescott should be able to easily thread the ball to receivers  CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . On the other side, Dallas is allowing 5.2 yards per carry, which could lead to a big game for Barkley. Read more .  -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick:  Cowboys 30, Eagles 20 
 Moody's pick: Cowboys 30, Eagles 17 
 Walder's pick: Cowboys 31, Eagles 20 
 FPI prediction: DAL, 82.9% (by an average of 9.4 points)

 Thanksgiving game memory for the Eagles: The "Bounty Bowl" in 1989. Rumors swirled heading into the game at Texas Stadium that coach Buddy Ryan had put a $200 bounty on former Eagles kicker Luis Zendejas, who had some critical words aimed at Ryan after leaving the team. That seemed to be confirmed when Eagles linebacker Jessie Small decked Zendejas on a kickoff, leaving the kicker shaken and angered. The game helped fuel one of the fiercest rivalries in football for decades. "I tried to talk to Buddy, but he wouldn't stay on the field. He took his big, fat rear end up the tunnel to the locker room," rookie Cowboys coach Jimmy Johnson said at the time, to which Ryan replied, "I've been on a diet and lost a few pounds. I thought I was looking good and [Johnson] goes and calls me fat. I resent that." -- McManus 

 Thanksgiving game memory for the Cowboys:  Backup quarterback Clint Longley leading the Cowboys to a win over Washington in 1974 is the "best" memory," ruling out Randy Moss' dominant showing in 1998 and Leon Lett's ill-timed trek in the ice in 1993. Longley's comeback vs. Washington came out of nowhere. With Roger Staubach knocked out in the third quarter, the Cowboys trailed 23-17 with less than 30 seconds to play when Longley, known as the "Mad Bomber," hit Drew Pearson for a 50-yard touchdown to defeat their rivals. -- Archer 

 

 Matchup must-reads:   Eagles' Woolen benched after missed tackles vs. Steelers  ...  Cowboys need to break a yearlong trend to make the playoffs  ...  Prescott continues hot streak, salutes Cowboys' offense after rout of Titans 

 

 
 

 Chiefs (8-2) at Bills (9-1) 
 Thursday, 8:20 p.m. ET | NBC | BUF -3 (47.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Chiefs: The Chiefs didn't celebrate much Sunday following their victory over the Cardinals . They know, after their experience losing to the Cowboys last year on Thanksgiving, that each hour leading up to facing the Bills is critical to their success on the road. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes talked Sunday about when his preparation would begin for the pivotal showdown, which has plenty of implications on the AFC playoff picture. "When I put [my] kids down, then I'll be studying the Buffalo Bills," Mahomes said. -- Nate Taylor 

 What we're hearing on the Bills: The challenges of facing Josh Allen and Mahomes aren't identical, but Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard -- who spent the past two seasons preparing for Mahomes in Denver -- draws one major comparison: They can beat you even when you're right and they're wrong. The extra wrinkle, of course, is the Chiefs' improved run game. "You take a very highly skilled group of athletes and you've got the trigger man in Mahomes who is able to just disperse the ball all over the place," Leonhard said. "Again, now that they are keeping teams a little bit more honest with the run game, downhill, power and physicality, that makes it even more difficult." -- Nick Suss 

 Stat the Chiefs are thankful for: If they had scored one more point in Week 11, they would've matched a franchise record of three straight games with 35-plus points. That was last done in 2018, when Mahomes became the Chiefs' starter. However, Kansas City did win its third straight game by 20-plus points, matching a franchise record from 1997.

 Stat the Bills are thankful for: They have not allowed a touchdown in three straight games, the longest streak in franchise history. The 43 straight defensive…

title: How Jeffery Simmons changed the Bears' defensive identity
summary: Simmons' impact isn't just measured by his own numbers, but also by how he has elevated his teammates.
full_text:
CHICAGO -- Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had an idea, but he needed an unselfish act from defensive end Austin Booker to make it work.

 The Bears were leading the New Orleans Saints 21-10 late in the fourth quarter Sunday, and coming out of the two-minute warning, the Saints were driving deep in Bears' territory. On first-and-10 from the 24-yard line, Simmons asked Booker to switch positions for one play.

 Since he joined the Bears before their Week 8 game in Seattle, Simmons has been double-teamed 92 times, tied for the most in the NFL. He thought if he could line up at end, he could work 1-on-1 against rookie right tackle Mason Murphy .

 He was right.

 Booker made the switch, and Simmons got down in a four-point stance and ripped through Murphy's inside shoulder. He made his way into the New Orleans backfield in 0.72 seconds -- his second-fastest get-off rate this season -- before wrapping his orange-sleeved arms around quarterback Tyler Shough and hurtling him to the ground.

 Simmons rose to his feet and pointed at the Bears' sideline, celebrating his third sack of the afternoon -- which tied a career high set in Week 9 of the 2021 season with the Tennessee Titans .

 While fans in Soldier Field erupted around him, quarterback Caleb Williams stayed seated on the bench, offering little more than a knowing nod at his teammate of less than a month.

 What used to feel like a game-changing splash play has become almost standard operating procedure for the Bears' defense, and Williams watched it unfold with the calm detachment of a quarterback who has already factored Simmons' dominance into the game plan.

 "He's so good," said Williams, who then said he appreciated general manager Ryan Poles and coach Ben Johnson for acquiring Simmons.

 

 The Bears, who have won five straight games, reshaped the capabilities of their defense on Oct. 29 when they sent their 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-rounder to the Titans in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The 29-year-old became the first defensive tackle to be traded for multiple first-round picks in the common draft era (since 1967).

 After five straight losing seasons in Tennessee, Simmons was traded to a Bears team that went all-in ahead of the trade deadline to upgrade its roster for a run at Super Bowl LXI. His impact was felt immediately with five sacks over Chicago's three straight wins against Seattle, Tampa Bay and New Orleans, giving him a share of the team lead with Booker.

 "This team believes in what they have here, and they want it right now," Simmons said. "My game, my passion, my energy, my leadership, I can only help this team even more than what it's got."

 The Bears (8-2, 0-2) face a huge NFC North Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Detroit Lions (1 p.m. ET, CBS). Chicago is off to its best start in 20 years, although it's still looking for its first division win.

 "We had a hunch of who we're acquiring," Johnson said, "and yet until you see it come to fruition in real life, you don't know for sure.

 "So, I don't think anybody in this building could be more pleased than Ryan and myself, just how well he has taken to this team. We're going to need to continue to have his effect on our defense, on our locker room, on our entire team, for us in this back half of the season."

 

 AROUND 10 P.M. , hours after the blockbuster trade was finalized, Simmons made his way down unfamiliar hallways in the Bears' facility before arriving at the office of his new defensive line coach, Jeremy Garrett. With Chicago's next game at Seattle four days away, the eight-year veteran wanted to have at least an understanding of the Bears' base plan ahead of his first practice.

 Before diving into gap assignments or pass rush angles, Simmons made sure to address the elephant in the room.

 "I know you went to Ole Miss," said Simmons, who like Garrett is a Mississippi native. Over the years, Garrett had kept track of Simmons' career from a five-star recruit to standout defensive lineman at Mississippi State. But aside from a few playful mentions, now was not the time to debate who would win this season's Egg Bowl.

 "You could just tell, man, [he was like] I want to make sure I'm not going to cost the team," Garrett said. "I want to do everything, I want to be aligned correctly, I don't want any mental errors."

 The next day, Garrett watched as Simmons offered tips to teammates -- most he barely knew -- as Chicago's defensive linemen repped individual pass-rush drills. Put your hands right here. Get your eyes here.

 Simmons arrived in Chicago with 46.5 career sacks, the second most among defensive tackles since he was drafted No. 19 by the Titans in 2019. He held the highest pass rush win rate (27%) as a defensive tackle through Week 7 and earned first-team All-Pro honors for the first time last season.

 

 "It's intoxicating to see somebody play the game the way he plays," defensive tackle James Lynch said. "And the way he talks, he wants us to do well together because it means we win.

 "So whenever you see him play his ass off, it's like, 'Why am I not doing that?' If I want to be that good, I've got to do those things as well."

 Four days after being traded and four plays into his Chicago tenure, Simmons notched his first sack as a Bear when he dropped Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold for a 6-yard loss. The defense turned in one of its best performances of the season in a 34-17 win by giving up one third-down conversion in 11 attempts (9.1% conversion rate, fifth lowest by a team this season).

 In several ways, that evening at Lumen Field altered the Bears' defensive identity. As Simmons was putting together a debut performance (one sack, six tackles, two for losses, one pass defensed) that would earn the first of two game balls, he spoke emphatically to his D-line teammates about holding their own.

 "Jeff was saying it to me all game," defensive end Montez Sweat said. "We need to get home with four [pass rushers]."

 Before Simmons' arrival, the Bears' standard pass rush (four or fewer pass rushers) produced a 25% pressure rate since Dennis Allen was hired as defensive coordinator in 2025, the fourth lowest by any defense in that span. In three games with Simmons, the Bears are getting home with their four down linemen on 32% of dropbacks. Opposing quarterbacks went from completing 70% of passes to 58% and have seen their off-target percentage on throws increase by 11% when facing the Bears' standard pass rush since Week 8.

 Allen hasn't had to rely on bringing extra rushers with Simmons in the fold nearly as often. The Bears have blitzed only 20% of the time with the defensive tackle on the field but 50% when he is not in the game, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Chicago's overall blitz rate has dropped from 25% to 10% since Simmons' arrival.

 

 "It allows you more flexibility in terms of how you can call the game," Allen said. "When you feel like you can get home with four, then that leaves you more flexibility, whereas if you don't feel like you can get home with four, you feel like I may have to bring a few more elements into the rush to try and affect the quarterback."

 Simmons has played no fewer than 87.3% of snaps since arriving in Chicago. Since Week 8, Chicago is giving up 4.5 yards per play with Simmons in the game compared with 7.1 yards per play when he's on the sideline, which has been for only 19 defensive snaps. The Bears are averaging 4.3 sacks per game compared with 2.7 from Weeks 1-7. And the way Simmons affects the game doesn't just impact his teammates up front.

 "He has a command and a presence about the room that you can really feel and it gets everybody going, especially in that back end," cornerback Clark Phillips III said. "When you got orange sleeves out there, you know they're going to have less time and you're going to be able to get that ball."

 

 NOT EVERYTHING WAS foreign to Simmons upon his arrival…

title: NFL survivor power rankings: Why this is the week to use the Jaguars or Texans
summary: ESPN NFL survivor pool strategy, predictions and ranking the top seven options for Week 12.
full_text:
Last week, there were five double-digit favorites, and all won. The two biggest favorites to lose were the Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars (both -6), but neither was popular given the alternatives.

 For the first time since Week 4, no teams are on bye. However, with teams like the Los Angeles Chargers , Miami Dolphins , Indianapolis Colts , and Arizona Cardinals all hosting other pedestrian teams, it is a quietly tricky week in Survivor.

 After their upset losses last week, the Jaguars and Bengals are the two biggest favorites of Week 12. However, very few users have those teams available, which will keep their selection down. The Jaguars are the clear preference of the two, as they are much bigger favorites with slightly lower future value, though it's a fine week to burn the Bengals, too.

 Outside of those two, the Dallas Cowboys are the strongest mix of win equity and lack of future value. They have the third-highest win probability blending the betting market and models from ESPN Analytics and Mike Clay, and they are unlikely to be favored again until Week 17.

 However, in a contest like Circa Survivor, the Cowboys could reach 60% selection, and if that is the case, you are likely better off taking the Denver Broncos or Los Angeles Rams , and even the Philadelphia Eagles become a consideration if you like them more than the market does.

 

 Then there are four teams favored around a touchdown. The Washington Commanders and New York Giants are widely available with little future value. The Houston Texans and Minnesota Vikings are the opposite -- very few entries have them, but they also have more value later.

 In double-pick contests like SplashSports, the Commanders' and Giants' percentages could both be over 35%, which could make pivoting to the next group of teams a smart choice. The Giants are trending to be the most popular pick of the week on both ESPN and Splash, which makes the Commanders the preferred pick of the two.

 The last realistic options are the Cleveland Browns and New York Jets , purely because they play the  Las Vegas Raiders  and Dolphins. However, both could have similar spots down the road against other bad teams, with the Browns still hosting the  Atlanta Falcons  and Colts, while the Jets will play the Cardinals and could play the Tommy DeVito -led  New England Patriots . They are an option only in double-pick pools, but in those contests, the selection discount is enough to have me seriously consider pivoting off the Giants and Commanders.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Future value based on Mike Clay's cheat sheet .  

 

 

 1. Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Tennessee Titans ) 

 

 If you have somehow made it this far without using the Jaguars, this is the time to deploy them. While they have future value, this is the best spot left on the schedule, they are the biggest favorites of the week, and they will be unavailable to most other entries. Just look ahead to Weeks 14 and 17 when you map out your path, as those are the main spots for them on the schedule.

 
 Chance to win: 89% (ESPN Analytics), 96% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Jaguars -14.5 (-1240 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Steelers (Week 14), vs. Commanders (Week 17), at Colts (Week 18) 
 Availability: 17% 
 ESPN Selection: 13% 
 

 

 2. Houston Texans (vs. Baltimore Ravens ) 

 The ESPN models like the Texans in this spot more than the betting markets do, and at low selection, Houston is a fantastic pick. Surprisingly, the Texans are still 60% available on ESPN compared to 34% on Circa and 9% on Splash, but they are still flying under the radar as a high-value pick.

 
 Chance to win: 83% (ESPN Analytics), 87% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Texans -6.5 (-314 moneyline) 
 Notable games: at Eagles (Week 16), vs. Titans (Week 18) 
 Availability: 60% 
 ESPN Selection: 3% 
 

 

 3. Dallas Cowboys (vs. Philadelphia Eagles ) 

 

 The Cowboys schedule gets a lot harder after this week, so this is likely the last chance to get them with at least 70% win equity. I expect them to be higher picked in a lot of contests than the 14% listed at ESPN, but with nearly 40% of the field already having used them, there is a cap on their popularity.

 
 Chance to win: 83% (ESPN Analytics), 87% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Cowboys -8.5 (-469 moneyline) 
 Notable games: None 
 Availability: 61% 
 ESPN Selection: 14% 
 

 

 4. Washington Commanders (at Arizona Cardinals ) 

 

 This is the first of back-to-back road games against downtrodden teams as the Commanders visit the Titans next week, so if you are using them, take a look at your options next week, too. It's a tricky spot on the road after a big "Monday Night Football" win, but the Cardinals are priced as the worst team in the NFL in Mike Clay's model, so taking their opponent is a viable strategy every week.

 
 Chance to win: 63% (ESPN Analytics), 85% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Commanders -7.5 (-413 moneyline) 
 Notable games: at Titans (Week 13), vs Falcons (Week 15) 
 Availability: 98% 
 ESPN Selection: 8% 
 

 

 5. Cincinnati Bengals (vs. New Orleans Saints ) 

 The Bengals are one of the most powerful trump cards remaining in Survivor, as almost nobody has them left, and they have one of the easiest remaining schedules. Getting a 10-point favorite at 7% selection sounds great, but this won't be the last time they are big favorites at minuscule percentage, so choose your spot wisely. I lean towards continuing to save them.

 
 Chance to win: 81% (ESPN Analytics), 92% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Bengals -10 (-610 moneyline) 
 Notable games: at Browns (Week 13), at Colts (Week 16), vs. Ravens (Week 17), vs. Browns (Week 18) 
 Availability: 17% 
 ESPN Selection: 7% 
 

 

 6. Minnesota Vikings (vs. Atlanta Falcons ) 

 

 This is the easiest game remaining for the Vikings according to both Mike Clay and ESPN Analytics. However, with several more usable weeks available, I lean towards saving them and whittling down their availability even more, especially given the number of similar-sized favorites on the board.

 
 Chance to win: 80% (ESPN Analytics), 92% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Vikings -7 (-351 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Panthers (Week 13), at Patriots (Week 14), vs. Commanders (Week 16), at Jets (Week 17) 
 Availability: 37% 
 ESPN Selection: 15% 
 

 

 7. New York Giants (at Indianapolis Colts ) 

 

 The Giants are likely going to be the most popular pick of the week, given their 92% availability and how bad the Colts have looked. Given their lack of future value, it will be great to advance with a Giants entry. However, the Giants are not a big enough favorite to justify the potential pick, so as of Wednesday, I am leaning elsewhere if possible.

 
 Chance to win: 47% (ESPN Analytics), 78% (Mike Clay) 
 Spread: Giants -6.5 (-321 moneyline) 
 Notable games: vs. Browns (Week 15), vs. Eagles (Week 18) 
 Availability: 92% 
 ESPN Selection: 30%

title: Best bets and top prop plays for Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills
summary: Odds, analysis and picks to help you bet Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving.
full_text:
Thanksgiving Day gives us a trifecta of NFL games. The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions get the day started in a game that has the highest total of Week 12.

 Next up is a rematch between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys . The Cowboys won the first matchup between NFC East rivals and are sizable favorites in the rematch.

 The Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills close out the day in what is one of the best matchups of the season.

 Let's get on to the analysis and best bets for the games. (You can find odds for every Week 12 game here .)

 Jump to: 
 Bears-Lions   | Eagles-Cowboys  | Chiefs-Bills 

 

 

 

 

 Chicago and Detroit enter Thanksgiving with identical 8-2 records, and the winner will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North. The Bears have won five straight, while the Lions have won six consecutive games. Ben Johnson returns to Detroit, where former boss Dan Campbell has had plenty of success against Chicago.

 

 The biggest challenge for the Bears will be containing Jahmyr Gibbs . He has rushed for 251 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games, and Chicago ranks 25th in yards per carry allowed. Jeffery Simmons has helped improve the Bears' defensive front, but slowing Gibbs will be critical.

 Chicago has favorable matchups of its own. Detroit has struggled against quarterbacks and tight ends, which should benefit Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland . With Cole Kmet out for the season, Loveland remains a major part of the passing game, despite seeing only three targets against the Saints in Week 11.

 Both offenses have the personnel to put up points, but Detroit's running game and Chicago's ability to contain explosive plays could determine the outcome. I'm leaning toward the Lions on the moneyline at home .

 Notable player props, bets 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs rushing yards OVER 92.5 (-114) 

 Gibbs has rushed for 251 yards over his last two games, handling 45 carries during that stretch. He has surpassed 92.5 rushing yards in five of his last six games and faces a Bears defense ranked 25th in yards per carry allowed. Detroit should continue leaning on Gibbs, especially against Chicago's improved pass rush. Gibbs' recent workload gives him a good chance to clear this number.

 Kyle Monangai longest rush OVER 9.5 yards (-119) 

 Liz Loza: Monangai didn't make much noise in his Week 11 return from injury. That doesn't mean, however, that Ben Johnson doesn't have plans for the slippery rusher in a highly anticipated duel on Thanksgiving, particularly given De'Andre Swift 's recent ball security issues. For context, Monangai has recorded seven runs of 10 or more yards over five contests. Meanwhile, the Lions' defense has surrendered seven runs of 20 or more yards thus far into 2026. In what's projected to be a close game with both offenses attempting to play keep away and maintain control, the sophomore back figures to rip off at least one double-digit run.

 

 Colston Loveland receiving yards OVER 53.5 (-112) 

 Loveland saw just three targets against New Orleans, but his playing time remained encouraging. He played 57 of Chicago's 61 offensive snaps and ran routes on 25 of 27 passing plays. He has averaged 7.4 targets over his last five games and should remain one of Williams' top receiving options. Detroit has allowed the third-most receiving yards per game to tight ends, giving Loveland a favorable matchup to bounce back.

 

 

 

 

 Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns in last week's 51-30 win over the Titans, and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 234 receiving yards and two scores. Philadelphia's secondary could have trouble containing both receivers, especially with Quinyon Mitchell dealing with a hamstring injury and Jonathan Jones (ankle) sidelined in practice.

 

 The Eagles improved to 3-7 after beating the Steelers, but their passing game continues to struggle without Jalen Hurts . Joe Milton has averaged just 155 passing yards in two starts and has yet to throw a touchdown pass.

 On the positive side, DeVonta Smith drew 12 targets against Pittsburgh in his return to the lineup and played 81% of the snaps. Saquon Barkley handled a season-high 17 carries and should have opportunities against a Dallas defense that has struggled against running backs.

 I lean toward Dallas covering , but the spread gives me some hesitation. The Cowboys have struggled with consistency this season, and Philadelphia's defensive front has the ability to pressure Prescott and keep the game competitive.

 Notable player props, bets 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 Joe Milton OVER 32.5 rushing yards (-111) 

 Loza: A bit of a revenge game for Milton, who was signed off the Cowboys' practice squad after Jalen Hurts was injured. Milton has posted 33 or more rushing yards in two of four contests in which he's also recorded 13 or more passing attempts. Likely to be in a negative game script, Milton figures to turn on the jets, frantic to gain yardage. That's a recipe that could work against a Dallas defense that's allowed a league-high 5.2 yards per carry as well as the third most rushing yards (266) to opposing signal callers.

 

 George Pickens receiving yards OVER 69.5 (-114) 

 Pickens had 18 receptions for 247 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games. The Eagles' injury situation gives him an opportunity to continue that production. Mitchell's availability for Philadelphia will be key, but Pickens' recent target volume and production put him in a good spot to clear this line.

 DeVonta Smith receptions OVER 5.5 (-107) 

 Smith caught just five passes last week, but the target volume was encouraging. Dallas has struggled against wide receivers, and the Cowboys being favored by more than a touchdown could force Philadelphia to throw the football. Milton's accuracy remains the biggest concern with Smith's prop. With that said, the target volume makes it worth considering.

 

 

 

 

 Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen have developed one of the league's most entertaining quarterback rivalries, but Thursday's game could be decided by the running backs.

 Buffalo ranks second in rushing yards per game, with James Cook III and Allen both capable of making plays on the ground. Cook has 10 rushing touchdowns this season for the Bills, who lead the league in rushing scores.

 

 Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (groin) will miss his third straight game, but Emmett Johnson has been productive in his absence, recording consecutive 100-yard rushing performances.

 Weather could also impact Thursday night's game. Rain and gusty winds are forecast for Orchard Park, potentially making it difficult to throw downfield.

 I lean under 46.5 , but I wouldn't chase the number much lower. Mahomes and Allen are capable of creating explosive plays, even in difficult conditions, and turnovers could give either team short fields.

 Notable player props, bets 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 James Cook III anytime touchdown (-105) 

 Cook has scored 10 rushing touchdowns in 10 games, and Buffalo leads the league with 21 rushing scores. Rain and windy conditions could lead to additional rushing attempts against Kansas City, although the Chiefs have been difficult to run against. Allen also remains a threat near the goal line, but Cook's workload -- he averaged 105.6 rushing yards over his last five games -- and touchdown production make him a reasonable option at these odds.

 Josh Allen rushing yards OVER 36.5 (-111) 

 Allen has rushed for 506 yards in 10 career games against the Chiefs, including the playoffs, averaging 50.6 yards per game. And he has cleared this line in seven of those matchups. With the forecast, Allen could see more designed runs and scrambles. He has surpassed this number just twice in 10 games this season, but he has consistently been more aggressive as a runner against Kansas…

title: NFL Week 12 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: Where could Daniel Jones land? What's the latest on coaching hot seats? What's next for Puka Nacua? And who is getting MVP love in league circles?
full_text:
Week 12 of the  2026 NFL season  comes with a serving of Thanksgiving football, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 We begin this week with updates on the coaching carousel. There were already two changes by this point last season (Titans and Giants), but zero teams have moved on from their head coaches so far in 2026. What's the latest on hot seats around the league? Could we really make it through the regular season with no jobs coming open?

 With Daniel Jones clearing waivers and becoming a free agent this week, our insiders also asked around on potential landing spots for him. And while Puka Nacua 's season might be over, his future is a big talker right now. Fowler and Graziano tried to get a sense of what comes next for the star receiver and whether the Rams will hand him a big extension in the offseason. And finally, they canvassed the league for a quick poll of who should win MVP as of now.

 It's all here, as Fowler and Graziano answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 12.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Head coach hot seat updates 
 Fits for Jones  | MVP candidates 
 Nacua's future | Fantasy advice 
 More notes, intel 

 
 

 Still no coaching changes? Where do things stand for head coaches on the hot seat? 
 Graziano: Well, it's not like no team has done anything . The Colts fired their GM weeks ago. The Panthers fired their defensive coordinator . The Cardinals  fired their defensive coordinator . The Cowboys didn't fire their defensive coordinator, instead demoted him and kept him around to suffer with everyone else. But you want to know about head coaches, so fine. Situations I'm watching for potential change at the end of the season include the Jets, Buccaneers, Colts, Eagles and maybe Commanders, though Dan Quinn seems to be turning things around  in D.C.

 

 Would any of those teams move on from their head coach before the end of the season? I personally doubt it, in large part because I'm not sure which coordinators or assistants would be candidates to have audition roles the rest of the season. It is still early, and things could get bad enough in one or more of these spots that a team could decide to change for change's sake, but that's my read right now. Jeremy, how did I do?

 Fowler: Nailed it! To be fair, there's usually a coaching change by this part of the season. The Titans' Brian Callahan and the Giants' Brian Daboll were properly fired before this point last season. Thanksgiving spelled the end for Chicago's Matt Eberflus in 2024. In 2023, Carolina's Frank Reich and Las Vegas' Josh McDaniels were gone before December. So, change is inevitable, and possibly soon. But I'm with you for this season, Dan -- it seems several ownership groups are willing to show some level of patience with their hot seat coaches.

 That seems to be the case in Washington, where Quinn is rallying the Commanders and has a soft schedule coming up. The Bucs could wait until season's end for clarity on Todd Bowles' future, though Monday night vs. Carolina feels important (the Bucs would be three games out in the NFC South with a loss). It seems like Aaron Glenn, fresh off a win , should get the rest of the season with the Jets. Why not give him more time to see what he can do? There's no real rush there. So, if we're taking temperatures, your gauge on the five jobs above is correct, and I'll raise you a few more for the radar: the Saints and Cowboys.

 Saints coach Kellen Moore making run-game staff changes during the bye week wasn't the best sign. And the vibes out of Dallas leadership are not great. The Christian Parker move was not universally well-received in the building. This might be a case where coach Brian Schottenheimer needs a playoff berth to ensure a third season.

 Graziano: A wild note I saw recently is that the Saints have trailed in all 27 games in which Moore has been their head coach. They must figure out if Tyler Shough is their long-term future at QB, and if they don't think Moore is the coach to help get the most out of him, that could spell trouble, even after only two seasons.

 And I agree on Schottenheimer. The Cowboys are more patient with coaches than their reputation would lead you to believe, but they had very high hopes for this season. If it fizzles out because they blew the defensive coordinator hire, and Schottenheimer gets to the end of the year with another losing record, I think there would be some smoke there.

 

 Fowler: The Chargers are firmly on the radar despite coach Jim Harbaugh's massive buyout on a five-year deal (do the math on what was reported as a five-year, $80 million deal in 2024). If Harbaugh finishes, say, 2-15 in Los Angeles, ownership must do some soul-searching at that point, no? (Particularly when the team plays home games in a stadium it doesn't even own.) And if the Chargers still believe in Harbaugh , the bigger question becomes: Do they trust him to hire a third offensive coordinator in as many years? The Mike McDaniel hire has been flashy but has produced a 30th-ranked scoring offense and lack of a clear identity. The McDaniel era pales in comparison to the Greg Roman era (Roman is thriving with the Giants, by the way).

 And Tennessee seems like one to watch because of the Titans' penchant for firings in recent years. I'm curious whether Tennessee breaks precedent and gives Robert Saleh time. The roster is not good, but no rebuild is ever easy for the coach because of the inevitably bad product. The Titans are 1-9, and a 51-30 loss to Dallas  prompted Saleh to call his defense "dogs---" in a news conference. I'm not sure where to go with that, but what I'm saying is Tennessee is usually a wild card based on recent history.

 

 
 Daniel Jones and Brandon Aiyuk are suddenly free agents after their respective releases. What's next, and where they could land? 
 Editor's note: As of Wednesday afternoon, Aiyuk is signing with the Commanders practice squad . 

 Fowler: Let's start with Jones. Now that he has cleared waivers, he must weigh whether to sign somewhere right away or wait this out to see what develops injury-wise around the league as the playoffs approach. Some people I've talked to inside the league wonder whether  he'll choose the latter . The natural fit right now is New England, which is 5-5 and will be without Drake Maye for what looks like the rest of the regular season . But coach Mike Vrabel seems intent on starting Tommy DeVito , at least this week. So, maybe that's the play -- wait this week out, see what happens with New England or if another team develops an opening.

 But I'm not sure which job would actually rebuild Jones' free agency value at this point. It depends what's important to him: a chance to start, take over for an older quarterback, be next season's bridge guy or learn a new system on a winning team.

 Graziano: If I were considering signing Jones, I'd be thinking more about next season than this one based on everything we've seen from him this year. An Achilles injury is awfully serious, and he wouldn't be the first player we've seen look a lot better in his second season after that surgery than his first. The notion that the 2026 version of Jones could step in and help save someone's season is far-fetched.

 

 I believe the Patriots want to go with DeVito in the hopes that he can keep their train on the track, but as we saw with that disastrous Carson Wentz start for the Vikings a couple of Monday nights ago , poor performance can absolutely change a team's plan. Jones seems like a guy who's going to get another chance somewhere at some point, but my expectations for him being a significant help to a team the rest of this season are quite low.
